WST.brief: West Pharmaceutical Services (WST) Sells SmartDose Rights To AbbVie To Refocus Its Business

EMP-A.brief: Empire Company Limited Announces Renewal of Normal Course Issuer Bid

DOL.brief: DOLLARAMA ANNOUNCES RENEWAL OF NORMAL COURSE ISSUER BID

CTHH.brief: Qwest Corp filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and suspend its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The filing covers its 6.5% Notes due 2056 (63 holders) and 6.75% Notes due 2057 (60 holders), relying on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and (2), 12h-3(b)(1)(i) and (ii), and 15d-6/22(b). No board recommendation or advisor was named. The action reflects that the notes are held by fewer than 300 holders, triggering deregistration. What to watch: the deregistration reduces SEC reporting obligations, potentially limiting bondholder transparency; no risk-arb angle as this is a debt instrument filing.

FTAIM.brief: FTAI Aviation Ltd. filed a Form 15-12G to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, covering its 8.25% Series C and 9.50% Series D Cumulative Perpetual Redeemable Preferred Shares, as well as its ordinary shares. The company certified that the approximate number of holders of record of each class as of the filing date was zero, thereby no longer having a duty to file reports under Sections 13(a) and 15(d). The termination was effective immediately upon filing. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms were disclosed. What to watch: Delisting/deregistration implications; no risk-arb angle as this is a regulatory termination.

ELVN.brief: Enliven Therapeutics filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a public offering of 8,933,334 common shares and pre-funded warrants for 1,733,333 shares at $37.50/$37.499 per unit. The total proceeds are ~$376 million before expenses. Shares are offered via underwriters including Jefferies and Goldman Sachs, with a 30-day greenshoe for up to 1,600,000 additional shares. This capital raise is a primary share issuance—a capital return event. The offering closes June 15, 2026. Watch for potential dilution and market reaction; no risk-arb angle as this is a straight equity financing.

ALM.brief: Almonty Industries filed a Form 6-K disclosing the issuance of US$800 million (plus US$100 million greenshoe) of 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031. The notes have an initial conversion price of ~US$27.40 per share, a ~32.5% premium to the US$20.68 closing price on June 4, 2026. Proceeds (~US$772.7 million net) will fund a capped call transaction (~US$83 million) and general corporate purposes, including potential acquisitions. The notes are senior unsecured, redeemable after July 1, 2029 under certain conditions, and subject to fundamental change put. The conversion premium suggests an equity-linked capital raise, not a special-situation catalyst.

AYA.brief: The filing is a Form 6-K by Aya Gold & Silver Inc., reporting results of its annual general meeting of shareholders. It shows nine director nominees were elected, with vote percentages ranging from 88.91% to 99.97%. KPMG was ratified as auditor, and the say-on-pay advisory resolution passed with 94.75% support. Two long-serving directors retired, and Ms. Ghislane Guedira was appointed Chair; women now represent 50% of the board. No transaction, tender offer, merger, or other special situation is involved. This is a routine AGM results filing and does not constitute a special situation event.

FOFO.company: Hang Feng Technology Innovation Co., Ltd.
FOFO.brief: Hang Feng Technology Innovation Co., Ltd. files Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval at an EGM on June 12, 2026, for a share capital reclassification (creating Class A and Class B ordinary shares), a US$400 repurchase of 4,000,000 Class A shares from Hang Feng International Holdings, and a simultaneous issuance of 4,000,000 Class B shares to the same entity at par value. The aggregate consideration for the repurchase is paid from the proceeds of the fresh issuance. Approximately 54.68% of shares were represented. These steps appear structured to grant Hang Feng International enhanced voting control via multi-class share structure with no premium or material cash outflow. Watch for potential future delisting risk or governance changes.

ING.brief: ING Groep N.V. filed a Form 6-K announcing its acquisition of an approximately 40% stake in Singular Bank, a Spanish wealth manager with about €19 billion in client assets. The stake is acquired from Warburg Pincus, which holds 93% of shares. Terms such as price per share or premium were not disclosed. The deal complements ING's launch of its own Private Banking in Spain. Singular Bank will remain independent, with management and other investors retaining shares. The transaction is expected to close pending regulatory approvals. Watch for closing conditions and potential synergies in asset management.

KSPI.brief: Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz filed a Form 6-K announcing results of its extraordinary general meeting held on June 11, 2026. Shareholders approved a dividend of KZT 850 per common share for 1Q 2026, payable in cash by wire transfer starting June 11, 2026, to holders of record on June 10, 2026. The meeting also approved the election of three members to the Counting commission. This is a routine capital return event, not triggering a special-situation category. No other strategic action (e.g., merger, tender, spinoff) is present.

LYG.brief: Lloyds Banking Group plc filed a Form 6-K disclosing a transaction in its own shares. On 3 July 2026, the company purchased 5,000,000 ordinary shares from Goldman Sachs International at a volume-weighted average price of 114.2565 pence per share. The purchases were made under an existing share buyback programme announced on 30 January 2026, with the shares to be cancelled. The buyback is a capital return mechanism. No additional terms or advisors were specified. Watch for pace of further buybacks and potential impact on EPS.

LOTWW.brief: Lotus Technology Inc. filed a 6-K reporting a convertible note purchase agreement with Geely International (Hong Kong) Limited. The company will issue a $128.3 million senior convertible note via private placement, expected to close in June 2026. The note matures in 364 days, bears interest at SOFR + 3.35%, and is convertible into ordinary shares or ADSs at the volume-weighted average price over the 10 days before conversion. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The transaction is a form of capital raising, structured as debt with conversion optionality, ranking senior to unsecured debt. Watch for dilution upon conversion and the use of proceeds.

MAAS.brief: Maase Inc. files Form 6-K to provide audited combined financial statements of Times Good Limited, acquired 100% on March 30, 2026, and unaudited pro forma combined financials. No terms, price, or premium disclosed. The acquisition closed previously; this is a post-closing financial filing. Board recommendation and advisors not stated. The filing incorporates by reference into a Form S-8. What to watch: integration progress; risk-arb angle not applicable as deal is closed.

NMR.brief: Nomura Holdings Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting its monthly share buyback for May 2026. Under a board resolution from January 30, 2026, it has authorized repurchase of up to 100 million shares for up to JPY 60 billion through September 30, 2026. During May, it continued repurchasing, bringing cumulative repurchases to 46.86 million shares for JPY 59.999 billion (100% of the monetary limit, 46.9% of shares). No disposition or cancellation of shares was reported in the month. This is a routine open-market buyback program. Nomura is the issuer. The filing reflects ongoing capital return to shareholders. Watch for utilization of remaining share authorization and any updates on cancellation plans.

ODD.brief: Oddity Tech's subsidiary Oddity Finance repurchased $50M of its 0% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2030 for $35M, implying a 30% discount. Closing expected June 17, 2026; after the transaction, $550M principal remains outstanding. This is a liability management transaction and a return of capital to noteholders, effectively reducing leverage. No board recommendation or advisors named. The repurchase is privately negotiated, subject to customary conditions. Watch for potential further liability management or equity-linked conversions; the discount is a positive for remaining noteholders but reduces the size of the outstanding exchangeable security.

PLBL.brief: Polibeli Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 12, 2026, announcing it is evaluating opportunities in the AI computing infrastructure services sector as part of its long-term growth strategy. The company has operational experience, business relationships, and customer resources across Southeast Asia, and believes AI represents a significant long-term trend. No specific transactions, terms, advisors, or timelines are disclosed. This is a general strategic evaluation announcement and does not constitute a formal strategic review or special situation.

RETO.brief: ReTo Eco-Solutions (Buyer) files Form 6-K reporting the closing of its acquisition of 51% of Seven Arrows Supply Chain Limited from Rei Shiba (Seller) through a share exchange. The consideration was newly issued ReTo Class A shares (no par value), with 25,500 ordinary shares of Seven Arrows acquired. The transaction closed on February 27, 2026. Alongside, ReTo provides audited financials of Seven Arrows and unaudited pro forma combined financials as Exhibits. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This is a completed stock-for-stock acquisition; no premium, price per share, or regulatory clock is specified. Watch for integration updates and future filings on combined operations.

SONY.brief: Sony Group Corp filed a Form 6-K reporting a monthly update of its ongoing share repurchase program authorized by its Board on May 8, 2026. The company repurchased 18,006,700 shares for ¥60,216,974,617 in open market purchases on the Tokyo Stock Exchange during June 1–30, 2026, under a discretionary trading contract. The overall program authorizes up to 230 million shares (3.89% of outstanding) and ¥500 billion through May 10, 2027. As of June 30, 2026, cumulative repurchases total 37,076,600 shares for ¥127,476,788,305. This routine open-market buyback returns capital to shareholders directly. Watch for execution pace against the authorized ceiling, which may support EPS and share price.

TFPM.brief: Triple Flag Precious Metals Corp. (NYSE/TSX: TFPM) filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of its wholly owned subsidiary's acquisition of a US$440 million gold stream on the producing Ravenswood Gold Mine in Queensland, Australia. The stream was previously disclosed in a June 12, 2026 news release. First gold delivery is expected in Q3 2026. The company increased its 2030 outlook to 150,000-160,000 GEOs. No financial terms (price per share, premium) are applicable as this is a streaming agreement, not an equity transaction. As a Canadian issuer, the 6-K furnishes the announcement to the SEC. Watch for operational updates on Ravenswood's ramp-up to ~200,000 oz gold per annum by 2028.

XRTX.brief: XORTX Therapeutics Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing its voluntary delisting from the TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV), while maintaining its Nasdaq listing. The decision is effective as of June 12, 2026, following board approval; no shareholder vote was required under TSXV policies due to the alternative market listing. No price, premium, or consideration is involved — this is a purely administrative delisting. The company cited cost savings, regulatory simplification, and management focus as reasons. No action is required from shareholders. Watch for the final delisting date and any potential Nasdaq compliance or liquidity risks.

AHT-PI.brief: Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc. (AHT) filed an 8-K reporting the completion of the sale of the Marriott Fremont Silicon Valley, a 357-room hotel in Fremont, California. The sale closed on July 1, 2026, for approximately $52.2 million in cash, net of selling expenses, under an Agreement of Purchase and Sale dated June 19, 2026, with SRE Acquisitions V, LLC as purchaser. The company also paid about $43.5 million to the mortgage lender, which holds a loan secured by 14 hotels including this property. No board recommendation or advisor is disclosed. Key watch: potential further asset sales to reduce debt and improve liquidity.

ADGM.brief: Adagio Medical Holdings disclosed on June 12, 2026 receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as its common stock closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. The company has 180 days, until December 9, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a $1.00 closing bid for 10 consecutive trading days. A second 180-day cure period may be available pending a reverse stock split and meeting other listing standards. The stock continues trading on The Nasdaq Capital Market. Watch for reverse-split announcements or further deterioration in bid price that could trigger delisting proceedings under Rule 5810(c)(3)(A).

APMCR.brief: AmperCap Acquisition Company filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering of 12,500,000 units at $10.00 per unit on June 4, 2026, generating $125 million in gross proceeds. Each unit consists of one ordinary share and one right to receive one-tenth of a share upon a future business combination. Simultaneously, the sponsor and others purchased 512,500 private placement units at $10.00 each, raising $5.125 million. On June 10, the underwriters partially exercised their over-allotment option for 1,837,500 additional units, bringing total trust proceeds to approximately $144.8 million. The sponsor is AmperSPAC LLC. The blank-check company must complete an initial business combination within a specified period or liquidate. Watch for target announcement and shareholder redemption risks.

ASBPW.brief: Aspire Biopharma filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Purchase Agreement to acquire all equity interests and assets of certain FireFish TopCo subsidiaries. Consideration includes at least $30M base purchase price plus $800K for deferred revenue, less tax and indebtedness adjustments. The filing does not disclose premium percentage, board recommendation, or advisors. The deal involves customary representations and is structured as a cash acquisition with Section 1060 asset allocation. Closing is expected after customary conditions. Watch for regulatory clearance and potential purchase price adjustments.

BNY-PK.company: Bank of New York Mellon Corp
BNY-PK.brief: The Bank of New York Mellon Corp filed an 8-K announcing a 19% increase in its quarterly cash dividend from $0.53 to $0.63 per share, expected to commence in Q3 2026 pending board approval. The filing also notes that the company's Stress Capital Buffer remains at the 2.5% floor following the 2026 Fed stress test, and that it continues to be authorized for share repurchases under an existing program announced in April 2026. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, or structured programs. No advisor or recommendation is noted. This is a shareholder return event, not a merger or acquisition. Watch for dividend declaration and actual buyback execution.

BCDA.brief: BioCardia, Inc. filed an 8-K (Item 3.01) updating its Nasdaq compliance status. On June 8, 2026, the company sold 3,509,604 shares at an average price of $1.279 via its ATM agreement with H.C. Wainwright. From April 1 to June 5, 2026, it sold 4,004,330 shares at ~$1.27, netting $4.9M. Believing stockholders' equity exceeds $2.5M, it regained compliance with Nasdaq Rule 5550(b)(1). Nasdaq granted an extension to October 7, 2026 but will monitor ongoing compliance. No board action or deal advisors were named. What to watch: risk of delisting if future periodic reports show non-compliance or equity falls again.

PHGE.brief: BiomX Inc. disclosed on June 10, 2026, that NYSE Regulation accepted its compliance plan to address its stockholders' deficit of $(1,302,000) as of December 31, 2025, and ongoing losses, which triggered non-compliance with Sections 1003(a)(i)-(iii) of the NYSE American Company Guide. The plan grants a cure period through September 25, 2027. During this period, the stock will trade with a .BC indicator and remain on the exchange's noncompliant list. If progress falters, delisting proceedings may follow. Key watchpoint: whether BiomX executes its plan milestones within the 15-month window or faces potential delisting, impacting liquidity and risk-arb dynamics.

CYAB.brief: On June 9, 2026, Cyabra, Inc. received Nasdaq deficiency notices for failing to maintain a minimum Market Value of Publicly Held Shares (MVPHS) of $15M and a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share, each for 30 consecutive business days ended June 8. The Company has 180 calendar days (until December 7, 2026) to regain compliance by closing at $15M MVPHS or $1.00 bid for 10 consecutive business days. Failure may lead to delisting, with appeal rights or a possible transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market. A potential second 180-day period exists for the bid-price rule. No board recommendation or advisor is disclosed. The stock continues trading under CYAB. Watch for compliance milestones and potential reverse split or shareholder action to cure deficiencies.

CELUW.brief: Celularity Inc received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 9, 2026, for failing to maintain a minimum Market Value of Listed Securities (MVLS) of $35 million over 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day grace period until December 7, 2026, to regain compliance, requiring MVLS of $35 million for at least 10 consecutive business days. The notice does not trigger immediate delisting. Alternatives include boosting stockholders' equity to $2.5 million. The board has not announced specific remediation actions. Watch for compliance progress and potential reverse stock split or other structural remedies.

ALFUW.brief: Centurion Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, filed an 8-K regarding Non-Redemption Agreements with certain shareholders to prevent redemption of 4,675,000 Class A ordinary shares at the upcoming EGM on the Extension Amendment Proposal, which would extend the business combination deadline from June 12, 2026 to June 12, 2027. In exchange, the Sponsor will transfer 1,558,333 Class A shares to these investors post-business combination. This is a SPAC extension inducement arrangement, not a definitive business combination. The filing details mechanics to secure the extension vote and reduce redemptions. Watch for the EGM outcome and any eventual de-SPAC announcement.

GLV.brief: Clough Global Dividend & Income Fund filed an 8-K announcing the Board's renewal of its open-market share repurchase program. The program permits the Fund to buy back up to 5% of its outstanding common shares through June 30, 2027. Repurchases are at the discretion of the adviser, subject to market conditions, and are designed to enhance shareholder value when shares trade at a discount to net asset value. The renewal follows an original June 2023 launch. There is no fixed price, premium, or tender offer mechanics. Watch for periodic disclosure of buyback volumes in shareholder reports and potential NAV discount narrowing.

GLQ.brief: Clough Global Equity Fund (GLQ) filed an 8-K to disclose the annual renewal of its open-market share repurchase program. The Board authorized the repurchase of up to 5% of outstanding common shares through June 30, 2027. The program, originally approved in June 2023, is designed to enhance shareholder value by buying shares at discounts to net asset value. Since inception through May 30, 2026, GLQ repurchased 386,500 shares. Repurchases are discretionary, subject to market conditions and regulatory limits. No adviser or deal advisor is named. Watch for ongoing NAV discount arbitrage and periodic disclosure of repurchase activity.

GLO.brief: Clough Global Opportunities Fund filed an 8-K announcing its Board of Trustees renewed an open-market share repurchase program, originally approved June 2023, allowing repurchase of up to 5% of outstanding common shares through June 30, 2027. The program aims to enhance shareholder value by buying shares when trading at a discount to net asset value. No specific price, premium, or advisor is named; purchases are at the adviser's discretion based on market conditions. This is a capital return initiative to reduce discount and support share price. Watch for periodic discount updates and repurchase pace.

BOTX.brief: Registrant DATZ World Holdings Corp., fka LeafBuyer Technologies, filed an 8-K reporting completion of its merger with RagingBull.com, LLC on June 8, 2026. Per the Merger Agreement dated Nov. 10, 2025, acquirer LB Acquisition Corp. merged into RagingBull, which survived as a wholly-owned subsidiary. Consideration was 15,000,000 newly issued common shares, representing ~95% ownership to RagingBull holders post-reverse split. Board and officers were reconstituted, with departures of Kurt Rossner (CEO/Chairman), Mark Breen (CFO), and others. The merger is treated as a tax-free exchange under IRC Sec. 368. Watch for potential OTC pink-sheet volatility and any post-closing adjustments.

GOAI.brief: Eva Live Inc. filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026, announcing the formation of a wholly owned subsidiary, Eva Defense Inc., to pursue acquisitions and partnerships in drone and defense technology. No specific deal terms, stake, price, or premium were disclosed. The board recommended the strategic initiative, though no advisors were named. The subsidiary will focus on acquiring companies with proprietary technologies in autonomous systems and defense. The filing is a forward-looking strategic announcement rather than a definitive special situation. To watch: whether Eva Defense identifies specific targets or completes any transactions.

FBLA.brief: FB Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a third stock repurchase program authorizing up to 1,606,837 shares, or 10% of outstanding common stock. The program will be conducted on the open market, potentially via a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, with no set price or premium. The board has not named an advisor. This follows completion of two prior programs repurchasing 1,983,750 and 1,785,375 shares respectively. The repurchase is discretionary and can be suspended at any time. Watch for execution pace and market conditions; no risk-arb angle as it is a pure capital return initiative.

HLX.brief: Helix Energy Solutions Group filed this 8-K to disclose the early termination of the HSR waiting period for its acquisition of Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc. Under the Merger Agreement, a wholly owned subsidiary of Helix will merge with Hornbeck, then the surviving corporation will merge into another Helix subsidiary. The transaction is expected to close in H2 2026, subject to Helix shareholder approval and other customary conditions. No specific price per share, premium, or deal value is stated in this excerpt. Advisors are not named. Watch for shareholder vote timing and regulatory approvals.

IBCP.brief: Independent Bank Corp (IBCP) filed an 8-K reporting that HCB Financial Corp shareholders approved the merger agreement dated March 18, 2026, in which IBCP will acquire HCB. The all-stock deal is expected to close July 1, 2026, pending customary conditions. No per-share price, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The filing notes Rule 425 communications. Watch for regulatory approvals and the closing mechanics; the narrow spread to close suggests low risk-arb opportunity.

INHD.brief: Inno Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that Nasdaq imposed a Trading Halt (Code T12) on its common stock post-market on June 8, 2026. In response, the board formed a special committee of independent directors to investigate unusual trading activities. The company states it is unaware of any material undisclosed corporate developments. This filing does not involve a transaction or a forced management change; it is an internal review of trading anomalies. There are no deal terms. Watch for findings of the investigation or potential regulatory actions.

IPFXU.brief: Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. VI, a blank-check company, filed an 8-K announcing a Business Combination Agreement with Quantum Space, LLC. The deal values the combined entity at a pro forma enterprise value of approximately $1.2 billion, structured as an Up-C. Inflection Point will domesticate to a Delaware corporation, and post-closing PubCo will rename to Quantum Space, Inc. The boards of both parties approved the transaction. Closing is expected in Q4 2026, subject to shareholder and equityholder approvals. This is a de-SPAC merger, with the SPAC as the acquiring shell. The key risk-arb angle is the potential for shareholder redemptions and the timeline to regulatory clearance. No price per share, premium, or break fee were disclosed.

LASE.brief: Laser Photonics Corp (LASE) disclosed it received a Nasdaq compliance notice on June 12, 2026, confirming the company regained compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) after filing its delinquent Form 10-Q for Q1 2026 on June 11. The filing resolved a non-compliance notice issued May 21, 2026, related to the late quarterly report. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The delisting risk is now closed, with no further regulatory clock. The stock remains listed on Nasdaq. What to watch: any future filing delays that could trigger a new deficiency. Risk-arb angle: not applicable given this is a compliance cure, not a transaction.

MBAVW.brief: M3-Brigade Acquisition V Corp. (a SPAC) filed an 8-K reporting mutual termination of its Business Combination Agreement with ReserveOne, Inc., originally signed July 7, 2025, due to changed market conditions in digital assets. The termination was effective June 12, 2026, under Section 7.1(a) of the BCA, with only customary survival provisions. Concurrently, the SPAC will seek shareholder approval to extend its combination deadline from August 2, 2026 to August 2, 2027. No termination fee was disclosed. No new target was announced. The risk-arb angle: watch for shareholder vote on extension and ability to find a new deal within the extended window.

MVIS.brief: MicroVision filed an 8-K on June 12, 2026, reporting amendments to its existing At-The-Market Issuance Sales Agreement with Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, and Craig-Hallum. Approximately $42 million of common stock remains unsold. The amendment updates the agreement to reference a new S-3 registration statement filed concurrently. Separately, the Company submitted an application to transfer its listing from the Nasdaq Global Market to the Nasdaq Capital Market to address a non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule. If approved, MicroVision would receive an additional 180-day grace period to regain compliance. The transfer is subject to Nasdaq staff review; there is no guarantee of approval or that compliance will be achieved.

MPWR.brief: Monolithic Power Systems filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 annual meeting voting results and declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $2.00 per share. The dividend will be paid on July 15, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 30, 2026. This is a routine capital return event with no premium, merger, or activist involvement. The company is returning capital to shareholders in the ordinary course. No special situation or extraordinary corporate event is present. Watch for any future changes in dividend policy or special dividends.

NMTC.brief: NeuroOne Medical Technologies (NMTC) filed an 8-K disclosing the filing of a Prospectus Supplement under its existing Capital on Demand Sales Agreement with JonesTrading for an at-the-market (ATM) offering of up to $13.4 million of its common stock. No price, premium, or specific terms are stated; the offering utilizes an existing registration statement (S-3). Honigman LLP issued a legal opinion on the shares. This ATM program allows the company to sell shares occasionally at market prices. Watch for sales volume and dilutive impact on stock.

OFAL.brief: OFA Group disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency letter granting an additional 180-day compliance period (until December 7, 2026) to regain the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for its Class A ordinary shares. The company initially failed the bid price rule on December 11, 2025, and the first 180-day period expired June 9, 2026. Nasdaq determined OFA met all other listing standards, including market value of publicly held shares. To cure, OFA may effect a reverse stock split. If noncompliant by the Compliance Date, a delisting notice will issue, subject to appeal. Watch for potential reverse stock split announcement and bid price trajectory; risk-arb angle minimal as this is a listing standards issue, not a transactional event.

PGACR.brief: Pantages Capital Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K disclosing shareholder approval of a one-year extension (until June 6, 2027) to complete a business combination, with monthly deposits of $0.033 per public share into the trust. Approximately 5.9M shares were redeemed at ~$10.60/share, removing ~$62.4M from trust. Post-redemption, 2.98M Class A and 2.16M Class B shares remain, with ~$29.0M in trust. This is a routine SPAC extension vote, not a special-situation event; the filing reports procedural steps. Watch for any future business combination announcement or further redemptions.

PMNT.brief: Perfect Moment Ltd. filed an 8-K reporting NYSE American's determination that it failed to regain compliance with minimum stockholders' equity requirements (Section 1003(a)(ii)) within the 18-month cure period. The board opted not to appeal and will transition listing to OTC Markets. Trading on NYSE American will be suspended the week of June 15, 2026, with OTCQB trading commencing immediately after. No price, premium, or deal terms are stated. The company remains subject to SEC reporting. Risk-arb angle: none; this is a delisting, not a transaction. Watch for OTC liquidity and any subsequent financing or restructuring.

QXO-PB.brief: QXO, Inc. filed an 8-K upon consummation of its acquisition of TopBuild Corp. via a merger agreement dated April 18, 2026. QXO acquired TopBuild through wholly owned subsidiaries Titanium MergerCo and Forward Merger Sub. No per-share price, premium, or deal value is stated in this excerpt. The filing also covers amendments to QXO's term loan facility to finance the acquisition. The board likely approved the transaction, though no recommendation or advisors are named. This is a definitive acquisition close. What to watch: integration risk and potential dilution if stock was used; no break fee or regulatory clock mentioned.

RCKTW.brief: Rocket Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K disclosing completion of the sale of its Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) to a large pharmaceutical company for gross proceeds of $180 million. The PRV was received upon FDA approval of KRESLADI (marnetegragene autotemcel), a gene therapy for LAD-I. The sale closed on June 10, 2026, under an asset purchase agreement dated April 26, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named in the excerpt. The transaction is a straightforward asset divestiture with no regulatory clock noted. Watch for potential use of proceeds and any updates on the company's capital allocation strategy.

RAAQW.brief: Real Asset Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) completed its de-SPAC merger with IQM Quantum Computers Oyj on July 1, 2026. Under the Business Combination Agreement, RAAQ merged with IQM's subsidiary, becoming an indirect wholly owned unit of IQM. IQM effectuated internal capital restructuring before the merger. Terms include the Sponsor forfeiting 1,375,000 founder shares for no consideration and up to 3,725,000 private placement warrants if redemptions exceeded set thresholds; no specific per-share price or premium disclosed. The combined entity's reporting is now IQM US LLC. The deal created a publicly traded quantum-computing company. Watch for post-merger stock performance, redemption levels, and potential Nasdaq listing compliance.

SWKS.brief: Skyworks Solutions filed an 8-K reporting results of early participation in its exchange offers and consent solicitations for Qorvo's outstanding 4.375% Senior Notes due 2029 and 3.375% Senior Notes due 2031. The filing is an update to a previously disclosed exchange offer as part of a merger agreement. No terms (price, premium, close date) are stated in this filing. The company is the issuer offering to exchange its securities for Qorvo notes. The structural detail is that this relates to a merger integration step. Watch for final exchange results and merger closing conditions; risk-arb focuses on successful exchange and shareholder approvals.

SNBRQ.brief: Sleep Number Corp filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026, disclosing that Nasdaq notified the company of its determination to delist Sleep Number's common stock (SNBR) following the company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing on June 12, 2026. The delisting is based on Nasdaq Listing Rules 5101, 5110(b) and IM-5101-1 due to public interest concerns, equity concerns for common stockholders, and compliance sustainability. Trading will be suspended on June 23, 2026. The company does not intend to appeal. After suspension, shares may trade over-the-counter. No board recommendation or financial advisor named. Monitor OTC trading liquidity and Chapter 11 proceedings for potential recovery or restructuring outcomes.

TYL.brief: Tyler Technologies disclosed entry into a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan to repurchase up to $150 million of its common stock from June 16 to July 30, 2026, as part of a $1.0 billion board-authorized repurchase program (February 3, 2026) with $332.7 million remaining. The plan is prearranged and complies with Rule 10b5-1 to allow repurchases even if material non-public information arises. Funding comes from cash and credit facility; no premium, tender, or structural changes. Watch for execution pace and impact on shares outstanding; no risk-arb angle as this is an open-market buyback.

TACHU.brief: Titan Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) filed an 8-K reporting a First Amendment to its Business Combination Agreement with OpenPayd Global Holdings Limited (PubCo), OpenPayd Holdings Limited (target), and related parties. The amendment clarifies that parties will use reasonable best efforts to redeem all outstanding purchaser warrants prior to or concurrent with acquisition closing. No financial terms (price, premium, implied value) disclosed. The SPAC targets a fintech/fintech infrastructure company. Watch for shareholder vote timing, redemption trends, and regulatory approvals to gauge deal completion risk.

WES.brief: Western Midstream Partners, LP filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its acquisition of Brazos Delaware II, LLC from Brazos Permian II, LLC for approximately $1.6 billion. Consideration consisted of $800 million in cash and 19,389,239 common units (worth ~$800 million based on a 20-day VWAP at signing). The board had previously approved the deal. Seller received registration rights and is subject to a six-month lock-up. The acquisition adds midstream assets in the Permian Basin. Key risk-arb factors include post-close unit price performance relative to the lock-up expiration and any integration issues.

XOMAP.brief: XOMA Royalty Corp filed an 8-K announcing the expected closing of its acquisition by Ligand Pharmaceuticals, originally disclosed April 27, 2026 and amended May 16, 2026. Closing is on or about July 14, 2026, subject to satisfaction of remaining conditions. Separately, XOMA delivered notices to redeem its Series A and Series B Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock in connection with the merger. The transaction is structured as a merger with Flex Merger Sub, Inc. Terms such as price per share, premium, and deal value were not restated in this filing. Watch for regulatory clearance and the July closing date as risk-arb events, with redemption mechanics signaling deal certainty.

GRAF-WT.brief: Graf Global Corp. filed an 8-K on June 26, 2026, reporting non-redemption agreements (NRAs) with certain shareholders covering 4,256,015 Class A ordinary shares. In exchange for not redeeming shares at the meeting to approve an extension amendment, Sponsor Graf Global Sponsor LLC agreed to transfer 425,602 founder shares to them after a business combination closes. NRAs are a common SPAC tactic to preserve trust cash. No deal price, premium, or expected close stated. Watch: shareholder vote on extension and subsequent business combination announcement.

NSA-PB.brief: National Storage Affiliates Trust (NSA) filed an 8-K on July 8, 2026, disclosing supplemental information regarding its pending acquisition by Public Storage. NSA is merging with a subsidiary of Public Storage, with shareholders set to vote on July 14, 2026. The filing updates on shareholder lawsuits challenging the merger, which were filed after the March 16, 2026 announcement. Deal terms include a merger agreement with Public Storage, but specific price/share or premium are not stated here. The board recommends approval. The expected close is subject to shareholder vote and regulatory conditions. Watch for lawsuit outcomes and shareholder approval risk.

ZDPY.brief: Zoned Properties, Inc. filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) reporting the partial closing of a real estate sale. Through subsidiaries, it sold two properties (Green Valley and Kingman) to Broken Arrow Herbal Center, Inc., for $1.0 million cash ($0.5 million each). A third property (Chino) closing was extended to August 31, 2026, with a possible further extension to September 30, 2026. The purchase agreement was previously filed on April 22, 2026, and those terms are incorporated by reference. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The deal is structured as a cash sale of non-residential buildings. Watch for the closing of the Chino property by the extended deadline; risk-arb centers on whether the buyer exercises the final extension.

FVNNR.brief: Future Vision II Acquisition Corp. (a Cayman Islands SPAC) filed an amended S-4 registering its proposed business combination with MicroTouch Technology Inc. The deal implies a valuation not explicitly stated but will be paid in stock (SPAC equity) to MicroTouch holders. The boards of both companies recommend the transaction. The SPAC must complete the merger within its charter deadline; public shareholders have redemption rights, creating potential overhang. The SEC review clock is ongoing. Key risk-arb watch: shareholder redemption levels and SEC clearance of the registration statement.

HBT.brief: HBT Financial filed Amendment No. 1 to its Registration Statement on Form S-4 with the SEC on June 12, 2026, originally filed on May 27, 2026. The amendment updates Part II, Item 21 (Exhibits) only; the prospectus remains unchanged. The registration statement relates to the formation of a holding company structure and a proposed public offering of securities. No specific stake, price, premium, or close date is disclosed. The filing includes standard indemnification provisions for directors and officers under Delaware law. Risk-arb watchers should monitor the SEC's effectiveness declaration and any further procedural updates.

MNTSW.brief: Momentus Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a best-efforts offering of 1,851,852 shares of Class A common stock at $13.50/share, for gross proceeds of $25M. The offering is not a special situation but an ordinary equity raise to fund operations. A.G.P./Alliance Global Partners is the placement agent, receiving a 7% cash fee and five-year warrants exercisable at 110% of the offering price. Delivery is expected on or about June 15, 2026. This is a routine capital raise, not a special situation. What to watch: dilution impact and use of proceeds; no risk-arb angle as it is not a merger or acquisition event.

AXIA-PC.brief: AXIA Energia S.A., formerly Eletrobras, filed a Form 6-K announcing the voluntary delisting of its Common ADSs (AXIA) and Class C Preferred ADSs (AXIA PRC) from the NYSE. The delisting consolidates liquidity on B3, as ADSs represent only ~2.5% of outstanding shares. Last trading day is on or about August 6, 2026; effectiveness 10 days after filing Form 25. Post-delisting, ADSs will trade OTC via a Level 1 sponsored ADR with Citibank. The company will file Form 15F to deregister and suspend Exchange Act reporting. Watch for any SEC objections and the 90-day suspension timeline.

BIRK.brief: Birkenstock Holding plc, via its indirect subsidiary Birkenstock Group B.V. Co. KG, announced the offering of €900M aggregate principal amount of senior notes due 2033. Proceeds will be used to redeem €428.5M of outstanding 5.25% Senior Notes due 2029, finance share repurchases, refinance other debt, and pay fees. The notes are senior unsecured and expected to be listed on The International Stock Exchange. This is a debt refinancing and capital management transaction, not a special situation event. No merger, tender offer, or activist activity is involved. Watch for pricing and completion risk; no premium or share price impact directly.

AIBZ.brief: Bitzero Holdings Inc. filed a Form 6-K with a press release marking its first week of Nasdaq trading and providing operational updates on its Nordic data center projects, including a binding letter for a US$2.6 billion 15-year lease at its Norway site and construction milestones. No special-situation corporate action (acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, tender offer, going-private, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC, or forced management change) is described. The filing is a routine business update typical of a foreign private issuer's current report, not an event that materially changes the corporate structure or triggers a special situation.

CGTL.brief: Creative Global Technology Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting results of its 2026 Extraordinary General Meeting and Class B Meeting. Proposals approved include: (1) increasing Class B share voting rights from 20 to 100 votes per share; (2) increasing authorized share capital from US$2M to US$90M; (3) reducing par value from US$0.001 to US$0.00001 per share (credited to share premium); and (4) adopting amended articles. All proposals passed with over 95% quorum. No offer, acquisition, divestiture, or activist campaign is disclosed; this is a routine shareholder authorization for capital structure changes. No deal terms apply. The filing is a foreign issuer's report of corporate governance amendments, not a special situation.

ELPC.brief: COPEL (Energy Company of Parana) filed a Form 6-K reporting a board resolution to divest its stake in Dona Francisca Energética S.A. (DFESA) to Gerdau S.A. The board also resolved not to exercise preemptive rights to acquire Celesc's shares in DFESA. Binding proposal from Gerdau is cited, motivated by high energy prices and self-generation benefits. The board approved the negotiation and signing of a Share Purchase Agreement. No financial terms (price, premium, close date) were disclosed in the filing. The decision was based on the proposal not meeting COPEL's profitability criteria. The transaction represents a strategic exit from a minority stake, with execution risk in the negotiation and regulatory steps.

GMAB.brief: Genmab A/S filed a Form 6-K to disclose a major shareholder announcement: Orbis Investment Management Limited reported holdings of 3,112,476 shares (4.99% of capital and voting rights) as of June 12, 2026, under Section 30 of the Danish Capital Markets Act. The filing is a regulatory disclosure of a passive threshold crossing, not an activist campaign or takeover event. No deal terms, board recommendation, or strategic action are involved. As a passive holding notification, it triggers no special-situation classification; the event is routine regulatory compliance.

GGB.brief: Gerdau S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting a binding proposal and Share Purchase Agreement to acquire COPEL's 23.03% equity stake in Dona Francisca Energética S.A. (DFESA) for an enterprise value of R$150 million, payable in cash at closing. The deal, together with a previously announced acquisition from CELESC, will give Gerdau 100% of DFESA for a total R$300 million enterprise value, adding 30.4 average MW of self-generation capacity. Closing is subject to antitrust approval in Brazil. The board recommends the transaction, aligned with Gerdau's decarbonization strategy. Watch for regulatory clearance timeline and integration risk.

GROY-WT.brief: Gold Royalty Corp. filed a Form 6-K announcing its acquisition of an additional 0.1875% indirect NSR royalty on the REN project for $6.25 million cash, increasing its total indirect NSR to 1.6875% plus a 3.5% Net Profit Interest. The REN project, a development-stage Nevada gold asset owned by Barrick (61.5%) and Newmont (38.5%), is expected to begin production in 2026 and ramp to full output by year-end 2027 at ~140,000 oz/year. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This bolt-on royalty acquisition expands Gold Royalty's existing position on a near-term producer without changing its capital structure. Watch for production milestones from Barrick and potential further consolidation in Gold Royalty's portfolio.

HLN.brief: Haleon plc filed a Form 6-K reporting daily purchases under its ongoing share buyback programme announced on 12 March 2026. On 8 June 2026 it bought 565,285 ordinary shares at a VWAP of 331.9552 pence, all for cancellation. No other trades occurred 9–12 June. Post-settlement, registered capital stands at 8,842,187,061 shares (12,025,084 in treasury; 8,830,161,977 with voting rights). The buyback reduces share count over time, enhancing EPS. No premium, tender, or special offer—routine open-market purchases under a disclosed programme. Watch for pace of future buybacks and potential programme extension or completion announcements.

HITI.brief: High Tide Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of J. Supply Holdings Inc. (Northern Helm) for $7.74M, including ~$3.2M assumed debt, ~$1.83M cash, and ~$2.75M in High Tide common shares priced at a 10-day VWAP with a floor. The acquisition adds four retail cannabis stores in Ontario, with an implied 4.5x annualized Adjusted EBITDA multiple. The deal is arm's length, subject to TSXV and AGCO approvals, with a four-month hold period on shares. Expected to close in weeks. Watch for regulatory clearance and integration into High Tide's 228-store network.

INCR.brief: InterCure Ltd. filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release announcing the initial closing of its acquisition of Botanico Ltd. (ISHI), an Israeli cannabis technology and brand company. The first tranche involves issuing 2,471,061 ordinary shares, with an additional 2,470,073 shares to be issued upon satisfaction of conditions. The company also initiated a strategic review of U.S. medical cannabis opportunities following federal rescheduling. The acquisition provides exclusive rights to U.S. cannabis genetics, brands, and AI-driven technologies. No advisors or premium were disclosed. Watch for regulatory milestones and integration progress.

BEKE.brief: KE Holdings Inc. filed a Form 6-K containing Next Day Disclosure Returns detailing an ongoing share repurchase program. The filing lists numerous open-market repurchases of its Hong Kong-listed WVR ordinary shares and US-listed ADSs between May 22 and June 10, 2026, at prices ranging from HKD 42.44 to HKD 45.01 per share and USD 5.30 to USD 5.76 per ADS. These are purchases by the issuer for cancellation, reducing outstanding share count. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is applicable as this is an issuer tender conducted on-market. The regulatory framework is the Hong Kong Listing Rules for equity issuers. The aggregate amounts imply a consistent, material return of capital to shareholders. Watch for the pace of future repurchases as a signal of management's view on intrinsic value.

NONOF.brief: Novo Nordisk filed a Form 6-K disclosing ongoing open-market B-share repurchases under a DKK 15 billion programme running from 4 February 2026 to early 2027. The filing reports daily transactions from 30 June to 3 July 2026, totaling 800,000 B shares for ~DKK 256 million, at average prices of DKK 314.24–326.71. As of 3 July, the company repurchased 23,009,179 B shares for DKK 6.22 billion overall. The programme follows Safe Harbour Rules (EU MAR). Shares are held as treasury, currently 0.9% of capital. Watch for continued buyback cadence and impact on EPS.

NTR.brief: Nutrien Ltd. filed a 6-K cautioning shareholders regarding an unsolicited mini-tender offer by Ocehan LLC to purchase up to 100,000 common shares (0.02% of outstanding) at C$70.20/share, a 24.91% discount to the TSX closing price and 26.13% discount to NYSE closing price on May 8, 2026. Nutrien does not endorse the offer and notes it lacks standard investor protections. Although this is a tender offer, it is de minimis, unsolicited, and at a deep discount, making it a cautionary filing rather than a substantive special situation. Watch for SEC/CSA advisories on mini-tenders.

RGNT.brief: Regentis Biomaterials Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting the withdrawal of its Registration Statement on Form F-1 (File No. 333-295510) effective June 15, 2026, abandoning its planned public offering. No financial terms, stake, or premium apply as no transaction was consummated. The board decided not to pursue the offering; no advisors named. This is a withdrawal of a securities registration, not a special situation. Watch for alternative financing or strategic alternatives.

RYAAY.brief: Ryanair filed a Form 6-K reporting weekly open-market share repurchases under its pre-announced buyback programme (announced May 20, 2025). During June 29–July 3, 2026, it bought 5,084 ordinary shares at a VWAP of ~€27.07 per share and 242,464 ADS-equivalent shares at ~$32.09 per ADS. All purchased shares are cancelled. The buyback is disclosed under EU MAR Article 5(1)(b). No board recommendation or advisor is named; the programme reduces share count and returns capital to holders. The filing is a routine weekly update, representing ordinary-course capital return rather than a special corporate event. What to watch: continuation of steady repurchase pace; no premium or tender offer structure.

SLBT.brief: SL Science Holding Ltd (issuer) filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of its business combination between SL BIO Ltd. and SPAC Horizon Space Acquisition II Corp., approved by SPAC shareholders on February 12, 2026. The combined entity's ordinary shares began trading on Nasdaq under ticker SLBT on June 15, 2026. The transaction implies an equity valuation of SL Bio of approximately $5.568 billion, with a concurrent $7.8 million PIPE financing. The combined company is led by CEO/Chairman William Wang and a reconstituted board with independent directors. This is a completed SPAC de-SPAC transaction; the closing event itself is now in effect. Risk-arb angle: given closing is completed and shares are trading, the focus shifts to post-merger operational execution and potential shareholder lockup expirations.

TM.brief: Toyota Motor Corp (TMC) filed on Form 6-K announcing the sale of all 74,100,604 shares of Toyota Industries Corp (24.66% stake) to Toyota Fudosan via a share repurchase by Toyota Industries, conditioned on completion of squeeze-out procedures. TMC expects non-consolidated gains of ¥1,206.3 billion and consolidated gains of ¥576.9 billion for FY ending March 2027. The consideration is cash, price per share not stated. No board recommendation or advisor named. The sale is part of a Master Agreement from March 30, 2026 press release. All transactions in TMC's planned tender offer and repurchase are now complete. Watch for any subsequent disclosures on the cash use or further unwinding of cross-shareholdings.

ZKH.brief: ZKH Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing the extension of its existing share repurchase program. The board authorized an extension for an additional 12 months through June 13, 2027, maintaining the $50 million authorization limit. As of the press date, the company had repurchased approximately 2.1 million ADSs. Repurchases may occur on the open market, in privately negotiated transactions, or block trades, funded from existing cash. No advisor or premium is noted. This is a routine capital return program extension, not a special situation; however, it is classified as 'Capital Returns' because the filing itself is the repurchase program update. Watch for execution pace versus market price.

RKDA.brief: Arcadia Biosciences, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a securities purchase agreement with an institutional investor for a private placement. The transaction involves the sale of pre-funded warrants at $1.0299 per unit, exercisable for shares at $0.0001, plus Series A-1 and A-2 investment options with $0.91 strike prices, expected gross proceeds of $4M. The board's recommendation is not disclosed; no advisor named. The pre-funded warrants and options include cashless exercise and a 4.99%-9.99% beneficial ownership blocker. This is a capital-raising event with no takeover or special-situation change. Watch for stockholder approval and registration statement effectiveness to gauge dilution effects.

ADSK.brief: Autodesk filed an 8-K disclosing entry into an Amended Revolving Credit Agreement and a new Term Loan Agreement to finance its pending acquisition of MaintainX Inc. The Revolver was upsized from $1.5B to $2.0B with looser borrowing conditions for up to $1.0B on the acquisition closing date. A separate $1.0B unsecured 364-day delayed draw term loan was also arranged, both with Citibank as agent. No purchase price, premium, or board recommendation are stated. The filings are financing mechanics; the key event is the acquisition announcement implied by the debt facilities. Watch for regulatory clearance and integration risk in the design/construction software space.

DBGI.brief: Digital Brands Group, Inc. filed an 8-K on July 6, 2026, announcing it retained the law firm Christian Attar to investigate potential naked short selling and market manipulation of its common stock. The company previously engaged Shareholder Intelligence Services (ShareIntel) to track shareholder data. The investigation follows an internal review of trading patterns raising concerns about securities law violations including naked shorting, spoofing, and beneficial ownership threshold breaches. The company intends to pursue legal action and provide evidence to the DOJ, SEC, and Ontario Securities Commission. No financial terms or transaction are involved; this is a corporate governance and legal action event.

ENSG.brief: Ensign Group filed an 8-K disclosing a $60 million increase to its existing $40 million stock repurchase program, bringing total authorization to $100 million. The program allows open-market or privately negotiated repurchases under Rule 10b-18 and 10b5-1 plans. No price per share, premium, or expiration date was specified; repurchases are discretionary based on market conditions and liquidity. The board approved the increase on June 12, 2026, with no advisor named. The filing is a capital-return event, signaling management's view of undervaluation. Watch for actual buyback pace and potential EPS accretion as risk-arb angles.

GWH.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist ESS Tech, Inc.'s warrants due to abnormally low selling price under Section 802.01D of the Listed Company Manual. The warrants, exercisable at $172.50 per share, will be removed from listing and registration effective July 13, 2026. Trading was suspended on July 1, 2026. ESS Tech did not exercise its right to appeal the NYSE's delisting determination. This is a regulatory delisting, not a merger or tender offer; no premium, shareholder vote, or deal structure is involved. The delisting is administrative, with no risk-arb angle; the warrants become worthless as a listed security.

ENHA.brief: Enhanced Group Inc. filed an 8-K regarding a securities purchase agreement for a private placement of 12,853,468 shares of Class A common stock and accompanying warrants at $3.89 per unit, the closing price on June 12, 2026, for $50 million gross proceeds. Participants include controlling shareholder Apeiron Investment Group and CEO Maximilian Martin. The offering closes in three tranches beginning June 17, 2026, subject to customary conditions. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes. Watch for subsequent tranche closings and shareholder consent; no premium or tender offer mechanics apply.

GSMT.brief: Global-Smart.Tech Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing that CEO and principal shareholder Yehor Rodin voluntarily surrendered 3,000,000 shares of common stock for cancellation at zero consideration. The board accepted the surrender, reducing outstanding shares from 6,134,780 to 3,134,780. No premium, date, or advisors were mentioned. The shares revert to authorized but unissued status, and authorized shares remain unchanged. This is a non-cash capital return via share cancellation. Watch for any follow-up capital allocation plans or liquidity events.

HCTI.brief: Healthcare Triangle, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a Securities Exchange Agreement with SecureKloud Technologies Ltd. on June 24, 2026. The Company will issue 2,828,167 common shares to SecureKloud (or its nominee) as a make-whole in exchange for the return of all Series B Preferred Stock previously issued under an earlier Asset Transfer Agreement. The exchange settles amounts owed by SecureKloud and is subject to stockholder approval per Nasdaq Rule 5635(b). No price per share or valuation is stated. The filing also includes an Amendment No. 1 to a Share Purchase Agreement with Teyame AI Holdings Inc. The transaction is structured as a settlement of prior asset-purchase consideration. Watch for stockholder vote and regulatory compliance.

IIPR-PA.brief: Innovative Industrial Properties Inc., through its operating partnership, issued $402.5 million aggregate principal amount of 6.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2029 in a private placement under Rule 144A. The offering included full exercise of a $52.5 million greenshoe option. The notes are senior unsecured obligations guaranteed by the company, ranking equal with other unsecured debt. Proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes including capital returns. Interest is payable semiannually. Watch for future use of proceeds—if directed toward share buybacks or dividends, this would be a classic capital-return event.

KIM-PM.brief: Kimco Realty OP, LLC filed an 8-K on June 15, 2026, solely to disclose the entry into a material definitive agreement for a preferred stock issuance. The filing details the terms of depositary shares representing 7.250% Class N Cumulative Convertible Perpetual Preferred Stock, along with Class L and Class M Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. No specific price per share, premium, or conversion terms are provided in the excerpt. The agreement creates a direct financial obligation and an unregistered sale of equity securities. This is a routine capital-raising transaction through preferred equity, not a special situation. No advisors or board recommendations are noted, and the focus is on the operational funding of the REIT. Monitor for future pricing and conversion details.

NGS.brief: Natural Gas Services Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 100% of Flatrock Compression Holdings LLC. The consideration includes 241,803 shares of common stock plus $110 million in cash, subject to adjustments for cash, debt, net working capital, and transaction expenses. Sellers also receive contingent royalty payments under a separate Royalty Agreement. A $2.25 million cash escrow secures post-closing adjustments. The transaction closed simultaneously with execution on June 12, 2026. The representations and warranties do not survive closing; recourse is via representation and warranty insurance. No break fee or premium disclosed. Watch for integration execution and royalty payment triggers.

NWS.brief: News Corp filed an 8-K to disclose an update to its existing $1 billion stock repurchase program. The filing notes daily disclosure to the ASX of any transactions under the program, with forward-looking statements regarding potential buybacks across Class A and Class B common stock. No specific terms (price, volume, dates) are provided beyond the aggregate $1B authorization. The board has already authorized the program; no advisor is named. The repurchases remain at management's discretion subject to market conditions and legal requirements. Watch for actual daily disclosure filings to assess execution pace and price support.

NEE-PS.brief: NextEra Energy filed an S-4 registration statement on July 9, 2026, in connection with its proposed business combination with Dominion Energy. The filing is a joint proxy statement/prospectus to register securities to be issued in the merger. The transaction involves NextEra Energy acquiring Dominion Energy. No deal terms, price per share, premium, or closing date have been disclosed in this filing. The board of each company recommends shareholders vote for the merger. The S-4 is not yet effective. The securities cannot be issued until the SEC declares the registration statement effective. What to watch: regulatory approval timeline, shareholder vote, and potential competing bids.

NMRA.brief: Neumora Therapeutics disclosed a 35% workforce reduction due to navacaprant discontinuation and amended its loan agreement to extend the interest-only period and revise liquidity covenants. The Third Amendment with K2 HealthVentures ties minimum liquidity to operational milestones and market cap (50%-110% of obligations or waived). The RIF and loan modifications indicate a strategic pivot amid pipeline restructuring. Watch for further clinical updates, compliance with covenants, and potential asset sales or additional financing to support operations.

NTRP.brief: NextTrip, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 51% of Yada Commerce Inc. from the founding shareholders for 50,000 restricted shares of NextTrip common stock. No price per share, premium, or dollar value is disclosed. The board of directors did not state a recommendation nor name an advisor. The Founding Shareholders retain operational control despite NextTrip's controlling interest; a five-member board with two designees from each side and a fifth appointed member is established. NextTrip receives a right of first refusal on future Yada share sales and serves as exclusive preferred travel provider. Watch for regulatory clearance, Nasdaq listing compliance, and risk-arb spreads given the stock-only consideration.

NIXXW.brief: Nixxy, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a binding letter of intent to acquire Tachyon 9 Corporation. The multi-step business combination values Tachyon's stock at approximately $1 billion, with Tachyon shareholders receiving Nixxy common stock at a variable conversion price based on a pre-disclosure VWAP, subject to a floor and cap. Post-closing, Tachyon stockholders are expected to hold at least 90% of the combined company. The deal targets Tachyon's proposed 620-acre hyperscale campus in North Dakota. Pre-closing, Tachyon will seek up to $75 million via a PIPE in convertible notes. What to watch: completion of due diligence on Tachyon's title and development rights; regulatory and shareholder approvals; the 'risk-arb' spread on Nixxy's stock.

OCAC-UN.brief: Ocean Capital Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K announcing the consummation of its initial public offering on June 10, 2026. The IPO comprised 11,500,000 units at $10.00 per unit, including full exercise of the underwriters' over-allotment, generating $115 million in gross proceeds. Each unit consists of one ordinary share, one right, and one redeemable warrant. Simultaneously, a private placement of 150,000 units raised $1.5 million. Net proceeds were placed in a trust account. This is a standard blank-check company IPO closing and not a special situation.

PDSB.brief: PDS Biotechnology Corp filed an 8-K disclosing the closing of a securities purchase agreement with YA II PN, LTD., issuing a $6,000,000 promissory note and a warrant to purchase up to 2,158,274 shares at $1.1824 per share. The net proceeds were used to repay existing indebtedness. The deal is a distressed financing structure akin to a PIPE; the issuer's role is that of capital raiser. No specific board recommendation or advisor was named. There is no premium or tender price; the warrant exercise price is stated. The regulatory clock is immediate, and the risk-arb angle is minimal given the debt and warrant structure.

PCTTW.brief: PureCycle Technologies filed an 8-K reporting the entry into an underwriting agreement for a registered offering of $287.5 million in 4.75% convertible senior notes due 2032. The offering included a $250 million initial tranche plus a $37.5 million over-allotment exercised in full. Morgan Stanley acted as representative of the underwriters. The notes are convertible into common stock, with customary lock-up agreements for insiders. While convertible offerings can signal capital structure changes, this is a standard debt capital markets transaction not fitting special-situation categories like restructuring or going-private. What to watch: dilution from conversion and note price performance post-close.

RBB.brief: RBB Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing two capital return actions: a board-authorized share repurchase of up to 1 million shares (~$25M at current price, ~6% of outstanding) through June 30, 2028, with open-market/private/buyback-plan mechanics; and a partial redemption of $40M principal of its 4.00% Fixed-to-Floating Subordinated Notes due 2031 at par plus accrued interest (~$40.7M total) on July 1, 2026, leaving $80M outstanding. The repurchase plan has no fixed obligation, while the redemption is mandatory upon notice. Watch for execution pace and subsequent tender/refinancing of remaining sub-debt.

SATA.brief: Strive, Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to announce that its board of directors maintained the 13.00% annual dividend rate on its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA) and declared daily cash dividends of $0.0493 per share for July 2026. This is a routine dividend maintenance and declaration with no acquisition, divestiture, or structural change. The filing also provides ROC dividend guidance regarding U.S. federal income tax treatment. No special-situation event is involved.

TLN.brief: Talen Energy Corp filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its acquisition of three natural gas power plants (Lawrenceburg 1,120 MW, Waterford 875 MW, Darby 456 MW) from Energy Capital Partners affiliates. The purchase price was $3.45 billion, consisting of ~$2.55 billion cash and 2,399,998 shares of common stock. The deal closed on June 15, 2026, with acquired entities expected to guarantee Talen's existing debt. No board recommendation or advisors are named in this excerpt. The acquisition was previously announced on January 15, 2026. Watch for integration execution and potential earnings accretion from the added 2,451 MW of gas-fired generation.

ZEOWW.brief: Zeo Energy Corp. filed an 8-K regarding a Note Purchase Agreement with White Lion Capital, LLC for up to $7.5M in unsecured convertible promissory notes. The first closing on June 9, 2026, issued a $1.67M note with $1.5M gross proceeds (10% OID). Notes mature in 24 months, bear 5% interest, and are convertible at a price equal to the greater of $0.50 or 95% of the 5-day VWAP. Additional closings up to $6M may occur through June 9, 2027. This is a structured equity line, not a special situation; watch for potential dilution from conversions at variable prices.

ENGNW.brief: enGene Therapeutics disclosed a workforce reduction of ~50%, effective June 14, 2026, to preserve cash while awaiting FDA durability data for its LEGEND cohort. The board approved the restructuring, with estimated cash costs of $5.7-6.4M (severance, benefits) and $4.7-5.0M non-cash stock-based compensation. The company retains resources for key milestones, including Cohort 1 completion, enrolling a surfactant cohort, FDA meetings, and BLA initiation in H2 2026. The filing includes Item 2.02 results and Item 8.01 update. Watch for regulatory feedback on detalimogene and potential delays in BLA submission timeline.

BANR.brief: Banner Corp filed an amended S-4 registration statement for its merger with Pacific Financial Corp. Under the agreement dated April 30, 2026, Pacific Financial will merge into Banner, with Bank of the Pacific subsequently merging into Banner Bank. Each Pacific Financial share will be converted into a fixed exchange ratio of Banner common stock (specific ratio not stated in filing). The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger. No price per share, premium, or break fee is disclosed. The merger requires shareholder votes at both companies and regulatory approvals. The filing includes a preliminary proxy statement/prospectus. Key watchpoints include shareholder approval timelines and regulatory clearance from banking regulators.

EURKU.brief: Eureka Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting Amendment No. 1 to its Business Combination Agreement with Marine Thinking Inc. and its subsidiary. The amendment revises post-closing director requirements under section 5.19 of the original October 29, 2025 BCA; no other terms (price, premium, deal value) are disclosed or changed. The registrant is the SPAC issuer entering into the de-SPAC transaction. The filing is a material definitive agreement amendment specific to the SPAC merger process. Watch for any future extensions, shareholder vote, or regulatory approvals that could affect closing timing.

NVA-WT.brief: Nova Minerals Ltd, an Australian company, filed a Form 15 with the SEC to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective June 16, 2026, following a redomiciliation under a statutory Scheme of Arrangement. Under the Scheme, Nova Minerals became a wholly-owned subsidiary of US Holdco (Nova Minerals Corp, a Nevada corporation). Holders of Nova Minerals ordinary shares listed on the ASX received one Chess Depositary Interest per ordinary share; OTC holders received one US Holdco common share per 12 ordinary shares; ADS holders (each representing 12 ordinary shares) received one common share per ADS; Nova Minerals warrant holders received three US Holdco warrants per Nova Minerals warrant. The Scheme constituted a succession under Rule 12g-3(a). Nasdaq filed a Form 25 to delist the ADSs and warrants, while US Holdco's common stock and warrants are expected to list on NYSE American starting June 17, 2026. The filing does not affect US Holdco's reporting obligations. Risk-arb watch: Monitor successful NYSE American listing and any regulatory delays.

CX.brief: Cemex files Form 6-K disclosing the first installment of a cash dividend approved at its March 26, 2026 AGM. The dividend totals USD $45.0 million, with per-share amounts of $0.017873 Mexican pesos (~$0.001039) for Series A/B shares, $0.053619 Mexican pesos per CPO, and $0.031170 per ADS. Payment dates are June 18, 2026 for shares and CPOs, and around June 29, 2026 for ADS holders. The dividend is sourced from Cemex's Net Tax Profit Account (CUFIN) as of Dec 31, 2013, making it tax-free to holders. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is applicable. The filing is a routine capital-return event under a foreign private issuer report, equivalent to a US 8-K announcing a cash dividend. Watch for subsequent installments or currency fluctuations in the MXN/USD exchange rate used for payment.

SBS.company: COMPANHIA DE SANEAMENTO BASICO DO ESTADO DE SAO PAULO-SABESP
SBS.brief: Sabesp filed a 6-K disclosing execution of a Protocol and Justification to merge with EMAE by absorbing EMAE's shares. The transaction follows an April 24, 2026 material fact. Terms are set for shareholder votes at EGMs on July 30, 2026. Exchange ratio and precise pricing are not specified in the excerpt; it is a stock-for-stock merger of two Brazilian publicly-held companies (both Category A issuers on B3). Regulatory references include CVM Resolution 78. Watch for shareholder approval and potential appraisal rights. The deal appears friendly, with boards calling meetings and recommending approval.

EC.brief: Ecopetrol S.A. filed a Form 6-K disclosing the temporary suspension of its tender offer (OPAV) in Brazil by its subsidiary Ecopetrol Investimentos do Brasil Ltda. The suspension follows requests for adjustments from the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM). The tender offer was initially announced on May 25, 2026. The auction is expected to resume on a date determined by the CVM once adjustments are approved and conditions precedent are satisfied. No other deal terms (price per share, premium, expected close) are disclosed. Investors should watch for regulatory clearance updates and the resumption timeline in Brazil.

EQNR.brief: Equinor ASA filed a Form 6-K reporting the completion of a share capital reduction. The annual general meeting on 12 May 2026 resolved to cancel and redeem 166,058,472 shares, reducing share capital by NOK 415,146,180 from NOK 6,392,018,780 to NOK 5,976,872,600. The creditor notice period expired, and the reduction was registered as effective on 2 July 2026. Post-reduction, share capital is NOK 5,976,872,600 divided into 2,390,749,040 shares at NOK 2.50 each. This is a capital return event to shareholders. What to watch: no additional risk-arb angle as it is a completed reduction.

FRFHF.brief: Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of the take-private acquisition of Kennedy-Wilson Holdings, Inc. by a consortium led by CEO William McMorrow, other senior executives, and Fairfax affiliates. The deal was for US$10.90 per share in cash, fully closed as of June 16, 2026. The KW Management Group retains operational control, while Fairfax holds a majority economic interest. A consortium affiliate entered a three-year US$1.3 billion term loan facility, guaranteed by Fairfax. No regulatory clock remains; the transaction is complete. Investors should monitor post-close debt servicing and Fairfax's economic exposure.

FFMGF.brief: First Mining Gold Corp. filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing that Cat Lake First Nation and Lac Seul First Nation authorized the Springpole Gold Project under a Term Sheet Agreement with 35 negotiated terms covering environmental water protections, cultural safeguards, economic participation, and community healing. No financial terms are disclosed; the authorization is conditional on finalizing a binding agreement. This is a project milestone / permitting update, not a standard special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or capital restructuring.

GIGM.brief: GigaMedia filed a 6-K reporting its subscription for 719.09 million Aeolus Robotics Series C preferred shares via conversion and settlement of convertible promissory notes originally purchased from September 2023 to February 2026, with total principal of US$12.37 million at an average price of ~US$0.0176 per share. Post-transaction, GigaMedia holds 719.83 million preferred shares representing approximately 33.35% voting rights, shifting accounting from available-for-sale to equity method. The transaction is a strategic investment to support Aeolus's AI-enabled service robot development. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for additional securities transactions and Aeolus's commercialization milestones.

HCHL.brief: Happy City Holdings filed a Form 6-K reporting a temporary trading suspension imposed by the SEC from June 12 to June 26, 2026, due to potential market manipulation via social media recommendations. The company also received an information request from Nasdaq. No specific deal terms, prices, or premiums are involved. The filing details a regulatory event rather than a merger, acquisition, or other special situation. The company denies involvement and is cooperating with authorities, while its business operations remain normal. Watch for further regulatory updates and the resumption of trading.

LKFT.brief: Lakefront Biotherapeutics NV filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release disclosing share repurchases under a program announced June 9, 2026. Between June 22-26, 2026, it repurchased 83,530 shares on Euronext Amsterdam at an average price of €25.24, for total consideration of €2,108,045.52. Prices ranged from €24.38 to €25.82. Post-repurchase, Lakefront holds 199,734 treasury shares. This is an issuer buyback returning capital to shareholders. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for filing of program completion and potential impact on share count.

NBP.brief: NovaBridge Biosciences filed Form 6-K to report FDA Fast Track Designation for givastomig in first-line HER2-negative metastatic gastric cancer. This regulatory milestone accelerates development but does not constitute a special situation such as M&A, restructuring, or capital return. The filing is a routine current report of a corporate development (product pipeline update). No deal terms are present. Category "Other" fits because the filing is not a standard special situation but is a material event outside routine operations.

PBR-A.brief: Petrobras filed a Form 6-K announcing the monetary adjustment and second installment payment of shareholder remuneration for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment is made as interest on capital, with the gross value per share adjusted by the Selic rate from December 31, 2025, to June 22, 2026. The record date is April 22, 2026, and the payment date is June 22, 2026 for Brazilian shareholders, and June 29, 2026 for ADR holders. The company also provides details on tax implications and credit instructions. This is a routine capital return event, not a special situation.

STM.brief: STMicroelectronics N.V. filed a Form 6-K disclosing weekly share repurchase transactions under a buyback program approved by shareholders (May 22, 2024) and the supervisory board. For the period June 29–July 3, 2026, the company bought 145,390 shares (0.02% of issued capital) at a weighted average price of €63.5445 per share, total €9.24M. The repurchases are made by a broker on Euronext Paris to meet obligations under share-based employee compensation plans. After these transactions, treasury shares total 18.88M, representing 2.1% of issued capital. This is a routine periodic disclosure of ongoing capital return activity.

KAZR.brief: Skyline Builders Group Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing a Nasdaq ticker symbol change from SKBL to KAZR effective June 17, 2026, ahead of its pending business combination with Cove Kaz Capital Group LLC, a critical minerals development company. The transaction was signed on April 30, 2026, and is expected to close before year-end, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. No financial terms, premium, or break fee were disclosed. Upon closing, the combined company will be named Kaz Resources Inc. and continue trading under KAZR.
