This is a de facto SPAC-like reverse merger where Skyline is the listed shell. What to watch: regulatory clearance and Form S-4 effectiveness timelines.

UMC.brief: United Microelectronics Corp (UMC) filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of its 22nd share buy-back plan. The repurchase period was April 30 to June 29, 2026, with a maximum of 50 million shares and a price range of NTD 52.50 to 109.50 per share. Actual repurchase occurred May 5–20, 2026, acquiring 30,551,000 shares (0.24% of outstanding) for NTD 3,095,665,789, averaging NTD 101.33 per share. The program was not fully executed due to market conditions and shareholder interest. No advisors named. This is a routine buyback involving issuer repurchasing own shares; watch for further buyback plan announcements or share cancellation.

WRN.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by Western Copper & Gold Corporation, a Canadian foreign private issuer, reporting a material change dated June 15, 2026. The company announced a further strengthening of its strategic partnership with Mitsubishi Materials Corporation by entering into an amended and restated investor rights agreement, extending rights until November 30, 2028, contingent on Mitsubishi Materials acquiring 1.2 million common shares through open market purchases, bringing its ownership back to ~5%. No new shares are issued, so no dilution. This is a routine strategic alliance update, not a special situation requiring classification as an acquisition or other event.

YPF.brief: YPF filed a Form 6-K reporting the completion of an open-market share repurchase program. Between 8 and 12 June 2026, the company acquired 461,311 Class D ordinary shares on the ByMA exchange at an average price of Ps. 83,321.2504 per share, for a total of Ps. 38,437,009,350. The purchases complied with a daily limit of 25% of average daily trading volume over the prior 90 business days. The board-approved buyback has now been fully executed. This is an issuer tender in the U.S. sense of an issuer purchasing its own shares. No financial advisor or specific premium was cited. Watch for future share cancellation and the impact on EPS.

YYGH.brief: YY Group Holding Limited filed a Form 6-K reporting completion of its at-the-market (ATM) equity offering program, under which it sold 93,880,252 Class A ordinary shares (adjusted for a 1-for-50 reverse stock split on March 23, 2026) for gross proceeds of $20 million. Net proceeds after a 3.75% sales agent commission and expenses were approximately $19.1 million. The ATM program, originally disclosed on February 27, 2026, was paused and relaunched, then concluded as of June 16, 2026. Net proceeds will be used to pay cash portions for 2025 acquisitions and for working capital and overseas expansion. The press release attached provides details.

AIRTP.brief: Air T, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that on June 10, 2026, through its subsidiaries, it completed a reorganization of its aviation asset management platform and the acquisition of Arena Aviation Partners B.V. As part of the transaction, Air T and a management-affiliated entity acquired the remaining 10% common interest in Crestone Asset Management from MRC Parties for aggregate cash consideration of $6.2 million ($3.1 million each). Immediately after, Air T and the affiliate redeemed ~99% of their CAM common. The acquisition merges Arena into the Crestone Air Partners platform. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing does not specify closing timelines or an expected close date. Watch for integration updates and any post-closing adjustments.

ACGLO.brief: Arch Capital Group Ltd. filed an 8-K disclosing early results and pricing of cash tender offers by its subsidiaries for up to $417,851,000 aggregate principal of two series of senior notes (5.144% Senior Notes due 2043 and 5.031% Senior Notes due 2046). The increased maximum amount targets debt reduction. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or specific price per share is stated. The mechanics involve issuer debt repurchase, reducing outstanding liabilities. What to watch: the final acceptance amount and any effect on credit profile; the risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a straightforward debt tender.

AZO.brief: AutoZone filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.5 billion in share repurchases under its ongoing buyback program, bringing total authorizations to $42.2 billion since 1998. No price per share or specific premium is given, as this is an open-market authorization. The program is discretionary and will be funded from free cash flow while maintaining credit ratings. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory clock applies. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on EPS, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is not a tender offer.

ACRG.brief: American Clean Resources Group filed an 8-K disclosing a Joint Exploration and Development Agreement with TRG Holdings, LLC for an integrated energy, critical minerals processing, and data center campus on its Millers Hub property in Nevada. The agreement, effective June 9, 2026, has an 18-month initial term and covers geothermal resource assessment, Solar Energy Zone pursuit, and federal land-use authorizations. It includes mutual exclusivity and cost-sharing provisions but does not transfer property interests or establish a definitive joint venture or operating partnership. The agreement is non-binding for commercial terms, with ACE expected to participate in future definitive agreements for energy offtake and data center integration. Watch for further definitive agreements and regulatory approvals from the Bureau of Land Management.

BMTM.brief: Bright Mountain Media, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the sale of its domain name www.mom.com and related social media handles to Static Media, Inc. for $1.1 million in cash via its subsidiary CL Media Holdings LLC. Proceeds were used to prepay approximately $613,000 of First Out Loans under the Credit Agreement, fully satisfying the June 2026 amortization payment; the remaining ~$1.0 million in Second Out amortization was paid-in-kind. The deal required and obtained consent from Centre Lane Partners and lenders. This is an asset sale, not a strategic transaction, and does not fall under standard special-situations categories.

CDTTW.brief: CDT Equity Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Loan Agreement and issuance of a senior secured convertible promissory note to J.J. Astor Co. for a principal amount of $1,971,000, with net proceeds of $1,460,000 funded in two tranches. The note is payable over 24 weekly installments of $82,125 starting June 18, 2026, with conversion rights commencing December 11, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. A first priority lien on collateral was granted. This is a financing arrangement, not a transformative event, so it does not fit any special situations category.

CCNEP.brief: CNB Financial Corporation filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026 announcing the completion of a partial redemption of $50 million of its 3.25% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2031. The redemption occurred on June 15, 2026 at par plus accrued interest, leaving $35 million outstanding. This is a capital structure action reducing debt and future interest expense, with no premium or accretion. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory timeline is mentioned. Watch for potential further redemptions or balance sheet repositioning; the risk-arb angle is negligible as this is a unilateral issuer action.

CNTN.brief: Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a share repurchase program approved by its board on June 11, 2026, authorizing up to $50 million of common stock repurchases. Repurchases may occur via open market or privately-negotiated transactions under Rule 10b-18. The company entered into a non-exclusive repurchase agreement with Virtu Americas LLC on June 12, 2026, paying $0.02/share commission. The program’s timing and amount depend on capital resources, market conditions, and securities law limits. Watch for execution pace and impact on share price.

FGN.brief: F&G Annuities & Life, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026, announcing CEO Chris Blunt will retire from his CEO role effective June 30, 2026, to focus on his roles as a Director and CEO of subsidiary Peak Altitude Equity, LLC. President and CFO Conor Murphy will become CEO and President, with Michael Bailey appointed as CFO effective August 3, 2026, and Mark Wiltse as Interim CFO. The Board has a process to explore strategic alternatives for Peak Altitude. No deal terms or shareholder vote triggered; a routine succession albeit with a strategic review of a subsidiary.

HLLK.brief: Hallmark Venture Group filed an 8-K reporting a change of control via a private agreement: Selkirk Global Holdings sold its 100% of Series A Preferred Stock (voting control) and Hallmark issued 50M common shares (~75.55% of common) to Equorix LLC. No consideration price was disclosed for the stock. Simultaneously, Hallmark acquired drone IP from Cho Sun Sik and Sundori Korea. Board changed with three new directors. As a private share issuance and asset acquisition, this is not a standard special situation. Watch for shareholder litigation or SEC scrutiny on valuation.

MXCT.brief: MaxCyte, Inc. reported in an 8-K filed June 16, 2026, that it received notice from Nasdaq on June 10, 2026, confirming the company regained compliance with the minimum bid price rule (Listing Rule 5450(a)(1)). The closing bid price remained at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days from May 27 to June 9, 2026. The delisting matter is now closed. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal terms were disclosed. No activist or new campaign is involved. Investors should monitor stock price maintenance above $1.00 to avoid future non-compliance.

NN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist warrants of NextNav Inc. (CIK 0001865631) under 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(1). The delisting is effective June 26, 2026, removing the warrants from Nasdaq listing. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or transaction structure was disclosed. The filing is a standard administrative action for security removal. What to watch: whether the warrants will trade over-the-counter or if a separate corporate event (e.g., merger) triggered the delisting; risk-arb angle is minimal as no tender or exchange offer is involved.

NHPBP.brief: National Healthcare Properties, Inc. (NHP) announced final results of its self-tender offers for up to $100M aggregate of Series A (7.375%) and Series B (7.125%) perpetual preferred stock at $22.50/share cash. The offers expired on June 19, 2026. The company accepted shares on a pro-rata basis, funded from cash on hand. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Mechanics: the issuer tender offer was conducted under Rule 13e-4; shares tendered were subject to proration if oversubscribed. The final acceptance and payment occurs promptly after the press release dated June 22, 2026. What to watch: any subsequent redemption or exchange of remaining preferred stock; risk-arb spread is minimal given a fixed cash price.

NCPLW.brief: Netcapital Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Securities Purchase Agreement with Dune Equity Holdings LLC, closing on July 2, 2026. The company issued a $290,000 promissory note and a warrant for 250,000 shares at $0.50/share, for a purchase price of $250,000 (reflecting $40,000 OID). Net proceeds were $224,500 after legal fees and placement agent costs. The note matures July 1, 2027, with amortization starting January 2, 2027. This is a structured financing with equity-linked features, not a transformative special situation. Watch for dilution from warrant exercise and note conversion.

PTCT.brief: PTC Therapeutics filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of a $500M 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 offering, with an underwriter option for an additional $50M. Concurrently, PTC will use ~$328.8M of net proceeds to repurchase $222M of its outstanding 1.5% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026 in privately negotiated transactions. Remaining proceeds go to general corporate purposes and potential additional repurchases. The notes are unregistered and convertible. The offering is not contingent on the repurchases. Watch for execution of the concurrent note repurchases and any follow-on actions to manage maturities.

RXT.brief: Rackspace Technology filed an 8-K disclosing a workforce realignment plan approved by its Executive Committee on June 10, 2026. The plan eliminates approximately 15% of the global workforce, targeting legacy Public Cloud delivery functions to redeploy resources toward enterprise AI. One-time charges of $14-$19 million are expected in 2026, with annualized run-rate savings of $75-$85 million. Notice was given on or about June 10; additional exits occur over six months. The company may implement further operational optimization measures. Watch actual savings relative to estimates, reinvestment pace into AI, and any future restructuring announcements.

SPCX.brief: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX) filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of a multi-tranche senior unsecured notes offering totaling $25.0 billion, with tranches ranging from 5.350% senior notes due 2031 to 6.650% senior notes due 2056. The offering is expected to settle on June 26, 2026. Proceeds will be used to repay the company's bridge loan facility in full, pay related fees and expenses, and for general corporate purposes. The offering was not registered under the Securities Act. As a debt financing event rather than a special situation like an acquisition or restructuring, this is classified as 'Other'.

ISNRU.brief: Snow Rothschild Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO of 20,000,000 units at $10.00/unit (gross $200M), closing on June 10, 2026. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-half of one redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50/share. Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 2,250,000 private placement warrants ($1.00/warrant) for $2.25M. Net IPO proceeds plus private placement funds ($200M total) were placed in a trust account. On June 12, the underwriters partially exercised their over-allotment option, purchasing an additional 2,600,000 option units at $10.00 (extra $26M gross). This filing documents a blank-check company's initial listing and trust establishment. The SPAC will now have a limited window to identify and complete a de-SPAC business combination, with shareholder redemption rights. Watch for target announcement and proxy filing.

WBS-PG.brief: This 8-K reports OCC approval of the bank-level merger between Webster Bank and Santander Bank, a step in the larger acquisition of Webster Financial Corp by Banco Santander S.A. Terms from prior announcement include an all-cash transaction at $64.50 per share (approx. $10.3B enterprise value). Boards of both companies had unanimously approved. Regulatory approvals remain from the Federal Reserve and ECB. Risk-arb focus: timeline to closing and any remaining antitrust hurdles.

YUMC.brief: Yum China filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026, announcing a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement to acquire Willow Glade Investments from Yum! Brands for US$1.2 billion in cash. The acquired entity holds Pizza Hut intellectual property and related rights in China. Yum China will also amend its existing KFC/Taco Bell master license agreement. Consideration is fixed and will be funded by cash and debt. Closing is subject to no law or order prohibiting the transaction. The acquisition consolidates brand rights; key watch is regulatory clearance and financing details.

TOON.brief: Kartoon Studios filed an 8-K/A to correct a settlement amount in a previously disclosed litigation settlement. The company reported that on June 11, 2026, it entered into a settlement agreement receiving $50,000,000 (corrected from $5M) from a settling party in the Augenbaum v. Anson Investments Master Fund LP case. The court approved the settlement. The action continues against two remaining defendants. This is a litigation-related event, not a special situation classified category.

QSEAU.brief: Quartzsea Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K announcing the postponement of its Extraordinary General Meeting from June 18 to June 23, 2026, to seek shareholder approval for an extension of its initial business combination deadline from June 19, 2026 to October 19, 2026 via up to four monthly extensions. In connection, the redemption right deadline is extended to June 23. The monthly contribution to the trust account will be the lesser of $0.033 per public share or $175,000. This is a routine SPAC extension filing typical of blank-check companies nearing their liquidation deadline. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and potential redemptions, which could affect trust size and deal feasibility.

DKS.brief: DICK'S Sporting Goods filed an S-4/A registration statement for an exchange offer to swap up to $381,932,000 of its 4.000% Senior Notes due 2029. The company is offering to exchange any and all outstanding notes issued September 11, 2025 for registered notes with substantially identical terms. The exchange is intended to satisfy registration rights obligations. There is no board recommendation, advisor, premium, or change in economic terms. The exchange is not conditioned on a minimum tender. The deal mechanics involve a like-for-like principal exchange with no cash consideration. No regulatory clock applies beyond SEC effectiveness. What to watch: execution risk is minimal; the arbitrage angle is absent as this is a registration rights exchange with no price dislocation.

XTND.brief: Xtend AI Robotics, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 with the SEC on June 16, 2026, registering securities in connection with a proposed business combination with JFB Construction Holdings (a Nevada corporation) and Xtend Reality Expansion Ltd. (an Israeli company). No specific terms (price per share, premium, closing date, or break fee) are disclosed. JFB's board has not yet recommended the transaction; no financial advisor is named. The transaction will close upon SEC effectiveness and stockholder approval by written consent. What to watch: pricing and structure details in subsequent amendments; risk-arb spread will depend on disclosed exchange ratio and regulatory timeline.

AIFU.brief: AIFU Inc. (Nasdaq: AIFU) filed a Form 6-K on June 17, 2026, disclosing a non-binding MOU to acquire Peakleap Ventures Limited, an industrial AI company focused on solid waste recycling and resource recovery. The MOU outlines a strategic transformation from a digital finance platform to a dual-engine business ecosystem of Industrial AI + Digital Finance. Terms such as price/share, implied value, and premium are not disclosed. The acquisition is subject to due diligence, definitive agreements, and regulatory approvals. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Structure is a proposed acquisition via MOU; no certainty of consummation. Watch for definitive agreement execution and regulatory clearance.

ASND.brief: Ascendis Pharma A/S filed a Form 6-K disclosing the completion of the sale of its Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) to an undisclosed buyer for $187.5 million in cash, before transaction-related expenses. The PRV was awarded by the FDA upon approval of YUVIWEL (navepegritide) in February 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, or additional deal mechanics were named. The transaction was previously announced and has now closed. As a non-US issuer, this 6-K serves as a current report equivalent. The one-time cash inflow boosts liquidity; watch for use of proceeds toward pipeline development or debt reduction. No risk-arb angle as the sale is completed.

BGM.brief: BGM Group Ltd. filed a 6-K pertaining to an Extraordinary General Meeting of shareholders scheduled for July 9, 2026. The meeting will consider a share capital reduction and reorganization proposal, reducing par value of each issued ordinary and preferred share from $0.00833335 to $0.0001, with the credit transferred to a distributable reserve. Authorized but unissued shares will be subdivided. The EGM notice and proxy card are attached. This filing describes a proposed corporate action rather than a definitive special situation. As a non-US filing, it corresponds to a shareholder meeting proxy or 8-K Item 5.07.

CURLD.brief: Curaleaf Holdings filed a Form 6-K reporting a material change: a 3-for-1 reverse stock split of its Subordinate Voting Shares, effective June 5, 2026, approved by the board. The consolidation reduced outstanding shares from ~698.7M to ~232.9M. Concurrently, Multiple Voting Shares were consolidated at the same ratio to preserve relative rights. No fractional shares were issued; rounding rules applied. This is a capital-structure adjustment, not a special situation like an acquisition or restructuring. The filing is routine and does not trigger a risk-arb event or strategic review.

DSWL.brief: Deswell Industries Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing its unaudited financial results for H2 and FY ending March 31, 2026, and declared a second-half cash dividend of $0.10 per share plus a special cash dividend of $0.20 per share. The company reported net income of $3.1M for H2 and $10.6M for FY, with basic EPS of $0.20 and $0.67, respectively. Dividends total $0.30 per share on approximately 15.9M shares outstanding. With $23.1M cash and no debt, the payout is well-covered. The board recommended the dividends; no advisor named. Mechanics: cash distribution, no record/pay date stated. Watch for ex-dividend and payment dates; risk-arb angle minimal as this is a regular capital return.

E.brief: Eni S.p.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting weekly treasury share purchases (29 Jun–3 Jul 2026) under a buyback program approved 6 May 2026. The issuer acquired 4,897,905 shares (0.16% of capital) at a weighted average price of €20.4169/share, total consideration ~€100M. Since program start (8 May 2026), 29,691,495 shares (0.98%) repurchased for ~€660M; total holdings after these purchases equal 3.85% of share capital. The buyback is part of a second tranche aimed at providing additional shareholder remuneration beyond dividends. No advisory or board recommendation is mentioned. The mechanics are standard open-market purchases on Euronext Milan, governed by shareholder authorization. Watch for continued execution pace and potential impact on share price and EPS; risk-arb is minimal as this is an issuer buyback, not a tender offer.

GLASF.brief: Glass House Brands filed a Form 6-K (material change report) disclosing a deconsolidation transaction to separate its dual-use cannabis business from its medical cannabis business. The company transferred its former dual-use assets into Glass House Retail, LLC (GHR), receiving non-voting, non-participating units that are non-convertible until the NYSE permits cannabis listings. A third-party investor (GHR Investor) holds all voting units, limiting Glass House's control. The move supports a planned NYSE listing application. No deal terms such as price or premium are disclosed. The transaction is structured via an LLC agreement with three unit classes. Key watch item: NYSE rule change on cannabis listing and regulatory approvals for asset transfers.

GMTL.brief: Guardian Metal Resources PLC filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing its acquisition of Lincoln Estates Group LLC, including 841 acres of real property and 2,540 acre-feet of annual water rights adjacent to its Tempiute Tungsten Project in Nevada. Total purchase price is US$1.3 million in cash, payable through wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary Golden Metal Resources, LLC. The acquisition is recommended by management, with CEO Oliver Friesen noting it de-risks and accelerates project redevelopment. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium disclosed. Expected close not specified. The seller's identity is the entity being acquired. Monitor regulatory approvals and integration with Tempiute's redevelopment timeline.

LNKS.brief: Linkers Industries Ltd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Linkers Asia Pacific Limited, filed a Form 6-K disclosing entry into a Share Sale and Purchase Agreement to acquire 150,800 shares representing 29% of LPW Electronics Co., Ltd. from Chairman Mr. Man Tak Lau for ~US$2,350,000, with outstanding LPW associate debt of ~US$6,160,000 to be settled in cash at closing. The registrant currently owns 20% of LPW and will hold 49% post-closing. Closing is expected on or around June 17, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or mechanics details are provided. The consideration is cash. Watch for regulatory approval and completion of debt settlement.

BMA.brief: Macro Bank Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting a cash dividend payment. The Board approved the third of three monthly equal, non-cumulative instalments of ARS 49,033,753,984.66 total, or ARS 76.6882980676 per share (7,668.8298% of outstanding capital). The record date is July 6, 2026, payable July 7, 2026 through Caja de Valores S.A. ADR holders will receive dividends via The Bank of New York Mellon. A 7% withholding applies under Argentina's Income Tax Law. This capital return follows CNV and Central Bank authorization. To watch: currency stability and ADR conversion mechanics.

NVNXF.brief: NOVONIX Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing ASX waivers for its Share Purchase Plan (SPP), part of a capital raising disclosed on 17 June 2026. The SPP offers shares at A$0.16, a ~31.2% discount to the 5-day VWAP, exceeding the standard 20% limit. The ASX waivers permit issuance without shareholder approval and allow director participation, with the number of SPP shares capped at 30% of existing shares. This is a non-US filing; the 6-K serves as the SEC-equivalent disclosure. Watch for investor participation uptake and potential dilution to existing holders.

POM.brief: POMDOCTOR Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing a strategic upgrade to become a predictive healthcare data and services infrastructure provider, moving from an online healthcare platform to an AI-enabled ecosystem. No financial terms, stake, price, or premium were disclosed. The filing describes three trends—chronic disease burden, technological shift, and payment transformation—but does not trigger a defined special situation. This is a forward-looking business strategy press release; the upgrade does not constitute a standard special-situation event such as an acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring. No recommended action.

PRZO.brief: This Form 6-K filed by ParaZero Technologies Ltd., a foreign private issuer, reports receipt of an additional order for its DefendAir Net Pod system from a second business unit of a Tier-1 Israeli-based global defense company. The order includes net pods and engineering integration support for autonomous ground Counter-UAS platforms. No financial terms (value, price per share, premium) are disclosed. The press release highlights the growing demand for kinetic interception capabilities in defense systems. This is a routine business development announcement, not a special situation transaction such as an acquisition, divestiture, or going-private. The filing updates the market on operational progress in ParaZero's defense product line.

VIV.brief: Telefônica Brasil S.A. filed a 6-K reporting a board resolution to merge its wholly-owned fiber subsidiary, Fibrasil Infraestrutura e Fibra Ótica S.A., into itself. The merger is based on an appraisal report prepared by PriceWaterhouseCoopers valuing Fibrasil's equity at R$ 812.6 million (book value as of Dec 31, 2025). The board recommends the merger, aiming to simplify structure, speed decisions, optimize operations, and reduce costs. Fibrasil is wholly owned, so no third-party consideration or premium applies; shares will be canceled. An EGM will be called to approve. Watch for shareholder vote and regulatory clearance under Brazilian law.

AVAT.brief: Avalanche Treasury Corp (Pubco) filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its business combination with Mountain Lake Acquisition Corp (MLAC) and related entities. On June 11, 2026, MLAC domesticated to a Delaware corporation and merged with Pubco's subsidiaries, with Pubco surviving. The transaction was governed by a Business Combination Agreement dated October 1, 2025, and amended in January and March 2026. No specific price per share, premium, or implied value was disclosed. The board recommended the transaction in the proxy statement/prospectus filed May 14, 2026. Registrant became the successor public company. Watch for post-combination trading dynamics and potential redemption impacts.

BBBY-WT.brief: Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc. filed an 8-K on July 9, 2026 to report the completion of its acquisition of The Container Store Holdings, LLC. The merger closed on July 8, 2026, with Merger Sub merging into TCS, leaving TCS as a wholly owned subsidiary. Consideration details (price per share, total value) are not disclosed in the excerpt. The board recommended the transaction. A Registration Rights and Lock-Up Agreement provides holders with shelf registration, demand (minimum $25M), and piggyback rights. The filing also notes convertible notes and a letter agreement. Monitor integration progress and any post-merger stock movements for risk-arb implications.

BTGO.brief: On June 17, 2026, BitGo Holdings, Inc., through a Form 8-K and press release, announced a share repurchase program authorized by its board for up to $50M of its outstanding Class A common stock (NYSE: BTGO). Repurchases may occur in open market (subject to Rule 10b-18 volume and pricing conditions), private negotiations, or through Rule 10b5-1 plans. Timing and amount are discretionary, dependent on market conditions. Funding will come from cash and operations. The program can be modified, suspended, or terminated at any time. No fixed expiration, per-share price, or tender offer structure is specified. Watch for execution pace and compliance with 10b-18 safe harbor; this program is a pure open-market repurchase, not a tender, thus no immediate risk-arb spread.

EAT.brief: Brinker International, Inc. filed an 8-K with Item 8.01 Other Events to announce the redemption of all its outstanding 8.250% Senior Notes due July 15, 2030. The redemption is set for July 15, 2026, at a price equal to 104.125% of principal plus accrued interest. No tender offer or exchange is involved; the company is exercising its call option. The notice of redemption was issued on June 16, 2026, and the form 8-K explicitly states it does not constitute a notice of redemption. This is a straightforward debt retirement, not a special situation, but it fits the issuer tender/redemption category. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory timeline beyond the redemption date is provided. The event removes the note overhang and reduces future interest expense; investors should monitor the redemption settlement and any subsequent refinancing plans.

ELTX.brief: Elicio Therapeutics filed an 8-K (Item 8.01, Other Events) on June 17, 2026, attaching a press release that reports preliminary clinical observations from its Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P study. The release highlights three metastatic pancreatic cancer patients who achieved complete radiographic and metabolic responses after receiving ELI-002 7P followed by nivolumab-based therapy. This is a clinical development update with no deal terms, transaction, or special-situation corporate event. The filing discloses no financial terms, board recommendation, or imminent structural change. The company plans a Phase 1 study in first-line metastatic KRAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, subject to funding. The press release serves as the sole exhibit. No special-situation categorization applies; the filing is a routine clinical update.

GENC.brief: Gencor Industries filed an 8-K (Item 3.01) disclosing it received a NYSE American notice on May 19, 2026, for failing to timely file its Q1 2026 10-Q by the May 18, 2026 extension deadline, triggering a six-month cure period. On June 12, 2026, the company filed the delinquent 10-Q within that period. On June 15, 2026, NYSE confirmed compliance was regained and removed the company from its late filers list. No board action, advisor, or premium was involved. Risk-arb watch: this delisting risk is now resolved, removing a potential overhang on the stock.

GCGRW.company: General Catalyst Global Resilience Merger Corp.
GCGRW.brief: General Catalyst Global Resilience Merger Corp., a blank-check company, filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026, announcing that holders of its GRAIL securities may elect to separately trade the underlying Class A ordinary shares and warrants starting June 22, 2026. Each GRAIL security consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-fourth of one redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50. The securities are listed on Nasdaq: GRAIL units (GCGRU), shares (GCGR), and warrants (GCGRW). No fractional warrants will be issued. Holders must contact Continental Stock Transfer to separate. This optional separation is a standard post-IPO milestone for SPAC units. No premium, price, or board recommendation is stated. What to watch: trading volumes upon separation and any subsequent business combination announcement.

HLIT.brief: Harmonic Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of the sale of its Video Business to Leone Media Inc. (d/b/a MediaKind) for $145 million in cash. The purchase price is subject to customary working capital, cash, indebtedness, and selling expense adjustments. The Asset Purchase Agreement, dated March 20, 2026, includes a three-year non-compete and reciprocal indemnification. Neven Haltmayer, SVP and GM of the Video Business, resigned upon closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Pro forma financials were omitted as the business was previously reported as discontinued operations. What to watch: integration execution by MediaKind and Harmonic's post-divestiture strategy; risk-arb is limited as the deal is closed.

ISRLF.brief: Israel Acquisitions Corp (IAC), a blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its business combination agreement with Gadfin Ltd., an Israeli drone logistics company, originally entered January 26, 2025 and amended multiple times. No deal terms are disclosed—no price, premium, or fees. The transaction structure involved IAC and Gadfin becoming subsidiaries of a new Israeli holding company, Gadfin Regev Holdings Ltd., via two mergers. Termination occurred June 22, 2026 by mutual agreement or per contractual termination rights. As a SPAC that failed to consummate a de-SPAC, IAC now faces liquidation or a new search; the OTC-listed units, shares, and warrants will likely trade on dissolution value.

JABRU.brief: This Form 8-K reports JAB Acquisition Corp I’s closing of its initial public offering (IPO) of 17,250,000 units at $10.00/unit, including the full over-allotment, generating $172.5 million in gross proceeds. Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 260,000 private units at $10.00/unit for $2.6 million. Each unit comprises one Class A ordinary share, one redeemable warrant (exercisable at $11.50/share), and one right to receive one-fourth of a Class A share upon a business combination. No additional sponsor units were sold on over-allotment exercise. The filing includes audited balance sheet reflecting the proceeds. As a blank-check SPAC, the company now has two years to complete an initial business combination or liquidate the trust, with the sponsor’s units providing downside protection. Watch for target announcement and shareholder vote dynamics.

KFRC.brief: Kforce Inc. filed an 8-K announcing adoption of a Rule 10b5-1 stock trading plan to repurchase its common stock under an existing board-authorized share repurchase program. No specific share number, price, or dollar amount was disclosed. Repurchases may begin June 16, 2026, through July 29, 2026, administered by an independent broker subject to price, volume, and timing constraints. The plan signals a commitment to return capital to shareholders via open-market buybacks, providing a floor for the stock without committing to a fixed amount. Watch for quarterly buyback volumes and potential program expansions.

MAC.brief: Macerich filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026, announcing the full exercise of the underwriters' 30-day option to purchase an additional 2,100,000 shares of common stock at $23.12325 per share, under an underwriting agreement dated June 15, 2026. The company entered into additional forward sale agreements with forward purchasers to borrow and sell the option shares. Closing occurred June 26, 2026. Proceeds depend on future physical settlement of the forward agreements, expected by June 16, 2027. The company may elect cash or net share settlement. This is a capital-raising equity forward transaction, not a special situation.

NEO.brief: NeoGenomics filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a $316.25M offering of 0.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032. The notes were priced at a 35% conversion premium over the $10.49 reference stock price ($14.16 conversion price). The notes are senior unsecured obligations, maturing July 1, 2032, with semiannual interest and customary covenants. Holders may convert before April 1, 2032 under specified circumstances; settlement may be in cash, stock, or a combination. The offering was upsized from $275M initial to $316.25M via greenshoe. Watch for dilution risk at conversion or any early repurchase provisions.

PLAG.brief: Planet Green Holdings Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the disposition of its 100% equity interest in Bless Chemical Co., Ltd. (HK) to Hongzhang Liang for nominal consideration. Bless HK indirectly owned Jingshan Sanhe Luckysky New Energy Technologies Co., Ltd., which had ceased operations. The Board approved the deal to streamline operations and focus on core businesses; no advisor or financial terms beyond nominal consideration were disclosed. The transaction closed on June 15, 2026, and the entities will be deconsolidated. Watch for any subsequent liabilities or write-offs arising from the discontinued operations.

RIGL.brief: Rigel Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K to report completion of an exclusive license agreement with Arvinas, Inc., Arvinas Operations, Inc., Arvinas Estrogen Receptor, Inc. and Pfizer Inc. as licensors. Under the deal, Rigel obtained exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize VEPPANU (vepdegestrant) and related products. Rigel paid a one-time upfront payment of $70.0 million. The closing followed early termination of the HSR waiting period and satisfaction of other conditions. This is an asset acquisition via exclusive license. Watch for milestone or royalty terms, regulatory progress, and potential competitive dynamics in the targeted therapeutic area.

RUMBW.brief: Rumble Inc. (now RUM Group Inc.) filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its business combination with Northern Data AG, a German stock corporation, on June 17, 2026. Concurrently, Rumble entered into a secured Credit Agreement with Tether Investments, involving a pre-funded warrant for 50% of Tether's receivable under an existing floating rate loan to Northern Data, and converting the remaining 50% into a credit agreement with a newly formed Irish subsidiary. The deal implies Rumble's acquisition of Northern Data, with Tether as a key counterparty. Terms include a secured credit facility; no price per share, premium, or advisor named. Watch integration and regulatory approvals.

SPFI.brief: South Plains Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Board Representation Agreement with shareholder Henry TAW LP, effective June 17, 2026. The agreement had granted the shareholder the right to designate one board nominee. At origination in 2019, the shareholder held about 16% of outstanding shares; its stake has since fallen below 10%. The board believes termination aligns with the company's maturation as a widely-held public entity. Richard D. Campbell, the designated representative, will remain on the board through his current term and is expected to be renominated. This is a governance change, not a special situation event.

SCCO.brief: Southern Copper Corporation filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of $1.25 billion 5.350% senior unsecured notes due 2036 in an underwritten registered public offering. The offering is expected to close on June 24, 2026. Proceeds will fund the Tia Maria project, capital expenditures, and general corporate purposes through its Peruvian branch. BofA Securities and Morgan Stanley acted as global coordinators and joint bookrunners. This is a straight debt issuance, not a special situation; watch for use-of-proceeds execution risk and copper price sensitivity.

SVIX.brief: VS Trust, via its sponsor Volatility Shares LLC, filed an 8-K announcing a 1-for-20 reverse share split for its 2x Long VIX Futures ETF (UVIX), effective July 1, 2026. The split increases net asset value per share proportionally while reducing shares outstanding, with fractional shares redeemed for cash. No consideration, premium, or deal structure is involved; it is a mechanical capital adjustment, not a special situation. The ticker remains unchanged, a new CUSIP is assigned, and taxable consequences may arise for holders of fractional shares. There is no event to monitor beyond standard post-split trading.

GNL-PD.brief: Global Net Lease, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement on June 17, 2026, in connection with its proposed merger with Modiv Industrial, Inc. Under the terms disclosed, GNL will acquire Modiv in an all-stock transaction. Modiv stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of GNL common shares per Modiv share, though specific ratios and implied values are not detailed in this filing. The boards of both companies have approved the transaction. GNL is using its S-4 to register the shares to be issued. The transaction requires Modiv stockholder approval and regulatory clearance; a special meeting is to be called. Risk-arb watchers should focus on stockholder sentiment and closing conditions.

SEQC.brief: SeeQC, Inc. filed an S-4/A registration statement for its merger with Allegro Merger Corp. Under the merger agreement dated January 16, 2026, Allegro will merge into a SeeQC subsidiary, with Allegro surviving as a wholly-owned SeeQC unit. Allegro security holders will receive up to 6,434,293 shares of SeeQC common stock. The filing does not disclose exact terms or pricing. The board recommendation or advisors are not named in this excerpt. Mechanics: standard reverse-merger structure; regulatory clock tied to SEC effectiveness. Watch for final exchange ratio, stock price volatility, and shareholder vote.

LC.brief: LendingClub Corp voluntarily delisted its common stock from the NYSE, filing Form 25 on June 18, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(c). No tender offer or acquisition; the issuer itself initiated removal. No price, premium, or consideration terms given. The board did not name an advisor; the filing cites compliance with exchange rules. The delisting became effective upon filing. With no overhang or ownership changes, this is a purely administrative event. Watch for any subsequent SEC deregistration under Rule 12g-4 or potential going-private transaction; risk-arb is inapplicable.

HKD.brief: AMTD Digital Inc. filed a Form 6-K attaching an announcement by its subsidiary, The Generation Essentials Group (TGE), of a share repurchase program. TGE's board approved up to $10 million in open-market or negotiated repurchases, funded from existing cash, under Rule 10b-18/10b5-1. Concurrently, controlling shareholder AMTD Digital, directors and management voluntarily locked up their shares for two years. No premium or per-share price stated. The filing highlights TGE's belief its shares trade at a deep discount to net asset value (~$971M). What to watch: pace of buybacks and potential NAV convergence.

AMTD.brief: AMTD IDEA Group filed a Form 6-K attaching an announcement by its subsidiary, The Generation Essentials Group (TGE). TGE's board approved a $10 million share repurchase program, funded from existing cash, allowing open-market, privately negotiated, or block-trade purchases subject to Rule 10b-18/10b5-1 requirements. Concurrently, controlling shareholder AMTD Digital Inc., directors, and management voluntarily agreed to a two-year lock-up on their TGE shares. The board believes TGE shares trade at a significant discount to asset values (total assets ~$1.7B post-acquisitions, net assets ~$971M). This capital-return move signals confidence and aims to enhance shareholder value. Watch for periodic board reviews of program size and price; no premium or fixed price per share specified.

BTQ.brief: BTQ Technologies Corp. filed a Form 6-K announcing final French FDI approval for its full acquisition of QPerfect SAS. Total consideration is up to €24,264,923.55, composed of €18,592,242.83 at closing (€2,024,000.13 cash + 2,195,929 common shares at ~€7.54/share) plus an earnout of up to €5,672,680.72 (€440,604.07 cash + 693,450 shares). QPerfect's CEO received 198,808 RSUs. French authorities imposed conditions including maintaining QPerfect's French registration, R&D continuity, IP protection. The acquisition adds quantum emulation and digital twin capabilities to BTQ's tech stack. Watch for milestone achievement triggering earnout and post-close integration risk.

BCDRF.brief: This is a Form 6-K filing by Banco Santander reporting weekly buyback transactions under a previously announced share repurchase programme. Between June 25 and July 1, 2026, the bank repurchased 8,399,608 ordinary shares on the XMAD exchange at a weighted average price ranging from approximately €11.81 to €12.03 per share. The total cash outlay since inception is €3.63 billion, reaching about 72.2% of the maximum investment amount, and has retired roughly 17.3% of shares outstanding as of 2021. The buyback is an open-market execution with no fixed price. Watch for pace of remaining purchases and capital return policy updates.

CMND.brief: Clearmind Medicine Inc. filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, attaching a press release announcing the grant of U.S. Patent No. 12,350,242 for its molecule MEAI, covering compositions and methods to regulate binge behaviors. This is a routine intellectual property milestone disclosure by a clinical-stage biotech company. No financial terms, transactions, or corporate actions are involved. The filing is a foreign private issuer report under Rule 13a-16, incorporated into existing registration statements. As a non-US filer, the Form 6-K serves as a current report equivalent. There are no deal terms, as this is not a special situation.

EMBJ.brief: Embraer S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing that its Board of Directors declared Interest on Equity (IoE) for Q2 2026 totaling R$ 200,000,000 (approx. R$ 0.28096472120 per share). The record date for B3 shareholders is June 23, 2026, with ex-IoE dates of June 24, 2026 (B3) and July 2, 2026 (NYSE). Payment is scheduled for May 24, 2027, with no adjustment or additional remuneration. The IoE will be imputed to mandatory dividends for the fiscal year. This is a routine capital return to shareholders, not a special situation involving structural corporate change. No premium, advisor, or strategic review is involved.

TGE-WT.brief: Generation Essentials Group filed a Form 6-K announcing a board-approved share repurchase program of up to US$10 million in open-market, privately negotiated, or block-trade transactions, funded from existing cash. Concurrently, controlling shareholder AMTD Digital Inc., directors, and management voluntarily agreed to a two-year lock-up on their TGE shares. The board believes shares trade at a significant discount to net asset value (approximately US$971 million, a 15.8% increase) and total asset value (~US$1.7 billion, up 17.7% after recent hotel acquisitions). Repurchases will comply with Rule 10b-18/10b5-1. The program enhances shareholder value; what to watch is execution pace and whether discount to NAV narrows.

ICCM.brief: IceCure Medical Ltd. filed a Form 6-K disclosing a private placement via a Securities Purchase Agreement with an institutional investor. The company will issue pre-funded warrants to purchase 1,833,334 ordinary shares at $0.0001 per share, along with Series D warrants (five-year term) and Series E warrants (one-year term) each exercisable at $3.00 per share, for a combined purchase price of $2.9999 per unit. Gross proceeds are approximately $5.5 million, with closing expected on or about June 18, 2026. Existing Series B and C warrants were amended to reduce exercise price to $3.00 and extend terms, subject to shareholder approval. A.G.P./Alliance Global Partners served as placement agent.

KB.brief: KB Financial Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Kookmin Bank, declared an interim cash dividend of KRW 3,460 per common share, totaling KRW 1,399,151,741,360. The record date is July 2, 2026, with payment expected on July 22, 2026, subject to change. The entire dividend will be paid to KB Financial Group Inc., as the sole shareholder of Kookmin Bank. The dividend is authorized under Article 53 of Kookmin Bank's Articles of Incorporation and Korean commercial law. This capital return to the parent company may precede a distribution to KB Financial Group's own shareholders or be used for corporate purposes. No premium or strategic change is involved; the filing is a routine dividend declaration, but it constitutes a capital return event at the subsidiary level. What to watch: the potential for further upstreaming of dividends to KB Financial Group's public shareholders and any impact on the group's capital ratios.

LGHL.brief: Lion Group Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 22, 2026, disclosing entry into an Investment Participation Agreement with Meili Capital Management Limited. Under the terms, Lion will participate in Meili's acquisition of a 10% equity interest in PT NUSANTARA BUMI SANGKARA for a total consideration of US$12 million, implying a post-money valuation of US$120 million. Consideration may be in cash, shares, or other forms per separate agreement. The deal is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals and due diligence. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for definitive documentation and completion timing.

LUD.brief: Luda Technology Group Ltd (NYSE: LUD) filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, announcing a signed MOU to acquire a 55% stake in Asia AI Data Centre Quantum Technology Company Ltd. The consideration is cash of USD 400,000 plus the issuance of ordinary shares valued at USD 535,000, totaling USD 935,000. The seller, Ms. Liu Liangping, is the target's CEO and Luda's COO, and she is married to Luda's CEO, Mr. Ma Biu. The board supports the strategic entry into data centre and AI computing infrastructure. The transaction is structured as a majority share acquisition, subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals. The MOU includes related-party considerations, as Ms. Liu is an insider. Watch for completion of due diligence and final terms; the small size and insider nature suggest low deal risk.

MTEN.brief: This Form 6-K reports that Mingteng International Corp Inc. entered into a Waiver Agreement and a Registration Rights Agreement with purchasers of Class A ordinary shares from a prior Securities Purchase Agreement. The Waiver lifts a 180-day lock-up restriction on shares held by those purchasers. The Registration Rights Agreement commits the company to file a resale registration statement (Form F-1 or F-3) within 180 days and keep it effective until all covered shares can be freely sold. This is a routine follow-up to a prior PIPE financing, not a standalone special situation.

NIVFW.brief: NewGenIvf Group Ltd issued 3,666,667 new shares and made a US$10 million investment to acquire a 10% equity interest in K25.ai, an AI-powered live-streaming prediction market platform, via strategic share purchase agreements. The filing is a Form 6-K with a press release attached, disclosing the transaction and reporting a market capitalization of ~US$7.6 million (as of June 18, 2026). No board recommendation or advisors are named. The deal increases outstanding shares to 10,073,535 and strengthens the balance sheet. Management views the market cap as a discount to NAV of ~US$25.98 million. Watch for regulatory compliance with Nasdaq's proposed $5 million MVLS threshold; risk-arb focus on integration and shareholder dilution.

OMH.brief: Ohmyhome Ltd filed unaudited pro forma financial statements to reflect its June 17, 2026 sale of wholly-owned subsidiary Ohmyhome (BVI) Limited to Sterling Oat Ltd. for cash consideration of $1. The divested entity comprises the company's former property-related business, representing a strategic shift to digital marketing services. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The disposal qualifies as discontinued operations for reporting purposes, and the pro forma statements assume the transaction occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented. The low purchase price suggests a de facto exit rather than a value-maximizing sale. Watch for operational performance under new digital marketing focus and potential wind-down costs.

PRFX.brief: PRF Technologies Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting a Standby Equity Purchase Agreement with YA II PN, LTD. (Yorkville) for up to $15.0 million in ordinary shares over 36 months. Shares are sold at 97% of the lowest of three daily VWAPs during a three-day period, with a 1.0% commitment fee paid partly in shares. A prior $10.0 million agreement terminated after full drawdown. Yorkville's ownership is capped at 9.99%. The deal functions as an at-the-market equity facility, providing PRF with flexible capital access. Watch for share dilution from subsequent advances and the effectiveness of the required registration statement.

AIIOW.brief: Robo.ai Inc. filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, reporting its acquisition of QC Capital Limited via its subsidiary Roboai Investments L.L.C-FZ. The registrant is the issuer/acquirer. The agreement, dated June 12, 2026, covers 100% of QC Capital for total consideration of US$60,000,000, payable in 20,491,805 Class B ordinary shares. Sellers receive 3% at closing; the remainder is locked for 8 years and released in five equal annual tranches starting from the fourth anniversary. Closing is expected on or before July 24, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee is stated. The deal supports technology development and commercialization. Watch for shareholder approval and regulatory conditions; lock-up reduces near-term overhang.

SAGT.brief: Sagtec Global Limited filed a Form 6-K reporting a definitive private subscription agreement with Director/CEO/major shareholder Ng Chen Lok for 1,500,000 Class A ordinary shares at US$1.04/share, totaling US$1,560,000. The price was based on market price as of June 17, 2026. Shares are newly issued, rank pari passu with existing shares, are restricted securities with no registration rights, and proceeds will fund working capital, corporate purposes, strategic initiatives, and expansion. The transaction closed June 17, 2026. This non-US filing reports a private placement to an insider; the small size and insider nature suggest a capital raise rather than a broader special situation, but classification is low confidence.

MSC.brief: Studio City Finance Limited, a subsidiary of Studio City International Holdings Ltd, filed a Form 6-K announcing a partial redemption of US$165,000,000 of its US$500,000,000 6.500% Senior Notes due 2028. The redemption price is 100.000% of principal plus accrued interest to the Redemption Date of July 18, 2026. This is a standard debt reduction transaction, returning capital to noteholders. The filing includes a notice of partial redemption under the indenture dated July 15, 2020, with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee. Watch for the impact on Studio City's leverage profile and any subsequent redemptions or refinancing plans.

TEO.brief: Telecom Argentina S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting the Argentine Antitrust Tribunal's conditional approval of its acquisition of exclusive control over Telefónica Móviles Argentina S.A. and its subsidiaries. The resolution imposes structural remedies requiring transfer of 6,000,000 mobile customers (4M in AMBA, 2M rest of country) and spectrum rights, plus 211,400 residential internet subscribers in 28 localities, along with behavioral remedies in corporate and wholesale segments. The transaction was first disclosed on April 30, 2026. The antitrust conditionality creates an unusual risk-arb angle: investors must assess the feasibility and buyer identification for the mandated divestitures.

TIMB.brief: TIM S.A. filed a Form 6-K attaching minutes of a Fiscal Council meeting approving a proposal to distribute interest on shareholders' equity (IE). The distribution totals R$400 million (approx. $80 million USD), at R$0.1674573219 gross per share. Payment is scheduled by July 22, 2026, with a record date of June 22, 2026; shares acquired after that date trade ex-dividend. A 17.5% withholding tax applies unless exempt. The board's fiscal council expressed a favorable opinion. This is a routine capital return via IE, a common Brazilian corporate tax-advantaged distribution equivalent to a dividend. No special situation beyond standard dividend policy is present. What to watch: the net cash impact and any future recurring distributions, but no risk-arb angle exists.

TURB.brief: Turbo Energy, S.A. filed a Form 6-K containing its Proxy Notice and Statement for the 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders. The meeting is scheduled for June 29, 2026, in Valencia, Spain, with remote attendance permitted. The agenda includes standard shareholder items; no extraordinary transactions are proposed. The filing is a routine foreign private issuer report. Category assigned as Other because, while not a traditional special situation, the proxy statement may involve management changes or other non-routine items. No deal terms applicable. What to watch: any voting outcomes and potential director elections.

UGP.brief: Ultrapar Participações S.A. (via its parent Ultrapar Holdings Inc.) filed a Form 6-K disclosing board approval of a share buyback program for up to 18 million common shares (1.61% of capital stock), to be executed on B3 (São Paulo stock exchange). The repurchased shares will be used for stock-based incentive plans, held in treasury, or canceled—no capital reduction. No price, premium, or advisor is stated. The program runs until June 17, 2027, under CVM Resolution 77/22. Watch for execution pace and impact on float and incentive plan dilution.

UXIN.brief: Uxin Limited filed a Form 6-K announcing a management share purchase plan. Chairman and CEO Kun Dai intends to use personal funds to buy up to $5 million of Uxin's ADSs over 12 months starting June 25, 2026, under applicable rules and the company's insider trading policy. This is an insider purchase plan that signals confidence but does not constitute an issuer tender or buyback program. No board recommendation, advisor, or specific price terms are provided. The plan is purely voluntary and not company-funded. To watch: actual buying pace and any subsequent Section 16 filings, which would indicate conviction and potential undervaluation.

ATXG.brief: Addentax Group Corp. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of 41.67% of Riches Family Office Limited (the Target) from Riches FO Holdings Limited and Mr. Wu Rui, the registrant's COO. The subsidiary Yingxi Industrial Chain Investment Co., Ltd acquired the stake in exchange for 33,500 shares of Addentax common stock, issued offshore under Regulation S to Mr. Wu Rui. No cash price per share, premium, or break fee was disclosed. The board did not name an independent advisor. The transaction closed on June 15, 2026. The stock consideration creates insider alignment but no public arbitrage spread. Watch for future disclosures on the Target's performance and potential further ownership changes.

ATNM.brief: Actinium Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K on June 18, 2026, disclosing submission of a compliance plan to NYSE American after receiving a notice on May 27, 2026, for non-compliance with continued listing standards under Section 1003(a)(ii) of the NYSE American Company Guide, which requires at least $4.0 million in stockholders' equity if losses occurred in three of the last four fiscal years. The plan outlines actions management intends to take to restore compliance. No specific terms (price, premium, stake) are stated. The filing does not name any advisor. The structural note is the listing standard deficiency and the compliance plan submission. Watch for NYSE American's acceptance of the plan and the company's ability to regain compliance within the allowed cure period.

RIME.brief: Algorhythm Holdings, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that it received a deficiency letter from Nasdaq on June 16, 2026, stating its common stock (RIME) no longer meets the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has a 180-day compliance period through December 14, 2026, and may regain compliance if the closing bid price is at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If not cured, an additional 180-day period may be available if other listing standards are met. The deficiency has no immediate effect on trading. No specific price, premium, or deal terms were disclosed. Watch for potential reverse stock split or other cure actions.

ALIT.brief: Alight, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a reverse stock split and related charter amendments approved by stockholders at its June 10, 2026 annual meeting. The reverse stock split is 1-for-20 for Class A common stock, Class B non-voting common stock, and Class V common stock, effective June 29, 2026. A corresponding 1-for-20 reverse unit split of Alight Units in a subsidiary was also executed. The charter amendments also included board declassification and officer exculpation under DGCL Section 102(b)(7). This is an ordinary corporate action with no special situation dynamics; no deal consideration, premium, or stakeholder contest is involved. Watch for any subsequent stock price adjustment to the reverse split.

BCO.brief: Brinks filed an 8-K disclosing two shareholder lawsuits challenging its pending acquisition of NCR Atleos. Under the February 26, 2026 Merger Agreement, a Brink's subsidiary will merge with NCR Atleos, which will then be merged into another subsidiary. The all-stock deal is subject to shareholder votes at special meetings on June 30, 2026. The complaints, filed in New York Supreme Court, allege negligent misrepresentation in the NCR Atleos proxy statement. Brink's took no position on the lawsuits. The combination would create a cash-management powerhouse. Watch for potential settlement or court ruling that could delay close, affecting risk-arb spread.

BAND.brief: Bandwidth Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of $316.25M aggregate principal amount of 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, including full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $41.25M. The notes were sold to Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC as representative of the initial purchasers via a private placement under Rule 144A. The notes bear no regular interest, but special interest may accrue up to 0.50% upon certain filing failures. Maturity is July 1, 2032, with early redemption or repurchase provisions. The proceeds likely support capital return activities such as buybacks or debt management, though the filing does not specify. The transaction is a convertible debt offering, which can be viewed as a capital returns strategy if proceeds are used for shareholder returns. Watch for use of proceeds and conversion mechanics.

AVGO.brief: Broadcom Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing pricing terms and results of cash tender offers for its outstanding senior notes. On June 17, 2026, Broadcom announced it would purchase, up to a $2.5 billion aggregate cap, six series of notes: 4.926% Senior Notes due 2037, 4.900% due 2038, 5.050% due 2030, 5.200% due 2032, 5.150% due 2031, and 4.900% due 2032. Pricing was set per the Offer to Purchase dated June 11, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium percentage, or specific price per note was disclosed. The tender is a liability-management transaction to reduce debt. Watch for completion timeline and potential upsize.

CMTV.brief: Community Bancorp /VT filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026 announcing its Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share, payable August 1, 2026 to holders of record July 15, 2026. The filing under Item 8.01 (Other Events) includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1. There are no deal terms, premium, or transaction mechanics; this is a routine dividend declaration with no change to corporate structure or capital return program. As a standard dividend announcement, it does not meet special-situation criteria.

CAES.brief: Cantor Equity Partners VII, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering (IPO) on June 18, 2026, offering 25 million Class A ordinary shares at $10.00 per share, generating $250 million in gross proceeds. Simultaneously, it completed a private placement of 600,000 shares to its sponsor, Cantor EP Holdings VII, LLC, for $6 million. Net proceeds of $250 million ($10.00 per public share) were deposited into a trust account with Continental Stock Transfer Trust Company. An audited balance sheet as of the closing date was included. This is a standard SPAC IPO filing; the trust structure is typical for blank-check companies. No business combination target has been announced. Watch for future disclosure of a de-SPAC transaction and shareholder vote.

LIEN.brief: Chicago Atlantic BDC, Inc. (LIEN) filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026, announcing it entered into a merger agreement to acquire Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance, Inc. (REFI). REFI will merge into LIEN, with LIEN surviving. No price-per-share, premium, or deal value was disclosed. The LIEN Board, on a special committee recommendation, unanimously approved the merger as fair to stockholders. Pre-merger, REFI will elect BDC status under the Investment Company Act, and management agreements will terminate without payment. The parties intend the merger to be a tax-free reorganization. Key watchpoints include stockholder votes and regulatory approvals; risk-arb focuses on structure and timing.

DYAI.brief: Dyadic International disclosed on June 18, 2026 that Nasdaq initiated delisting proceedings for non-compliance with the $1.00 bid price rule (Rule 5450(a)(1)) and the continued listing standards (Rule 5550(b)). The company failed to regain compliance by the June 17, 2026 deadline and did not meet the $5 million shareholders' equity condition for an extension. Additionally, it has not satisfied the $2.5 million equity, $35 million market value, or $500,000 net income tests. Dyadic plans to request a hearing before a Nasdaq hearings panel, which will automatically stay any delisting action until the panel's decision. Watch for the hearing outcome or any pre-hearing cure efforts.

DAAQU.brief: Digital Asset Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) filed an amended S-4/A for its pending business combination with Old Glory Holding Co, a commercial bank. Terms call for Old Glory shareholders to receive a mix of cash and stock; exact per-share price and premium were not disclosed in this filing. The SPAC's board recommends the deal; no advisor named. Mechanics include the typical SPAC structure with Class A common stock and warrants; the transaction is subject to regulatory approval including bank regulators and SEC effectiveness. The parties target closing by year-end. Watch for shareholder redemption levels and regulatory timeline.

ECHO.brief: EchoStar Corp filed an 8-K reporting that subsidiary DISH DBS Corporation made delayed interest payments on three series of notes (5.25% secured notes due 2026, 5.75% secured notes due 2028, and 5.125% unsecured notes due 2029) within the 30-day grace period, avoiding an Event of Default. The payments were deferred to preserve liquidity pending receipt of $20.25 billion from the AT&T Transactions, which have received FCC and DOJ approvals but remain subject to final FCC order and other closing conditions. This filing reflects debt management and liquidity planning rather than a transformative event.

ESOA.brief: On June 17, 2026, Energy Services of America Corporation declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.04 per common share, payable July 15, 2026 to shareholders of record on June 30, 2026. The dividend represents a routine capital return to shareholders and does not involve a tender, buyback, or special dividend. No board recommendation, advisor, or unusual structural mechanics are noted. The filing is a standard 8-K Item 8.01 disclosure. What to watch: ongoing dividend policy and potential future increases, but no risk-arb angle present.

ENPH.brief: Enphase Energy filed an 8-K disclosing a Tax Credit Transfer Agreement to sell up to $150 million of Section 45X advanced manufacturing production tax credits to a leading financial institution for up to $139.5 million, payable in four installments through 2027. The agreement involves standard conditions precedent, covenants, indemnification, and termination provisions. This transaction monetizes tax credits generated from eligible component production in the US. As a non-deal special situation, it falls under 'Other' categories like tax credit sales. Watch for payment milestones and the company's ability to generate sufficient credits to fulfill the agreement.

FATAQ.brief: This 8-K reports the auction of substantially all assets of Fat Brands Inc. and Twin Hospitality Group Inc., following their Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing on January 26, 2026. The Bankruptcy Court approved bidding procedures on April 9, 2026; the auction was held April 27, 2026. Provisional winners included FBG Bid Co. LLC for FAT Brands assets and Amazing Brands, LLC for HDOS assets. Exact terms (price per share, premium, implied value) are not stated in the excerpt. No board recommendation or advisor named. The sale is subject to Bankruptcy Court approval; a hearing to approve the sale is scheduled. What to watch: final court approval, potential competing bids, and closing timeline.

GPUS-PD.brief: Hyperscale Data, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an At-the-Market Issuance Sales Agreement with Spartan Capital Securities, LLC as sales agent. The agreement allows the company to sell up to $300 million of Class A common stock from time to time via an ATM offering under Rule 415, pursuant to its effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3. Shares will be sold at market prices, with the company setting parameters including minimum price and daily volume limits. No premium, fixed price, or board recommendation is stated. This equity issuance is intended to raise capital, which falls under capital returns as a financing event, though no direct return to shareholders is specified. The filing is an ordinary shelf takedown, but given the scale, it is classified as a capital return with medium confidence. What to watch: dilution impact and market reception. No risk-arb angle.

OMER.brief: Omeros Corporation filed an 8-K reporting private repurchases of its 9.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029. It completed a $16.0M principal repurchase for ~$31.3M and entered agreements to repurchase up to ~$14.5M additional principal for up to ~$31.0M, with pricing dependent on common stock trading price during an averaging period. Post-repurchases, ~$40.3M principal will remain outstanding. The company may refinance with non-convertible debt. No board recommendation or advisors named. Watch for completion of averaging period and potential refinancing impact on leverage.

PKBK.brief: Parke Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a cash dividend of $0.20 per share, payable July 17, 2026 to shareholders of record July 3, 2026. The dividend is a regular quarterly distribution, subject to Board discretion based on financial condition and regulatory restrictions. No premium or special terms are involved. The filing includes a press release and an inline XBRL exhibit. As a routine dividend declaration, this is not a special-situation transaction. No deal structure, advisor, or regulatory clock applies. Watch for future dividend sustainability given potential regulatory constraints on bank holding company distributions.

TRAK.brief: The filing is an 8-K reporting ReposiTrak, Inc.'s declaration of a quarterly cash dividend of $0.02 per share ($0.08 annualized) payable on/around August 14, 2026 to holders of record June 30, 2026. The dividend is funded from the company's cash flows. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The mechanics are a regular quarterly cash distribution; no special dividend or buyback is indicated. The registrant is the issuer. This is a routine capital return event, not a special situation, though it involves return of capital to shareholders. What to watch: sustainability of the dividend payout relative to earnings and cash flows.

SRBK.brief: SR Bancorp, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on June 18, 2026, announcing its Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.06 per share, a $0.01 or 20% increase from the prior dividend. The dividend will be paid on July 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of June 30, 2026. As the issuer, the company highlights its earnings strength and commitment to shareholder value. No other special-situation mechanics (e.g., tender, restructuring, acquisition) are present. This is a routine dividend increase disclosure, thus classified under Capital Returns.

TTMI.brief: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026, announcing definitive stock purchase agreements to acquire two privately-held European companies: Swiss Technology Group AG (Zurich) and ILFA GmbH (Hannover, Germany). Both transactions are for all-cash consideration, with no specific price per share, premium, or implied value disclosed. Regulatory approvals are required; the company expects to close subject to those conditions. The board recommends the acquisitions, but no advisor is named. The combined acquisitions would establish TTM's presence in Europe, adding PCB and materials capabilities in medical, aerospace/defense, and other markets. Investors should watch for regulatory clearance timing and potential integration risks; no break fee or deal mechanics details are provided.

CIIT.brief: Tianci International filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of a public offering on June 17, 2026. The company sold 4,055,000 units at $0.81 per unit and 2,000,000 pre-funded units at $0.809 per unit, raising approximately $4.9 million in gross proceeds. Each unit consists of one share of common stock (or a pre-funded warrant exercisable at $0.001 per share) and one common warrant exercisable at $0.81 per share for three years. The offering is an equity capital raise with warrants attached; net proceeds will fund working capital. The pre-funded units reduce the effective per-share cost for investors. No advisor was named. The capital return structure is dilutive to existing shareholders with warrant overhang. What to watch: potential near-term dilution from warrant exercises and impact on stock price.

TDACW.brief: Translational Development Acquisition Corp. (TDAC) filed an 8-K reporting shareholder redemption results and extension vote outcome related to its proposed business combination with ProLogium Holding Inc. 85% of shares (approx. $156.8M in trust) were not redeemed, and 95% of votes favored extension. The merger, announced May 27, 2026, targets ProLogium, a lithium ceramic battery firm serving AI data centers, aerospace, robotics, defense, and EVs. No per-share price or premium stated; no advisors named. The filing combines Rule 425 and Rule 14a-12 communications. Watch for definitive proxy/prospectus and shareholder vote on the business combination; risk-arb centers on regulatory clearance and trust preservation.

VREOD.brief: Vireo Growth Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its entry into an Arrangement Agreement to acquire all outstanding common shares of C21 Investments Inc. via a statutory plan of arrangement under British Columbia law. Each C21 common share will be exchanged for 0.023052 Vireo subordinate voting shares (Exchange Ratio), implying an undisclosed per-share value and premium. C21 options become replacement options in Vireo; restricted/deferred share units vest and settle pre-closing; warrants and debentures are assumed. No board recommendation or advisor named. The share-based consideration and cross-border structure create a risk-arb spread tied to Vireo's stock volatility. Watch for regulatory approvals, dissenting shareholder rights, and anti-dilution adjustments.

WHR-PA.brief: Whirlpool Corp. filed an 8-K regarding a First Supplemental Indenture entered into by its Luxembourg finance subsidiary, the issuer, to amend the indenture governing its 1.100% Notes due 2027. The amendment, approved via consents solicited in a concurrent tender offer, reduces the satisfaction-and-discharge waiting period from one year to two years. As of June 12, 2026, approximately 91.12% of the €600M notes ($546.7M aggregate) had been tendered. The change facilitates earlier defeasance of the notes once all tendered notes are purchased. No premium, consideration type, or board recommendation is disclosed. This is a bond indenture amendment rather than a classic special situation. Watch for completion of the tender settlement.

YICCU.brief: Yorkville International Capital Corp. filed an 8-K to report the closing of its IPO of 23,000,000 units at $10.00/unit, including full exercise of the underwriters' over-allotment, raising $230,000,000 in gross proceeds. Simultaneously, the sponsor and underwriter purchased 6,300,000 private placement warrants at $1.00 each, generating $6,300,000. Proceeds were deposited into a trust account, standard for blank-check companies. The audited balance sheet is included as an exhibit. As a newly formed SPAC (SIC 6770), the company has 24 months to complete a business combination. Watch for target announcement and shareholder vote; risk-arb centers on deal certainty and redemption risk.

ALISU.brief: Calisa Acquisition Corp filed an amended S-4 registration statement for its business combination with Goodvision AI Inc. Under the merger agreement, Goodvision AI will merge with a subsidiary of Calisa, with Calisa continuing as the publicly traded entity. The transaction values Goodvision AI at an implied enterprise value of approximately $250 million. Calisa's board unanimously recommends the deal. The combined company will focus on AI-driven data processing. Closing is subject to regulatory approvals and a shareholder vote, expected by year-end 2026. Investors should watch for redemption trends and any regulatory pushback.

MCFN.brief: McCarthy Finney, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement with the SEC on June 18, 2026, relating to a business combination. The filing does not disclose specific deal terms such as price per share, premium, or expected close date. No board recommendation or financial advisor is named. The S-4/A is typical for mergers or exchange offers requiring SEC review; no structural details (collateral, overhang, ownership split) are provided.
