The regulatory clock continues as SEC reviews the amended registration. What to watch: subsequent amendments or a declared effective date signaling proxy solicitation and shareholder vote.

CSCIF.brief: COSCIENS Biopharma Inc. filed a Form 15 on July 6, 2026, to voluntarily terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and suspend its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The action, certified by CFO Giuliano La Fratta, cited Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and other available provisions. As of the filing, the company had only 153 holders of record of its common shares, well below the 300 threshold for deregistration. Going dark reduces public disclosure obligations; risk-arb should note limited liquidity and potential shareholder challenges.

PRIF-PL.brief: Priority Income Fund, Inc., an externally managed closed-end investment company, launched an issuer tender offer to repurchase up to 1,550,812 shares of its common stock (2.5% of shares outstanding as of June 30, 2025). The purchase price equals the net asset value per share as of July 31, 2026; as of April 30, 2026, NAV/share was $3.70, but the actual price may differ. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The offer is entirely cash, with no fixed premium; it provides liquidity for shareholders given the absence of a public market. Watch for the final NAV calculation and any proration if oversubscribed.

IOBTQ.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed a Form 25-NSE to delist the common stock of IO Biotech, Inc., effective June 18, 2026. The delisting follows Nasdaq Staff's determination on March 31, 2026, that the company no longer qualified under Listing Rules 5101, 5110(b), and IM-5101-1. The company did not appeal, and its stock was suspended on April 7, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was noted. The delisting is procedural, with no financial terms or ownership changes. Watch for potential OTC trading or regulatory developments post-delisting.

EXOZ.brief: ExoZymes Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a firm-commitment unit offering of 592,270 common shares and 296,135 warrants at $18.00 per unit. The warrants have a $11.24 exercise price, five-year term, and redemption features. MDB Capital, a conflicted underwriter due to its 46.1% pre-offering ownership, is lead underwriter; Lucid Capital Markets serves as qualified independent underwriter for FINRA Rule 5121. The offering is a capital raise, not a special situation. Risk-arb angle: monitor dilution impact and potential warrant-driven volatility.

NYXH.brief: Nyxoah SA filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a follow-on public offering of 55,232,558 ordinary shares at $1.72 per share, raising ~$95M. The offering includes a 30-day over-allotment option for 8,284,883 additional shares. Certain directors/affiliates indicated interest in buying 13,712,900 shares, but no binding commitment. Underwriters are BofA, Degroof Petercam, and B. Riley. Shares listed on Nasdaq ($1.45 close) and Euronext (€2.46). Settlement T+2 on June 9, 2026. This is a capital-raising event with no change in control, strategic review, or special situation beyond a secondary offering.

AIIR.brief: AIR Global PLC filed a Form 6-K on June 8, 2026, attaching a press release detailing key metrics following the closing of its business combination with Cantor Equity Partners III, Inc. (CAEP), a SPAC. The Nasdaq-listed entity (AIIR) reports ~160.39M shares outstanding, a US$6.91 closing price, and a Forward Purchase Agreement with Harraden Circle for ~5M shares at a redemption price of US$10.49, enhancing liquidity. Earnout shares vest at US$12.50/US$15.00 thresholds by May 31, 2031. The company also reports ~US$268M net debt. Watch for stock price dynamics and FPA valuation date.

AEC.brief: Anfield Energy filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release providing an operational update on the renewal and reactivation of its radioactive materials license for the Shootaring Canyon Uranium Mill. The company completed drilling 8 additional monitoring wells, began removal of existing leach tanks for refurbishment, and continues detailed engineering with PSE Engineering. License renewal is expected by end of 2026, with production targeted for 2027. No special-situation event is present; this is a routine operational update.

BBVA.brief: BBVA filed a 6-K reporting progress on the third tranche of its share buyback program. Between 1-3 July 2026, it repurchased shares for €918.3M, reaching 62.9% of the tranche's €1.46B maximum cash amount. Citigroup Global Markets Europe AG acts as manager. The buyback is conducted under EU Market Abuse Regulation. No specific price per share or premium is disclosed. This is a capital return program returning excess capital to shareholders. Watch for completion of the tranche and potential impact on EPS and capital ratios.

BNTX.brief: BioNTech SE filed a 6-K announcing the commencement of a share buyback program for its ADSs on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The program, authorized on May 7, 2026, allows repurchases of up to $1.0 billion through May 6, 2027, under existing AGM authorization for up to 24.9 million shares (10% of share capital). Repurchases are subject to price limits (within 10% above/20% below 3-day VWAP) and comply with EU MAR, Rule 10b-18, and 10b5-1. A mandated credit institution makes independent trading decisions. The buyback aims to satisfy ordinary course obligations and enhance capital efficiency. Watch for actual repurchase pace and impact on share price.

EH.brief: EHang Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing a Board-approved US$30 million share repurchase program for its ADSs or ordinary shares over 12 months. Repurchases may occur via open market, private negotiations, or block trades, subject to market conditions and SEC rules (10b5-1, 10b-18), funded from existing cash. Management discretion governs timing and amount, with no fixed price, premium, or expiration beyond the period. The program signals management's confidence in long-term growth and capital allocation discipline. No advisor or recommendation is stated. Watch for execution pace and market reaction to the buyback's impact on share count.

GNTOF.brief: Gentor Resources Inc. filed a Form 6-K with a press release announcing an annual and special shareholders meeting on June 26, 2026. At the meeting, shareholders will vote on a special resolution to consolidate common shares on a 2-for-1 basis, reducing outstanding shares from ~38.9 million to ~19.5 million, subject to board discretion and NEX approval. The share consolidation aims to attract additional capital. No price, premium, or advisor is mentioned. This is a routine corporate action, not a special situation; the event is a share consolidation proposal.

NCT.brief: Intercont (Cayman) Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting a Subscription Agreement for Class B Shares with Beverly Holding Limited, a company wholly owned by CEO Muchun Zhu. The subscriber agreed to buy 650,000 Class B shares at $3.00 per share, total $1.95 million. The Audit Committee approved the issuance. Closing requires shareholder approvals: increasing authorized capital to $250M (100B shares), changing Class B voting rights from 30 to 100 votes per share, and adopting amended articles. This is a related-party capital raising with governance changes, not a transformative special situation, so category is 'Other'.

FMFC.brief: Kandal M Venture Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 24, 2026, disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency letter on December 22, 2025, and a subsequent grant of an additional 180-day compliance period (until December 21, 2026) from Nasdaq on June 23, 2026. No price, premium, or transaction terms are stated. The board is evaluating options to regain compliance. The filing is a routine regulatory update on a listing standard deficiency, not a special-situation event. Watch for any future reverse stock split or other compliance plan.

MTLS.brief: Materialise NV filed a Form 6-K reporting a weekly update on its share buyback program originally announced on 30 October 2025. Under the program, the company has a discretionary mandate to repurchase up to EUR 30 million of its own shares. During the week ending 3 July 2026, it bought 9,745 shares at an average price of EUR 6.29 per share (total EUR 61,341). Since program launch on 26 January 2026, Materialise has repurchased 1,080,342 shares (1.8% of outstanding shares) for EUR 5,271,605. This is a routine capital-return update, not a special-situation event. Watch for future progress updates and any acceleration of the buyback pace.

FMX.brief: FEMSA filed Form 6-K reporting a strategic equity investment by QED Investors into its lending business unit. FEMSA retains a majority stake; specific terms like stake percentage, price, premium, or dates are not disclosed. The partnership aims to leverage QED's fintech expertise for credit solutions in Mexico. No board recommendation or advisors named. The filing is a routine foreign private issuer report of a minority investment, not a transformative special situation.

MWC.brief: Micware Co., Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting the results of its annual general meeting of shareholders conducted by written resolution. Shareholders holding 56,141,914 votes (100% of exercisable votes) unanimously approved the financial statements for the 23rd fiscal year and elected Kazunori Mori as a director. The meeting details were previously disclosed in a May 19, 2026 Form 6-K. The filing is a routine post-meeting report under the Companies Act of Japan, equivalent to an 8-K Item 5.07 disclosure. No special situation is present; the director election is routine and not forced or abrupt.

PUK.brief: Prudential plc filed a Form 6-K reporting a continuation of its on-market share buyback program announced 6 January 2026. From 29-30 June 2026, the company repurchased 794,515 ordinary shares (5p each) on the London Stock Exchange via JP Morgan Securities at a volume-weighted average price of approximately 10.056p per share. All shares were cancelled, reducing the issued share count to 2,510,209,955. Program to date aggregate purchases: 43,737,014 shares at a VWAP of 1,096.2799p. The buyback is conducted under shareholder authority from the 2025 AGM and in compliance with UK MAR and Hong Kong Code on Share Buy-Backs.

ZTO.brief: ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc. filed a Form 6-K providing next-day disclosure returns and a monthly return detailing ongoing share buybacks under Hong Kong listing rules. The filing lists multiple open-market repurchases of ADSs (each representing one Class A ordinary share) at prices ranging from ~$22.12–$22.86 per ADS, totaling 10 tranches between May 20 and June 2, 2026. These buybacks are part of a previously announced capital return program; no board recommendation or advisor is named. The repurchased shares are held as treasury and not yet cancelled. The filing is a routine ongoing disclosure of share repurchases, confirming an active return of capital to shareholders. What to watch: pace of future buybacks and potential cancellation of treasury shares.

ARLP.brief: Alliance Resource Partners LP via its subsidiary Alliance Minerals acquired all non-owned general and limited partner interests in AllDale Minerals III and IV for ~$206.2 million, subject to post-closing adjustments, while related entities of Joseph W. Craft III purchased $100.0 million of limited partner interests in AllDale III. The acquisition was funded with cash, revolver borrowings, and a new $150 million Term Loan due January 1, 2028 with quarterly principal payments of $18.75 million and SOFR-based interest. The filing primarily details the financing and related agreements; board recommendation and advisors are not named. Watch for regulatory integration and credit facility covenant compliance.

BSTR.brief: BSTR Newco, LLC entered a $2.5M loan agreement with BSTR Holdings (Cayman) for operating costs and expenses related to a pending business combination with Cantor Equity Partners I, Inc. Interest is SOFR plus 3.90%, payable annually; principal due at earliest of business combination consummation, dissolution, or two years. No price/share, premium, or board recommendation stated. This is a financing arrangement supporting a previously announced deal, not a standalone special situation. Watch for progress on the business combination and any default triggers.

BHM.brief: Bluerock Homes Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a series of dispositions of 24 single-family residential units from its Ballast portfolio (Arizona, Colorado, Washington) to unaffiliated third parties. The aggregate sales price was approximately $8.5 million, yielding net proceeds of $7.8 million after closing costs and adjustments. The dispositions occurred over January 1–June 2, 2026. The registrant holds a 95% interest in the joint venture that owned the portfolio. No board recommendation or advisor is mentioned. The filing includes unaudited pro forma financial statements. This is a routine asset sale, not a transformative special situation; the aggregate value is modest relative to the company.

CERS.brief: Cerus Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 8, 2026, reporting entry into a Second Amended and Restated Credit, Security and Guaranty Agreement (Term Loan) and a Second Amended and Restated Credit, Security and Guaranty Agreement (Revolving Loan) on June 5, 2026. These agreements amend and restate existing credit facilities with MidCap Financial Trust and MidCap Funding IV Trust. The Term Loan Credit Agreement provides a secured term loan facility of up to $65.0 million, with an initial $35.0 million draw to refinance existing term loans. Additional tranches up to $30.0 million are available for working capital and general corporate purposes. Interest is Term SOFR plus 5.50% (1.00% floor). Interest-only payments apply for 48 months then 12 months of amortization. No early termination fee after one year. This is a routine refinancing and credit facility amendment, not a special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or activist campaign.

CELC.brief: Celcuity Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a $575M underwritten public offering of 0.250% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032. The offering included a full over-allotment exercise, generating net proceeds of ~$557M. Proceeds will repay outstanding loan obligations and fund working capital, clinical trials, commercialization, and potential acquisitions. The notes are unsecured senior obligations. Investors should watch for dilution risk from conversion and the company's use of proceeds for business development.

ZONE.brief: CleanCore Solutions filed an 8-K disclosing entry into a Contribution Agreement, LLC Agreement, and Master Platform Agreement with HST Technologies (Platform Co) to form a joint venture for data center development. CleanCore will contribute up to $100M cash for a 99% capital interest; Platform Co contributes assets for a 1% interest and 20% carried participation after a 12% preferred return. The JV targets up to $2B total commitments. Platform Co manages, but CleanCore has major-decision approval and removal rights. This is a non-M&A capital commitment, not a classic special situation. What to watch: funding timing and potential dilution if commitments are missed.

GOCOQ.brief: GoHealth, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing Nasdaq's delisting determination for its Class A common stock (GOCO) following the company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing. The delisting is effective June 16, 2026, based on public interest concerns, residual equity holder issues, and non-compliance with the $35M minimum market value rule (Nasdaq Rule 5550(b)(2)). The company will not appeal. Post-delisting, shares may trade on OTC markets, which present reduced liquidity. The delisting is not expected to affect the Chapter 11 cases. Watch for over-the-counter trading commencement and plan confirmation milestones in the bankruptcy proceedings.

HUBB.brief: Hubbell Incorporated filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of NSI Electrical Buyer, Inc. (NSI Industries) for $3.0 billion in cash. The purchase was funded via a $900 million unsecured term loan, $1.9 billion in senior notes, and commercial paper. The target provides electrical fittings and wire management products for industrial, infrastructure, and commercial markets. All issued and outstanding shares were acquired from seller NSI Buyer, LP. Terms include customary cash, debt, working capital, and expense adjustments. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee stated. The deal closed on June 9, 2026, with no further regulatory hurdles; watch integration progress and debt servicing.

INCY.brief: Incyte filed an 8-K under Items 8.01 and 9.01 announcing the completion of its acquisition of Vega Therapeutics, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Star Therapeutics LLC. The deal closed on July 6, 2026, with terms not disclosed. The acquisition adds VGA039, an anti-Protein S monoclonal antibody in Phase 3 for von Willebrand disease, to Incyte's hematology pipeline. No price, premium, board recommendation, advisors, or breakup fee were stated. The filing confirms consummation, not a new announcement. Watch for Phase 3 data readouts and potential label expansion, as VGA039 could be first-to-market for VWD prophylaxis. No risk-arb spread since terms are undisclosed.

NOTVQ.brief: Inotiv, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a $65.5M debtor-in-possession credit facility on June 5, 2026, following its Chapter 11 filing on June 3, 2026. The DIP facility includes a $25M new money tranche (SOFR +11.5%, 4.5% upfront) and a $40.5M roll-up of prepetition bridge loans (3.5% upfront). The facility is superpriority secured and priming, with exit financing expected. The prepackaged plan of reorganization contemplates emergence. Watch for Bankruptcy Court approval, DIP budget constraints, and the conversion to exit term loans.

AVO.brief: Mission Produce, Inc. filed an 8-K to report financial results for the quarter ended April 30, 2026, and disclose a new $100 million stock repurchase program authorized by the Board on June 3, 2026, replacing the prior program with $11.2 million remaining. The buyback runs 36 months with no fixed price or expiration. The filing also notes the completed May 28, 2026 acquisition of Calavo Growers. The repurchase represents a capital return to shareholders. Watch for buyback execution pace and potential impact on share price; no risk-arb angle as this is an issuer buyback.

MITI.brief: Mitesco, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 8, 2026, disclosing a bridge financing and a non-binding term sheet for an equity line of credit (ELOC). Two historical investors purchased 2026 Bridge Notes: Monroe Street Capital for $75,000 and Pinz Special Opportunities Fund for $150,000, each with a 10% OID and 12-month maturity, convertible at $0.15 per share. The ELOC facility contemplates up to $30 million and requires registration via Form S-1. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The convertible notes represent a small capital injection rather than a broader return-of-capital plan, but the potential for future equity draws suggests a capital-return-like structure.

NPACU.brief: New Providence Acquisition Corp. III issued unsecured promissory notes totaling $1.5 million to co-CEOs Gary Smith and Alexander Coleman for working capital. The notes bear no interest, mature upon business combination or liquidation, and are convertible into units at $10 per unit, each comprising one Class A share and one-third warrant. A prior $200,000 sponsor advance is payable on demand. This is a routine SPAC working capital facility, not a business combination or special situation.

OCFC.brief: OceanFirst Financial Corp. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of a previously disclosed sale of $1.3 billion of multifamily loans acquired via the Flushing Financial merger. The portfolio, largely NYC rent-regulated, was sold at a price consistent with initial valuation estimates. The repositioning reduces rent-regulation exposure to under 2.5% of total assets. BofA Securities advised; Morgan Lewis provided legal counsel. No specific price per share, premium, or terms were disclosed. This is a balance-sheet repositioning, not a special-situation transaction. Watch for second-quarter earnings for further details on financial impact.

PDYNW.brief: Palladyne AI Corp. filed an 8-K on June 8, 2026, announcing an MOU and posting a press release and investor presentation for an investor call on June 9, 2026. Reg FD disclosure suggests potential strategic initiatives, but no specific terms (price, premium, stake %) or definitive agreement were provided. The board recommendation and advisors were not named. The filing may indicate a strategic review or partnership exploration, but details are absent. Watch for updates from the investor call or subsequent filings for clarity on the MOU's implications.

PTACW.brief: Patriot Acquisition Corp. (a blank-check company) filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its IPO on May 18, 2026, of 16,000,000 units at $10.00/unit for $160M gross proceeds, plus the partial exercise of the underwriter's over-allotment option for an additional 1,500,000 units on May 21, 2026, generating $15M. Simultaneously, it completed a private placement of 5,200,000 private placement warrants at $1.00 each to the sponsor and KBW. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing details the capital structure (units, ordinary shares, warrants) and regulatory disclosures. Watch for the de-SPAC timeline and potential target announcement, with risk-arb focus on redemption levels and shareholder approval.

SIG.brief: Signet Jewelers filed an 8-K reporting an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Goldman Sachs to repurchase $50 million of its common shares. The company made an upfront payment and expects an initial delivery of ~480,000 shares on June 8, 2026. Final settlement is based on VWAP during the calculation period, expected between June 12 and July 17, 2026, with potential adjustments. The ASR is part of Signet's 2017 Share Repurchase Program, leaving ~$355 million in remaining authorization. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This deal represents a capital return via share buyback. Watch for final settlement timing, any adjustments to share delivery, and overall repurchase activity under the remaining authorization.

SENS.brief: The filing is an 8-K reporting the closing of previously disclosed local asset purchases by Senseonics Holdings (acquirer) from Ascensia Diabetes Care Holdings (seller) of certain European Eversense CGM assets in Italy, Germany, Spain and Sweden, under a master asset purchase agreement dated Dec 31, 2025. No financial terms, price, or premium are disclosed. The closings occurred on June 1 and June 8, 2026, with an effective accounting date of June 1. The transaction appears to be a bolt-on asset acquisition, not a transformative M&A event. Watch for potential operational integration updates.

SVACU.brief: Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III filed an 8-K reporting an amended business combination agreement with General Fusion Inc. and NewCo. The original agreement, entered on January 21, 2026, was amended on May 12, 2026. The deal involves SVIII continuing from Cayman Islands to British Columbia, amalgamating with NewCo, and adopting new articles. No financial terms (price per share, premium, or valuation) were disclosed. The filing includes Rule 425 communications. The combination is structured as a SPAC merger expected to close post-shareholder vote. Watch for shareholder approval and regulatory clearances; risk-arb centers on redemption levels and deal timing.

TWOD.brief: Two Harbors Investment Corp. (TWO) filed an 8-K reporting stockholder approval at a special meeting on July 2, 2026 of the CCM Merger, under which TWO will become a wholly owned subsidiary of CrossCountry Intermediate Holdco, LLC (CCM). The merger agreement, dated March 27, 2026, was approved by TWO common stockholders via a proxy statement first mailed on or about April 20, 2026. Terms (price per share, premium, implied value) are not disclosed in this excerpt. The board recommended the merger; no advisors named. The structural step is a reverse triangular merger with Merger Sub. Watch for regulatory clearances and the expected close timeline for risk-arb.

VRRM.brief: Verra Mobility Corporation filed an 8-K reporting that its Board formed a Transformation Committee on June 5, 2026, to oversee a transformation initiative. The committee will support management's review of business and financial strategies, cost optimization, growth opportunities, capital allocation, portfolio composition, financing, and capital expenditure plans, and make recommendations to the Board. The committee comprises Raj Ratnakar (chair), Douglas Davis, and John Rexford. No specific terms, premium, or advisor are disclosed. This is an early-stage strategic review. Watch for further updates on potential divestitures, restructuring, or capital allocation changes; no immediate risk-arb angle.

ATYR.brief: aTyr Pharma (ATYR) filed an 8-K (Item 3.01) disclosing Nasdaq granted a 180-day extension to November 30, 2026, to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule. The company previously failed the 10-day closing bid price test by the June 2, 2026 initial compliance date. Nasdaq determined aTyr meets the market value of publicly held shares and other initial listing standards. aTyr intends to cure via a reverse stock split if necessary. No board recommendation or advisor named. If compliance is not achieved by November 30, 2026, delisting proceedings may begin. Watch for potential reverse-split announcement or further price action affecting compliance.

APURR.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Aperture AC (CIK 0002093524), a blank-check company, under SEC Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The delisting was effective June 9, 2026, and the security's registration was withdrawn. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal terms were disclosed. The filing indicates involuntary removal from Nasdaq; no shareholder vote, collateral, or ownership split is specified. What to watch: Delisting may precede a liquidation or target-acquisition failure; risk-arb remains irrelevant.

BIYA.brief: Baiya International Group Inc. (Baiya) sold its wholly owned subsidiary Starfish Technology-FZE to Shengshi International Group Inc. for US$1,000,000 cash, as disclosed in Form 6-K filed July 6, 2026. Baiya previously acquired Starfish under a September 2025 agreement where Baiya issued 2,320,000 Class A shares to the prior sellers; those shares remain with the prior sellers post-closing. The deal is structured as a straightforward cash sale, with no board recommendation or advisors named. The filing provides limited terms but confirms divestiture of a foreign subsidiary, likely to streamline operations. Watch for closing conditions or any regulatory approvals in Dubai; given small size, risk-arb is minimal.

HTOO.brief: Fusion Fuel Green PLC filed a 6-K reporting that shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting approved the acquisition of Royal Uranium Inc. via a Share Exchange Agreement dated February 18, 2026. The resolution passed with 816,174 votes for, 831 against, and 3,116 abstentions. The number of shares to be issued or consideration was not stated. The board recommended the deal; no advisors named. The acquisition requires completion of the share exchange agreement; regulatory clock unspecified. Watch for closing conditions or material changes from the agreement.

TGHL.brief: The GrowHub Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Determination Letter dated June 5, 2026, indicating that the company's securities are subject to delisting from the Nasdaq Capital Market for failure to comply with the minimum bid price requirement ($1.00) under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) by June 1, 2026, and for non-compliance with stockholders equity requirements (Rules 5550(b)(1)-(3)). The company intends to request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel and seek an extended stay of suspension. No price, premium, or advisors are named. Watch for the Panel's decision on the stay and the company's compliance plan submission; risk-arb is not applicable as this is a regulatory delisting proceeding.

IBG.brief: Innovation Beverage Group Ltd (IBG) filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release from its 51%-owned subsidiary BlockFuel Energy, Inc., announcing the acquisition of a six-well oil and gas package in Payne County, Oklahoma. The deal includes four producing horizontal wells, one drilled uncompleted well, and one saltwater disposal well plus infrastructure. No price per share, premium, or total consideration is disclosed. The board recommends the transaction; IBG also has a proposed merger with BlockFuel. The acquisition adds to BlockFuel's 55-well footprint and includes an eight-well vertical drilling program planned for H2 2026. Watch for merger completion and regulatory approvals affecting the subsidiary structure.

KWMWW.brief: K Wave Media Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing the planned retirement of 9,827,057 ordinary shares, representing approximately 13% of outstanding shares. The shares are to be returned under a Rescission and Termination Agreement dated May 29, 2026, which rescinds an earlier equity purchase agreement for Solaire Partners. The shares will be transferred to the Company within 60 days and then retired and cancelled. Management views this as streamlining the corporate structure. No price per share or premium is applicable as this is a share cancellation, not a buyback. The expected close is by end of July 2026. Watch for completion of the return and any associated regulatory filings.

LBGJ.brief: Li Bang International Corp Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the effectiveness of a Share Capital Reorganization and adoption of an amended and restated memorandum of association, approved at an EGM on April 30, 2026. The reorganization reduces par value from US$0.01 to US$0.00001 per share, reduces authorized capital from US$31,505,000 to US$35,000, and creates 3.15B Class A and 350M Class B shares. This is a structural capital change, not a special situation. No special situation terms apply; the filing is a routine corporate action.

NEXRW.brief: Nexera Technologies Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 9, 2026, reporting its majority-owned subsidiary Fort Technology Inc. received Nasdaq listing approval and commenced trading under ticker FRTT on June 8, 2026. Nexera holds approximately 70.94% of Fort’s common shares, and Fort will continue trading on TSXV under FORT. No financial terms, premium, or board advisors were disclosed. The mechanics involve a partial carve-out listing without a full spin-off distribution. The Nasdaq listing provides Fort independent access to capital markets. Watch for potential dilution from any future secondary offerings or eventual full spin-off.

RELX.brief: RELX PLC filed a Form 6-K reporting a series of open-market share repurchases executed through J.P. Morgan Securities plc on the London Stock Exchange. Between April 27 and May 15, 2026, RELX bought back a total of 9,148,450 ordinary shares at volume-weighted average prices ranging from 2,465 to 2,697 pence per share. The repurchased shares are held in treasury. Since January 2, 2026, RELX has purchased 48,282,705 shares. This is a routine capital return program, not an issuer tender offer. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory clock is involved. Watch for ongoing buyback execution and potential impact on share count.

THCH.brief: TH International Ltd filed a 6-K covering Q1 2026 results and disclosed a definitive agreement with THRI to issue up to US$55.0 million of additional senior secured convertible notes. Terms: up to $55 million aggregate principal, senior secured convertible notes. No price per share, premium, or board recommendation stated. The notes are issued by the company to a related party (brand owner/founding shareholder). Mechanics involve secured convertible debt, likely with conversion terms to be detailed. Watch for expansion funding and potential dilution risk.

TAC.brief: TransAlta Corp filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of a C$350 million bought deal offering of 18.23 million common shares at C$19.20 per share. The net proceeds will fund the previously announced acquisition of two natural gas-fired peaking facilities totaling 318 MW near Denver, Colorado. The offering was led by CIBC and RBC and includes a 30-day over-allotment option for up to 2.73 million additional shares. The acquisition is expected to close early Q4 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. If the acquisition fails, proceeds may be used for other growth or debt reduction. Watch for regulatory clearance on the acquisition, which would also de-risk this capital raise.

XXII.brief: 22nd Century Group commenced a warrant inducement offering, agreeing to issue Inducement Warrants for 100% of shares exercised by holders of Existing Warrants (5,345,591 shares at $3.57) at a reduced exercise price of $0.4626. All Existing Warrants must be exercised immediately for cash. Inducement Warrants will be exercisable after stockholder approval, expire in five years, and include anti-dilution adjustments. The company will file a resale registration statement by June 30, 2026. Watch for stockholder meeting outcome and potential dilution from full exercise; risk-arb angle centers on the steep discount and share overhang.

BNAIW.brief: Brand Engagement Network Inc. filed an 8-K/A amending its initial Form 8-K to correct share count in its acquisition of all equity interests of Cataneo GmbH, a German limited liability company. The aggregate purchase price is $19.5 million, comprising $9 million cash and 277,190 shares of common stock. The filing does not state a per-share price, premium, board recommendation, advisor, or expected close date, but the acquisition was completed as of June 30, 2026. The transaction is a cross-border private acquisition; watch for integration risks and any post-closing adjustments.

BAM.brief: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. filed an 8-K to disclose a joint venture with Mitsubishi HC Capital to form a renewable energy company in Europe. The JV's seed portfolio includes ~570 MW of operating assets valued at ~EUR 400 million equity, highly contracted with ~10-year weighted average PPAs. Brookfield will manage operations; both partners will approve future acquisitions funded pro rata. No price per share, premium, or board recommendation is provided. The filing is a business formation announcement without a transaction classification, thus categorized as Other. Watch for future asset acquisitions and governance updates.

COF-PN.brief: Capital One Financial filed an 8-K on June 9, 2026, to file a prospectus supplement registering an additional 39,843 shares of common stock for resale by selling security holders. This brings total registered shares to 10,385,749, issued as consideration for the company's acquisition of Brex Inc., which closed on April 7, 2026. No price per share, premium, or advisor is specified in the filing. The shares are part of an automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3. The filing updates the resale prospectus to allow selling holders to offer the stock. Watch for the resale activity and any impact from the underlying acquisition of Brex, a fintech firm, by Capital One.

CYCUW.brief: Cycurion (NASDAQ:CYCU) filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026 to disclose it had entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement on June 24 to acquire substantially all assets of Kustom Entertainment's (NASDAQ:KUST) video-solutions division, including the Digital Ally brand's in-car/body-worn cameras and evidence management. Terms were not disclosed. The acquisition provides ~1,000 clients and ~58 patents. Closing is expected in early July 2026. Cycurion's board has approved the transaction. This is a transformative bolt-on acquisition, non-dilutive per the filing. Watch for close timing and any regulatory or Nasdaq listing compliance issues.

EVTC.brief: EVERTEC filed an 8-K disclosing a cybersecurity incident where unauthorized access to client data occurred via a third-party support platform. The breach potentially exposed transaction records, payment card numbers, and customer names of financial institution clients in Puerto Rico. The company has contained the intrusion, notified law enforcement, and engaged external experts. No operational disruption has occurred. The investigation is ongoing, with full impact undetermined; expenses are expected but insurance coverage uncertain. This is a regulatory disclosure of an operational event, not a special situation—no deal terms or strategic action is involved. Risk-arb angle is not applicable.

EDGM.brief: Edgemode, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a non-binding term sheet with Pure Data Centres Group Limited to sell its equity interests in entities holding leasehold land sites in Cordoba, Palma, Vianos and Caceres, Spain, for data center development. No price, stake size, or premium was disclosed. The term sheet is non-binding, subject to purchaser due diligence and definitive documentation. Edgemode granted a 60-day exclusivity period. The registrant is the seller. The structure involves a share purchase agreement with an option for a joint venture. What to watch: completion of due diligence and execution of definitive agreements; no definitive deal until then.

FGNXP.brief: FG Nexus Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a reduction in executive compensation due to a smaller digital asset business, alongside disclosure of ongoing share repurchase programs. Through June 5, 2026, the company repurchased approximately 2,984,212 common shares (35% of pre-buyback outstanding) at an average ~$13.62/share, and 264,465 Series A Preferred shares (30% of outstanding) — no fixed price, premium, or board recommendation cited. Capital return is purely a buyback; no advisor named. Watch for execution pace and impact on float, especially given reduced scale of operations.

GTLL.brief: Global Technologies, LTD filed an 8-K reporting a Binding Letter of Intent with FORCARA, LLC to pursue a strategic business relationship potentially leading to FORCARA becoming part of Global Technologies' operating platform. The letter includes an interim joint venture with revenue sharing, a $12,500/month management fee, and 50/50 EBITDA sharing. No definitive terms, price per share, or implied value are stated; the transaction remains subject to due diligence, board approval, and definitive agreements. The filing is preliminary with no guarantee of completion, making the deal highly uncertain. Watch for definitive agreement execution or termination.

HOFT.brief: Hooker Furnishings Corp filed an 8-K announcing a quarterly cash dividend of $0.115 per share declared by its board on June 9, 2026, payable June 30, 2026, to holders of record June 19, 2026. This is a routine capital return event; no other special-situation activity is disclosed. The filing includes only the dividend declaration and a press release. Watch for future dividend consistency or potential changes in payout policy.

HWH.brief: HWH International Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a $10M PIPE with Smart Dynamics Technology Ltd for 20M shares and warrants for up to 160M shares at $0.63; also a $500k stock sale to majority shareholder Alset Inc. at $2.00/share. The PIPE adds a Nasdaq compliance extension condition. Board/advisor not named. The warrant overhang is massive. Risk-arb: watch shareholder approval and Nasdaq listing compliance.

IPCXR.brief: Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. III filed a definitive proxy statement for its business combination with Air Water Ventures Limited. The SPAC's board unanimously approved the deal, recommending shareholders vote for it. Per the agreement, Inflection Point will merge into PubCo, which will then acquire Air Water via a second merger. The combined company will issue up to 232.5M ordinary shares, 66k Series A preferred shares, and 90M warrants. A pre-closing PIPE of $4M via IPF and a $20M August PIPE with IPF and others are part of the financing. Shareholder vote and regulatory approvals are required; risk-arb focuses on closing conditions and potential redemptions.

JSPRW.brief: Jasper Therapeutics disclosed on June 3, 2026 that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the minimum $1.00 bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) for 30 consecutive business days. The company has 180 calendar days, until November 30, 2026, to regain compliance by having its common stock close at $1.00 or more for ten consecutive business days. If non-compliant by that date, it may seek a second 180-day period if it meets other standards and implements a reverse stock split. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The stock (JSPR) and warrants (JSPRW) continue trading. Watch for potential reverse stock split or further delisting risk.

KYNB.brief: The 8-K reports Kyntra Bio's receipt of the final $4.0 million holdback from AstraZeneca, completing the sale of its China operations. On August 29, 2025, Kyntra sold its China business via FibroGen International (Hong Kong) Ltd. for total consideration of ~$220 million ($85M enterprise value + ~$135M net cash), with $210M paid at closing. The remaining $10M was held back for adjustments and indemnity; the $6M adjustment holdback was received in November 2025. No indemnity claims were made. The transaction closed and all payments received. Watch for Kyntra's reinvestment of proceeds.

TMSWW.brief: Teamshares Inc filed this 8-K to report completion of its business combination with Live Oak Acquisition Corp. V, a SPAC. Legacy Teamshares merged with SPAC subsidiaries, becoming the surviving public company, renamed Teamshares Inc. The filing notes the Merger Agreement was signed Nov 14, 2025, amended twice, and closed June 18, 2026. It references the Proxy Statement/Prospectus for terms but does not disclose price, premium, or specific deal mechanics here. The registrant was the target entity; this is a de-SPAC going-private transaction. What to watch: post-merger stock and warrant trading under new symbols TMS and TMSWW.

NOVTU.brief: Novanta Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into an Equity Purchase Agreement on June 8, 2026, to acquire all limited liability company interests of Runway Buyer from Runway Midco for $1.2B cash at closing, plus a $250M milestone payment due by Jan 8, 2027. The acquisition vehicle is Novanta Medical Technologies Corp. Closing conditions include HSR Act clearance, no Material Adverse Effect, and customary reps/ warranties. The deal will be financed through cash and existing credit facilities. Watch for antitrust timeline and integration risk at closing.

IPDN.brief: Professional Diversity Network, Inc. (Seller) filed an 8-K on July 6, 2026, reporting its entry into a Stock Purchase Agreement on July 2, 2026, to sell 100% of the shares of its wholly owned subsidiaries NAPW, Inc. and IAW, Inc. to MEB Holding LLC (Buyer) for an aggregate purchase price of $150,000. The board approved the transaction on July 2, with economic effect from June 30, 2026. The transaction closed on July 3, 2026, upon payment. The sale was exempt from registration under Section 4(a)(2)/Rule 506(b). Given the negligible price and immediate close, this appears to be a de minimis divestiture; watch for any subsequent related-party disclosures or potential wind-down of the sold entities.

QRED-RI.brief: QuasarEdge Acquisition Corp (QRED), a SPAC, filed an 8-K reporting entry into a definitive merger agreement with Robseek Intelligence Inc. to effect a business combination. The transaction involves a SPAC merger and acquisition merger, with QRED merging into its wholly owned Purchaser subsidiary, followed by Merger Sub merging into Robseek. Existing QRED ordinary shares and rights will convert into Purchaser equivalents. No deal price, premium, or valuation is disclosed. Shareholder vote and regulatory reviews are pending. Watch for shareholder redemption risk and SEC review of the proxy statement.

SLNHP.brief: Soluna Holdings, Inc filed an 8-K reporting entry into a joint venture agreement for Project Kati 2, a multi-phase data center development in Texas. Soluna's subsidiary contributed property, a purchase agreement, and ~$3.5M in expenses, with a further ~$19M capital commitment and up to $2M for expenses. After recovering contributions and a 14% IRR plus $100K/MW, distributions are 50/50 with Metrobloks. This is a strategic operating JV, not a special situation. Watch for development milestones and capital calls.

SOBR.brief: SOBR Safe, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement with the SEC on June 9, 2026, under the Securities Act of 1933. The filing does not disclose a specific transaction, target, or terms such as price per share, premium, or implied value. It includes the company's insider trading policy, adopted May 31, 2024, for directors, officers, and employees with access to material nonpublic information. The filing references various equity instruments, warrants, and PIPE offerings from prior periods. No board recommendation, advisor, or expected closing date is provided. The filing's structure suggests it may relate to a business combination or exchange offer, but details are absent. What to watch: look for a subsequent definitive agreement or merger proxy that specifies the counterparty and deal terms; the risk-arb angle is unclear until terms emerge.

BREZR.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE on June 10, 2026, to delist Breeze Acquisition Corp. II (CIK 0002095443) under Rule 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(2). The exchange cites the security's failure to maintain listing standards. The delisting is effective June 10, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The action removes the SPAC's units, shares, or warrants from Nasdaq, potentially accelerating a liquidation or merger timeline. Overhang risks and trading illiquidity follow. Watch for a subsequent going-private transaction or dissolution vote; the risk-arb angle focuses on remaining trust value per share versus current trading price.

SMCIP.brief: Super Micro Computer, Inc. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a $1.25B common stock offering (price to be determined; June 9, 2026 close $40.64). Concurrently, it is offering 75M depositary shares representing mandatory convertible preferred stock and plans a $2B ATM program. No board recommendation or advisor named. Proceeds will fund component purchases to fulfill ~$39B in AI server orders and for general corporate purposes. Closings are not conditioned on each other. Watch for pricing, overallotment option exercise, and impact from the concurrent financings on stock price.

ABEV.brief: Ambev S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting share repurchase transactions during May 2026, including open-market purchases via Santander totaling R$ 48–50 million per day at prices from R$ 15.73 to R$ 16.87 per share. The company also acquired shares directly through delivery of restricted shares and option exercises. The filing satisfies Brazilian CVM Instruction #44/2021 disclosure requirements. As a foreign private issuer, this equates to a US issuer's periodic share buyback report. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is stated. Watch for ongoing buyback pace and any acceleration; no arbitrage angle exists as this is a routine capital return activity.

BMGL.brief: Basel Medical Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing a 1-for-12 reverse share split effective June 22, 2026, to regain compliance with Nasdaq's minimum $1 bid price rule. No shareholder approval was required under British Virgin Islands law. The share count will reduce from 18,785,750 to ~1,565,480; fractional shares will be rounded up. The stock will trade under the same symbol BMGL with a new CUSIP. This is a capital structure adjustment, not a special situation, intended to avoid delisting. Watch for Nasdaq compliance confirmation post-split.

CNCKW.brief: Coincheck Group issued a Form 6-K announcing the completion of KDDI Corporation's strategic investment. KDDI purchased 28,536,516 newly issued shares at $2.28 per share for $65 million aggregate cash, representing 14.9% ownership. The investment closed pursuant to a May 12, 2026 Subscription Agreement. KDDI receives registration rights and the right to nominate one non-executive director at the September 2026 AGM. Concurrently, Coincheck's Japanese subsidiary entered a business alliance with KDDI for digital asset market expansion in Japan. The filing is a completion announcement of a previously disclosed private investment in public equity (PIPE). Watch for operational synergies and board changes.

ENRDW.brief: Einride AB (foreign private issuer) files Form 6-K to announce the closing of its business combination with SPAC Legato Merger Corp. III, approved by Legato shareholders on June 4, 2026. Einride's ADSs and warrants begin trading on Nasdaq under ENRD and ENRDW as of June 10, 2026. The transaction valued Einride at a pre-money equity value of approximately $1.35 billion and included an oversubscribed $113 million PIPE financing supported by EQT Ventures and a West Coast asset manager. TD Cowen acted as lead financial and capital markets advisor to Einride; Graubard Miller served as legal counsel to Legato. Post-combination, the combined entity is publicly traded. Watch for liquidity and stock price performance post-listing, as well as any lockup expiration effects.

AVAL.company: Grupo Aval Acciones Y Valores S.A.
AVAL.brief: Grupo Aval Acciones y Valores S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting that on June 9, 2026, the Contributing Shareholders (Grupo Aval, Banco de Bogotá, Banco de Occidente, and Banco Popular) transferred all of their 52.80% common shares in Corficolombiana via in-kind contributions at book value to Corporación Financiera Centroamericana (Ficentro). The transfer is an intra-group reorganization within the Aval Financial Conglomerate. Banco Popular remains the consolidating entity via a voting agreement. No premium, price, or outside consideration is specified. This is an internal restructuring, not a market-facing special situation. Watch for any subsequent regulatory or minority shareholder actions.

IRS.brief: IRSA Inversiones y Representaciones filed a Form 6-K reporting its acquisition of Los Gallegos shopping mall in Mar del Plata, Argentina. IRSA acquired 100% of the entities owning the asset for a purchase price of USD 13.5 million, with USD 12.5 million paid at closing and USD 1 million retained as collateral. The mall has about 10,500 sqm of gross leasable area, 49 retail stores, 14 stands, two movie theaters, a department store, and 115 parking spaces. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The acquisition expands IRSA's portfolio to 18 malls and over 400,000 sqm of GLA. Watch for integration risk and potential synergies in the Argentine commercial real estate market.

KNOP.brief: KNOT Offshore Partners LP filed a Form 6-K on June 10, 2026, updating its vessel acquisition schedule under its omnibus agreement with sponsor Knutsen NYK. The Conflicts Committee declined to pursue shuttle tankers Frida Knutsen and Sindre Knutsen due to insufficient charters, while negotiations continue for Hedda Knutsen. No terms, price, or premium were disclosed. The update is a routine report on potential related-party acquisitions, not a definitive deal. No advisor or recommendation was mentioned. Watch for future definitive agreements or charter developments.

KT.brief: KT Corp filed a Form 6-K disclosing its mid-term growth strategy and future business plan to transform into an AX Platform Company. The plan includes strengthening telecom competitiveness, expanding cybersecurity, and investing KRW 6 trillion over 5 years in AX infrastructure (AI data center and submarine cable) plus KRW 12 trillion over 3 years in cybersecurity, IT, and network. No specific price per share, premium, or deal terms are provided. The timeline is 2026-2031. The filing is a voluntary strategic update, not a definitive transaction. No recommendation or advisor is named.

RY.brief: Royal Bank of Canada (RY on TSX/NYSE) filed a 6-K announcing a normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 45 million common shares (~3.24% of shares outstanding as of May 29, 2026) for cancellation, approved by the TSX and OSFI. Purchases may start June 12, 2026, and run until June 11, 2027, at prevailing market prices through TSX, NYSE, and other exchanges, with daily TSX purchases capped at 886,352 shares (25% of average daily volume). An automatic share purchase plan will be used via RBC Dominion Securities. The prior bid concluding June 11, 2026, repurchased 19,168,210 shares at ~C$215.85 average price. This is a straightforward open-market share buyback program for capital management and shareholder return, not a tender offer. Watch for execution pace and market conditions affecting repurchase timing.

ZOOZW.brief: ZOOZ Strategy Ltd. announced a board-authorized review of strategic alternatives to complement its bitcoin treasury strategy. No specific transaction, price, or advisor is disclosed; the review may include business combinations, acquisitions, investments, partnerships, or capital markets initiatives. Management reaffirms strong conviction in bitcoin and states the review is intended to supplement, not replace, its bitcoin focus. No timetable or decision guarantee is provided. The filing is a Form 6-K press release. What to watch: any subsequent announcement of a specific deal or partnership that could shift the company's asset mix or capital allocation.

WRB-PH.brief: W. R. Berkley Corp filed an 8-K reporting the passing of founder and Executive Chairman William R. Berkley. The Board immediately appointed President/CEO W. Robert Berkley Jr. as Chairman. This is a leadership succession event triggered by death, not a forced departure. No financial terms, price, premium, or deal mechanics are involved. The filing is an obituary-style disclosure of a natural transition. Watch for any secondary strategic impact; no risk-arb angle.

BHR-PD.brief: Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that indirect subsidiaries entered into an Agreement of Purchase and Sale to sell The Ritz-Carlton Sarasota, Hotel Yountville, and Bardessono Hotel and Spa for $437.5 million in cash. The sale is expected to close in 20–35 days, subject to customary conditions. No premium, board recommendation, or advisor is mentioned. The transaction is a straightforward asset sale; watch for regulatory or third-party consents and the risk of a failed closing.

DAICW.brief: CID Holdco, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 10, 2026, announcing that after a strategic review it entered two non-binding letters of intent: a convertible preferred stock investment of up to $5.0 million and a sale of a portion of its operating business for about $6.0 million in cash plus assumption of up to $3.0 million in liabilities. The investor may also provide additional funding for value-creating initiatives. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The transactions remain non-binding and subject to definitive agreements, stockholder, lender, Nasdaq, and regulatory approvals. Watch for definitive agreement execution and risk of deal failure.

CE.brief: New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the 4.777% Senior Notes Due 2026 guaranteed by Celanese Corp. The entire class of securities was called for redemption on June 25, 2026, with sufficient funds deposited and made available to holders. The delisting will be effective at the opening of business on July 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine administrative notice following full redemption; no structural or contest dynamics apply. The risk-arb angle is nil — all securities have been retired and paid.

FITB-PK.brief: Fifth Third Bancorp filed Form 25 to voluntarily delist multiple securities from Nasdaq, including common stock and several series of preferred and depositary shares. The delisting is effective June 11, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(c) for voluntary withdrawal. No board recommendation, advisor, or shareholder vote was mentioned. The move appears to be a strategic decision to exit public listing, likely to reduce regulatory costs or restructure capital. No deal premium, price, or implied value is stated. Watch for whether the company seeks to deregister under Section 12(g) or pursue a going-private transaction; risk-arb angle is limited as this is a delisting, not a buyout.

FACWW.brief: Factorial Energy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of a business combination between Cartesian Growth Corp III (SPAC) and Factorial Inc., whereby CGC domesticated to Delaware, merged Merger Sub into Factorial, and Factorial became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the registrant. The transaction closed on June 5, 2026. No per-share price, premium, or implied value is stated; the filing notes the merger agreement dates December 17, 2025, with two amendments. Board recommendation is not detailed. Structurally, the SPAC de-SPAC'd with a domestication and reverse merger, creating a publicly listed operating company. Watch for post-close warrant conversions and lockup expirations; risk-arb focuses on redemption levels and trading liquidity.

FIGR.brief: Figure Technology Solutions filed an 8-K announcing a definitive merger agreement to acquire Kiavi, Inc. for $532.4 million in cash. Under the agreement, a wholly owned subsidiary will merge with Kiavi, with Kiavi surviving as a subsidiary. Consideration is all cash, subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt, and working capital. Conditions include HSR antitrust clearance, supermajority Kiavi equityholder approval, and a pre-closing restructuring. The filing does not name advisors or a board recommendation. Risk-arb watchers should monitor antitrust review and the concurrent joint venture sale.

GAVA.brief: Grayscale Avalanche Staking ETF (GAVA) on Form 8-K disclosed implementing Delayed Delivery Orders to manage digital asset liquidity constraints. The sponsor, Grayscale Investments Sponsors, LLC, acting as Liquidity Engager, may arrange these redemption orders with participating Liquidity Providers to address adverse liquidity events when the Liquidity Sleeve is exhausted. No specific terms like price, premium, or dates are provided. This event modifies trust mechanics for NAV-based redemptions under staking constraints. It is not a traditional special situation. Per the filing, this is a structural liquidity measure and not an acquisition, divestiture, or other standard category. The role is issuer for the trust's operational adjustment.

JJSF.brief: J&J Snack Foods filed an 8-K regarding Amendment No. 2 to its credit agreement, extending the revolving facility maturity to 2031, increasing capacity by up to $200M (or EBITDA-based amount), and raising leverage ratio covenants. No acquisition, divestiture, or special situation event is announced; this is a routine credit facility amendment. The filing includes departure of a named officer (item 5.02), but no forced departure details are provided, and terms/advisor are absent. Watch for future acquisition use of the expanded facility.

KEYYU.brief: Keystone Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO of 28,750,000 units at $10.00/unit ($287.5M gross), plus a private placement of 8,468,750 warrants at $1.00 each ($8.47M gross) to sponsor and underwriters. Net proceeds of $288.2M are placed in trust. This is a SPAC IPO—a blank-check company—following the standard SPAC trust structure. No business combination target is announced yet. Investors should watch for de-SPAC announcement within 18-24 months; risk includes dilution from warrants and sponsor promote.

CUBWU.brief: Lionheart Holdings (a SPAC) filed an 8-K disclosing it will enter into Non-Redemption Agreements with unaffiliated shareholders to reduce redemptions at the June 15, 2026 extraordinary general meeting, which seeks to extend the deadline to complete a business combination to March 20, 2027. In exchange for not redeeming Class A ordinary shares, the Sponsor will transfer Class B ordinary shares (expected ratio of one Class B per five Non-Redeemed Shares) post-business combination. The filing does not specify price, premium, or advisor. This is an ad hoc redemption reduction mechanism, not a standard special situation, so category is Other.

MBNKO.brief: Medallion Financial Corp. filed an 8-K announcing preliminary results from its 2026 annual meeting. The activist ZimCal Asset Management LLC sought to replace three director nominees, but shareholders re-elected the company's slate with approximately 78% of votes cast (activist nominees received ~19%, down from ~22% in 2024). This marks ZimCal's third consecutive defeated proxy contest. No deal terms were provided. Watch for potential ongoing activist pressure or board-level engagement given repeated campaigns.

RIBBR.brief: Ribbon Acquisition Corp., a blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting a $125,000 extension payment deposited into its trust account to extend the deadline to consummate a business combination from June 15, 2026 to July 15, 2026. Additionally, Nasdaq notified the company it regained compliance with Listing Rule 5250(f) following payment of past-due fees. The filing is a routine compliance update and trust extension, not a special-situation event. No deal terms, premium, or recommendation. Watch for subsequent announcements on a potential business combination.

VISM.brief: Visium Technologies filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its incubation arrangement with ConnexUS AI, including a proposed 100% equity acquisition under an LOI and a related services SOW. The Board terminated the agreements on June 8, 2026, after determining the incubation failed to achieve objectives. All ATHENA IP remains with ConnexUS; no ownership passed. The parties signed a mutual release extinguishing obligations, with only confidentiality and IP confirmation surviving. What to watch: whether Visium will pursue another AI acquisition or focus on its core RAG/agentic initiatives.

VNRX.brief: VolitionRx Ltd filed an 8-K to disclose a securities purchase agreement for a registered direct offering of 2,960,000 shares of common stock and warrants to purchase up to 1,480,000 shares of common stock, priced at $1.55 per share and accompanying warrant. Net proceeds are approximately $4.1 million. The warrants have a five-year term, exercise price of $1.55, and include blocker provisions at 4.99%/9.99% beneficial ownership. Pre-funded warrants were authorized but not sold. This is a capital-raise event with no strategic special situation such as M&A, activist campaign, or restructuring. Watch for dilution impact and stock price reaction post-offering.

BYNO.brief: SPAC byNordic Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting a monthly extension of its business combination deadline from June 12 to July 12, 2026, funded by a $17,470 deposit into the trust account. This is a routine mechanical extension previously authorized by shareholders on August 6, 2025, allowing up to twelve additional months through August 12, 2026. No target, price, or premium terms are involved. The board approved the deposit in advance. The trust is collateral for the SPAC structure; actual share redemptions absent a deal. Watch for whether a definitive merger agreement is announced before the July 12 deadline, else risk liquidation.

ALYAF.brief: Alithya Group filed a Form 6-K attaching an amending agreement to its credit facility, which references the sale of multiple Datum entities (Datum Consulting Group, LLC, Datum Consulting Group Australia Pty Limited, Datum Consulting Group S.R.L., Datum Solutions DOO (Serbia), DCG Spain, S.L.U., DCG UK Limited, Datum Cybertech India Pvt Ltd., Datum Solutions DOO (Montenegro), and 9467-8778 Quebec Inc.) to Medivra Holdings LLC, effective as of March 31, 2026. No financial terms, premium, or board recommendation are disclosed. The filing is a credit agreement amendment to reflect the divestiture, which was previously consented to by lenders. Watch for closing conditions and potential regulatory approvals; risk-arb hinges on final consideration and any undisclosed earnouts.

USAS.brief: Americas Gold & Silver Corp. filed a Form 6-K disclosing the closing of two previously announced agreements to settle delivery obligations. Under the first, the company issued 7,956,696 shares at US$5.57 per share to Sprott Mining Inc. to terminate a remaining obligation to deliver 592,000 ounces of silver. Under the second, it delivered 5,000 ounces of gold and issued 2,652,532 shares at US$5.86 per share to International Royalty Corporation (affiliate of Royal Gold, Inc.) to settle a remaining obligation to deliver 8,861 ounces of gold. The filing is a routine operational update on debt-for-equity swaps rather than a transformative special situation.

AVCRF.brief: Avricore Health Inc. filed a Form 6-K furnishing several exhibits: a notice of annual general meeting (AGM) set for June 18, 2026, with record dates, a management information circular, proxy materials, and a news release announcing a $1.25 million financing. No specific terms (price per share, premium) are provided for the financing; it appears to be a routine capital raise combined with standard AGM documentation. No board recommendation or advisor is named for the financing. The filing is entirely procedural: an AGM notice and a general financing announcement, not a transformative or negotiated special situation. What to watch: whether the financing terms are disclosed in subsequent filings; otherwise, no risk-arb angle applies.

HELP.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by Cybin Inc. (Helus Pharma) announcing participation in a conference (H.C. Wainwright Neuro Perspectives). It is a routine investor event announcement, not a special situation. The document is a news release about a fireside chat; no transaction, activist, restructuring, or strategic change is disclosed. It is a foreign private issuer report under the 1934 Act, equivalent to a US press release. No special-situation category applies.

EBON.brief: Ebang International Holdings Inc. filed a Form 6-K on June 11, 2026, announcing its subsidiary won a bid for industrial land in Inner Mongolia, China, for an amorphous and nanocrystalline new materials project. Terms include the land acquisition price, which is not disclosed. The board recommends the project as a strategic expansion into renewable energy and new materials. Structural notes involve the subsidiary's bid and plans for production facilities compliant with U.S. DOE standards. Watch for further details on land cost, financing, and timeline; no arbitrage angle given real asset nature.

FER.brief: Ferrovial N.V. filed a Form 6-K reporting transactions under a share repurchase program initiated December 15, 2025. For the period May 25-June 26, 2026, the company repurchased shares on multiple venues including XMAD, CEUX, and US trading platforms at weighted average prices around €58-€60 per share, totaling 5,072,474 shares for €295.2 million since program inception. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The program is a buyback returning capital to shareholders. Watch for cumulative repurchase progress relative to announced authorization and any impact on share count and EPS.

FCHL.brief: Fitness Champs Holdings filed a 6-K announcing an EGM on June 29, 2026, to vote on increasing authorized share capital from US$500,000 to US$23,000,000 via a massive increase in Class A shares (from 177.8M to 10.2B) while keeping Class B and preferred shares unchanged. This is a structural capital change, likely to facilitate future capital returns or acquisitions. No price, premium, or advisor details; the board recommends approval. The mechanics involve amending the memorandum and articles. Watch for shareholder approval and subsequent use of the authorized shares—potential dilution or capital return event.

TGS.company: GAS TRANSPORTER OF THE SOUTH INC
TGS.brief: Transportadora de Gas del Sur S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting the execution of commercial agreements for its Integrated NGLs Project. Under Argentine law, this is a material fact disclosure; the US equivalent would be a Form 6-K. The project involves construction of pipelines, a processing plant, fractionation plant, storage and marine terminal with an estimated total investment of US$3 billion. Counterparties include YPF, Pluspetrol and Chevron. The filing is a routine project update, not a special situation. No deal terms are stated. Watch for construction milestones and regulatory approvals under Argentina's RIGI regime.

ISOU.brief: IsoEnergy Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Toro Energy Limited via a scheme of arrangement under Australian law. Toro shareholders received 0.036 IsoEnergy common shares per Toro share; approximately 4,359,568 ISO Shares were issued. The deal was approved by Toro shareholders on June 9, 2026, and by the Federal Court of Australia on June 15, 2026, becoming effective June 16, 2026. Toro shares were suspended from ASX trading and will be delisted. IsoEnergy's CEO commented on strategic benefits of the Wiluna Uranium Project. Watch for integration updates and uranium market conditions affecting combined portfolio.

MTEKW.brief: Maris-Tech Ltd. filed a Form 6-K on June 11, 2026, disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq conditional compliance determination regarding the minimum stockholders' equity requirement. The company had been notified of non-compliance on May 22, 2026, and subsequently demonstrated compliance via a Form 6-K filed June 10, 2026. Nasdaq will monitor compliance, and failure to maintain it at the interim financials filing for the six months ending June 30, 2026, may lead to delisting proceedings. No price per share, premium, or other deal terms are stated. Watch for potential delisting if equity falls below $2.5 million threshold.

SGHC.brief: Super Group (SGHC) Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 11, 2026, announcing a regular cash dividend of $0.05 per share declared by its board on June 9, 2026. The dividend is payable on June 30, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 23, 2026. Combined with a prior Q1 distribution of $0.05 per share paid on March 30, 2026, total year-to-date dividends are $0.10 per share. CEO Neal Menashe cited strong cash generation and disciplined execution. The event is a routine capital return with no premium, advisory, or structural complexities. Watch for future dividend patterns as a potential signal of ongoing shareholder return policy.

TRLEF.brief: Trillion Energy International Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting that it advanced a US$250,000 earn-in payment toward its earn-in obligations and announced attendance at a conference. The filing does not describe a specific transaction with terms such as price per share, premium, or board recommendation. It appears to be a routine update on contractual earn-in progress and corporate events, not a conventional special situation. As a foreign private issuer report, it maps to no US equivalent special situation category. What to watch: no material event triggering a special situation classification.

VRXAW.brief: This Form 6-K filed by Veraxa Biotech Holding AG announces the completion of its business combination with Voyager Acquisition Corp., a SPAC sponsored by Cantor Fitzgerald and others. The transaction closed on June 10, 2026, after shareholder approvals in March and February 2026. Veraxa merged into Veraxa Biotech AG, listing shares and warrants on Nasdaq under VRXA and VRXAW. The filing discloses a $27.5 million secured note and a $50 million share purchase agreement to fund pipeline development. No deal value, premium, or advisor is stated. The de-SPAC creates a publicly traded biopharma focused on bispecific TCEs and ADCs. Watch for post-merger trading volume and execution of clinical milestones.

WFF.brief: WF Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K with a notice of extraordinary general meeting to approve a share restructuring. Proposals include increasing authorized share capital from $50,000 to $25 billion (100 trillion ordinary shares), creating a new Class A share with 100 votes each convertible 1:1 into ordinary shares, and redesignating 10 trillion ordinary shares into Class A shares held by key shareholders. The special resolution adopts amended articles. This is a capital structure change to consolidate control, not an acquisition, tender, or other special situation. Watch for shareholder approval at the July 10, 2026 meeting; no price/per-share terms or advisor named.

ADIL.brief: Adial Pharmaceuticals acquired Azora Therapeutics via a two-step merger under an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 11, 2026. Adial issued 437,474 shares of common stock and 12,930.617 shares of Series A convertible preferred stock (each convertible into 1,000 common shares) to Azora stockholders. The transaction is structured as a tax-free reorganization. No per-share price, premium, or implied value is stated. The board's recommendation and advisors are not named. The merger closed immediately upon filing, with no regulatory clock mentioned. Watch for conversion mechanics of the preferred stock and any overhang from the newly issued shares; risk-arb is moot as deal is closed.

AMAL.brief: Amalgamated Financial Corp. filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized an additional $31.4 million in share repurchases, bringing total authorization to $40 million. The program has no expiration date and allows purchases in open market, privately negotiated, or block trades at management's discretion. No specific price, premium, or timeline was disclosed. The existing program had $8.6 million remaining. The issuer is returning capital to shareholders via open-market buybacks. Watch for pace of repurchases and any suspension or extension.

COPL-WT.brief: Copley Acquisition Corp, a SPAC, filed an 8-K on June 10, 2026, announcing a Business Combination Agreement with Ignite Proteomics, LLC. The deal involves a Cayman-to-Delaware re-domicile, followed by a merger where SPAC Merger Sub merges into Copley, and Company Merger Sub merges into Ignite, with Pubco as the combined publicly traded entity. No specific price per share, premium, or advisors are disclosed. The filing notes that post-merger, all outstanding SPAC securities will be cancelled in exchange for Pubco securities. The transaction is subject to SPAC shareholder approval and regulatory conditions. Monitor the redemptions by SPAC shareholders and the probability of deal completion; risk-arb will focus on the redemption threshold and trust per-share value.

IVFH.brief: Innovative Food Holdings filed an 8-K reporting that Sam Klepfish exercised a previously disclosed right to become a Board Observer on May 20, 2026, after ceasing to be a director, triggered by his 3%+ share ownership. The Board Observer attends meetings in a non-voting capacity with access to materials, subject to confidentiality. No deal terms or financial consideration are involved. This is a governance arrangement, not a special situation transaction.

MH.brief: McGraw Hill, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its board approved a $50.0 million common stock repurchase plan on June 2, 2026, disclosed alongside fiscal Q4 and full-year results ended March 31, 2026. The buyback authorizes repurchases from time to time with no specific price, premium, or expiration terms set forth. The board authorized the plan; no external advisors or transaction mechanics are detailed. As a capital return to shareholders via open-market repurchases, this is a discretionary capital-allocation action. Watch for periodic repurchase disclosures and any impact on share float or EPS accretion.

MACIU.brief: Melar Acquisition Corp. I filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of a $1.5M promissory note to its sponsor, Melar Acquisition Sponsor I LLC, for working capital advances. The note bears 17.5% interest, matures upon business combination or liquidation, and permits conversion of up to $1.5M unpaid principal into warrants at $1.00 per warrant, identical to those issued in its IPO. This is a typical SPAC working capital bridge loan to fund operations until a de-SPAC transaction. The filing is exempt under Section 4(a)(2). However, the note itself is not a definitive agreement for a business combination; the sole event is the SPAC's financing. Therefore, this filing does not represent a special situation on its own.

PNRG.brief: PrimeEnergy Resources Corp filed an 8-K (Items 5.07, 8.01) on June 11, 2026, reporting annual meeting voting results and a board-authorized share repurchase program. The board authorized repurchase of up to 300,000 shares via open-market or privately negotiated transactions, at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and cash availability. No premium, expiration, or material terms were disclosed beyond authorization. The repurchase is a capital-return signal, reducing float and returning cash to shareholders. Watch for actual execution pace and any subsequent tender offers, as the open-market nature limits typical risk-arb precision.

PROP.brief: Prairie Operating Co. received a Nasdaq notice on July 2, 2026, indicating its common stock closing bid price has been below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, failing Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has a 180-day grace period until December 29, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a $1.00 closing bid for ten consecutive days. An additional 180-day period may be available if it meets other listing standards. If the stock trades at or below $0.10 for ten straight days, Nasdaq will immediately delist. Prairie is evaluating options, but no assurance of compliance exists.

SHOTU.brief: RMG ML Sports Holdings, a blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its $200M initial public offering of 20M units at $10.00/unit on June 11, 2026. Each unit comprises one Class A ordinary share ($0.0001 par) and one right to receive one-eighth of a Class A share upon an initial business combination. The IPO was underwritten by Santander US Capital Markets LLC under a June 9 underwriting agreement. The filing also includes a rights agreement and letter agreement with the sponsor. This is a standard SPAC IPO event executed to raise trust capital for a future de-SPAC merger. Investors should monitor the sponsor's progress in identifying and announcing a target business combination within the typical 18-24 month window.

STTK.brief: Shattuck Labs filed an 8-K disclosing an underwritten public offering of 10,879,376 shares at $4.00/share plus pre-funded warrants for 7,870,624 shares at $3.9999/share, with a full underwriter option for 2,812,500 additional shares exercised. Proceeds go to the issuer. No premium, recommendation, or advisor named; the offering was conducted under an effective shelf registration. The warrants are exercisable immediately with a 4.99%-19.99% beneficial ownership blocker. Expected close is June 11, 2026. Watch for dilution impact and potential share price drift post-closing.

SPKLW.brief: Spark I Acquisition Corp (SPKL), a blank-check company, filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement with ZincFive, Inc., a nickel-zinc battery solutions provider. The business combination involves SPKL domesticating from Cayman Islands to Delaware and merging through two merger subs. The transaction was unanimously approved by all relevant boards.
