No specific price per share, premium, or deal value is stated in the filing. The closing is expected in H2 2026, subject to SPKL shareholder approval and customary conditions. The SPAC will be renamed ZincFive upon close. Watch for shareholder vote and redemptions given SPAC mechanics.

VSEEW.brief: VSee Health, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a note financing. On June 8, 2026, it entered a securities purchase agreement with an institutional investor, issuing an 8% OID secured promissory note with an aggregate principal amount of $271,739.13 (including $21,739.13 OID). The note carries an 18% interest rate, matures December 8, 2026, and is prepayable with a 10% fee; mandatory repayment occurs upon proceeds from an equity line with the same holder. The note is secured by certain assets under a security agreement. No equity or M&A implications; this is a high-cost debt arrangement typical for distressed liquidity. Watch for default acceleration triggers.

VENU.brief: Venu Holding Corp filed an 8-K reporting the sale of approximately 9.5 acres of land underlying its Ford Amphitheater to O'Neil Roth Ford, LLC for $49.7 million, plus an adjacent 1.1-acre undeveloped parcel for $10.00. The buyer is co-owned by a shareholder and the CEO/Chairman, making it a related-party transaction. The sale is part of a sale-leaseback strategy to generate liquidity, with the purchase price set at an independent appraisal. No specific premium, close date beyond closing, or board recommendation is detailed. Watch for the leaseback terms and any related-party governance scrutiny.

WDC.brief: Western Digital Corp filed an 8-K Item 8.01 disclosing privately negotiated exchange agreements with institutional investors. The company will exchange 1,038,681 shares of Sandisk Corp common stock it holds for an equal-value number of shares of its own common stock, based on three-day volume-weighted average prices from June 16-18, 2026. The exchange closes June 22, 2026. This is an in-kind swap reducing Western Digital's Sandisk stake, not a conventional M&A or capital-return event; no premium, break fee, or board recommendation is cited. Watch for any subsequent 13D/13G filings from investors adjusting holdings post-closing.

XERS.brief: Xeris Biopharma filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated exchange agreements with noteholders to exchange ~$23M (69%) of its 8.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 for cash (principal amount) plus common stock valued using a 21-day VWAP. $10.5M of notes will remain outstanding. Closing expected ~July 15, 2026. The exchange reduces debt overhang and is a form of capital return via liability management; shares issued will be unregistered under Section 4(a)(2). Watch for the VWAP calculation and remaining noteholder dynamics.

YHNAU.brief: YHN Acquisition I Ltd disclosed in an 8-K that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 10, 2026, for failing to meet the 400 total holders requirement under Listing Rule 5450(a)(2). The notice has no immediate delisting effect; trading continues under YHNAU, YHNA, and YHNAR. The company has 45 calendar days to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant up to 180 additional calendar days. Alternatives include appealing to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel or transferring to the Nasdaq Capital Market. Watch for the compliance plan submission and potential shareholder base expansion efforts.

BKHAU.brief: Black Hawk Acquisition Corp (SPAC) files amended S-4/A to register securities in connection with its proposed merger with Vesicor Therapeutics, Inc. The transaction implies a post-combination equity value tied to trust proceeds; no specific per-share price, premium, or break fee is stated. The SPAC board recommends the deal; no financial advisor is named. Upon closing, Black Hawk will domesticate from Cayman Islands to Delaware. The merger requires SEC effectiveness and shareholder approval. The risk-arb angle: monitor trust value erosion, redemption dynamics, and regulatory clearance timeline.

BCARU.company: D. Boral ARC Acquisition I Corp.
BCARU.brief: On July 7, 2026, D. Boral ARC Acquisition I Corp. (BCAR), a SPAC, filed a Form 8-K disclosing the scheduling of an Extraordinary General Meeting for July 29, 2026, to vote on its previously-announced business combination with Exascale Labs Inc. The target, Exascale, is an AI infrastructure company. Under the January 2026 merger agreement, Exascale will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of a new public company (PubCo) expected to trade as XLAB on Nasdaq. The board recommends approval (inferred), with legal counsel Loeb & Loeb LLP. The filing confirms record date of July 6, 2026, and virtual meeting instructions. Key watch items: shareholder vote outcome and potential redemptions, which could pressure trust account balances and require minimum cash conditions for closing.

BFLY.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the warrants of Butterfly Network, Inc., each exercisable for one share of Class A common stock at $11.50/share, due to abnormally low selling prices under Section 802.01D of the Listed Company Manual. Trading was suspended on January 14, 2026, and the company did not appeal, making delisting effective February 13, 2026. This is a regulatory removal, not a merger; the common stock remains listed. The delisting eliminates warrant overhang and liquidity. Watch for any potential impact on common shares or alternative venue trading.

VIST.brief: Vista Energy filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of its acquisition of a 25.1% non-operating working interest in the Bandurria Sur block and a 35.0% interest in the Bajo del Toro block from Equinor. The purchase price was $712 million, composed of $387 million upfront cash (including tax gross-ups) and 6,223,220 ADSs representing Vista series A shares, plus $131 million in adjustments for debt, working capital, and leakages. The acquired blocks are consolidated as of May 1, 2026. Vista will update 2026-2028 guidance on May 11, 2026. No break fee or regulatory timeline was disclosed; watch for integration updates and production guidance.

ZH.brief: Zhihu Inc. filed a Form 6-K attaching Next Day Disclosure Returns under Hong Kong listing rules, reporting multiple open-market share repurchases for cancellation between April and June 2026. The repurchases totaled approximately 5.6 million shares at prices ranging from about USD 0.94 to USD 1.28 per share, representing a capital return to shareholders. As an NYSE and HKEX-listed foreign private issuer, Zhihu is reducing its share count, increasing EPS. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is stated. The shares repurchased are not yet cancelled. Watch for the pace of future buybacks and impact on liquidity.

CARE.brief: Carter Bankshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completed sale of its membership interest in Bearing Insurance Group, LLC to an unaffiliated third party, effective May 1, 2026. The estimated pre-tax gain is approximately $35.8 million, to be recognized in Q2 2026. No specific price per share, premium, or break fee was disclosed. The board did not issue a recommendation; the transaction closed on announcement. The filing provides no structural mechanics beyond the gain estimate. The closed nature means no regulatory clock remains; watch for subsequent earnings reports to confirm actual gain and potential redeployment of proceeds.

FRMEP.brief: First Merchants Corporation filed an 8-K disclosing board approval of a stock repurchase program for up to 3,125,000 shares (~5% of outstanding) with a $100M aggregate cap. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, or Rule 10b5-1 plans at management's discretion, with no obligation to buy. The program replaces a March 2025 plan. No premium, price terms, or advisors are named. The mechanics allow flexible execution under Rule 10b-18. Watch share buyback pace and market conditions; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a discretionary capital return, not a fixed tender.

LAZ.brief: Lazard, Inc. filed an 8-K to disclose its agreement to acquire all issued shares of Campbell Lutyens Holdings Limited, a private capital advisor. Total consideration is up to $660 million: $460 million initial (primarily in Lazard common stock at $46.50/share), $115 million deferred at two-year anniversary, and up to $85 million earn-out based on 2030 revenue targets. The transaction is expected to close with 100% ownership. Board supports the deal. Risk-arb focus: stock election mechanics, regulatory clearances, and earn-out achievability.

MIDDV.brief: The Middleby Corporation filed an 8-K on July 6, 2026, reporting the completion of its spin-off of Midera Food Processing, Inc. into a new publicly traded company. 100% of Midera's common stock was distributed to Middleby stockholders on July 5, 2026. The separation was governed by a Separation and Distribution Agreement, Tax Matters Agreement, and Employee Matters Agreement. Middleby retained no ownership interest in Midera, which holds the food processing business. The deal was non-cash and tax-free to stockholders. Watch for Midera's first-day trading performance and post-spin operating updates; arbitrage focuses on relative valuation vs. Middleby's remaining business.

PB.brief: Prosperity Bancshares filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Stellar Bancorp effective July 1, 2026. Each Stellar share was converted into 0.3803 Prosperity shares plus $11.36 cash, implying a total per-share consideration valued using a $71.44 reference price for Prosperity stock. Stellar stock options were cashed out based on the per-share merger consideration value. The merger was structured as a tax-free reorganization with Prosperity as the surviving entity, followed by a bank merger into Prosperity Bank. The deal closed with no disclosed regulatory hurdles; future updates may address integration milestones and accretion.

RICK.brief: RCI Hospitality Holdings disclosed on Form 8-K that it received a Nasdaq notice on May 20, 2026 for noncompliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) due to failure to file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026. The company has until July 20, 2026 to file or submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days from the due date (November 16, 2026) to regain compliance. The notice has no immediate effect on the listing of RICK on the Nasdaq Global Market. Watch for the filing of the 10-Q or acceptance of a compliance plan; risk-arb impact is minimal as this is a procedural delisting notice.

STRD.brief: Strategy Inc filed an 8-K disclosing it repurchased ~$1.50B principal of its 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for ~$1.38B cash, a ~$120M discount funded by cash, ATM proceeds or bitcoin sales. Settlement expected May 19, 2026, after which the repurchased notes will be cancelled, leaving ~$1.50B outstanding. The repurchase reduces debt overhang and is a capital-return event for equity holders. No board recommendation or advisor is named. What to watch: final repurchase price depends on MSTR stock VWAP during a measurement period; risk-arb angle is small as this is a liability management exercise, not an equity tender.

VSECU.brief: VSE Corp filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, reporting the May 5, 2026 closing of its acquisition of Precision Aviation Group (PAG) from GenNx360 Capital Partners. The deal was structured via a stock purchase agreement with rollover and cash purchasing subsidiaries. Terms such as price per share and premium were not disclosed in the filing; consideration appears to be cash and stock. Board recommendation is implicit as the company executed the acquisition. The closing triggers entry into exchange/redemption and registration rights agreements. Watch for integration execution and any post-closing adjustments.

PGIM.brief: PGIM Private Credit Fund launched a tender offer to repurchase up to 537,259 shares, representing ~5% of outstanding shares as of March 31, 2026, across Class I, D, and S shares. Pricing is at net asset value (NAV) per share, with no fixed premium disclosed. The board has not publicly recommended acceptance; PGIM Investments LLC serves as adviser. The offer is a standard issuer self-tender for a non-traded BDC, with no collateral or overhang. Regulatory clock runs from filing. Watch for the proration level and any NAV adjustments, as the spread to NAV is the key risk-arb metric.

AUDC.brief: AudioCodes Ltd. (issuer) disclosed the adoption of a Rule 10b5-1 stock trading plan to repurchase its ordinary shares, enabling buybacks during blackout periods. Terms include price, volume, and timing constraints under Rule 10b-18, with an independent broker executing trades per plan parameters. No specific price, share count, or premium stated. The plan allows capital returns without insider trading restrictions. Watch for actual repurchase volumes and impact on share price.

CIGI.brief: Colliers International Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the completion of its previously announced acquisition of Ayesa Engineering S.A.U., the engineering division of Ayesa Inversiones S.L.U. The transaction closed on May 27, 2026. Terms were not disclosed in this filing. Ayesa Engineering's leadership retained significant equity under Colliers' partnership model. Alantra acted as financial advisor and Uría Menéndez as legal advisor to Colliers. The acquisition adds over 3,300 professionals, expanding Colliers' Engineering segment to 23 countries. As a closed deal, the risk-arb angle is moot; focus shifts to integration and potential earn-out performance linked to retained equity.

LTM.brief: LATAM Airlines Group S.A. filed a Form 6-K with the SEC, reporting a Material Fact under Chilean securities law. The Board of Directors approved summoning an Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting on August 3, 2026, to consider a share repurchase program affecting up to 5% of subscribed and paid shares, with a maximum duration of five years. The program aims to acquire shares, with pricing to be set by the Board. The filing is the US equivalent of a material fact notice for a share buyback proposal. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and subsequent open-market acquisition execution.

BLIN.brief: Bridgeline Digital disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has 180 calendar days, until July 28, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a closing bid price of $1.00 or more for at least ten consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, it may qualify for an additional 180-day cure period, subject to meeting market value and initial listing standards. No board recommendation or advisor was referenced. The notice does not trigger immediate delisting. Watch for potential reverse stock split or other curative actions if the stock remains below $1.

SKY.brief: Champion Homes, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 26, 2026, announcing its Q4 FY2026 earnings and a $50 million increase to its existing share repurchase program, refreshing the authorization to $150 million. The filing covers Items 2.02 and 8.01; no M&A, activist, or other special-situation trigger is present. The repurchase program increase is a discretionary capital-return action. The company's board approved the expansion; no advisor or timeline is stated. The purchases will occur in the open market or via other methods. Watch for the pace of buybacks and potential EPS accretion as the company executes the program.

MEVOW.company: M Evo Global Acquisition Corp II

MWYN.brief: Marwynn Holdings disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice on January 29, 2026, for failing to maintain the $1.00 minimum bid price per share under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), based on 30 consecutive business days of closing bid prices through January 28, 2026. The Nasdaq Capital Market listing is unaffected currently. The company has a 180-day grace period until July 28, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at $1.00 or more for at least ten consecutive business days. Failure may lead to an additional grace period or delisting. Management is evaluating options to cure the bid-price deficiency, making share price trends and any reverse-split proposals the key risk-arb focus.

MLAAU.brief: Mountain Lake Acquisition Corp. II (MLAC II), a blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting that exclusivity under its non-binding letter of intent with Terra Quantum AG has expired. The SPAC may now pursue discussions with other targets. No definitive terms, price, or timeline have been disclosed. The filing signals a potential shift in business combination efforts. Investors should monitor for a new target announcement or liquidation if no deal is reached before the deadline.

NCRA.brief: Nocera, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a letter of intent to acquire up to 9.99% of INERGX Energy Optimisation Ltd. The proposed transaction may involve cash and stock consideration with a VWAP collar, but no specific price or valuation is given. The LOI is non-binding pending due diligence, definitive agreement, and approvals. This is a preliminary minority stake acquisition with an uncertain structure and timeline, making it a low-conviction special situation.

OLB.brief: OLB Group disclosed on an 8-K that Nasdaq notified it on January 29, 2026 of non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)) for 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day grace period to July 28, 2026 to regain compliance by closing at $1.00 or more for 10 consecutive business days. Failure could lead to delisting, subject to appeal. No board action or advisor was named. The stock continues trading during the cure period. Watch for reverse-split potential or other bid-boosting measures; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a listing standards issue.

QUBT.brief: Quantum Computing Inc. (QUBT) filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of NHanced Semiconductors, Inc. via a Stock Purchase Agreement. Aggregate consideration comprises $68.1M cash (subject to adjustments) plus ~$5.0M in QUBT stock, with $20.0M of the cash held in escrow contingent on NHanced's 2027-2028 revenue thresholds. Additional earnout of up to $72.0M based on revenue and EBITDA targets is payable in cash or stock. No price per share or premium was disclosed. The board recommended the transaction; advisors are not named. Watch for QUBT's dilution and integration risk; earnout mechanics and potential stock issuance create complexity.

LEDS.brief: SemiLEDs Corp disclosed on Form 8-K that on January 30, 2026, it received a Nasdaq notice for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(b)(1) due to stockholders' equity falling below the required $2.5 million minimum, and it also fails the alternatives of market value of listed securities or net income from continuing operations. The company has 45 calendar days to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant an extension of up to 180 calendar days from the notice date. No board recommendation or advisor was named. What to watch: the company's ability to submit a viable plan and whether it can secure additional equity or restructure to regain compliance within the extension period.

BSBR.brief: Banco Santander (Brasil) S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting the minutes of an extraordinary general meeting held June 30, 2026, where shareholders approved the merger of Esfera Fidelidade S.A. into the company. The meeting had a 95.02% voting capital quorum. The merger was approved under Brazilian law, based on an appraisal report by PricewaterhouseCoopers Auditores Independentes. The registrant is the absorbing entity in a corporate restructuring, effectively the seller of Esfera's separate identity. This is a routine internal merger, not a transformative special situation. No financial terms, premium, or board recommendation were disclosed. The filing is a foreign private issuer report of a non-US corporate action.

BRAG.brief: Bragg Gaming Group announced a further restructuring on July 9, 2026, via a Form 6-K filing (equivalent to a U.S. current report). The plan includes a ~19% workforce reduction and ~$6M in incremental annualized cost savings, adding to ~$4.5M from a prior restructuring, for total ~$10.5M savings. One-time costs of ~$0.6M are expected in H2 2026. CEO Matev Mazij emphasized focus on core iGaming content/tech and cash generation. No deal terms, premium, or consideration are involved. Watch for execution risk and potential future M&A given management's reference to market consolidation.

ELPW.brief: Elong Power Holding filed a Form 6-K reporting a debt settlement and a private placement of Class B ordinary shares with an insider. The company issued 33,881 shares to Gracedan Co., Limited at $0.974 per share to settle a $33,000 loan from CEO Xiaodan Liu, and separately sold 66,119 Class B shares at the same price to the same buyer for cash. The transactions were exempt under Section 4(a)(2) and Regulation S. The aggregate implied value is ~$97,000. No board recommendation or advisor mentioned. Watch for insider control dilution and compliance with Nasdaq listing standards given reliance on private exemptions.

ICON.brief: Icon Energy Corp. filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release with a routine commercial update on vessel chartering. The company disclosed that its panamax vessel Alfa's floating-rate charter was converted to a fixed rate of $18,000/day for June-December 2026, adding ~$3.7M to minimum contracted revenue. Two other vessels remain on index-linked charters. No acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, tender offer, going-private, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC transaction, or abrupt management change is reported. This is an ordinary operational update, not a special situation.

MRM.brief: Medirom Healthcare Technologies Inc. filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failure to timely file its Form 20-F for FY2025, risking delisting. The company has 60 days (until July 27, 2026) to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days (to November 11, 2026) to regain compliance by filing the overdue 20-F. If the plan is rejected, an appeal to a Hearings Panel is available. This is a non-US filer (Japan) reporting a NASDAQ listing standard violation. Watch for the company's ability to file its 20-F within the grace period to avoid suspension/delisting.

VNTG.brief: Vantage Corp (Singapore) filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of its $1.0 million share repurchase program. Under the program, the company repurchased 1,076,610 Class A ordinary shares at an aggregate net cost of US$997,897.72, executed in open-market purchases from November 5, 2025 to June 30, 2026. The program was authorized and previously announced; no specific per-share price or premium is disclosed. CEO Andresian D Rozario stated the repurchases reflect management's belief that shares are undervalued. As a completed open-market buyback with no tender or fixed-price terms, this is a routine capital return. What to watch: future buyback authorizations or alternative capital allocation strategies.

TECH.brief: Bio-Techne Corp filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement with Merck KGaA and its wholly-owned subsidiary EMD Holdings NewCo, Inc. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Bio-Techne, with Bio-Techne surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent. Shareholders will receive $73.00 per share in cash, valuing the equity at an implied enterprise value based on the cash consideration. The board has approved the merger, declared it advisable, and recommends shareholder approval. No premium percentage or break fee was stated. The transaction is subject to shareholder approval and customary closing conditions. Watch for shareholder vote timeline and potential competing bids.

CDW.brief: CDW Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a $1 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, effective immediately. The increase is incremental to approximately $484 million remaining under the program as of March 31, 2026. Purchases may occur in open market or private transactions based on market conditions; no specific price, premium, or timeline is set. The board authorized the increase without naming an advisor. The program does not obligate CDW to repurchase any shares and may be modified or suspended. The filing is a routine capital return disclosure with no M&A or special-situation catalyst; watch for ongoing buyback execution.

RAL.brief: Ralliant Corp filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, disclosing entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $100 million of its common stock under a pre-existing Board-authorized buyback. The repurchase price is based on the average daily Rule 10b-18 volume-weighted average price during the program term, with settlement expected by end of Q2 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The ASR is a cash-settled structure reducing share count. Watch for final settlement shares repurchased and any impact on EPS; no arbitrage angle exists as this is an issuer capital return.

BKKT-WT.brief: Bakkt, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Bakkt Opco Holdings, LLC, was allotted 47,500,000 warrants from Transchem Ltd. in a preferential allotment, paying $9,409,784 (25% of total). This is an investment rather than a transformative special situation. There is no M&A, activist, or strategic review. The warrants entitle the holder to acquire Transchem ordinary shares. The filing does not specify a board recommendation or advisor, and there is no regulatory clock or arbitrage angle. The event is a routine equity investment disclosure, not a special situation.

BCE.brief: BCE Inc. filed a Form 6-K disclosing two public debt offerings by its subsidiary Bell Canada: C$1.6B in Canadian MTN Debentures (Series M-69 and M-70) and US$650M in US senior notes. Proceeds will be used to repurchase/refinance existing indebtedness via concurrent tender offers. The MTN debentures are not registered under the U.S. Securities Act. The closings are not conditioned on each other. This is a routine refinancing, not a transformative special situation. What to watch: completion of the tender offers and any early redemption calls.

GENI.brief: Genius Sports Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the consummation of its acquisition of Zeal Ltd (Legend) via its wholly-owned subsidiary Lion Bidco (Guernsey) Limited. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026, with consideration comprising $800 million in cash (subject to customary adjustments) and 10,088,781 ordinary shares of Genius (issued at a volume-weighted average share price). The Seller Parties are subject to a six-month lock-up on the stock consideration. Additional earn-out consideration may be payable in cash or shares at Genius's election. The acquisition was financed with a new $825 million term loan and $220 million revolving credit facility, secured by substantially all assets. The filing confirms an earn-out and orderly sell-down structure; the regulatory clock has expired as the deal is closed. Watch for integration risk and earn-out triggers.

OBE.brief: Obsidian Energy Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of its acquisition of Belly River light oil assets in Wilson Creek, Willesden Green. Total consideration was approximately $98 million inclusive of adjustments, funded via credit facilities. The deal adds ~2,500 boe/d production (76% liquids) and 35 net sections of land. Board/management recommended the transaction; no advisors named. Guidance raised for 2026. Watch for integration execution and drilling program results in 2027.

SKM.brief: SK Telecom Co., Ltd., a South Korean telecom, filed a Form 6-K disclosing board approval on June 29, 2026, to acquire 642 new shares of affiliate SK hynix NAND Product Solutions Corp. (SKHNPS) for approximately 397.1 billion Korean won (about $257 million). The stake after acquisition will be 0.62%. The purchase is for cash, intended to facilitate synergies with SKT's AI business, with a scheduled acquisition date of July 23, 2026. The transaction is a minority equity investment in a semiconductor affiliate, not a control acquisition. Watch for exchange-rate adjustments and completion timing.

TRI.brief: Thomson Reuters filed a Form 6-K reporting Q1 2026 results and disclosed a completed $605 million return of capital transaction on May 4 via a share consolidation reducing share count by 6.5 million shares, representing a 10% annualized dividend increase to $2.62 announced in February, and $262 million in open-market repurchases under a $600 million program authorized Feb 25, 2026. The board maintains its 2026 outlook. No tender offer or share buyback by issuer was launched in this filing; the filing simply reports executed capital returns. The transaction reduced float by roughly 4% based on prior outstanding shares. Watch for continued execution of the remaining repurchase authorization and potential further capital return initiatives.

ATPC.brief: Agape ATP Corp filed an 8-K reporting it regained compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid price rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)) after its stock closed at or above $1.00 for 10+ consecutive days. Previously, the company faced delisting due to a low stock price (closing bid $0.10 or less). On March 10, 2026, Nasdaq's Hearings Advisor confirmed compliance, cancelling the March 17 delisting hearing. The stock将继续 listed on Nasdaq. No shareholder action, deal terms, or activist involvement. Key watch: sustained bid price and any future compliance risk.

CCXIW.brief: Churchill Capital Corp XI (SPAC) filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement to acquire Agility Robotics, Inc. via a reverse merger. The SPAC will domesticate from Cayman to Delaware and change its name to Agility Robotics. Terms such as implied equity value, price per share, and premium are not disclosed in this excerpt. The transaction requires shareholder approvals and customary closing conditions. No board recommendation or advisors are named here. The SPAC's trust cash plus a PIPE investment (defined but not quantified) will fund the deal. Watch for shareholder vote timeline and redemption risk; the risk-arb angle hinges on trust value per share and PIPE backstop.

IRHOU.brief: Iron Horse Acquisition II Corp. filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, disclosing an amendment to its merger agreement with Electra Vehicles, Inc. The amendment revises the Aggregate Merger Consideration, Conversion Ratio, earnout shares, and bridge financing treatment. As a SPAC, IRHO is the issuer filer in a de-SPAC business combination. The board has not disclosed a recommendation change; the registration statement on Form S-4 was filed May 15. No price per share or premium is stated. Watch for shareholder vote timing and redemption risk; the risk-arb angle focuses on IRHO's trust value and potential redemptions ahead of close.

MCFT.brief: MasterCraft Boat Holdings filed an 8-K to report its acquisition of Marine Products Corporation via a two-step merger. Under the terms, Marine Products shareholders received 0.232 MasterCraft shares plus $2.43 cash per share, implying a mixed cash-and-stock consideration. The exact price per share and premium are not stated in this excerpt. The board of both companies approved the transaction; no advisors are named. The deal closed on May 15, 2026, the filing date. Watch for post-close integration updates and potential dissenting shareholder litigation.

PTEN.brief: Patterson-UTI Energy filed an 8-K regarding a $500M offering of 6.050% Senior Notes due 2036 via an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, and Scotia Capital. Proceeds will redeem its 3.95% Senior Notes due 2028 (approx. $482.5M outstanding) plus general corporate purposes. The conditional redemption notice requires debt offering completion by June 4, 2026; close expected May 19, 2026. This is a refinancing transaction, not a return of capital to shareholders; thus categorized as Capital Returns with medium confidence as it primarily redeems existing debt.

IIIV.brief: i3 Verticals, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its board approved a new $100 million share repurchase program for its Class A common stock, replacing a prior program that was fully expended. Repurchases may be made in open market, privately negotiated transactions, or under Rule 10b5-1 plans through May 11, 2027, subject to market conditions, liquidity, contractual restrictions, and securities law compliance. The program is discretionary and may be suspended or terminated at any time. Watch for actual repurchase activity and impact on diluted share count; no premium or fixed price is specified.

EXE.brief: Expand Energy Corp filed Form 15 to terminate registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act for its Class A, B, and C Warrants, as of February 18, 2026. The filing indicates zero holders of record for each warrant class at certification, meeting the conditions for deregistration. The company, formerly Chesapeake Energy, is an Oklahoma-based oil and gas producer. The move suspends reporting obligations under Sections 13(a) and 15(d) for the warrants. No transaction terms, board recommendation, or advisor are mentioned. Watch for any remaining common stock reporting requirements and potential delisting implications.

LSBCF.brief: LakeShore Biopharma Co., Ltd. filed a Form 15-12G to terminate its SEC registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act. The filer certified that its ordinary shares, par value $0.0002 per share, were held by a single holder of record as of the filing date, meeting the threshold for deregistration under Rule 12g-4(a)(1). The action effectively suspends the company's duty to file periodic reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). No board recommendation or advisor was named. The deregistration eliminates public disclosure and reporting obligations, reducing administrative costs. Investors should note that deregistration may reduce liquidity and transparency; the stock may trade over-the-counter with limited information.

LANV.brief: The NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Lanvin Group Holdings Ltd's redeemable warrants (exercisable for one ordinary share at $11.50) due to an abnormally low selling price under Section 802.01D of the Listed Company Manual. Trading was suspended June 25, 2026, and the company declined to appeal by July 6, 2026. Delisting becomes effective July 17, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. No merger or tender offer is involved; the action solely removes the warrant class from exchange listing and SEC registration. Watch for potential further corporate actions or OTC trading of the warrants.

FSUN.brief: FirstSun Capital Bancorp filed an 8-K to report that its subsidiary Sunflower Bank completed the sale of approximately $336 million in performing municipal loans to an unaffiliated third party. This sale was part of the balance sheet repositioning announced in connection with FirstSun's acquisition of First Foundation Inc., which closed on April 1, 2026. Proceeds will be used to pay down high-cost deposits acquired from First Foundation. The filing updates progress on post-acquisition integration, not a new special situation event. No deal terms are disclosed.

FBLG.brief: FibroBiologics, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a delisting notice from Nasdaq for continued failure to meet the $35M market value of listed securities (MVLS) rule. The company received an initial MVLS deficiency notice on August 4, 2025, with a compliance deadline of February 2, 2026, and was formally notified on February 3, 2026, that non-compliance is an additional basis for delisting, to be considered alongside an existing bid price deficiency by the Nasdaq Hearings Panel. The board has sought shareholder approval for a reverse stock split (1:5 to 1:30) to regain compliance. Trading continues pending the Panel's decision. What to watch: the Panel's ruling and shareholder vote outcome.

GIPRW.brief: Generation Income Properties, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a property sale by its indirect wholly owned subsidiary GIPFL 10002 N Dale Mabry, LLC. The asset was a Starbucks-occupied net lease retail property in Tampa, Florida, sold to Andrew Livingstone (later assigned to 10002 N Dale Mabry, LLC) for $2,964,000, yielding net proceeds of $1,959,170 after prorations. No board recommendation or advisor is named; the sale appears independent. Pro forma financials adjust for the disposition as if closed January 1, 2025. Watch for use of proceeds and any further portfolio streamlining.

IRAB-WT.brief: Iris Acquisition Corp II (SPAC) filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its non-binding letter of intent for a business combination with Freedom Metals Corporation, originally announced on March 9, 2026. No deal terms, price per share, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The termination is effective May 13, 2026, per the registrant's notification to the target. As a blank-check company, this leaves the SPAC without a pending transaction, triggering a search for an alternative target or potential liquidation if it fails to complete a deal within its charter deadline. The risk-arb angle is nil; the focus shifts to the SPAC's remaining timeline and whether it can secure a new merger partner before dissolution.

LEXX.brief: Lexaria Bioscience Corp. received a Nasdaq Bid Price Deficiency Notice on February 4, 2026, for non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has 180 calendar days, until August 3, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a closing bid price of at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, it may qualify for a second 180-day period by meeting other listing standards and indicating intent to cure via a reverse stock split. Failure could lead to delisting and a hearing appeal. Watch for management's remediation strategy and stock price trajectory. No advisor or board recommendation noted.

MGRX.brief: Mangoceuticals, Inc. (MGRX) disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the minimum $1.00 bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as its common stock closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. The company has 180 calendar days, until August 3, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a closing bid price of $1.00 or more for at least 10 consecutive business days. Nasdaq's notice does not immediately impact listing or trading. The company plans to monitor the bid price and consider options to resolve the deficiency. No board recommendation or advisor was named. No specific terms (price, consideration) were stated, as this is a listing compliance notification rather than a transactional event. The risk-arb angle is minimal; focus on potential reverse stock split or other remedial actions to maintain listing.

RNXT.brief: RenovoRx disclosed it received a Nasdaq notice on July 1, 2026 granting an additional 180-day period (through December 28, 2026) to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule. The company had failed to meet the requirement by the original June 30, 2026 deadline. Compliance may be achieved if the closing bid price is at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days during the second compliance period. Failure to regain compliance by December 28, 2026 will result in delisting, subject to appeal. The disclosure follows Rule 8-K Item 3.01. Watch for bid-price movements and any reverse-split plan.

TPST.brief: Tempest Therapeutics filed an 8-K disclosing a warrant exercise inducement letter with a holder of existing warrants originally issued in November 2025. The holder exercised 1,172,414 shares at a reduced price of $1.73 per share (from $3.50) for ~$2M gross proceeds. As consideration, the company issued a new warrant to purchase up to 2,344,828 shares at $1.73, exercisable upon stockholder approval and expiring May 29, 2028. H.C. Wainwright acted as placement agent, receiving a warrant for 82,069 shares at $2.1625. A resale registration statement will be filed. This is a capital-raising transaction with inducement warrants, not a traditional special situation—no change of control, merger, activist campaign, or restructuring. What to watch: stockholder approval for new warrant exercisability and registration effectiveness.

VTGN.brief: Vistagen Therapeutics filed an 8-K on April 2, 2026, disclosing non-compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2) following the April 1 resignation of board member Mary Rotunno, which reduced the audit committee from three to two members. Nasdaq listing is unaffected during the cure period, which expires at the earlier of the next annual meeting or one year from April 1, 2026 (or 180 days if the meeting occurs within 180 days). The board intends to regain compliance before expiration. No price, premium, or deal terms are involved. Watch for the timing of director appointments to restore audit committee size.

NWE.brief: NorthWestern Energy Group filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFM14A) regarding its all-stock merger with Black Hills Corporation, announced August 18, 2025. Under the agreement, NorthWestern shareholders will receive 0.98 Black Hills common shares for each NorthWestern share held. The combined company, to be renamed (Newco), will list on NYSE. Both boards recommend the deal; no advisor named. Special shareholder meetings are set for April 2, 2026, held virtually. Merger sub will merge into NorthWestern, making it a Black Hills subsidiary. No break fee or regulatory timeline specified. Watch for shareholder votes and any regulatory hurdles; the 0.98 ratio may shift with Black Hills stock price.

LMND.brief: NYSE American LLC filed a Form 25-NSE on February 9, 2026, to delist Lemonade, Inc.'s warrants (ticker: LMND) from the exchange, effective February 20, 2026. The delisting follows the warrants' conversion into other securities via operation of law, with trading suspended on February 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The warrants now only represent the right to receive an immediate cash payment per Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). The delisting removes the warrants' public market, creating a mandatory cash-out event for holders. Watch for the final cash payment terms and any residual claims; risk-arb focuses on valuation versus the cash-out price.

NTB.company: Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Ltd
NTB.brief: Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Ltd (the Company) filed a Form 6-K to report entry into a share purchase agreement with CIBC on May 27, 2026, to acquire CIBC's 91.67% stake in CIBC Caribbean Bank Limited. Consideration is a mix of 11,577,367 ordinary shares (exchange ratio 0.008008 per CIBC Caribbean share) plus cash of US$0.6918 per share—aggregate cash $1.091 billion. The board recommends the deal; no advisor named. A mandatory take-over bid for the remaining 8.33% minority at equivalent terms follows. Conditions include shareholder approval, regulatory consents, and NYSE listing. Watch minority take-up and regulatory timeline in Caribbean jurisdictions.

UK.brief: Ucommune International Ltd (Nasdaq: UK) filed a Form 6-K disclosing a securities purchase agreement dated May 6, 2026, under which it issued 150 Series A Convertible Preferred Shares at $10,000 per share to an institutional investor. Proceeds partially funded the purchase of NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU server equipment, which was leased to a QumulusAI subsidiary under a ~$1.3M, three-year lease with a purchase option, marking the company's entry into compute infrastructure. The filing includes a two-year lockup on equity issuances and a ban on variable rate transactions. The private placement exempt under Rule 506(b). This is a capital-raise and business-expansion disclosure, not a special situation. Watch for shareholder dilution upon conversion and lease performance.

SCWO.brief: 374Water Inc. disclosed two material events in an 8-K filed 2026-02-09. First, it entered Amendment No. 1 to a December 2025 Letter Agreement with Yaacov (Kobe) Nagar, providing for a Replacement Candidate to the board one year after the third mutually-agreed candidate's appointment, effective through that appointment. Second, board member James Vanderhider resigned immediately on 2026-02-04, creating an Audit Committee vacancy and triggering non-compliance with Nasdaq Rule 5605(c)(2)(A) requiring three members; the company intends to rely on the cure period. No other terms (stake, price) were stated. Note the board-advisor dynamic with Nagar and monitor Nasdaq compliance timeline for risk-arb implications.

AMC.brief: AMC Entertainment filed an 8-K announcing a registered direct offering of 95.25 million shares at $2.10 per share, raising ~$200M gross proceeds. The company will use net proceeds of ~$189M to redeem its $125.5M 6.125% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027, with the balance for general corporate purposes. Roth Capital Partners acted as placement agent, receiving a 5.5% cash fee. The offering closes June 24, 2026, and AMC agreed to a 45-day lock-up on new equity issuances. This is a capital-return event via debt redemption funded by equity issuance; monitor the redemption mechanics and any impact on the company's leverage profile.

SHFSW.brief: SHF Holdings disclosed on April 22, 2026 receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency letter for failing to maintain a minimum $1.00 bid price for 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day compliance period through October 19, 2026 to regain compliance by closing at $1.00+ for 10 consecutive days. A second 180-day extension may be available. The board intends to monitor prices and evaluate options, but delisting risk remains if unresolved. No advisor named. Key watchpoints: potential reverse stock split, trading dynamics, and any investor outreach to support the stock price.

SSACU.brief: SPACSphere Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) filed an 8-K disclosing a Business Combination Agreement with Mobilewalla Holdco, Inc. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge into Mobilewalla, making Mobilewalla a wholly-owned subsidiary of SPACSphere. The boards of both companies approved the transaction. Prior to closing, SPACSphere will convert its Class B shares into Class A shares and domesticate from the Cayman Islands to Delaware. No specific price per share or premium was stated. Advisors, break fee, and expected close date were not disclosed. The risk-arb angle is the typical SPAC timeline and potential shareholder redemptions.

UPXI.brief: Upexi, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a strategic partnership with Blueprint, an affiliate of Hivemind Capital Partners, to stake a portion of its Solana holdings via Blueprint's institutional-grade validator. No financial terms, stake percentages, or board recommendations are disclosed. The partnership is operational rather than transactional, involving treasury management and network support. This 8-K is furnished under Item 8.01, not filed, indicating no material transactional event. The filing lacks deal mechanics, premium, or close date. What to watch: any future disclosures on staking yields or changes in treasury strategy, but no immediate risk-arb angle.

VHCPU.company: Vine Hill Capital Investment Corp. II

BLDC.brief: Blockfusion Digital Infrastructure, Inc. filed Amendment No. 3 to its S-4 registration statement on June 30, 2026, relating to a business combination with Blockfusion USA, Inc. The merger consideration is not explicitly stated in this excerpt. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The transaction, structured as a merger under the Business Combination Agreement, requires SEC effectiveness and satisfaction of conditions. The registration statement also registers securities for the combined entity. Watch for the final proxy statement/prospectus with deal terms, shareholder vote, and regulatory clearance timeline.

APTOF.brief: Aptose Biosciences Inc., a Canadian biological products company, filed a Form 15-12G with the SEC to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective July 1, 2026. The filing indicates the company had only one holder of record of its common shares as of the certification date. Aptose relied on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and other provisions to suspend its duty to file reports. The action was signed by Chairman, President, and CEO William G. Rice. This deregistration likely follows a significant reduction in shareholder base, possibly after a going-private transaction or reverse stock split. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms were disclosed. Watch for potential SEC inquiries into the deregistration justification.

CAN.brief: Canaan Inc. filed Form 6-K reporting Nasdaq approval to transfer its ADS listing from the Nasdaq Global Market to the Nasdaq Capital Market, effective July 1, 2026, after receiving a minimum bid price deficiency notice on January 14, 2026. The company has applied for an additional 180-day compliance period to regain the $1.00 minimum closing bid price for 10 consecutive days. No price, premium, or advisor is named. The transfer is structural, not a sale or dissolution. Watch for Nasdaq's decision on the extension and the company's ability to execute a reverse stock split or other remedy.

NGEN.brief: NervGen Pharma Corp. filed a Form 6-K disclosing a Sales Agreement with Leerink Partners LLC to sell up to US$50 million of common shares through an at-the-market offering. The agreement allows for periodic placements at the issuer's discretion with parameters set per Placement Notice. This is a standby equity facility, not a transformative event. The filing is an ordinary equity shelf takedown arrangement, not a special situation like an acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring. What to watch: actual drawdowns and dilution impacts.

BYAH.company: Park Ha Biological Technology Co., Ltd.
BYAH.brief: This filing reports a strategic partnership announcement by Park Ha Biological Technology Co., Ltd., a foreign private issuer, regarding a joint development of an AI-driven ecosystem with Cloud Factory Technology Holdings. No financial terms, stake, or board recommendation are provided; the collaboration is non-binding and non-transactional. As a routine partnership disclosure without definitive terms or structural changes, it does not meet special-situation criteria. Filing on Form 6-K, equivalent to a US 8-K announcement. What to watch: any subsequent definitive agreements or material financial commitments that could trigger a reclassification.

SUZ.brief: Suzano S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of its acquisition of a 51% equity interest in FamPro Tissue Holdings B.V. (Arbex) from Kimberly-Clark Corporation. The total cash consideration was USD 1.3 billion, with the joint venture assuming approximately USD 1.0 billion in net debt. The transaction was first disclosed on June 5, 2025, and closed after conditions precedent were satisfied. Suzano holds controlling shareholder status with a defined governance structure including a joint venture agreement and ancillary service and IP agreements. The price is subject to customary adjustments. Watch for the integration of Arbex's operations and potential synergies in the tissue paper market.

ZCMD.brief: Zhongchao Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting held June 18, 2026. The meeting approved a massive increase in authorized share capital from US$20 million to US$10 billion, corresponding to a 500x increase in authorized shares, and authorized the board to implement one or more share consolidations with ratios between 2:1 and 250:1 over a three-year period. No specific transaction is announced—these structural amendments enable future flexibility. No price, premium, or advisor named. This is a governance filing, not a deal. Watch for subsequent board actions on consolidation or capital markets transactions.

RILYZ.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE to delist BRC Group Holdings, Inc. (formerly B. Riley Financial) 5.50% Senior Notes Due 2026, effective 2026-03-30. The delisting is pursuant to Rule 12d2-2(a)(1), indicating the notes are no longer traded on Nasdaq. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing triggers removal from exchange listing. The regulatory clock is immediate; trading in the notes ceased as of the effectiveness date. What to watch / risk-arb angle: Delisting may impair liquidity; noteholders should evaluate alternative trading venues or potential redemption terms.

FLYX-WT.brief: FlyExclusive Inc. filed an S-4/A registration statement with the SEC, amending its prior registration related to a business combination. The filing does not specify a new offer price, premium, or expected close date. The board has not yet issued a formal recommendation; no advisor is named. The S-4/A provides supplemental disclosures and financial statements for the combined entity. Structural notes include the ongoing transition from a SPAC (EG Acquisition Corp.) and the registration of shares underlying warrants and convertible instruments. The SEC review and shareholder vote timeline remain key catalysts. The risk-arb angle centers on regulatory clearance and any material changes to deal terms.

JACS-RI.brief: Jackson Acquisition Co II received a NYSE noncompliance notice on Feb 6, 2026, for failing to maintain the required minimum of 300 public stockholders under Section 802.01B. The blank-check company has 45 days to submit a business plan to NYSE demonstrating how it will regain compliance within 18 months. NYSE will then have 45 days to review the plan. No immediate impact on listing or trading, provided the plan is approved and other listing standards are met. Failure to comply or submit an acceptable plan may lead to suspension and delisting. Watch for the business plan submission in late March and NYSE's subsequent review; risk-arb focus on potential de-listing timeline and SPAC liquidation risk.

STAI.brief: ScanTech AI Systems received a delisting notice from Nasdaq on February 6, 2026, after a Hearing Panel denied its request to continue listing on the Nasdaq Global Market, citing violations of Listing Rules 5250(c)(1) and 5450(b)(2)(A) (periodic filing and market value of listed securities). Trading will be suspended at the open on February 10, 2026. The company has 15 days to appeal to the Nasdaq Listing and Hearing Review Council and intends to apply for quotation on the OTCQB Venture Market. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for any appeal filing and the timeline for OTCQB approval.

RIG.brief: Transocean Ltd. filed an 8-K disclosing its agreement with Equinor for semisubmersible rigs valued at over $1 billion in contract backlog across seven rig years, with a base day rate of $399,000 increasing above $400,000 at commencement. Additionally, Transocean is acquiring Valaris Limited in a stock-for-stock business combination, exchanging 15.235 shares per Valaris share. Closing is conditional on CFIUS clearance and HSR Act waiting period expiration; a June 29, 2026 CFIUS notice extended the review to 45 days. Watch for regulatory approvals and potential risk-arb spread on the Valaris combination.

IPW.brief: iPower Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an additional optional closing under its existing senior secured convertible note facility. The company entered into Amendment No. 1 to increase facility capacity by $2M and remove use-of-proceeds restrictions. The investor purchased $2M aggregate principal amount of Series A Notes at a 6% OID, with $1.88M net proceeds received. The note carries a fixed conversion price of $2.39 (120% of Nasdaq close on July 2, 2026). Series A Notes are convertible into common stock, with shares registered for resale. The filing details a structured capital raise via a convertible note facility, not a tender or buyback. Watch for dilution impact and conversion activity.

CONE.brief: Compass Sub North, Inc. filed Amendment No. 3 to Form S-4 in connection with the proposed mergers and asset sale involving Green Dot Corporation, CommerceOne Financial, and affiliates of Smith Ventures LLC. No specific deal terms (price, premium, close date) are disclosed in this filing. The registration statement covers securities to be issued in the merger, with a preliminary proxy statement/prospectus dated May 6, 2026. The board of directors of Green Dot recommends shareholders vote in favor of the transaction. Regulatory effectiveness under the Securities Act is pending. Risk-arb angle: watch for SEC effectiveness, shareholder vote timing, and any regulatory approvals.

GFS.brief: GlobalFoundries filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release from its 2026 Investor Day announcing its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, payable July 14, 2026 to holders of record June 24, 2026. The board also approved a new capital allocation framework targeting returning up to 50% of trailing twelve-month Non-IFRS adjusted free cash flow to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases. No financial advisor or specific repurchase program was disclosed. This is a non-event-driven capital return initiative, not tied to any special situation. Watch for future buyback execution and earnings trajectory to gauge sustainability.

GRABW.brief: Grab Holdings Ltd (Grab) filed a Form 6-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of 100% equity in U.S. digital financial services company Stash Financial, Inc. (Stash). At closing on July 1, 2026, Grab paid for a 50.1% stake; the remaining interest will be paid at fair market value over three years post-closing. Terms such as total price, premium, and advisor names are not disclosed. The transaction is now closed, with deferred payments tied to future valuations. Watch for any post-closing disputes over earn-out valuation or integration risks.

MDXH.brief: MDxHealth SA filed a Form 6-K disclosing a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price rule over 30 consecutive trading days. The company has a 180-day cure period until December 28, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at $1.00 or higher for 10 consecutive days, with a possible additional 180-day extension if other initial listing standards are met. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The company is evaluating actions but provides no assurance of compliance. What to watch: risk of delisting if bid price does not recover, which would impair capital raising and financial condition.

SFL.brief: SFL Corp Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting results of its 2026 Annual General Meeting held on May 11, 2026. The meeting re-elected directors, reappointed auditors, and approved board remuneration. A shareholder proposal to redesignate authorized shares as preference shares and authorize their issuance was voted against. No special situation event such as an acquisition, divestiture, tender offer, or restructuring is present; the filing is a routine corporate governance update. Foreign private issuer filing mapped to U.S. equivalent 8-K for shareholder meeting results.

VCIG.brief: VCI Global announced via Form 6-K that its subsidiary V Gallant entered a definitive Share Sale Agreement to acquire 70% (14,000 ordinary shares) of PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia for $65,000, payable in V Gallant consideration shares (60M Class A shares with 1 vote each and 5M Class B shares with 20 votes each). The deal is contingent on V Gallant completing a NASDAQ listing within 12 months; otherwise, either party may rescind. A rescission right exists for material breach within 12 months post-completion. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for NASDAQ listing progress and regulatory approvals.

ABPO.brief: Abpro Holdings disclosed on May 28, 2026, that the Nasdaq Listing and Hearing Review Council reaffirmed the Panel's decision to delist the company's securities for failing to meet the minimum equity standard under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1) by a February 16, 2026 deadline. Nasdaq is expected to file a Form 25 to effect the delisting and deregister the securities under Section 12(b). Trading already moved to the OTC Pink Market on February 23, 2026, for common stock (ABP) and warrants (ABPWW). No board recommendation or advisor was named. Key risks include limited liquidity, reduced transparency, and no assurance of market maker support on OTC Pink.

KIDZW.brief: Classover Holdings filed an 8-K announcing a ChEF Purchase Agreement with Chardan Capital Markets LLC, under which the Company may sell up to $100 million of newly issued Class B common stock at a 4% discount to the volume-weighted average price. The Company controls timing and amount, subject to conditions including an effective registration statement. The corresponding Registration Rights Agreement provides for liquidated damages if filing deadlines are missed. This at-the-market equity facility is classified as a capital-return transaction due to its equity issuance structure under a committed facility. Watch for regulatory effectiveness and stock overhang.

LOCL.brief: Local Bounti disclosed an NYSE delisting notice received Feb. 5, 2026, for failing the minimum market capitalization standard ($50M avg over 30 trading days and stockholders' equity <$50M). The company has 45 days to submit a cure plan; if accepted, it gets up to 9 months to regain compliance. No stated premium, price per share, or board recommendation. Stock continues trading during the cure period. Key watch items: plan submission timing, NYSE acceptance, and any equity or strategic alternatives to boost market cap.

SSKN.brief: STRATA Skin Sciences, Inc. filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, effective March 2, 2026. The company certified it had 157 holders of record of its common stock. The filing relies on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and other provisions to suspend its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). No board recommendation or advisor was named. This deregistration removes public reporting obligations, reducing transparency; watch for potential liquidity or delisting risks as the company reduces its public footprint.

SVAQW.brief: Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (SVAQ), a Cayman Islands blank-check company, filed an 8-K on June 23, 2026, announcing a definitive Business Combination Agreement dated June 17, 2026, to acquire EigenQ, Inc. via a merger. Merger Sub will merge into EigenQ, making EigenQ a wholly-owned subsidiary of SVAQ. The boards of both parties approved the transaction. SVAQ will domesticate as a Delaware corporation prior to closing. No deal price, stake, premium, or advisor disclosed. Watch for SVAQ shareholder vote, redemptions, and regulatory approvals; risk-arb centers on deal spread and potential Nasdaq listing for combined entity.

BTAFF.brief: British American Tobacco p.l.c. filed a Form 6-K reporting share repurchases from May 26-29, 2026, as part of its ongoing buyback programme announced March 18, 2024. The issuer purchased 471,544 ordinary shares at a volume-weighted average price of approximately 4,738 pence per share. Shares will be cancelled, reducing issued capital to ~2.168 billion shares. No premium or tender offer terms are stated. This is an open-market buyback, not a tender offer. Watch for continued execution pace and any updates to the buyback programme announcement.

BNT.brief: Brookfield Wealth Solutions Ltd. filed a Form 6-K furnishing a management information circular for a court-approved plan of arrangement to simplify corporate structure with Brookfield Corporation, combining into one publicly traded company, Brookfield Corporation Ltd. The transaction requires shareholder approval from both entities. No specific price per share, premium, or consideration terms are stated in this excerpt. The board recommends the transaction; advisors are not named. The deal involves a structural merger via plan of arrangement, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and court sanction; risk-arb focuses on approval likelihood and timing.

CHKP.brief: On May 11, 2026, Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing its board authorized a $2.0 billion expansion of its ongoing share repurchase program. As of March 31, 2026, the company had ~104 million shares outstanding and has repurchased ~230 million shares for ~$17.4 billion since program inception. Shares may be repurchased through open-market or private transactions, and the company may enter a Rule 10b5-1 plan. The program has no fixed number of shares, can be suspended or discontinued, and will be funded from working capital. Watch for potential tender offers or accelerated buyback execution.

MICC.brief: This Form 6-K reports the results of Magnum Ice Cream Co N.V.'s Annual General Meeting held on May 7, 2026, where all proposals were passed, including adoption of financial statements, director remuneration, reappointment of directors, and board authorizations. The filing is a routine corporate governance update with no special-situation event such as an acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring. The document is a standard AGM outcome notice under Dutch law, filed as a foreign private issuer report. No deal terms, strategic changes, or unusual actions are present.

XP.brief:
XP Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting a cash dividend of US$0.20/share payable June 18, 2026 (record June 10, 2026), aggregating ~R$500M, and a new share repurchase program authorizing up to R$1.0B (USD equivalent) of Class A common shares from May 19, 2026 to May 20, 2027. Purchases may be made under Rule 10b-18/10b5-1 safe harbors via an appointed broker; the program may be modified or discontinued at any time. This is a capital-return event, funded from existing cash, without a fixed commitment for any specific share number.

What to watch: execution pace of buybacks and any expansion/suspension of the program based on market conditions.

EXPE.brief: Expedia Group filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results and declaring a $0.48/share quarterly dividend ($0.48 annualized, payable June 18, 2026 to holders of record May 28, 2026). Additionally, the board authorized a $5 billion share repurchase program, complementing $700M in buybacks during Q1. The filing highlights strong operational performance (13% gross bookings growth, 15% revenue growth, 83% Adj. EBITDA increase). No advisor or premium is applicable, as this is a capital-return event. The mechanics involve a regular dividend and open-market repurchases. Watch for execution pace of the buyback and any impact on EPS.

LNAI.brief: Lunai Bioworks filed an 8-K/A (Amendment No. 1) on May 11, 2026, supplementing Item 3.01 of its original May 1 filing. The amendment discloses an April 28, 2026 Nasdaq staff determination that Lunai remains non-compliant with the $35 million market value of listed securities (MVLS) requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(2) after the grace period expired April 27. This adds to the existing bid-price deficiency under Rule 5550(a)(2). A hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel was held March 26. The company previously solicited shareholder votes for proposals at a special meeting, now concluded. The stock trades on Nasdaq under LNAI. Watch for the Panel's decision and potential delisting.

RPC.brief: Ridgepost Capital, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of all equity interests of Stellus Capital Management, LLC for $125M cash plus 11,191,149 Ridgepost LLC units and 579,096 shares of its Class A Common Stock. The units are exchangeable into Class A Common Stock on a one-for-one basis, and shares are subject to staggered lock-up restrictions: one-third on the first anniversary, two-thirds on the second, and full on the third. The transaction is governed by a February 4, 2026 purchase agreement. Watch for seller lock-up expirations and potential dilution from unit exchanges.

SGA.brief: Saga Communications filed an 8-K announcing a quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on its Class A Common Stock, payable June 12, 2026, to holders of record May 22, 2026. The aggregate payment is approximately $1.6 million, funded from cash on hand. The board retains discretion over future dividends and any stock buyback program. This is a routine capital-return event within a regular dividend policy, not a special situation. What to watch: any change in dividend pattern or introduction of a share repurchase program.

VHUB.brief: VenHub Global received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on April 30, 2026, for failing the minimum $1.00 bid price rule (30 consecutive business days below $1.00). The company has a 180-day cure period ending October 27, 2026; if it closes at $1.00+ for 10 consecutive business days, compliance is regained. If not cured, it may seek a second 180-day period by meeting all other Nasdaq Capital Market listing standards and committing to a reverse stock split. The stock (VHUB) continues trading normally. Key risk-arb angle: monitor bid price trajectory and potential reverse-split catalyst.

FTV.brief: The New York Stock Exchange LLC filed a Form 25-NSE to delist Fortive Corp's 3.700% Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The securities were redeemed or paid at maturity on February 13, 2026, with trading suspended same day. Delisting becomes effective at the opening on February 24, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This is a routine notification of maturity, not a merger or take-private. The notes are fully collateralized by the issuer's obligation to pay. No overhang, ownership split, or regulatory clock applies. What to watch: confirm the full redemption price; risk-arb angle is negligible as this is a scheduled maturity event.

AGRZ.brief: Agroz Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the adoption of a Second Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association, approved by special resolution on May 22, 2026. The amendment increases authorized share capital from US$11,500 to US$102,000, re-designates existing ordinary shares as Class A ordinary shares, creates 900,000,000 new Class A ordinary shares and 5,000,000 Class B ordinary shares with 100 votes per share. The filing is a routine capital reorganization, not a special situation event.

RTB.brief: RTB Digital, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of RTB via a reverse merger, where a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ryvyl (now RTB Digital) merged with RTB. Under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated September 28, 2025, RTB issued 4,384,504 shares of common stock to former RTB shareholders as consideration. The merger closed on May 12, 2026, after stockholder approval and Nasdaq listing approval. The deal creates a combined entity focused on Web3 media. No advisor or break fee is mentioned. The regulatory clock ended. Watch for post-merger integration and stock performance under new symbol RTB.

NRIM.brief: Northrim BanCorp filed an S-4/A to register an exchange offer for its 6.875% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2035. The offer covers any and all outstanding unregistered notes issued in a private placement on November 26, 2025, with the registered New Notes. No cash proceeds or increase in indebtedness results. The exchange is pursuant to registration rights agreements. The offer expires at 5:00 p.m. ET on a date to be set. Watch for the expiration date and whether any holders tender; no premium or price per share applies as this is a debt exchange.

MMYT.brief: MakeMyTrip Ltd filed a final amendment to its Schedule TO reporting the results of its repurchase offer for its 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028, convertible at par. As of the February 12, 2026 expiration, no notes were surrendered; the $230M aggregate principal remains outstanding under existing indenture terms. The issuer conducted the repurchase under Rule 13e-4 (issuer tender offer). No board recommendation or advisor is noted. Structural note: no overhang or ownership split since no notes were repurchased. The risk-arb angle is moot; the flat outcome leaves capital structure unchanged. Watch for any future liability management or conversion events.

AON.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist Aon plc's 2.875% Senior Notes due 2026 (SEC file 001-07933). The notes were called for redemption/maturity on February 14, 2026, with funds deposited and made available to holders. Trading was suspended on February 17, 2026, and removal from listing is effective March 2, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, or contest is involved. This is a routine debt-security delisting per Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). Risk-arb angle: no equity event; watch for future debt issuances by Aon.

ALP.brief: Alpha Compute Corp filed a 6-K reporting the exercise of Put Options by two investors from its September 2025 private placement. The investors forced the company to repurchase 1,196,295 Ordinary Shares and 633,931 Pre-Funded Warrants in exchange for returning 2,114,583 TON tokens and 5,136,459 USDC tokens — the initial consideration — with no value adjustment. The Put Options became exercisable six to twelve months after the September 25, 2025 closing. This is an issuer tender obligation triggered by side letters. Watch for any shareholder dilution or liquidity impact from the token payouts and mechanics of share cancellation.

CCEP.brief: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners plc filed a Form 6-K updating its share buyback programme. The company announced a second tranche of up to $500M, completing a total $1B return to shareholders. The programme is executed on both US and London trading venues via Goldman Sachs as riskless principal. Shares purchased will be cancelled. The second tranche runs from July 6 to December 18, 2026, with up to $130M allocated to London. The maximum shares purchasable is 42,289,442. This is a structured capital return, not an opportunistic repurchase. Watch for execution pace and any acceleration.

PRENW.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by Prenetics Global Ltd, announcing a multi-year global partnership with Jay Shetty. Shetty becomes a Global Ambassador and a shareholder of Prenetics. The filing includes a press release but does not detail specific terms such as stake percentage, price per share, or implied value. The partnership is part of the company's marketing and growth strategy, not a corporate transaction change. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This is a routine press release announcement, not a special situation category.

RNWWW.brief: ReNew Energy Global plc filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding going-private proposal from Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and founder/CEO Sumant Sinha to acquire all shares not owned by the Consortium at US$6.75 per share cash. The transaction will be structured as a UK scheme of arrangement, with shareholders receiving cash unless they affirmatively elect a rollover. A Special Committee of independent directors chaired by Manoj Singh is evaluating the proposal, advised by Rothschild & Co and Linklaters LLP. No assurance of a final deal exists. Watch for the Special Committee's recommendation and competing bids; risk-arb spread will hinge on regulatory clearance and shareholder vote.

BAYAR.brief: Bayview Acquisition Corp disclosed on July 2, 2026 that Nasdaq's Hearings Panel determined to delist its securities for failing to complete its business combination with Oabay, Inc. by the June 19, 2026 deadline. Trading was suspended effective July 7, 2026; a Form 25-NSE will follow to remove listing and registration. The delisting stems from prior noncompliance with Nasdaq Listing Rules 450(b)(2)(A), 5450(a)(2), 5620(a), and 5450(b)(2)(B). Bayview intends to request Council review within 15 days, though success is uncertain. No deal terms or board recommendation are provided. Watch for council review outcome; risk-arb angle is moot given no pending transaction.

BFRGW.brief: BullFrog AI Holdings disclosed on Feb 19, 2026, that Nasdaq determined it failed to meet the terms of an extension to regain compliance with the minimum $2.5M stockholders' equity requirement (Listing Rule 5550(b)(1)). The company received a delisting notice but intends to request a hearing before an independent Nasdaq Hearings Panel, which will automatically stay any suspension or delisting pending the hearing and any extension granted by the Panel. At the hearing, BullFrog AI plans to present its compliance plan and request additional time. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Key risk-arb angle: delisting would impair liquidity, quoting, and capital-raising ability; outcome hinges on the Panel's decision.

MREO.brief: Mereo BioPharma Group plc disclosed on Form 8-K that on February 17, 2026, it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain a minimum $1.00 bid price per ADS over 30 consecutive business days (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)). The company has a 180-day compliance period until August 17, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a closing bid of at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days. Non-compliance may allow an additional 180-day grace period if other listing standards are met. The ADSs continue trading under MREO. Risk-arb angle: monitor share price and any reverse-split or corporate action to cure bid-price deficiency.

PSQH-WT.brief: PSQ Holdings disclosed receipt of a NYSE delisting notice for non-compliance with minimum market capitalization/stockholders' equity (Rule 802.01B) and minimum average closing price (Rule 802.01C) over 30 consecutive trading days. The notice does not trigger immediate delisting. PSQ will submit a compliance plan within 10 business days for Rule 802.01B and respond within 45 days with a plan to cure within 18 months. Quarterly monitoring applies if the plan is accepted. No board recommendation or advisor named. Risk-arb: watch NYSE acceptance of the plan; failure risks eventual delisting, pressuring the stock.

SGI.brief: Somnigroup International Inc. (formerly Tempur Sealy) filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement on July 8, 2026, in connection with its proposed merger with Leggett & Platt, Incorporated. The merger agreement was entered into on April 13, 2026. Under the terms, Leggett & Platt shareholders will receive a combination of cash and Somnigroup stock (consideration structure not fully specified in this excerpt). The board of Leggett & Platt recommends shareholders vote for the merger; Cleary Gottlieb and Latham & Watkins are advisors. The merger requires regulatory approval and shareholder votes. The filing is a proxy statement/prospectus; the transaction is subject to SEC effectiveness and customary closing conditions. What to watch: shareholder vote timing and antitrust review risk.

TLGYF.brief: TLGY Acquisition Corp. filed Form 15 to terminate registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act after consummating its business combination with StablecoinX Inc. on June 25, 2026. In the de-SPAC merger, TLGY merged with a subsidiary of StablecoinX and became a wholly owned subsidiary. As a result of the combination, the number of record holders of TLGY's securities dropped to one. No specific deal terms (price, premium, board recommendation) were disclosed in this filing. The form is a post-closing administrative step; the key risk-arb angle is the completed merger, with no remaining publicly traded stub. Investors should monitor StablecoinX's ongoing reporting obligations.

HDRNW.brief: This Form 8-K reports the consummation of a business combination (de-SPAC) between GigCapital7 Corp. (a SPAC) and Hadron Energy Operating Company Inc., with the combined entity renamed Hadron Energy, Inc.
