The transaction closed on May 22, 2026, following shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on May 7, 2026. The Form 8-K provides updates on changes in control, board composition, and registrant status, and includes required financial statements. No specific price per share or premium is stated in this excerpt. The closing marks the transition from shell company to operating energy business, converting public SPAC units into combined company stock and warrants. Watch for post-combination trading performance and any shareholder redemptions.

AMPGR.brief: AmpliTech Group filed an 8-K terminating its equity distribution agreement with Maxim Group and announcing a $10 million stock repurchase program over 24 months. Repurchases may be made via open market, private transactions, or block trades under Rule 10b-18, with potential use of a 10b5-1 plan. The program is discretionary and can be suspended anytime. No specific price targets or structural details are disclosed. This capital return event returns cash to shareholders without triggering a special situation such as a tender offer. Key watch factor: actual buyback execution pace against market conditions.

ICL.brief: ICL Group Ltd. filed a 6-K to supplement a prior dividend report of May 13, 2026. The company announced a $69 million dividend, equal to $0.05350 per share (or ILS 0.1504955 for shekel recipients). The record date is June 2, 2026, and payment on June 17, 2026. Only shareholders entitled to at least US$2 will receive payment. Israeli withholding tax rates are described: nil for resident companies, 25% for resident individuals, and 25% or lower per treaty for foreign residents. This is a routine capital return—a cash dividend—with no special-situation event. The filing is a foreign private issuer’s supplemental report (6-K mapping to a U.S. Form 8-K Item 2.02-type update). What to watch: no risk-arb angle; it is a straightforward distribution.

BBLR.brief: Bubblr Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing its February 18, 2026 downgrade from the OTCQB market to the OTCID market due to failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement. The company received an OTCQB notice on November 11, 2025, after its bid price remained below $0.01 for over 30 consecutive days. A 90-day cure period was granted, requiring a $0.01 bid for 10 consecutive days, which Bubblr did not achieve. The downgrade is effective immediately. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Bubblr remains a reporting issuer under the Exchange Act. Management is evaluating strategic options. The risk-arb angle is limited; watch for potential financing or reverse split to regain compliance.

CIMG.brief: CIMG Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into securities purchase agreements with non-U.S. investors to sell up to 43.33 billion units at $0.015 each for gross proceeds up to $650M. Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at $0.015 for two years. Consideration may be paid in Bitcoin or USD, with a Bitcoin reference price of $65,000. An initial closing of 900M units raised ~$13.5M, with warrants fully exercised, issuing 1.8B shares total. The filing describes a capital raising transaction, not a special situation. What to watch: further tranches and Bitcoin volatility affecting pricing.

CORZZ.brief: Core Scientific, Inc., through its subsidiary Core Scientific Finance I LLC, filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a private offering of $3.3 billion in 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 2031. The notes were issued at 99.250% of par to qualified institutional buyers, yielding net proceeds of ~$3.24 billion after discounts and expenses. Proceeds will fund a debt service reserve account and then be distributed upstream to Core Scientific, which plans to repay its outstanding Bridge Facility delayed draw term loans. No board recommendation or advisor is named; the structure involves subsidiary guarantors and a collateral package. What to watch: successful repayment of bridge debt reduces near-term refinancing risk but adds significant leverage—monitor credit rating actions and Bitcoin mining economics for covenant headroom.

GVA.brief: Granite Construction closed a private offering of $600M 6.375% senior notes due 2034, generating ~$590M net proceeds. The proceeds, plus cash on hand and capped call payments, will redeem all outstanding 3.75% convertible notes due 2028, repay credit facility borrowings, and for general corporate purposes. The notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries that are borrowers under the credit facility. The filing primarily describes a refinancing and debt restructuring rather than a pure capital return, but the redemption of convertible notes with cash qualifies as a capital return to prior noteholders. Watch for interest rate environment shifts and credit rating impact.

LIMNW.brief: Liminatus Pharma filed an 8-K reporting entry into an Amended and Restated Merger Agreement to acquire InnocsAI LLC. The transaction was revised to allow closing before stockholder approval: merger consideration of 1.6B shares will be paid as ~19.99% of pre-close common stock (max without Nasdaq approval) plus newly designated Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock (convertible at 10,000:1 into common). No price per share, premium, or advisor named. The structure avoids stockholder vote initially; the preferred stock cannot convert until shareholder approval. Watch for Nasdaq listing rule compliance, conversion mechanics, and potential dilution overhang; risk-arb centers on regulatory and shareholder approval timeline.

CCFN.brief: Muncy Columbia Financial Corp (CCFN) filed an 8-K announcing a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.155 per share and a new treasury stock repurchase program authorizing repurchase of up to 530,611 shares (5% of outstanding). The dividend is payable June 11, 2026 to holders of record May 26, 2026. The buyback is effective May 15, 2026 through May 15, 2028, conducted in open market or private transactions, with all repurchased shares held as treasury. No premium, board recommendation, or advisor was named. This is a standard capital return event; watch for ongoing execution pace and any acceleration of buybacks.

OLOX.brief: Olenox Industries Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 100% of CS Digital Ventures, LLC via an Amended Membership Interest Purchase Agreement dated June 16, 2026. Aggregate consideration includes $30 million upfront, plus additional shares and assumption of liabilities (specific per-share price not stated). Concurrently, the Company entered an Exchange Agreement to convert Series D Preferred Stock into Series E Preferred Stock, cancelling the Series D. The filing does not name a board recommendation or financial advisor. The acquisition closed on the same date, indicating immediate control. The structure involves equity conversion and cash consideration. Watch for post-closing adjustments or shareholder litigation regarding the preferred stock exchange.

OTLK.brief: Outlook Therapeutics (OTLK) filed an 8-K disclosing it regained compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid price rule. The Nasdaq Staff notified the company on June 26, 2026, that its common stock closed at $1.00 or greater for ten consecutive business days through June 25, 2026, satisfying Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). This follows a prior February 18, 2026 delisting notice. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal structure applies. Nasdaq's closure of the matter removes immediate delisting risk. What to watch: sustained price stability above $1.00 and potential equity market or operational catalysts.

REFR.brief: Research Frontiers disclosed receipt of two Nasdaq deficiency notices on June 2, 2026. The company fails the $1.00 minimum bid price (Rule 5550(a)(2)) and the $35M minimum market value of listed securities (Rule 5550(b)(2)) requirements. It has 180 calendar days, until November 30, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above those thresholds for 10 consecutive business days per criterion. Management currently does not plan a reverse stock split. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for potential reverse split, delisting appeal, or shareholder action if pricing does not improve; risk-arb angle minimal due to going-concern listing risk.

FTH.brief: Sensei Biotherapeutics filed an 8-K providing unaudited pro forma financials for the conversion of Series B Preferred Stock into common stock, which will exceed 20% of outstanding shares and result in a change of control, requiring stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rules 5635(a) and 5635(b). The conversion is to be voted on at the June 10, 2026 annual meeting. No price per share, premium, or advisor is disclosed. The pro forma data is illustrative and preliminary. Watch for stockholder vote outcome and potential Nasdaq compliance considerations.

AEFC.brief: Aegon Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the initiation of a EUR 200 million share buyback program beginning July 1, 2026, with expected completion by December 23, 2026. This follows the completion of a prior EUR 227 million buyback that repurchased 33,909,553 shares at an average price of EUR 6.68 per share. Largest shareholder Vereniging Aegon (18.4% voting rights) agreed to participate pro-rata for EUR 37 million. Shares repurchased will be canceled or used for compensation plans. The program complies with EU regulations and existing shareholder authority. Watch for repurchase pace and cancellation impact; no premium or tender offer involved.

ELVR.brief: Elevra Lithium Ltd filed a 6-K announcing its purchase and termination of a spodumene offtake agreement previously granted to Waratah Capital Advisors for the Moblan Lithium Project, which is 60%-owned by Elevra. Consideration comprised US$5 million in Elevra ordinary shares (at A$12.20 per share) and US$0.5 million in options exercisable at a 50% premium to the issue price, closings on May 12, 2026. The board recommended the deal, citing enhanced strategic flexibility and economics. The shares rank equally; options are exercisable after 120 days and vest over three years. Watch for potential dilution and execution of the scoping study for NAL expansion.

RTNTF.brief: Rio Tinto filed a Form 6-K for June 2026, attaching various routine announcements including total voting rights, share issuances, director interest changes, media releases on joint trials with China Baowu and BHP/Caterpillar, and a loan rate adjustment in Mongolia. No acquisition, divestiture, tender offer, restructuring, or strategic review is described. The filing is a compilation of standard periodic updates for a foreign private issuer.

CMIIW.brief: Columbus Circle Capital Corp II (blank-check company) filed an 8-K on June 26, 2026, announcing a business combination agreement with Elroy Air, Inc. Under the deal, Merger Sub will merge with and into Elroy Air, with Elroy Air as the surviving entity; the SPAC will rename to Elroy Air, Inc. post-closing. The board of both parties approved the transaction. No financial terms (price per share, premium, enterprise value) are disclosed. The closing is expected in Q4 2026, subject to shareholder approvals from both entities and customary conditions. A full proxy/prospectus detailing valuation and risk-arb spread is needed before assessing arbitrage potential.

FIVN.brief: Five9, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing the commencement of an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with JPMorgan Chase to repurchase $90.0 million of its common stock under an existing authorization. The company will make a $90 million payment on May 5, 2026, and expects an initial delivery of ~3.1 million shares. The final repurchase price will be based on the VWAP over the term, less a discount. Settlement is expected by September 30, 2026. This is a capital return to shareholders; watch for VWAP performance and final share count delivery.

GPN.brief: Global Payments Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $500 million of its common stock, part of a previously announced board-approved repurchase plan. Approximately 5.74 million shares will be received on May 8, 2026, with final settlement expected by June 30, 2026. The total shares repurchased will be based on the average daily VWAP during the repurchase period, less a discount and subject to adjustments. This is a capital return event via an ASR, not a tender offer. Watch for the final share count and impact on EPS.

HCWB.brief: HCW Biologics disclosed it received a Nasdaq Hearings Panel decision that it regained compliance with the Bid Price Rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)) per the Panel's letter dated May 29, 2026, as amended. If the Company satisfies remaining terms through September 22, 2026, a Discretionary Panel Monitor will be imposed for one year; a Mandatory Panel Monitor applies until June 17, 2027. During monitoring, any non-compliance with the Bid Price Rule will result in an immediate Delist Determination Letter without cure periods. No stake, premium, or terms involved.

TELO.brief: Telomir Pharmaceuticals filed a definitive proxy (DEFM14A) soliciting votes for seven proposals at its March 23, 2026 annual meeting, including approval of share issuance exceeding 20% of outstanding stock pursuant to its merger with TELI Pharmaceuticals (the Merger). Under the Merger Agreement dated November 20, 2025 and amended February 4, 2026, TELI will merge into a Telomir subsidiary, with TELI surviving. Outstanding TELI common shares will convert into Telomir common stock based on a valuation-determined exchange ratio per Moore. Other proposals include director elections, auditor ratification, plan amendments, bylaw quorum reduction, option grants, and adjournment. The board recommends a vote for all proposals. Watch for stockholder vote outcome and Nasdaq listing rule compliance.

PLGO.brief: Fidelis Insurance Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing its board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.15 per share, payable June 26, 2026, to shareholders of record June 15, 2026. This is a routine capital return event, not a special situation. No premium, advisor, or structural complexities are involved. The filing also mentions a planned rebranding, but that does not alter the classification. What to watch: the dividend payment date and any future capital allocation updates.

CSAI.brief: Cloudastructure filed an 8-K reporting an exchange agreement with Streeterville Capital. The company issued a $1,299,870 promissory note (9.5% interest, matures July 2027) in exchange for 1,170 shares of Series 2 Convertible Preferred Stock held by Streeterville. The exchange was exempt under Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act. The note is unsecured with monthly redemption rights of $108,332.50 and includes trigger events leading to potential acceleration and default interest. This restructuring of preferred equity into debt reduces dilution but increases leverage. Monitor Streeterville's redemption activity and any trigger events for risk of default or forced conversion.

NXB.brief: Off The Hook YS Inc. (the Company) filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its acquisition of Apex Marine, LLC, Apex Marine Sales, LLC, and Apex Marine Stuart, LLC (collectively Apex) on May 13, 2026, per a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement dated February 13, 2026. The aggregate purchase price was $5,966,667, consisting of $1.2 million cash, 679,012 shares valued at $2.70/share ($1,800,000), and two promissory notes: one for $2,466,667 (secured by the purchased interests, 6% interest, 24 monthly payments) and one for $500,000 (due in 365 days, no interest except default). The seller was Ismael Pereira, with no prior relationship. Financial statements will be filed within 60 days. Watch for integration execution and note repayment performance.

KTTAW.brief: On February 20, 2026, Pasithea Therapeutics disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain the $1.00 minimum bid price per Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has 180 calendar days, until August 19, 2026, to regain compliance by having its common stock close at or above $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If not cured, it may seek an additional 180-day period if it meets other listing standards and signals intent to effect a reverse stock split. The notice does not trigger immediate delisting; the company is evaluating options. The key risk-arb angle is the timeline to cure and potential reverse split overhang.

RAINW.brief: Rain Enhancement Technologies Holdco disclosed it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain a $35M market value of listed securities (MVLS) for 30 consecutive business days as of Feb 17, 2026. The company has a 180-day cure period through Aug 17, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above $35M MVLS for ten consecutive business days. Failure would trigger a delisting notice, subject to appeal. No board recommendation, advisor, or structural mechanics are mentioned. The stock and warrants (RAIN/RAINW) continue trading. Watch for periodic MVLS updates and any potential reverse stock split or other cure actions.

LNC-PD.brief: Lincoln National Corporation filed an S-4 registration statement on February 20, 2026, for an exchange offer to swap up to $500 million of outstanding 2.330% Senior Notes due 2030 (issued May 15, 2025) for registered notes with identical terms. The exchange is being made to satisfy registration rights; no new capital is raised. The board supports the transaction; Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz serves as legal counsel. Mechanics: holders exchange existing notes (CUSIP 534187 BM0) for registered notes (CUSIP 534187 BY4) on a like-for-like basis. There is no premium, break fee, or regulatory clock beyond SEC effectiveness. The transaction is purely a registration cure, not a tender or consent solicitation—risk-arb is inapplicable; focus on SEC effectiveness timing and any holdout dynamics.

MS-PQ.brief: Morgan Stanley filed an 8-K to announce a quarterly common stock dividend increase to $1.15 per share from $1.00, a 15% rise. The dividend applies to the common stock and will commence with the declaration expected in the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The board authorized the increase, reflecting strong capital position. Terms include per-share amount only; no premium, advisors, or structural conditions. This is a routine capital return action not linked to any other event. Watch for sustained earnings coverage and payout ratio evolution.

SB-PD.brief: Safe Bulkers filed a Form 6-K reporting the sale of two drybulk vessels: MV Xenia (2006 Post-Panamax) for $13.0M and MV Pedhoulas Commander (2008 Kamsarmax) for $14.7M, totaling $27.7M. The company announced this as part of a fleet renewal strategy, citing recent investments in modern newbuilds and delivery of thirteen IMO GHG Phase 3 NOx Tier III vessels since 2022, with eleven additional newbuilds on order. Both vessels are to be delivered after their current voyages with dry-docking due. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The sales are asset divestitures, not a corporate sale. Watch for cash proceeds use and fleet age profile improvements.

TOPS.brief: TOP Ships Inc. filed a Form 6-K disclosing amendments to two related-party transactions. The first amendment extends the deadline for a $16.1 million balance owed to Central Mare Inc. for the acquisition of Tanker SPVs to July 31, 2026. The second extends to the same date an option to acquire Dubai residential real estate assets (estimated value >$200M) at a 10% discount, for which $23.5M in advance payments have been made. The extensions were requested to evaluate geopolitical conditions in the Middle East. No new event triggers a special situation; amendments to existing terms maintain the status quo pending further evaluation.

ATRA.brief: Atara Biotherapeutics disclosed it received a Nasdaq notice for failing the $50M minimum market value of listed securities (MVLS) requirement under Listing Rule 5450(b)(2)(A). The company has 180 calendar days, until October 27, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above $50M for at least 10 consecutive business days. The notice has no immediate delisting effect; shares continue trading under ATRA on Nasdaq Global Select. Atara may evaluate options including transferring to The Nasdaq Capital Market. If noncompliant by the deadline, Nasdaq will issue a delisting notice, subject to appeal. Risk-arb angle: monitor MVLS trajectory and potential uplisting steps.

BTBDW.brief: BT Brands filed an 8-K announcing termination of its Agreement and Plan of Merger with Aero Velocity Inc. The merger, under which Aero would become a wholly owned subsidiary via a merger sub, was terminated on May 1, 2026 because the registration statement was not declared effective and the closing did not occur by the extended deadline of April 30, 2026. Company exercised termination right under Section 7.1(b); no termination fee is payable, and each party bears its own expenses. Watch for any litigation or alternative transaction.

CULP.brief: Culp Inc. filed Form 25 with the SEC on March 5, 2026, to voluntarily delist its common stock from the New York Stock Exchange. The company cited compliance with NYSE rules and SEC Rule 12d2-2(c). The delisting was effective March 5, 2026. No price per share, premium, or consideration was disclosed. Management recommended the delisting and no advisor was named. The filing indicates a voluntary withdrawal, with no collateral or ownership change. Watch for potential deregistration under Section 12(g) and future shareholder actions.

TRNR.brief: Interactive Strength Inc. filed an 8-K for its agreement to acquire STEPR Inc. and STEPR PTY LTD. The deal has two parts: secondary purchase of all STEPR shares from Seller, then primary purchase of newly issued shares. Cash consideration includes $1.5M initial working capital, up to $1.2M repayment of an AFS loan, up to $2.5M post-closing contributions, and up to $1M on the first anniversary ($500K for shareholder loans, $500K to designees). A secured note of up to $1.5M is available pre-closing. The consideration also includes shares of Interactive's newly designated preferred stock. The board has not yet disclosed a recommendation; advisors are not named. Closings are subject to customary conditions. Watch for regulatory and shareholder approvals, and integration risk given the cross-border Australian entity.

KDP.brief: Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. filed an 8-K on June 23, 2026, disclosing that Coffee Operating Unit head Rafa Oliveira will depart at end of July 2026 for an external CEO role. CEO Tim Cofer will temporarily oversee the coffee business while the Board searches for a CEO of Global Coffee Co., a standalone entity expected from the previously-announced separation of KDP's coffee and beverage businesses. The filing also reaffirms 2026 guidance. No deal terms were provided. This event updates the progress of a planned spin-off, announced earlier, which is the core special situation. The filing does not trigger a new deal category but supports the existing spin-off classification. Watch for further separation details and CEO appointment timeline.

MLM.brief: Martin Marietta Materials filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a Securities Sale Agreement to acquire all outstanding equity interests in Lhoist North America (LNA) from LNA Holding SRL for $13.5 billion total consideration, composed of $7 billion cash and 10,953,543 newly issued shares valued at $6.5 billion (based on VWAP). The board has not yet made a formal 13e-3 recommendation; terms include regulatory condition (HSR) and a $350 million reverse break fee payable if regulatory clearance fails beyond the extended long-stop date of June 15, 2027. Watch for antitrust review duration; risk-arb spread depends on MLM stock price and deal timeline.

VEEAW.brief: Veea Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Note Conversion Agreement with NLabs Inc., an affiliate of the CEO, exchanging $4.13M in principal and accrued interest on demand notes for 41,329 Series A-1 preferred shares (stated value $100 per share, convertible into 13.3M common shares) and warrants to purchase 13.3M common shares at $0.31, exercisable from January 2027 to June 2031. The conversion resolves debt overhang and bolsters equity, with registration rights for the underlying shares. The board presumably approved; advisors not named. Watch for dilution impact and potential shareholder reaction.

AMGN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Amgen Inc.'s 2.000% Senior Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The delisting is effective as of February 24, 2026, and reflects the securities' maturity. No premium, stock consideration, or board involvement applies. This is a routine administrative removal of matured notes, not a merger or tender. The filing has no regulatory clock or risk-arb implications; the notes will cease trading on Nasdaq. What to watch: any residual claims or conversion rights tied to the matured notes.

AHL-PF.brief: Aspen Insurance Holdings terminated its SEC registration on March 6, 2026, following its acquisition by Endurance Specialty Insurance (parent). The merger closed February 24, 2026, under an August 27, 2025 agreement, with Merger Sub merging into Aspen, leaving Aspen as a wholly owned subsidiary of Endurance. The filing certifies fewer than 300 shareholders of record, with Aspen now held entirely by one holder—Parent. The class A ordinary shares, depositary shares, and preference shares are deregistered under Rule 12g-4(a)(1). Watch for the completion of any remaining reporting obligations and the redemption of outstanding preference shares, offering no risk-arb opportunity as the deal has closed.

BNS.brief: Scotiabank files Form 6-K incorporating by reference legal opinions for a dual-tranche senior medium-term note offering: US$1.1B 4.578% fixed-to-floating notes due 2029 and US$1.0B 4.904% fixed-to-floating notes due 2032, issued under an existing Distribution Agreement and Terms Agreement. The notes are issued under an indenture with Computershare trustees. This is a routine debt issuance, not a special situation. No special-situation mechanics, premiums, or activist elements appear. The filing merely registers the debt securities and supporting legal opinions.

FMS.brief: Fresenius Medical Care AG disclosed a share buyback program via Form 6-K (EU equivalent of a share repurchase plan). The program runs from May 28, 2026 to May 27, 2027, authorizing up to 29,341,344 shares (ISIN DE0005785802) for up to EUR 1 billion. The first tranche is up to EUR 600 million until December 15, 2026. Repurchased shares will primarily be cancelled, with a small portion used for incentive plans. A credit institution makes independent trading decisions in line with EU safe-harbor rules. The company may repurchase up to 10% of share capital. Watch for execution pace and impact on share price and EPS.

EXPD.brief: Expeditors International filed an 8-K on May 5, 2026, announcing a semi-annual cash dividend of $0.81 per share declared May 4, 2026, payable June 15, 2026 to holders of record June 1, 2026. This represents a 5% increase from prior dividends. The company also highlighted a new $3 billion share repurchase program authorized in February 2026 and cumulative returns of nearly $2 billion to shareholders since 2024. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine dividend declaration and ongoing buyback program disclosure. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; this is a steady capital return policy.

HTCR.brief: HeartCore Enterprises sold its 51% majority stake in Sigmaways, Inc. (229,500 shares) and $2.19M in promissory notes to Semaphore Technologies. Consideration is up to $650,000: $1,000 cash at close plus up to $649,000 earn-out equal to 10% of Sigmaways gross revenue above $5.5M over 12 months. Additionally, a SAFE note in Heart-Tech Health (original $350,000) was contributed as part of mutual releases. The transaction closed on June 22, 2026. Watch for earn-out metrics and potential collections on the transferred debt.

GRMLW.brief: Greenland Mines Ltd filed an 8-K regarding a Share Exchange Agreement dated June 15, 2026, to acquire 19,958,503 common shares (9.9% post-closing) of AnorTech Inc., a TSXV-listed company. The consideration was 12,400,000 shares of Greenland common stock, valued based on volume-weighted average price, with a six-month option to acquire up to an additional 25,168,669 AnorTech shares at CAD$0.30 per share or last closing price, payable in stock. The board recommended the transaction; no advisor named. Greenland issued shares under Section 4(a)(2)/Regulation D. The deal grants a toehold stake with potential for further accretion. Watch for regulatory (TSXV) approvals and stock price adjustments on option exercise.

OILD.brief: BMO Financial Group files Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing a definitive agreement to sell its Transportation Finance and Vendor Finance businesses to Stonepeak. The businesses comprise a combined loan and lease portfolio of approximately C$14.5 billion as of March 31, 2026. BMO will retain a 19.9% equity interest in the businesses post-sale, enabling continued participation in long-term value creation. The transaction is described as accretive to capital ratios and ROE, aligning with BMO's strategy to sharpen focus on core markets and improve capital efficiency. No purchase price, premium, board recommendation, or advisors are named in the press release. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions; watch for regulatory clearance timelines and any competing bids. Risk-arb angle: structural equity interest reduces downside, but regulatory hurdles could delay close.

EHLD.brief: Euroholdings Ltd., via a Form 6-K, reported Q1 2026 results and disclosed the acquisition of a 49,997 DWT MR product tanker vessel, M/T Hellas Fighter (built 2015), from a related party of majority shareholder Marla Investments Inc. (not under common control) for $39.25 million. Delivery is expected between mid-June and mid-August 2026. The transaction was approved by an independent committee of disinterested directors. Financing will use own funds and debt. This acquisition expands the fleet and continues the company's shift into product tankers, with the vessel expected to contribute to profitability. Risk-arb angle: watch for financing details and regulatory approvals for the related-party purchase.

HSBC.brief: HSBC Holdings plc filed a Form 6-K giving notice of redemption of $2.3B 5.887% Fixed/Floating Rate Notes and $700M Floating Rate Notes due 2027 at par ($1,000 per $1,000 principal) on August 14, 2026. Accrued interest from the last payment date to the redemption date will also be paid. This is a voluntary, full redemption by the issuer under the indenture terms. No premium above par, board recommendation, or advisor is mentioned. The redemption is a straightforward debt retirement. Watch for any delays in surrender of securities or tax withholding issues.

BATL.brief: Battalion Oil Corp's subsidiary entered a Third Amended and Restated Senior Secured Credit Agreement on June 30, 2026, refinancing existing debt. The deal provides a $162.5M term loan funded at close and a discretionary $175M delayed draw facility maturing Dec 31, 2029. Interest is SOFR-based plus credit spread. No acquisition, divestiture, or shareholder return; it is a routine refinancing of secured credit facilities. Watch for future draws under delayed facility and covenant compliance.

ALOY.brief: Realloys Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Securities Purchase Agreement entered into on June 24, 2026, to sell ~7.02M shares at $14.25/share to accredited investors in a private placement raising ~$100M gross. Clear Street LLC acted as placement agent. The deal includes customary reps/warranties and a 45-day lock-up on further equity issuance. Net proceeds are for general corporate and working capital. Close expected June 26, 2026, subject to conditions. A registration rights agreement covering resale was also signed. This is a capital-raising event (PIPE-like), not a transformative M&A or activist campaign, but fits 'Capital Returns' as a direct equity issuance for corporate purposes.

LFST.brief: LifeStance Health Group filed an 8-K reporting a secondary offering of 35 million shares by selling stockholders, with the issuer repurchasing 6 million shares from the underwriter at the same price. The company received no proceeds; the closing occurred on May 12, 2026. The filing is an ordinary equity offering disclosure under Item 8.01, not a special situation. No activist, strategic review, or transformative event is present. The filing is a routine current report.

JOE.brief: The St. Joe Company filed an 8-K disclosing a $150.8 million increase in its share repurchase authorization, bringing total capacity to $200.0 million under the existing Stock Repurchase Program with no expiration date. The company had $49.2 million remaining prior to the expansion. This is an issuer-initiated capital return via open-market buybacks, not a tender offer. There is no stated price, premium, or timeline. The board authorized the additional repurchase capacity as a discretionary use of corporate cash. Investors should watch actual repurchase execution pace and any impact on diluted share count or earnings per share.

SOUL-UN.brief: Soulpower Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K disclosing issuance of a $2.5 million unsecured promissory note (B Note) to sponsor affiliate Soulpower Management LLC. The note is non-interest bearing, non-convertible, and will be forgiven automatically upon consummation of an initial business combination; otherwise due at liquidation or default. Proceeds are for general working capital. The lender is controlled by CEO Justin Lafazan. This is a classic SPAC working capital bridge loan, a routine funding mechanism to extend the SPAC's runway while it seeks a target. Watch for the SPAC's deadline to announce/complete a deal; the note structure may create tension between sponsor and public shareholders.

DFNSW.brief: T3 Defense Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 2.01 completing the acquisition of 60% of Project 35, an Israeli defense supplier, for 21,059,871 shares of common stock and a $1,250,000 promissory note (12% interest, due July 5, 2027). T3 also commits to invest $2,500,000 in Project 35 over 12 months. The seller is X S.A. Security and Defense Ltd. No board recommendation, fairness opinion, or advisor is named. The deal adds unmanned aerial and counter-drone systems. No premium or closing date is disclosed; regulatory approvals are not mentioned. Watch for integration updates and the additional capital commitment.

TTD.brief: Trade Desk, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-03-25 that it fell out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rules 5605(c)(2)(A) and 5605(d)(2)(A) after the resignations of directors Alexander Kayyal (3/19) and Kathryn Falberg (3/23). The audit and compensation committees lost minimum independent director counts. Nasdaq granted a cure period through 9/21/2026. The board appointed Andrew Vollero as Class II director and to the audit committee effective 4/3/2026, partially addressing the vacancies. No shareholder vote, premium, or price is involved. Watch for appointment of additional independent directors to regain compliance by the deadline; delisting risk remains if uncured.

BCTXL.brief: Nasdaq filed a Form 25-NSE to delist BriaCell Therapeutics Corp. securities under SEC Rule 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(2) as of February 26, 2026. The delisting is based on the exercise of a warrant causing the security to no longer be eligible for listing. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or transaction price was disclosed. The filing is automatic and does not involve shareholder approval or a merger. The removal date is immediate. What to watch: whether BriaCell pursues an appeal or seeks alternative listing; risk-arb is not applicable as no buyout is involved.

CM.brief: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) filed a Form 6-K announcing TSX approval of a new normal course issuer bid (NCIB) to repurchase for cancellation up to 30 million common shares (~3.3% of shares outstanding), replacing a completed prior NCIB. Aggregate repurchases represent ~5.5% of public float. Purchases at market price commence on or after June 8, 2026, within daily volume limits (max 673,084 shares), and conclude by June 7, 2027. An automatic share purchase plan allows trading during blackouts. CIBC Capital Markets acts as designated broker. Prior NCIB bought 20M shares at avg ~C$129.68 for C$2.6B.

ESEA.brief: Euroseas Ltd. filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing the ordering of four new feeder containerships: two 2,800 teu high-reefer vessels at ~$46.5M each and two 1,800 teu vessels at ~$32.5M each, with options for up to four more. Deliveries are scheduled from June 2028 to January 2029. The orders expand the existing newbuilding program to ten vessels, financed with debt and equity. No special-situation M&A, activist, or restructuring event is disclosed; this is an ordinary capital-expenditure update.

GLOB.brief: Globant S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing a new share repurchase program authorizing up to $50 million per quarter, with a maximum aggregate of $125 million, to run from Q2 2026 through Q4 2027. The prior $125 million program was completed on April 6, 2026. Repurchases may be made via open market or accelerated share repurchases at management's discretion, subject to market conditions, regulatory requirements, and corporate liquidity. There is no obligation to repurchase any specific amount, and the program may be suspended anytime. The filing also includes Q1 2026 earnings results and disclosure of a securities class action filed on April 24, 2026, which the company disputes. Watch for pace of repurchases and any impact from the litigation on execution.

CIB.brief: Grupo Cibest S.A. filed a Form 6-K disclosing a clarification regarding its Board compensation policy. The filing explains that 70% of board compensation is paid in cash and 30% via contributions to the SVA Institutional Fund, which invests primarily in Grupo Cibest shares, subject to a two-year holding period. The Board authorized Luis Fernando Restrepo Echavarría to partially redeem units in the Fund that have satisfied the holding period. This is a routine corporate governance disclosure, not a special situation. No deal terms, premium, or strategic action are present. Watch for any future strategic moves, but this filing itself is ordinary.

ZTEK.brief: Zentek Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing the formation of a U.S. joint venture, Strategic Graphite Partners LLC, with ALO Graphite Partners LLC. The JV is 90% owned by a Zentek subsidiary and 10% by ALO Partners. Zentek granted 50,000 stock options (C$0.56, 24-month term) to consultants Jeremy Roenick and Nicolas Perkin. The JV aims to advance Albany ultra-high-purity graphite sales in U.S. national-security markets. No price, premium, or deal terms were disclosed. The filing reports a business development, not a special situation.

FRMM.brief: Forum Markets filed an 8-K to disclose a Side Letter Amendment No. 2 to its Series B-3 Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement with Zippy, Inc. The amendment replaces a single true-up determination date for the Final Make Whole Amount with three separate measurement and payment dates (July 31, September 30, December 31, 2026). Zippy may sell up to 285,714 shares per period, with unsold shares carried forward. The company pays any make-whole amount in cash within ten business days after each date. This is a contractual adjustment to a prior financing arrangement, not a standalone special-situations event.

FSBW.brief: FS Bancorp filed an S-4 registration statement for its merger with Pacific West Bancorp, where Pacific West will merge into FS Bancorp. Terms were not disclosed in this preliminary filing. The Pacific West board approved the merger agreement and recommends shareholders vote in favor. FS Bancorp will issue shares as consideration; no cash component or per-share price is stated. The registration is not yet effective, with a special meeting of Pacific West shareholders to be held in 2026—date and location noted. The transaction requires SEC clearance, shareholder approval, and customary closing conditions. Watch for definitive terms, premium disclosure, and regulatory timeline.

INTU.brief: Intuit Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a restructuring plan to simplify its organizational structure, reducing its workforce by ~17% and considering site closures. The company expects $300-$340 million in charges, primarily for severance and benefits, mostly in Q4 fiscal 2026 ending July 31, 2026, with actions substantially completed by Q1 fiscal 2027 ending October 31, 2026. The board approved a cash dividend. This is a cost-cutting restructuring, not a sale or acquisition. Watch for execution risk and further charges.

IMAQ.brief: International Media Acquisition Corp. filed Form 8-K reporting a $2,000 deposit into its trust account to extend its deadline to complete an initial business combination from June 2, 2026 to July 2, 2026. This is the 18th of 24 possible monthly extensions under the Trust Agreement. No target, terms, or advisors are identified. The filing is purely procedural to avoid liquidation. Watch for whether the SPAC announces a definitive agreement or faces a redemption/trust wind-down if no deal is reached by the final deadline.

SND.brief: Smart Sand, Inc. filed an 8-K to disclose adoption of a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan for its share repurchase program, authorizing up to $2.5 million in buybacks. Trades may commence June 1, 2026, and expire upon full use or August 10, 2026. The plan allows repurchases during blackout periods via a broker. No price or premium is specified. This is a capital return event executed through open-market repurchases. Watch for periodic disclosures of actual repurchase activity in subsequent 10-Q/K filings; risk-arb angle is not applicable as it is a non-discretionary buyback plan.

TBTC.brief: Table Trac Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a Board-declared cash dividend of $0.02 per share, payable June 12, 2026 to holders of record May 29, 2026. The dividend reflects disciplined capital allocation and returning value to shareholders. No premium, stake, advisors, or other deal terms were disclosed. The filing is a routine capital return event, not a special situation warranting a different category. Watch for continued quarterly dividends or changes in payout policy.

TETEF.brief: Technology Telecommunication Acquisition Corp filed a definitive proxy statement for its extraordinary general meeting on March 30, 2026, to approve a two-step business combination with Bradbury Capital Holdings Inc. The deal values Holdings at $1.1 billion, payable in 110 million newly issued PubCo ordinary shares. The board recommends shareholders vote for the proposal; no advisor is named. The transaction involves a reincorporation merger of TETE into PubCo, followed by an acquisition merger of merger sub into Holdings. Post-close, Holdings shareholders will own PubCo. The meeting is in-person and virtual in Kuala Lumpur. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and redemptions; risk-arb focuses on approval and timeline.

URBN.brief: This 8-K Item 8.01 filing reports Urban Outfitters, Inc.'s earnings release for the quarter ended April 30, 2026, disclosing record net sales of $1.48 billion (up 11.4%) and net income of $115.7 million ($1.30 EPS). No strategic event or transaction is announced; it is a routine earnings disclosure without any special-situation elements such as M&A, activism, or restructuring. The filing is purely informational and does not trigger corporate action.

CYTOF.brief: Altamira Therapeutics Ltd. (Bermuda) filed Form 15-12G on February 27, 2026, certifying termination of registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The company reported approximately 48 holders of record of its common shares ($0.002 par value). The filing relied on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and/or (a)(2) to suspend reporting duties under Sections 13 and 15(d). This deregistration likely reflects the company's minimal public float and shareholder base. Structurally, no deal terms or premiums are involved; the action terminates SEC reporting obligations. The regulatory clock is immediate (effective same day). The risk-arb angle: no transaction; watch for potential delisting from any exchange and reduced liquidity.

EFC-PC.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE to delist Ellington Financial Inc.'s 6.750% Series A Fixed-to-Floating Rate Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. The entire class was called for redemption on February 27, 2026, with funds sufficient for payment deposited and made available to holders. Trading was suspended as of that date, and delisting becomes effective at the opening of business on March 10, 2026, per Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). No board recommendation or advisor was noted. This is a routine mandatory delisting following a full redemption; the risk-arb angle is moot as the security is being retired at par.

BBDO.brief: Banco Bradesco S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing that its Board of Directors approved the payment of interim interest on shareholders' equity totaling R$3.5 billion (R$0.31536 per common share and R$0.34689 per preferred share). The record date is July 3, 2026, with ex-rights on July 6, 2026. Payment will occur by January 29, 2027, net of 17.5% withholding tax for most shareholders. This distribution is approximately 18.3x the prior monthly interest payment and will count toward mandatory dividends. The filing is a routine capital return, not a special situation beyond a regular distribution.

CURR.brief: Currenc Group Inc. (Nasdaq: CURR) filed a Form 6-K announcing its board unanimously ratified the suspension of active business operations of its indirect subsidiary PT Walletku Indompet Indonesia due to lack of working capital and forfeiture of its authorized distributor status. The company authorized up to $150,000 from the holding company for severance and debt settlement through September 2026. The action follows a 46.9% revenue decline and $0.45 million net loss for WalletKu in FY2025. The restructuring aims to refocus on an AI Web3 roadmap. No price, premium, or advisor named. Watch for completion of debt settlement and potential further segment shut-downs.

TV.brief: Grupo Televisa, S.A.B. filed a 6-K reporting the issuance of zero-coupon mandatory convertible debentures totaling MXN 6,917,800,007.42. The debentures will mandatorily convert into Series A, B, D, L shares and/or CPOs on the one-year anniversary, subject to regulatory approvals, representing 19.48% of the company's capital stock with a one-year lock-up. The subscription price was based on the 30-day VWAP of CPOs. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, including potential telecom sector transactions or debt prepayment. Fintech Latam S.à r.l. subscribed and will hold 22.3% post-conversion, with passive investment status. The issuance is a capital return via mandatory convertible debt. Watch for conversion and regulatory clearance.

ORISF.brief: Oriental Rise Holdings filed a Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval and board authorization of a reverse share split. The split ratio is set at 1-for-4, with a permissible range of 1-for-2 to 1-for-100. The reverse split applies to both issued and unissued ordinary shares; fractional shares will be rounded up. No specific market effective date or price per share is provided. The move is likely intended to meet listing standards. There are no advisors, premiums, or deal terms disclosed. Watch for the effective date announcement and potential NASDAQ compliance updates.

DVLT.brief: Datavault AI Inc. filed an 8-K on May 30, 2026, announcing a non-binding term sheet with Helmex Global LLP for a potential $2.0 billion structured financing across four tranches of up to $500M each. The company will issue shares at $1.55-$2.00 per share to the counterparty in exchange for preferred units in an investment vehicle. Datavault must pay a non-refundable $25M fee by June 4, 2026, plus $25M per additional tranche. Completion requires due diligence, definitive agreements, stockholder approval, regulatory/CFIUS clearance, a charter amendment, fairness opinion, and independent valuation. The counterparty may nominate one director per tranche. Watch for definitive agreement execution and regulatory hurdles; the fee structure raises governance and dilution concerns.

COCHW.brief: Envoy Medical, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its At The Market Offering Agreement (ATM Agreement) dated January 17, 2025, effective June 24, 2026. The ATM facility authorized up to $15 million in common stock sales. The termination was announced via press release, reflecting management's confidence in the company's capital position. No price, premium, or advisor details are provided. This is a voluntary termination of an equity facility, not tied to a broader special situation. Watch for future financing needs or capital market activity as the company relies on existing cash.

JUNS.brief: Jupiter Neurosciences (JUNS) filed an 8-K reporting a non-binding term sheet with PharmAla Biotech for exclusive U.S. rights to ALA-002, a next-generation MDMA formulation. Upfront consideration is $3.33M (1.5M cash + $1.83M stock with a 180-day lock-up; JUNS may elect all-cash). Additional milestones include $3.33M on Phase 3 initiation and $20M on FDA approval, plus commercialization milestones up to $33.33M tied to net sales thresholds. The parties aim for a definitive agreement within 90 days, subject to due diligence. Watch for completion risk, as the term sheet is non-binding and JUNS must secure financing for cash consideration.

MCHB.brief: Mechanics Bancorp, via its wholly owned subsidiary Mechanics Bank, filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) reporting the completed sale of its Fannie Mae Delegated Underwriting and Servicing business line to Fifth Third Bank for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $126 million. The transaction closed on May 1, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee were disclosed. The sale was previously announced and is now complete, with the registrant receiving cash. This is a non-core asset divestiture. Watch for potential use of proceeds, such as capital returns or reinvestment, and any impact on future earnings.

TNONW.brief: Tenon Medical received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on May 21, 2026, for failing to meet the $2.5M minimum stockholders' equity requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), reporting $1.895M in equity as of March 31, 2026. The company has 45 days, until July 6, 2026, to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq can grant up to 180 additional days to cure. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The notice does not immediately affect trading. Notably, the company also does not meet alternative compliance standards (market value or net income). Key to watch: whether Tenon can submit an acceptable plan and secure an extension, or risk eventual delisting, which could pressure the stock. No deal terms or activist filer are involved.

EIIA.brief: Eagle Point Institutional Income Fund launched a modified Dutch auction issuer tender offer to repurchase up to 5% of its NAV. Shareholders may tender shares at a price equal to the NAV per share calculated as of the Valuation Date, with no stated premium. The offer commenced May 28, 2026; notice and withdrawal deadline is June 26; Valuation Date is June 30; Acceptance Date is July 27. The board has not publicly recommended action. No advisor named. The purchase will be funded from available cash. Overhang is negligible given the cap; the deal is non-contested. Watch the take-up rate and NAV calculation date for any deviation.

AERTW.brief: Aeries Technology, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that on March 31, 2026 it received a Nasdaq Staff determination that its securities will be delisted due to non-compliance with the minimum bid price requirement (Bid Price Rule). The company had been granted a 180-day grace period ending March 30, 2026 but failed to regain compliance and is ineligible for a second grace period because it does not meet the minimum stockholders' equity standard for initial listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market. Aeries intends to request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel, which will automatically stay any delisting action pending the Panel's decision. No specific terms, premiums, or deal mechanics were disclosed. What to watch: outcome of the hearing, any extension granted, or the company's exploration of alternative listing venues.

ALBT.brief: On April 15, 2026, Avalon GloboCare Corp. disclosed in an 8-K that Nasdaq notified it of non-compliance with the minimum bid price rule (Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)). The company's common stock closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days from March 1 to April 14, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The company has 180 calendar days, until October 12, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a $1.00 closing bid for 10 consecutive days. It may request a second 180-day period or effect a reverse stock split. Failure could lead to delisting and an appeal hearing. The risk-arb angle hinges on whether management pursues a reverse split to cure the deficiency.

GYRE.brief: Gyre Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting completion of its acquisition of Cullgen Inc. via a merger, with Cullgen surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary. The all-stock transaction valued Cullgen at approximately $300 million. At closing, shares of Cullgen capital stock were converted into shares of Gyre’s Series B Convertible Preferred Stock or common stock based on an exchange ratio of 0.4753. The merger is intended to qualify as a tax-free reorganization under Section 368(a). No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee was disclosed. The deal closed on May 4, 2026. Watch for integration execution and potential dilution from the preferred stock terms.

MYSZ.brief: My Size, Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that on March 2, 2026, it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has 180 calendar days (through August 31, 2026) to regain compliance by having a closing bid price of at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, it may qualify for a second 180-day period. The company is evaluating options, including a reverse stock split. The stock continues trading under 'MYSZ' with no immediate delisting. Risk-arb angle: monitor bid price and potential reverse-split implementation; speculative, no deal terms.

NCL.brief: Northann Corp. (NCL) filed an 8-K disclosing that NYSE American accepted its compliance plan (the Plan) for continued listing under Section 1003(a)(i) of the Company Guide, extending the cure period to June 8, 2027. The company initially received a non-compliance notice on December 11, 2025, and submitted a Plan by January 7, 2026. No price, premium, or deal terms apply. Common stock remains listed and traded on NYSE American under symbol NCL during the Plan Period. Risks include insufficient progress or failure to regain compliance by the deadline, which could trigger delisting proceedings.

PULM.brief: Pulmatrix, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement in connection with its acquisition of Eos Senolytixs Inc. The merger will involve the issuance of Pulmatrix common stock to Eos shareholders, with exact terms including the exchange ratio and implied value to be detailed in the proxy/prospectus. The board recommends the deal, and financial advisors have not been named in the excerpt. The transaction structure includes the assumption of Eos stock options and warrants, subject to regulatory approval under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act. The expected close is uncertain, pending SEC review and shareholder votes. Key watchpoints: shareholder approval timeline and potential overhang from Eos stock conversion.

PUBC.brief: Purebase Corp filed an 8-K reporting a binding MOU with CoreTer LLC, which is owned by its CEO A. Scott Dockter. Under the MOU, Purebase receives 20% of net proceeds from CoreTer's mining agreement with Dexter Mining LLC in exchange for waiving corporate opportunity claims. No price per share, premium, or deal value is stated; consideration is a proceeds share. The agreement is subject to a definitive asset transfer agreement and may terminate on change of control or CEO removal. This appears to be a related-party arrangement, not a classic acquisition or strategic review. What to watch: board/advisor involvement and definitive terms.

BZFDW.brief: BuzzFeed, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting two share purchase agreements dated June 17, 2026. Under the first, Allen Family Digital, LLC (Byron Allen's family office affiliate) purchased 4,000,000 shares (2,173,155 newly issued, 1,826,845 treasury) at $1.44/share, the June 15 closing price, for ~$5.8 million. Under the second, individual purchasers bought 216,999 shares at the same price. Both were board-approved, exempt under Section 4(a)(2), and closed June 18. This private placement is not a transformative special situation; it is a routine capital raise with no premium or change of control.

UAN.brief: CVR Partners, LP filed an 8-K on March 3, 2026, disclosing the death of director Brian A. Goebel on February 20, 2026. His passing reduced the board to five members (two independent) and the audit committee to two independent members, violating NYSE Section 303A.07(a) requiring a three-member independent audit committee. The company notified the NYSE on February 25 and received a non-compliance notice on March 3. It has initiated a search for a new independent director to fill the audit committee seat. No deal terms or activist involvement are present. Watch for the timing and appointment of a qualified independent director to restore NYSE compliance.

MNSBP.brief: MainStreet Bancshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing open-market share repurchases of 207,000 common shares at an average price of $24.09/share since Q2 start. The stock is slightly below tangible book value of $25.63 as of March 31, 2025. The repurchases are conducted under Rule 10b-18 with no obligation to continue, and the program can be suspended or discontinued at any time. This is a routine capital return disclosure rather than a transformative special situation. No material event risk or arbitrage angle; watch for ongoing buyback pace as a signal of management's view on valuation.

VNOM.brief: Viper Energy filed a prospectus supplement to its automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3 for the sale of up to 3,691,796 shares of Class A common stock by a selling stockholder. The filing includes an opinion of Latham & Watkins LLP on the legality of the securities. No terms such as price per share or premium are disclosed; the registrant is the issuer facilitating a secondary sale. This is a routine shelf takedown, not a transformative special situation. The event is a capital markets transaction with no advisory, board recommendation, or structural complexity beyond equity distribution. Watch for selling shareholder identity and potential market overhang.

GATX.brief: GATX Corporation filed an 8-K on July 1, 2026, disclosing the exercise of the first call option under a pre-existing Call Option Agreement to acquire an additional interest in GABX Leasing Holding LLC (Blocker), increasing its indirect interest in the GABX Leasing LLC joint venture from 30% to approximately 33.535%. The remaining ~66.465% is held by Brookfield Infrastructure partners. Concurrently, the Blocker LLC agreement was amended and restated, granting GATX joint approval rights over fundamental actions and admitting it as a member while Brookfield remains Managing Member. The Call Option Agreement was previously filed on January 5, 2026. This is a contractual step-up, not a transformative event—no price, premium, or tender terms disclosed. Watch for subsequent call exercises per the option agreement schedule.

SWKHL.brief: SWK Holdings Corp filed Form 15 to terminate its SEC registration after merging with Runway Growth Finance Corp. The merger agreement was signed October 9, 2025, and the merger closed on April 6, 2026. Shareholders received consideration under the merger agreement (terms not specified in this filing). The board of SWK approved the deal; no advisor named. As a result, SWK has no record holders of its common stock. The filing is a procedural deregistration post-closing. What to watch: no further public filings or trading expected; risk-arb focus is on merger consideration delivery and potential appraisal rights.

RSKD.brief: Riskified Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $75 million share repurchase program (a 'distribution' under Israeli law) on June 4, 2026, supplementing an existing $375 million authorization of which ~$344.4 million had been used. The program is subject to completion of Israeli regulatory procedures, including a 30-day creditor objection period. Repurchases may be executed in open-market or private transactions under Rule 10b5-1, funded from cash reserves. No price or timing is specified. Watch: regulatory clearance timeline and pace of buyback execution as a signal of management's view on intrinsic value.

XWEL.brief: XWELL, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Securities Purchase Agreement to sell all equity interests in its subsidiaries XpresSpa Holdings (airport spa retail) and XpresTest (airport bio-surveillance testing) to Express Wellness Group, LLC. Base purchase price is $13M subject to customary closing adjustments (net working capital, indebtedness, expenses, cash). At closing, $2.65M of the price will be placed in escrow for post-closing indemnities and adjustments. Outstanding XpresTest restricted stock awards will vest and be cancelled for cash based on agreed per-share valuation. XWELL retains its ex-airport health/wellness retail locations. The transaction involves standard representations and warranties. Watch for regulatory clearance, closing conditions, and any competing bids that might surface.

VICI.brief: VICI Properties filed an S-4/A registering shares to be issued in connection with its acquisition of Golden Entertainment, Inc. VICI will issue VICI common stock to holders of Golden common stock as merger consideration. The board of Golden has recommended the transaction; no advisor named in the excerpt. The merger will be effected under Minnesota law; VICI common stock is to be listed on NYSE. The transaction is subject to regulatory approval and Golden stockholder vote. What to watch: execution risk from regulatory clearance and stockholder approval; risk-arb spread will depend on VICI share price volatility.

ITRN.brief: Ituran Location and Control Ltd. filed a Form 6-K to announce a $10 million cash dividend ($0.50 per share) approved by its Board of Directors for Q1 2026. The dividend, net of 20% withholding tax under Israeli tax law, will be paid on July 8, 2026 to shareholders of record as of June 24, 2026. The Board confirmed the distribution meets Israeli law criteria and will not impair operations; retained earnings post-distribution are $221.3 million, with $108 million cash on hand and no bank debt. This is a regular quarterly capital return, not a special situation.

SSYS.brief: Stratasys Ltd. filed Form 6-K announcing a definitive agreement to acquire Markforged, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Nano Dimension, for $42.5 million in all-cash consideration. Nano Dimension will retain Markforged's Metal Binder Jetting product line. The transaction is expected to close in H2 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions. No board recommendation or advisors are named in the filing. The acquisition is expected to be accretive and add positive adjusted EBITDA within the first year after close. Watch for regulatory clearance and revenue contribution from remaining FFF business.

VOXR.brief: VOX Royalty Corp. filed a Form 6-K announcing its subsidiary Vox Cayman agreed to sell its capped gold offtake stream (i-80 Stream) to i-80 Gold Corp. for $4.8 million, satisfied through issuance of freely tradeable i-80 common shares. The stream covered 100% of gold production from Ruby Hill, Cove & Granite Creek up to 40k oz/yr through Dec 2028; Vox acquired it Sep 2025 in a portfolio purchase. Vox's carrying value was ~$2.6M, implying ~2x multiple. Closing expected by June 30, 2026. Watch for timely share issuance and Vox's redeployment of capital into uncapped assets.

BBCQW.brief: Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II filed an 8-K reporting Amendment No. 2 to its business combination agreement with Pasqal Holding SAS (French quantum computing firm). The amendment revises the post-combination board composition to 9 directors (5 must be French/European non-U.S. residents) and adjusts the equity incentive plan terms. This is a de-SPAC transaction, with Bleichroeder as the blank-check issuer. No price/share, premium, or close date are stated; the filing focuses on governance modifications. Watch for shareholder vote timing and any redemptions, as typical SPAC risk-arb centers on deal completion and trust account dynamics.

PMTS.brief: CPI Card Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a partial redemption of its 10.000% senior secured notes due 2029. On July 2, 2026, the Company issued a notice to redeem $26.5 million of the $265.0 million aggregate principal, at a redemption price of 103.000% of par plus accrued interest, with redemption effective July 15, 2026. This is a routine debt management action, not a special situation. No board recommendation or advisors are named. Watch for any impact on leverage ratios or future refinancing steps.

CMLSQ.brief: Cumulus Media Inc. confirmed its Joint Prepackaged Chapter 11 Plan of Reorganization on April 15, 2026, after filing voluntary petitions on March 4, 2026. The Plan, modified on April 13, 2026, provides for debt restructuring and ownership reorganization, with FCC approval pending. The company operates as debtor-in-possession. No price per share or premium is stated. Stake and consideration details are not specified. The effective date awaits regulatory approvals. Watch for FCC clearance timeline and potential creditor disputes over recoveries; risk-arb centers on regulatory and execution risk.

FLYE.brief: Fly-E Group, Inc. disclosed on an 8-K that on April 17, 2026, it received a deficiency letter from Nasdaq for failing to hold an annual meeting within 12 months of its fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, violating Listing Rule 5620(a). The letter is not an imminent delisting notice. The company has 45 days (until June 1, 2026) to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant an exception until September 28, 2026. The delay was administrative. No board recommendation or advisor named. Key watch: ability to convene a shareholder meeting within the grace period and avoid potential delisting proceedings.

GLED-RI.brief: GalaxyEdge Acquisition Corp (a SPAC) filed an 8-K announcing a business combination agreement with Rongcheng Group Limited. Pursuant to the merger, GLED will merge into a subsidiary (Purchaser), and Merger Sub will merge with Rongcheng, making Rongcheng a wholly owned subsidiary of Purchaser. Existing GLED shareholders receive one Purchaser share per GLED share. Rongcheng shareholders receive 35,000,000 Purchaser shares valued at $10.00 per share ($350 million aggregate). The SPAC merger and acquisition merger occur concurrently. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Watch for shareholder approval, the SPAC redemption deadline, and any impact from trust proceeds on the final valuation.

PAYC.brief: Paycom Software filed an 8-K announcing a $0.375/share quarterly cash dividend and a new $2.0 billion stock repurchase plan with no expiration date. The dividend will be paid June 8, 2026 to holders of record May 26, 2026. Repurchases may be executed via open-market, privately negotiated, or Rule 10b5-1 programs at the board's discretion. No break fee or premium applies; this is a pure capital-return initiative. The company may use cash or its credit facility to fund repurchases. Watch for execution pace and any suspension triggers based on market conditions; no risk-arb angle as there is no M&A.

TMRC.brief: Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (TMRC) entered a definitive merger agreement on March 4, 2026, with USA Rare Earth, Inc. (USAR). Outstanding TMRC shares will be exchanged for a pro-rata portion of 3,823,328 USAR shares (valued at $24.64/share as of June 18, 2026), effectively an all-stock consideration. The TMRC board recommends approval; no advisor named. The transaction involves two successive mergers, resulting in TMRC becoming a wholly owned USAR subsidiary, with fractional shares paid in cash. Expected close is Q3 2026, subject to majority stockholder vote at a special meeting on July 28, 2026. Risk-arb focus: stock consideration creates valuation uncertainty tied to USAR's share price; watch stockholder approval and any dissenter rights.

Z.brief: Zillow Group filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 Annual Meeting results and an amendment to its 2026 repurchase program. The board amended the program to bar share repurchases that would cause any single shareholder to own more than 45% of voting power; no current shareholder exceeds that threshold. The original program authorized up to $1.25 billion in repurchases of Class A common stock or Class C capital stock. All other terms remain unchanged. This is a share buyback program update, not a tender offer or going-private transaction. Watch for potential 13D filings by large holders or any stock price reaction to the ownership cap.

CL.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE to remove from listing and registration the entire class of Colgate-Palmolive Co's 0.500% Notes due 2026, effective at the opening on March 17, 2026. The action follows the redemption or maturity of the notes on March 6, 2026, as permitted under SEC Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading of the notes was suspended on March 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This is a routine delisting for matured debt; no premium or shareholder vote applies. The filing confirms the final extinguishment of the security. Watch for any residual claims or conversion terms; risk-arb implications are nil.

BILI.brief: Bilibili Inc. filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release and voluntary HKEX announcement updating its two-year $300 million share repurchase program adopted in June 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the company had repurchased 1.9 million listed securities at a total cost of ~$31.3 million under the program, and 4.8 million securities for ~$100.1 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026. No specific price per share, premium, board recommendation, or advisor was disclosed. This is an ordinary capital return update with no special situation mechanics, overhang, or regulatory clock. Watch for future repurchase pace as an indicator of management's capital allocation confidence.

BGLWW.brief: Blue Gold Ltd filed a Form 6-K on July 9, 2026, disclosing strategic balance sheet optimization transactions to regain Nasdaq compliance. The registrant entered a Deed of Settlement and Conversion converting $3.6M in accounts payable and a $3.5M deposit assignment into 7,117 shares of Series A Perpetual Convertible Preferred Stock, convertible into 7.1M common shares (1:1,000), capped at 19.99% of outstanding common (subject to stockholder approval). The company also announced a reverse share split EGM on July 24, 2026. The transactions aim to increase shareholders' equity by ~$30M for continued listing. Watch for stockholder approval and Nasdaq compliance timeline.

DSX-WT.brief: Diana Shipping Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing an extension of its tender offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Genco Shipping & Trading not already owned by Diana. The offer is $27.34 per share, comprising $24.80 cash plus one Diana share valued at $2.54, representing a 53% premium to Genco's undisturbed price. As of June 26, 10,583,484 shares (28.4% of outstanding not owned by Diana) were tendered. The offer is supported by $1.433 billion in committed financing from six banks with no financing condition. The extended tender expires July 10, 2026. Watch for potential negotiated deal with Genco board and regulatory clearance.

NAAS.brief: NaaS Technology Inc. (the Company) filed a Form 6-K reporting its entry into a Share Acquisition Agreement to acquire 100% of China Newlink Holding Limited from Newlink Digital Energy Holding Limited, an affiliate of its controlling shareholder. The aggregate consideration is US$15 million, satisfied by issuing 16 billion Class A ordinary shares (5 million ADSs) at a reference price of $3.00 per ADS. The acquisition is a related-party transaction, not subject to shareholder approval, relying on home country practices. Closing conditions include establishing a WFOE, securing data assets, regulatory approvals, and Audit Committee fairness determination. Watch for regulatory and shareholder scrutiny given related-party nature and share issuance.

ALLR.brief: Allarity Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting results of its June 26, 2026 annual meeting. Seven proposals were voted, including election of director Jesper Hoiland (3.75M for, 187k withheld), ratification of auditor Wolf Company P.C. (8.33M for), amendment to 2021 equity plan increasing authorized shares from 1,521,990 to 2,021,990 (3.08M for), advisory say-on-pay (3.62M for), approval of share issuance under a January 2026 common stock purchase agreement with Tumim Stone Capital LLC (3.17M for), a failed officer liability limitation amendment (3.52M for, below required majority), and approval of meeting adjournment (7.31M for). Also disclosed that June 30, 2026, the Nasdaq Staff determined the company regained compliance with the minimum bid price rule. The filing is a routine shareholder meeting report and a compliance update, not a special situation event requiring further analysis.

AACBU.brief: Artius II Acquisition Inc., a SPAC, filed an 8-K regarding an amended working capital promissory note with its sponsor, Artius II Acquisition Partners LLC. The note, originally up to $1M convertible, was restated to remove the conversion feature, making it payable solely in cash. Separately, the company disclosed it previously received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain 300 public holders (Listing Rule 5452(a)(2)(A)). Nasdaq accepted the company's compliance plan on March 23, 2026, granting an extension to August 31, 2026, to regain compliance. No deal consideration, premium, or board recommendation is implicated. Watch for the company's progress in regaining public holder count and any potential business combination deadline extensions.

BYND.brief: Beyond Meat filed an 8-K reporting entry into warrant agreements with Big Geyser, Inc. in connection with a distribution agreement. The warrants allow Big Geyser to purchase up to 4,166,667 shares (0.8% of outstanding common stock) at $0.60 per share. This is an equity-linked incentive for a distribution partner, not a standalone special situation. The filing describes terms of two tranches but no board recommendation or advisors are named. Warrants are exercisable for 18 months and are not transferable. This is a routine commercial agreement with a warrant component, not a transformative event.

BRLSW.brief: Borealis Foods received a Nasdaq notice on July 2, 2026, for failing the minimum $35M Market Value of Listed Securities (MVLS) requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(2), based on 30 consecutive business-day non-compliance. The company also does not meet alternative standards for stockholders' equity or net income. No immediate delisting effect; shares and warrants continue trading. Borealis has a 180-day cure period until December 29, 2026, to regain compliance by closing MVLS at or above $35M for 10-20 consecutive business days. Failure may lead to delisting and appeal rights. Monitor compliance progress and potential reverse stock split or other remedies.

COHN.brief: Cohen & Co Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its operating subsidiary owns a portion of and serves as managing member of the sponsor of Columbus Circle Capital Corp. II (CMIIU), a SPAC that on June 26, 2026 entered into a definitive business combination agreement with Elroy Air, Inc. Under the agreement, a merger sub will merge with Elroy Air, making it a wholly owned subsidiary of the SPAC. Cohen Company Capital Markets (CCM), a division of Cohen's broker-dealer subsidiary, acted as lead underwriter for the SPAC's IPO and is joint financial advisor and co-placement agent for this business combination. The transaction is subject to shareholder approvals and customary conditions. Watch for shareholder vote timing and potential redemptions.

HWNI.brief: High Wire Networks, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Securities Purchase Agreement with GHS Investments, LLC, under which it issued 46 shares of Series G Preferred Stock at $1,000/share for $34,000 cash plus a 12-share equity incentive. The preferred stock has a stated value of $1,200, carries a 12% dividend, and is convertible into common stock. An additional 70 shares may be sold in future closings. This is a private placement of equity securities, not a special-situation event like a tender offer, going-private transaction, or restructuring. No premium, board recommendation, or advisor is disclosed. This appears to be a routine capital-raising arrangement filed under Items 1.01 and 3.02.

IVDAW.brief: Iveda Solutions disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency letter on March 6, 2026, noting its common stock failed to maintain the $1 minimum bid price for 30 consecutive business days, violating Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has 180 calendar days, until September 2, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a closing bid price of at least $1 for ten consecutive business days. No board recommendation or advisor is mentioned. If non-compliance persists, Nasdaq may delist the shares; the company may appeal to a Hearings Panel. Watch for bid price movements and any potential reverse stock split or other curative actions.

NRDY.brief: Nerdy Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that on March 5, 2026, the NYSE notified it of non-compliance with Section 802.01C because its Class A common stock averaged below $1.00 over 30 consecutive trading days. The company has a six-month cure period and intends to regain compliance, potentially via a reverse stock split requiring stockholder approval by the 2027 annual meeting. It also noted sufficient liquidity ($47.9M cash, plus a term loan) and said the notice does not affect operations or listing. Watch for any reverse split proposal or price recovery; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a listing standard cure, not a transaction.

OPAD.brief: Offerpad Solutions disclosed on March 3, 2026, that it received an NYSE notice of noncompliance with Section 802.01C due to its Class A common stock's average closing price falling below $1.00 over 30 consecutive trading days. The NYSE notice does not trigger immediate delisting; the company has a six-month cure period. To regain compliance, Offerpad may consider a reverse stock split, subject to stockholder approval at its next annual meeting. During the cure period, the stock will remain listed and tradable.
