BTSGU.brief: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an underwriting agreement dated June 3, 2026 for a secondary offering of 14,999,771 shares of common stock at $58.75 per share by selling stockholders, including KKR Phoenix Aggregator L.P. and management stockholders. The company did not receive proceeds except from stock option exercises, and repurchased 1,026,465 shares from the underwriter. The offering was made under an existing Form S-3ASR. While the share repurchase is a capital return element, the filing primarily discloses a secondary sale by existing holders, not a transformative special situation. Watch for any further KKR stake reduction or insider selling; no risk-arb angle applicable.

LIPO.brief: Lipella Pharmaceuticals Inc. and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on March 30, 2026, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania. The company intends to pursue a 363 sale process to maximize value for creditors. No stake, price, premium, or advisor was disclosed. Trading in common stock during the case is highly speculative and may bear little relation to recovery. First-day relief motions are expected to maintain operations, including cash management and employee wages. What to watch: 363 sale timeline, credit bids, and any stalking horse bidder emergence; risk-arb perspective is absent given equity likely wiped out.

ORMP.brief: Oramed Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K reporting two events. First, board approved amendments to its bylaws regarding record dates and written consent procedures. Second, the company agreed with Scilex Holding to extend maturity of senior secured promissory notes (Tranche A ~$29.5M, Tranche B ~$6.7M) plus a $1M cash extension fee payable by Scilex. No special-situation deal terms such as price, premium, or change of control are involved. This is a routine operational and debt extension filing.

RNGE.brief: Range Impact, Inc. filed an 8-K to disclose its indirect subsidiary Range Sky View Land, LLC entering into an Operating Agreement with Time Complexity WV, LLC to form a 50/50 joint venture, Time Complexity Appalachia, LLC, for a power generation and data center project at the Fola mine site in West Virginia. Neither member is required to make initial cash capital contributions; future capital needs may be funded by member loans secured by JV assets on a pari passu basis. Management comprises a three-person board with each member appointing one manager and the third mutually agreed. This filing is not a traditional special situation (e.g., merger or acquisition), but rather a joint venture formation. Key watchpoints include project development milestones and debt structuring. No premium, price, or closing date disclosed.

SRJN.brief: Spire Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its sale of all membership interests in Belle Butte LLC (which owns Spire Storage West and Spire Storage Salt Plains) to Subterra Energy Borrower, an affiliate of I Squared Capital, for total consideration of $657 million. The consideration consists of $607 million cash at closing (subject to customary adjustments) and $50 million deferred consideration payable by September 30, 2027. The board approved the transaction; no advisor named. The deal closed following HSR Act waiting period expiration and other customary conditions. Net proceeds will support regulated utility operations, capex, and debt reduction. Watch for use of proceeds and any further restructuring.

SNAL.brief: Snail, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Nasdaq Staff Determination to delist its Class A common stock for failing to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Rule 5550(a)(2)) by June 29, 2026, and for not meeting continued listing standards (Rule 5550(b)). The company intends to request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel to appeal, which will automatically stay delisting pending the hearing and any extension granted. No terms, premium, or close date are specified. What to watch: the hearing outcome and whether Snail can demonstrate compliance or secure an extension to avoid delisting.

EMAT.brief: On May 21, 2026, Evolution Metals Technologies Corp. received a Nasdaq notice for failure to timely file its March 31, 2026 Form 10-Q, violating Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The company filed the Form 10-Q on May 22, 2026, curing the deficiency, and received a Nasdaq compliance notice on May 26, 2026. The event is a routine listing compliance matter with no impact on trading. The delisting risk is resolved; no premium, deal terms, or activist involvement. Monitor for any future periodic filing delays.

CMBT.brief: CMB.TECH NV filed a Form 6-K reporting the sale of two Suezmax vessels (Brest and Brugge, each 156,851 DWT, built 2023), generating a capital gain of approximately $100.5 million in Q3 2026. The sale price and buyer are not disclosed. Deliveries to the new owner are expected in Q3 2026. The board, through CEO Alexander Saverys, characterized the sale as opportunistic to unlock value at an attractive point in the cycle, with proceeds to be deployed per the company's capital allocation strategy. No financial advisor or break fee is mentioned. This is an asset divestiture, not a corporate-level restructuring. Watch for subsequent capital allocation announcements and future vessel sale updates.

POET.brief: POET Technologies filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of a US$400 million registered direct offering to a single institutional investor. The company issued 19,047,620 common shares and warrants for 19,047,620 shares at $21.00 per unit, a 2% premium to the $20.57 closing price. The warrants are exercisable at $26.25 for three years. Proceeds will fund manufacturing expansion, R&D, acquisitions, and working capital. The non-brokered structure avoided underwriting fees. Watch for dilution from warrant exercise and execution of the capacity scale-up plan.

PLUT.brief: Plutus Financial Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting a Third Amendment to its Merger Agreement with Choco Up Group Holdings Ltd, extending the Outside Date from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026. The original agreement, dated July 9, 2025, involves Plutus acquiring all outstanding equity interests in Choco Up in exchange for newly issued Class A and Class B ordinary shares in a transaction exempt from SEC registration. The extension is to allow additional time for satisfying closing conditions, including Nasdaq approval. No deal terms (price per share, premium) are disclosed. What to watch: Whether Nasdaq approval is obtained by the new deadline; risk-arb focus on regulatory timeline.

ACNT.brief: Ascent Industries Co. filed an 8-K disclosing the adoption of a written trading plan under Rule 10b5-1 to repurchase up to 1,750,000 shares daily at specified price targets. The plan is effective June 29, 2026 through August 10, 2026. The repurchase plan is part of the company's stock repurchase program, executed by a broker to allow repurchases during blackout periods. No board recommendation or advisor is named. All purchases will be disclosed in periodic filings. Watch for execution pace and price range; no risk-arb angle as this is an issuer buyback.

MKC-V.brief: McCormick & Co. filed an 8-K regarding a Term Loan Agreement for up to $2.0 billion to finance its pending combination with Unilever's foods business via a merger agreement dated March 31, 2026. The term loan bears floating interest (Term SOFR + 0.750%-1.500% or Base Rate + 0.000%-0.500%) and matures three years post-close; it includes a 3.75x interest coverage covenant. Citibank is administrative agent. The ticking fee of 0.10% starts July 29, 2026. Watch for regulatory approvals and merger closing conditions; risk-arb spread hinges on deal certainty and financing terms.

TNMG.brief: TNL Mediagene (Nasdaq: TNMG) filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq staff delisting determination letter on June 22, 2026. The delisting action is based on the company's ordinary shares closing below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days (May 7–June 18, 2026), violating Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). Because a reverse stock split occurred in the prior year, no compliance period is available under Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv). An additional basis is non-compliance with the $2,500,000 minimum stockholders' equity requirement (Rule 5550(b)(1)). The company intends to request a hearing before a Nasdaq Hearings Panel, which will automatically stay suspension and Form 25-NSE filing pending a decision. There is no certainty of continued listing.

AYTU.brief: AYTU BioPharma, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the mutual termination of its exclusive license agreement (Metadate Agreement) with Lannett Company, Inc., originally entered in 2022 and amended twice. The termination is effective June 23, 2026, via a Termination Agreement. AYTU may sell existing inventory and will continue royalty reporting/payments until sales cease; net revenue from Metadate CD for Q ended March 31, 2026 was only $49,000. No financial terms of the termination were disclosed, and the agreement's full text will be filed in the 10-K. No advisors or break fees mentioned. Watch for any litigation or impact on AYTU's product pipeline.

CTSO.brief: CytoSorbents Corp (CTSO) disclosed on June 29, 2026, receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the $35 million minimum Market Value of Listed Securities (MVLS) requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(2). The company has 180 calendar days, until December 28, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining MVLS at or above $35 million for at least ten consecutive business days. Alternatively, it may consider increasing stockholders' equity to at least $2.5 million. The notice does not trigger immediate delisting. If unresolved, Nasdaq will issue a delisting notification, subject to appeal. Watch for the company's compliance strategy and any reverse-stock-split or capital-raising actions.

FUSEW.brief: Fusemachines Inc. filed an 8-K to correct beneficial ownership information for director Timothy Gocher, who previously over-reported shares held by Dolma Impact Fund I. Gocher lacks voting/dispositive power over those shares. The filing includes an updated 5%+ ownership table based on 28,985,302 shares outstanding as of July 1, 2026. No transaction, premium, or strategic event is involved—this is a routine compliance correction, not a special situation.

RKTO.brief: Hoth Therapeutics, Inc. filed an 8-K to report changing its name to Rocket One Inc., effective May 26, 2026, via a Certificate of Amendment filed in Nevada. No shareholder approval was required. The common stock trading symbol will change to RKTO on Nasdaq starting May 28, 2026. The CUSIP number remains unchanged, and no shareholder rights are affected. This is a routine corporate name/symbol change with no financial terms, deal structure, or special-situation event.

AEON.brief: AEON Biopharma received a second NYSE American non-compliance notice for failing Section 1003(a)(ii) (stockholders' equity ≥$4M after three of four fiscal years of losses). As of Dec 31, 2025, AEON reported a ~$55M stockholders' deficit. The company remains under a previously accepted compliance plan (Plan Period until Aug 3, 2026) and its Class A common stock continues trading on NYSE American with a .BC indicator. AEON intends to execute its plan to regain compliance by the deadline but faces uncertainty. Watch for periodic NYSE American reviews and potential delisting if the plan fails.

ARAI.brief: Arrive AI Inc. disclosed on June 2, 2026 that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Listing Rule 5450(a)(1)) for 30 consecutive business days. The notice has no immediate delisting effect. The company has 180 calendar days, until November 30, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a closing bid price of at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, it may qualify for a second 180-day period if it meets other listing standards. Management is evaluating options, but noncompliance could lead to delisting and a hearing. Risk-arb watch: monitor stock price trajectory and potential reverse stock split or other remedial actions.

CITR.brief: CitroTech Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into Stock Exchange and Stockholders Agreements on May 28, 2026. The issuer reacquired 1,666,667 shares of Series A Preferred Stock, issuing 103,558 shares of Series C Convertible Preferred Stock to BoltRock Holdings at closing and agreeing to issue 467,012 shares to TC Special Investments after 18 months or upon a change of control (including board appointment of Theodore S. Ralston). No price per share, premium, or board recommendation is stated. The transactions eliminate all Series A Preferred Stock and grant board observer/registration rights. Watch for future issuances and potential control shifts.

JENA-UN.brief: JENA Acquisition Corp II disclosed on April 1, 2026, it received a NYSE staff notice for non-compliance with Section 802.01A, which requires maintaining a minimum of 300 public shareholders. Within 45 days, the company must submit a business plan to NYSE demonstrating how it expects to regain compliance within 18 months. The NYSE then has 45 days to review the plan. The notice does not immediately affect listing or trading. As a blank-check SPAC, this listing-standard deficiency highlights ongoing challenges. What to watch: whether the plan is accepted; if not, delisting risk could pressure the stock.

MTNB.brief: Matinas BioPharma Holdings received an NYSE American notice on June 24, 2026, for non-compliance with Section 1003(a)(ii), requiring ≥$4M stockholders' equity, given $3.022M equity and losses in five of the last five fiscal years. Previously flagged under Section 1003(a)(iii) ($6M threshold). The company's May 4 plan to regain compliance was accepted, with a plan period through October 2, 2027. During this period, NYSE American will monitor progress; failure to comply by the deadline or make sufficient progress may trigger delisting proceedings. What to watch: execution of the plan to boost equity; any capital raise or restructuring efforts.

VEEE.brief: Twin Vee PowerCats reincorporated from Delaware to Nevada effective April 10, 2026, following stockholder approval at the December 4, 2025 annual meeting. The reincorporation was effected via filings with both states' secretaries of state and adoption of a Nevada charter and bylaws. No consideration, premium, or price per share was involved; shares and outstanding equity awards automatically converted on a one-for-one basis with no change in terms. The company retains the same name, assets, liabilities, management, and Nasdaq listing (VEEE). The reincorporation shifts corporate governance from the DGCL to the Nevada Revised Statutes. Watch for potential shareholder litigation over Nevada's different fiduciary standards.

HVIIR.brief: Hennessy Capital Investment Corp. VII (HVII) filed an 8-K disclosing a Second Omnibus Amendment to its Business Combination Agreement and Promissory Note with ONE Nuclear Energy LLC. The amendment extends the outside date for closing the business combination from June 30, 2026, to August 15, 2026, and similarly extends the promissory note maturity. The maximum principal amount of loan advances under the note is increased from $300,000 to $316,975 for third-party expenses. No price per share, premium, or advisor is mentioned. As a SPAC, HVII is pursuing a de-SPAC transaction. Watch for shareholder vote and regulatory clearance ahead of the new deadline.

DCBG.brief: Dime Community Bancshares voluntarily filed Form 25 to delist its common stock, Series A preferred stock, and 9.000% subordinated notes from Nasdaq, effective April 6, 2026. The issuer certified compliance with Exchange Act Rule 12d2-2(c) for voluntary withdrawal. No consideration, premium, or shareholder vote was required. The delisting likely precedes a going-private transaction, merger, or capital restructuring. Watch for a subsequent Schedule 13E-3 or merger announcement detailing a buyout or consolidation. Risk-arb focus: whether a public-to-private premium emerges.

EICA.brief: The NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Eagle Point Income Co Inc.'s 8.00% Series C Term Preferred Stock due 2029. The exchange states the entire class was called for redemption on April 6, 2026, with funds deposited and made available to holders on that date. Trading was suspended April 6; the delisting becomes effective at the open on April 17, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named because this is an issuer-requested redemption and exchange-ordered removal. Mechanics: the security is being retired; no overhang or ownership split issues. Watch for the scheduled closing date and confirmation that all holders were paid.

INVZ.brief: Form 25-NSE filed voluntarily by Nasdaq Stock Market LLC to remove Innoviz Technologies Ltd. from listing and registration under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The delisting applies to the company's warrants, citing compliance with Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). No premium, price, or shareholder action is involved. The filing was made on April 6, 2026, with immediate effectiveness. No board recommendation or advisor is noted. This is a regulatory form to effect a securities delisting; there is no transactional component or risk-arb angle. Watch for any subsequent deregistration or going-private steps, though this filing alone is procedural.

HTCO.brief: High-Trend International Group announced on Form 6-K the cancellation and retirement of 630,000 Class A ordinary shares previously issued to Streeterville Capital under an October 2025 securities purchase agreement. The shares were returned after a payoff and termination agreement satisfied all obligations. The cancellation reduces issued and outstanding Class A shares by 630,000, improving the capital structure and reducing dilution. No price, premium, or valuation was disclosed. Chairman Christopher Nixon Cox highlighted the optimization of flexibility. This is a capital-return event via share retirement. No advisor named; the regulatory clock is immediate. Watch for potential further capital-management actions or dilution reduction.

SAIHW.brief: SAIHEAT Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 5, 2026, disclosing a change in control. Peng Zhang transferred one ordinary share of Energy Science Artist Holding Limited, representing 100% of its issued capital, to Longwin Global Limited for $1,000,000. This transaction resulted in Longwin Global becoming the sole controlling shareholder of SAIHEAT. The filing is a foreign private issuer report under Rule 13a-16. It does not detail a board recommendation or advisors. The share transfer effectively acquires the corporate entity that holds control of SAIHEAT. Watch for further regulatory filings and any strategic changes under the new controlling shareholder.

UYSCU.brief: UY Scuti Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) filed an 8-K reporting a $450,000 deposit into its trust account to extend the deadline to consummate a business combination with Isdera Group (Xinghui Automotive Technology). The deposit was loaned by Isdera HK Limited, an affiliate of the target, and the company expects to issue a promissory note. The extension is a routine procedural step to maintain its SPAC timeline under the trust agreement. No fundamental change in deal terms has been disclosed; the merger agreement remains pending. What to watch: regulatory proxy or shareholder vote on the business combination.

STKE.brief: SOL Strategies Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting its June 2026 monthly business update, including the closing of the Houdini Swap acquisition on June 1, 2026. No financial terms of the acquisition (price, consideration, or premium) were disclosed. The filing also details the integration of Houdini Swap with Jumper, debt settlement via sale of 65,001 SOL for CAD 5.75M, wind-down of non-Solana validators, and treasury holdings of 460,017 SOL. The board did not issue a recommendation, and no advisor was named. The acquisition closed without regulatory or structural complications. Watch for operational synergies from the Jumper integration and impact on revenue.

GNE.brief: Genie Energy Ltd. received an NYSE noncompliance notice on April 1, 2026, for failing to timely file its Form 10-K for FY2025 due to a restatement of audited financials for FY2023 and FY2024. Per NYSE Section 802.01E, the company has six months to file a remediation plan and regain compliance; trading continues under symbol GNE during this period. The board has not issued a formal recommendation. The delayed filing stems from a restatement effort rather than operational distress. Risk-arb watch: monitor filing timeline, NYSE acceptance of the plan, and any related financing or restructuring events.

RWAYI.brief: Runway Growth Finance Corp. filed an 8-K announcing a second quarter 2026 regular dividend of $0.33 per share, declared by the board on May 6, 2026. The record date is May 18, 2026, with payment on or about June 2, 2026. The company intends to distribute substantially all available earnings quarterly. This is a routine capital return declaration by the issuer, not tied to any special event such as a tender or activist campaign. What to watch: consistency of future dividend payments aligns with BDC sector norms; no risk-arb angle exists.

CLST.brief: Catalyst Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing that Lakeside Bancshares shareholders approved their pending merger and all regulatory approvals have been obtained. The merger agreement was dated April 7, 2026; Lakeside will merge into Catalyst and Lakeside Bank into Catalyst Bank, with Catalyst surviving. No financial terms (price/share, premium, break fee) or advisors were disclosed. The deals are expected to close on or about July 14, 2026, subject to remaining conditions. Watch for closing announcement and post-merger integration updates; risk-arb focuses on timing certainty given regulatory clearance is secured.

NUAIW.brief: New Era Energy & Digital filed an 8-K disclosing a pending settlement agreement with the U.S. Trustee for bankruptcy estates of Acacia Resources and Acacia Operating Company. The company will pay $1.0 million to resolve all claims by New Mexico, with dismissal with prejudice upon Bankruptcy Court approval. No admission of liability. The CEO faces separate individual claims. The settlement is contingent on court approval, with no specific timeline or advisor named. Watch for Bankruptcy Court hearing and potential impact on environmental liabilities.

INSW.brief: International Seaways, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 11, 2026, disclosing entry into an Equity Distribution Agreement to sell up to $200 million of its common stock in at-the-market offerings through agents BTIG, B. Riley, Clarksons, and Fearnleys. Each agent receives up to 3% commission. No shares have been sold yet. This ATM program is a capital-raising mechanism rather than a definitive capital return event. As an issuer shelf takedown with no immediate transaction, it does not fit standard special-situations categories. The filing is routine and not a special situation.

NWTG.brief: Newton Golf Company, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into Exchange Agreements with holders of existing convertible promissory notes. On July 6, 2026, the Company issued an aggregate of 24,092.61 shares of newly designated Series A Convertible Preferred Stock at $1.00 per share in exchange for approximately $2.3 million of existing notes, inclusive of accrued interest. The exchange was conducted at 105% of outstanding principal. The Series A Preferred Stock is convertible into common stock at $1.00 per share. The Chairman participated on the same terms. The exchange relied on SEC Rule 3(a)(9) exemption. A Registration Rights Agreement was also entered into, requiring an initial registration statement within 30 days. This exchange restructures the company's debt-to-equity, reducing leverage. Watch for potential shareholder dilution and conversion mechanics.

HTLM.brief: HomesToLife Ltd filed a Form 6-K on May 5, 2026, announcing the appointment of Zhengjie Jeff Chai as Chief Financial Officer, effective May 1, 2026. Mr. Chai had served as interim CFO since November 2025. His appointment follows a completed search. He will perform CFO duties via a services agreement between the company and HTL Furniture Inc., a related party. The filing includes the services agreement as an exhibit. No transaction, stake, price, premium, or board recommendation is involved. This is a routine management appointment, not a forced departure or abrupt change. What to watch: none — a routine corporate formality.

ACGCW.brief: ACP Holdings Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K to announce two routine operational updates: the separate trading of its units into Class A ordinary shares and warrants effective May 28, 2026, and the partial forfeiture of founder shares following the expiration of the over-allotment option from its April 2026 IPO. The IPO of 20,000,000 units at $10.00 each generated $200M gross; 1,461,600 over-allotment units were also issued. No transaction, acquisition, divestiture, or activist event is involved. This is a standard SPAC post-IPO housekeeping filing with no special-situation implications.

AMODW.brief: Alpha Modus Holdings entered an exchange agreement with the CEO's family trust on April 8, 2026. The trust will exchange 3,870,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock for 109,588,265 shares of Class A common stock. The issuance is conditioned on shareholder approval per Nasdaq Rule 5635; the trust agreed not to sell the common shares until June 13, 2026. The exchange aims to increase market value to regain compliance with Nasdaq's MVLS standard and reduce stockholders' deficit. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The deal is a non-cash recapitalization with potential dilution; overhang risk exists given the large share issuance. The regulatory clock depends on the shareholder vote and Nasdaq compliance review.

CABR.brief: Caring Brands, Inc. disclosed on April 7, 2026 that it received a Staff Delisting Determination letter from Nasdaq for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), which requires minimum $2.5M in stockholders' equity. The company reported equity of $2,091,324 in its FY2025 10-K. Nasdaq provided 45 days (until May 22, 2026) to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days (until October 4, 2026) to evidence compliance. Trading continues under 'CABR' with no immediate effect. The company intends to take all reasonable measures to regain compliance. Watch for the compliance plan submission and Nasdaq's acceptance decision; risk-arb angle: potential delisting overhang on equity value.

DEVSF.brief: On July 7, 2026, DevvStream Corp. and Karbon-X Corp. mutually terminated their October 28, 2024 Carbon Credit Forward Purchase Agreement. No performance had occurred under the agreement; the termination was without penalty, eliminating all further obligations. The agreement had called for Karbon-X to deliver carbon credits for USD $2,892,000 (at $120/unit), with DevvStream issuing 444,923 common shares at a deemed $6.50/share. This is a clean break with no financial or legal consequences. What to watch: whether DevvStream seeks alternative carbon credit supply; no risk-arb spread exists given the termination.

QETAU.brief: Quetta Acquisition Corp disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq Staff notice on April 30, 2026, indicating non-compliance with the minimum Market Value of Publicly Held Shares requirement ($15 million) under Listing Rule 5450(b)(2)(C). The deficiency was based on MVPHS over 30 consecutive business days through April 29. The company has 180 calendar days, until October 27, 2026, to regain compliance; it may also consider transferring to the Nasdaq Capital Market. No board recommendation or advisor named. The filing does not involve a business combination or tender offer. Key watchpoint: ability to boost MVPHS via reverse split, capital infusion, or listing transfer.

WORX.brief: SCWorx Corp. disclosed on Form 8-K that on April 7, 2026, Nasdaq notified the company of delisting from the Capital Market due to failure to maintain a minimum $1 bid price per Nasdaq Rule 5550(a)(2). The company received a 180-day extension on October 8, 2025, expiring April 6, 2026. Trading will be suspended at open on April 14, 2026, and a Form 25-NSE will be filed. SCWorx has appealed the delisting determination to a Nasdaq hearings panel and, on April 7, 2026, effected a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effective April 10, 2026, to regain compliance. The stock must close at or above $1.00 for ten consecutive trading days. The outcome of the appeal and split effectiveness remain uncertain; the risk-arb angle is binary—delisting vs. continued listing.

UPLD.brief: Upland Software disclosed via 8-K that on April 7, 2026 it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain a minimum $1.00 closing bid price for 30 consecutive business days (Rule 5450(a)(1)). The notice is not an immediate delisting; shares continue trading under UPLD. The company has 180 days, until October 5, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a $1.00 closing bid for 10 straight business days. If not cured, a second 180-day period may be available by transferring to the Nasdaq Capital Market, subject to meeting other listing standards. Failure could lead to delisting and a potential appeal to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel. Watch for any reverse stock split or other remediation plan.

SECZ.brief: Securitize Corp. (f/k/a Securitize Holdings, Inc.) completed its business combination with Cantor Equity Partners II, Inc. (CEPT) on July 1, 2026. Under the merger agreement, each CEPT ordinary share was converted into one share of PubCo common stock. Approximately 28.5% of CEPT Class A shares (6,842,508 shares) were redeemed for ~$10.60/share, totaling ~$72.5M. The combined entity renamed to Securitize Corp. trades on NYSE under SECZ. No board recommendation or advisor named. The reverse merger structure created a public listing for the crypto-finance platform; no break fee or earnout disclosed. Watch for post-merger shareholder overhang and integration of Securitize's tokenization business into the CEPT shell.

CAMT.brief: Camtek Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting a First Amendment to its Second Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement with Priortech Ltd. and Chroma ATE Inc. The amendment extends the agreement by five years to June 18, 2031, and lowers the demand registration threshold to 1% of outstanding share capital. The change is a routine contractual housekeeping matter, not a transformative special situation. It requires only corporate approvals. There are no deal terms, no premium, no transaction price, and no involvement of advisors. No risk-arb angle exists; the filing merely updates registration mechanics for existing shareholders.

JXG.brief: JX Luxventure Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of a share exchange agreement dated April 13, 2026, with Dazzly Investment, Inc. and its shareholders. The company acquired 3,500 shares (10% of total outstanding capital stock) of the seller. In exchange, JX Luxventure issued 2,783,046 shares of its common stock, $0.0001 par value, on a pro rata basis. Upon closing, the seller shareholders received 397,578 exchange shares each, and the company now has 12,059,877 common shares outstanding. The shares were issued under Section 4(a)(2) and/or Regulation S exemptions. No financial terms, premium, board recommendation, or advisors were disclosed. Watch for dilution impact and potential integration risks.

SPWRW.brief: SunPower Inc. reported entering into separate exchange agreements with holders of its 12.0%, 10.0%, and 7.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029. Holders agreed to exchange approximately $10.7 million of cash interest otherwise due on July 1, 2026, October 1, 2026, and January 1, 2027 for 19,300,991 shares of common stock. The exchange closed on July 1, 2026. No Board recommendation or advisors were named. Shares were issued under Section 4(a)(2) exemption. The transaction effectively converts near-term cash interest obligations into equity, reducing near-term cash outflows. Watch for potential dilution impact and any further debt restructuring moves.

AHRO.brief: Authentic Holdings, Inc. filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, effective April 15, 2026. The filing certifies that the company has fewer than 300 holders of record of its common and preferred stock (164 holders as of the notice date), satisfying the deregistration threshold. No tender offer, premium, or board recommendation is involved; the action is a voluntary deregistration based on reduced shareholder count. The company will suspend its duty to file periodic reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The risk-arb angle is minimal, as this is not a going-private transaction; watch for potential subsequent delisting or reduced liquidity.

CTRM.brief: Castor Maritime Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing the acquisition of a 2024-built Kamsarmax bulk carrier, M/V Magic Saturn, for $41.9 million from an unaffiliated third party, and the delivery of a previously announced 2023-built Kamsarmax, M/V Magic Jupiter, on June 29, 2026. Both acquisitions were funded with cash on hand. This is an ordinary-course vessel acquisition, not a transformative special situation. The filing is a routine press release for a foreign private issuer. No board recommendation, advisor, or structural details beyond cash funding are provided. What to watch: impact on fleet size and cash reserves; no risk-arb angle as it is a standard asset purchase.

TORO.brief: Toro Corp. filed a Form 6-K on June 5, 2026, reporting shareholder election results for a special dividend declared on April 22, 2026. The $0.90 per share dividend was payable in cash or common shares, with elections resulting in $3.8 million in cash and 5,707,246 shares distributed. The stock portion was priced at $3.8821 per share based on the 20-day VWAP. The dividend was paid on June 5, 2026, to holders of record as of May 4, 2026. Broadridge served as election agent. This capital return to shareholders reduces retained earnings and slightly increases share count via the stock component. Watch for potential dilution impact and future capital allocation decisions.

TCRT.brief: Alaunos Therapeutics received a Nasdaq notice on April 9, 2026, for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), requiring minimum $2.5M stockholders' equity; its reported equity was $2.153M, and it also fails alternative standards (market value or net income). The company has 45 days (until May 26, 2026) to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days to regain compliance. Failure could lead to delisting, with appeal rights via hearing. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch: plan acceptance, equity-restoration actions, and potential trading impact.

ETON.brief: Eton Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K reporting a supply and distribution agreement for U.S. commercialization rights to IMPAVIDO (miltefosine) from a Knight Therapeutics affiliate. Terms include $4.25 million in fixed fees through 2032, up to $4 million in milestone payments tied to net sales, and ongoing royalties (55% up to $7M annual sales, 50% above). Eton handles sales/marketing; supplier covers product/regulatory costs. Exclusive rights begin Sept 26, 2026. This is a product licensing deal, not a full acquisition or divestiture. Categorized as 'Other' since it expands the rare disease portfolio but does not fit standard special-situation categories.

YHC.brief: LQR House Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an additional closing under a Share Purchase Agreement with Fusion Five Continents Securities Limited, a New Zealand company, and seller Dean Shields. LQR acquired 3,000 shares (30%) for $39,000,000 in Tether (USDT), increasing its total stake to 54% (5,400 shares), achieving majority ownership. The agreement was initially disclosed in an April 2026 8-K, and no board recommendation or advisor is named in this filing. Consideration was paid in crypto USDT, not cash. This is a staged acquisition of a cross-border brokerage. Watch for regulatory approval (cross-border financial services) and settlement mechanics given USDT-based consideration; risk-arb centers on valuation of the remaining 46% and subsequent closings.

TRAW.brief: Traws Pharma, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a new prospectus supplement to its existing At The Market Offering Agreement with Citizens JMP Securities. The supplement allows the company to sell up to $3.13M of common shares under its current baby shelf limitation, down from the original $50M ATM facility. The shares are sold through Citizens as agent under an effective S-3 shelf. This is a routine financing update, not a special situation. No terms like price or premium are stated. No activist, M&A, or restructuring element. The filing is a procedural update to an existing equity distribution program.

BMNP.brief: Bitmine Immersion Technologies voluntarily delisted its common stock from NYSE American by filing Form 25 on April 16, 2026. The company, a finance services firm in the crypto assets space, cited compliance with NYSE rules and SEC Rule 12d2-2(c) for withdrawal. No price, premium, or stake was disclosed. CEO Chi Tsang signed the filing. The delisting is effective immediately, with no stated going-private transaction or shareholder vote. Structural notes: Form 25 triggers removal from listing and Section 12(b) registration; the company may continue trading over-the-counter. What to watch: potential subsequent going-private tender offer or regulatory filing for deregistration under Rule 12g-4.

CREG.brief: Smart Powerr Corp. disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq delisting notice on May 1, 2026, for failing to meet the $1.00 bid price rule for 30 consecutive days. The company is ineligible for a compliance period due to a reverse stock split within the prior year. Trading is set for suspension on May 12, 2026, unless the company appeals by May 8, 2026. Smart Powerr intends to timely request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel, which will automatically stay delisting pending the hearing and any granted extension. The company may consider another reverse stock split to regain compliance. Watch for hearing outcome and potential trading suspension risk.

FACTW.brief: FACT II Acquisition Corp., a Cayman Islands SPAC, filed Amendment No. 2 to its S-4 for a business combination with Precision Aerospace & Defense Group, Inc. (PAD). The merger implies an enterprise value not explicitly stated; PAD shareholders will receive shares in New PAD (renamed Precision Aerospace Defense), and FACT shareholders will vote on the deal. FACT will domesticate to Delaware prior to closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named in this filing. Structural notes: the deal lacks a stated break fee, price per share, or premium. The regulatory clock is tied to SEC effectiveness and shareholder vote. What to watch: the risk-arb angle hinges on SPAC redemption rates and PAD's financial disclosures in the final proxy.

GITS.brief: Global Interactive Technologies filed an 8-K announcing it regained compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing rules. The company had received delinquency notices for failing to file its Form 10-Q (quarter ended March 31, 2026) and Form 10-K (year ended December 31, 2025). After filing the 10-K on May 26, 2026, and the 10-Q on June 22, 2026, Nasdaq confirmed compliance on June 24, 2026. No terms, premiums, or close dates are disclosed. The delisting risk is now removed, but investors should monitor future filing timeliness and any underlying operational issues.

KUST.brief: Kustom Entertainment filed an 8-K reporting entry into an Asset Purchase Agreement to sell its video-solutions division to Cycurion, Inc. Consideration comprises $1.25M cash, a $4.25M secured promissory note, up to $1M earnout, and warrants for 2M shares of Buyer's common stock at $2.80 per share. The deal is expected to close July 15, 2026. Closing conditions include due diligence, carve-out financials, and board approvals. No premium, price per share, or break fee stated. Watch for regulatory clearance and diligence outcomes.

MBIO.brief: Mustang Bio filed an 8-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq Staff notice on April 15, 2026, that its common stock bid price closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, triggering non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The company has a 180-day grace period through October 12, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a $1.00 closing bid for 10+ consecutive business days. If not cured, an additional 180-day period may be available if Mustang meets initial listing criteria and intends to effect a reverse stock split. Non-compliance could lead to delisting, subject to hearing rights. Watch for potential reverse split or other cure actions and timeline risk.

NKLR.brief: Terra Innovatum Global N.V. (Nasdaq: NKLR) disclosed receipt of a deficiency letter from Nasdaq for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) due to failure to timely file its Form 10-Q for Q1 2026 and remaining delinquent on its Form 10-K for FY 2025. The notice has no immediate effect on listing or trading. The company has until June 15, 2026, to submit a plan to regain compliance; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant an exception until October 12, 2026. This is a procedural disclosure (8-K Item 3.01); no deal terms or activist involvement. Watch for the company's compliance plan submission and Nasdaq's response, as failure could lead to delisting.

HDB.brief: HDFC Bank Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing the conclusion of a previously initiated legal review into the resignation letter of former director Mr. Atanu Chakraborty. The review was conducted by external law firms Wilson Sonsini Goodrich Rosati and Wadia Ghandy over three months, involving document review and interviews. The firms found Mr. Chakraborty's statements were not substantiated. This is a governance event, not a special situation transaction.

ATIIU.company: Archimedes Tech SPAC Partners II Co.
ATIIU.brief: Archimedes Tech SPAC Partners II Co. filed an 8-K announcing a press release from target Forge Nano, Inc. about a strategic partnership with Samsung SDI. This is a de-SPAC business combination originally disclosed in a merger agreement dated April 20, 2026. Terms remain as filed in the S-4 registration statement; no specific price-per-share or premium is restated here. The SPAC's board has not issued a new recommendation in this filing; prior S-4 details apply. The transaction requires shareholder vote at an extraordinary general meeting, SEC registration effectiveness, and regulatory clearances. Watch for shareholder approval and potential redemption risk.

BTOC.brief: Armlogi Holding Corp. (BTOC) disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice on April 17, 2026, for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5450(b)(1)(C) because its Market Value of Publicly Held Shares (MVPHS) remained below $5,000,000 for 30 consecutive business days. The company has 180 calendar days, until October 14, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining an MVPHS of at least $5,000,000 for ten consecutive business days. Potential remedies include appealing a delisting determination or transferring to The Nasdaq Capital Market. Shares continue trading on Nasdaq Global Market under BTOC. Key watch items: MVPHS trajectory and any capital actions (reverse split, buyback, or transfer application) undertaken within the cure period.

ITP.brief: IT Tech Packaging disclosed it received a delinquency notice from NYSE American on April 16, 2026, for failing to timely file its Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, by the April 15, 2026 due date. The notice triggers cure procedures under NYSE American Company Guide Section 1007. The company must contact NYSE and issue a press release within five days. There is no immediate effect on listing; a six-month initial cure period runs from the filing delinquency. NYSE may grant an additional six-month cure period. If not cured, suspension and delisting procedures commence. Watch for filing status and potential NYSE discretion on extension.

LEEEF.brief: Leef Brands completed its acquisition of Standard Holdings (SHI) via a merger of a wholly owned subsidiary (Merger Sub) into SHI, with SHI surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary. Consideration: 12,592,960 Leef common shares to SHI senior preferred stockholders and $10,000 cash to common/series seed holders. SHI stock options/warrants were cancelled for no consideration. Merger shares are subject to a 12-month lock-up releasing one-third every 4 months. Leef retained certain SHI executive officers. No listed premium, pricing, or advisor names. Watch for lock-up expirations and integration execution.

ONMDW.brief: OneMedNet Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a standby equity purchase agreement with YA II PN, Ltd. (Yorkville) allowing the company to sell up to $25M of common stock at 97% of market price over 36 months. Each advance is capped at greater of 500K shares or 100% of 5-day average daily volume. Yorkville is limited to 4.99% beneficial ownership and a 19.99% exchange cap unless shareholder approval is obtained. This is an equity line facility providing flexible capital access. Watch for registration statement effectiveness and utilization pace for potential dilution.

RANGU.brief: Range Capital Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, filed a Form 8-K to modify the terms of a proposed extension to its business combination deadline. The company will ask shareholders to approve an amendment at an extraordinary general meeting on June 18, 2026, to extend the deadline from 18 months after its December 2024 IPO to up to 27 months, in monthly increments. For each one-month extension, the sponsor will deposit $0.03 per outstanding public share (max $60,000) into the trust account in exchange for an unsecured promissory note. The filing supplements the definitive proxy statement filed May 5, 2026. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and potential redemption pressure.

CLIK.brief: Click Holdings Ltd. filed a 6-K announcing its acquisition of 100% equity of Axiom Digital Ltd. via a stock-only consideration of 4,500,000 Class A and 800,000 Class B ordinary shares. The target, wholly owned by CEO Chan Chun Sing (a related party), operates a construction HR tech platform in Hong Kong. The board recommends the deal; no termination fee, price per share, or premium is stated. Closing is expected in June 2026, subject to customary conditions. Watch for minority shareholder approval and fairness opinion disclosures given the related-party nature.

CRMLW.brief: Critical Metals Corp. filed a Form 6-K providing historical financial statements and pro forma information for two previously disclosed acquisitions: (1) the April 29, 2026 acquisition of a 50.5% interest in Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S, increasing ownership to 92.5% (Tanbreez Transaction), and (2) the binding May 18, 2026 Scheme Implementation Deed to acquire all shares and listed options of European Lithium Ltd. via two interdependent Australian schemes of arrangement (EUR Transaction). The EUR Transaction is conditional on European Lithium shareholder approval and expected to close in H2 2026. No deal price, premium, or advisor is disclosed in this filing. The filing is purely procedural to comply with Regulation S-X. Watch for shareholder vote timing and regulatory clearance for the EUR Transaction.

AFJKU.brief: Aimei Health Technology Co., Ltd. filed an 8-K reporting termination of its business combination agreement with United Hydrogen Group Inc. and related entities. The agreement, originally entered on June 19, 2024, and amended on June 6, 2025, was terminated by Aimei Health on July 7, 2026, under Section 9.1(b). No deal value or premium was specified in the filing. The termination means the proposed business combination will not close. A press release was issued. The SPAC must now seek a new target within its remaining time or liquidate. Risk-arb: watch for shareholder redemption or extension vote.

CHARU.brief: Charlton Aria Acquisition Corp (a SPAC) disclosed on Form 8-K that it received a Nasdaq notice on May 22, 2026, for failure to timely file its Q1 2026 Form 10-Q, adding to a prior delinquency for its FY2025 Form 10-K. Nasdaq has set a June 15, 2026 deadline for the company to submit a compliance plan. If accepted, the company may receive up to 180 days from the 10-K due date (until October 12, 2026) to regain compliance. Failure could lead to delisting. The company intends to file the overdue reports promptly or submit a plan. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch Nasdaq's acceptance of the compliance plan and the timing of the delinquent filings, as non-compliance risks delisting and affects trading liquidity for units, shares, and rights.

HHH.brief: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (HHH) filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of Vantage Group Holdings Ltd. for $2.1 billion in cash via its subsidiary Howard Hughes Insurance Holdings, LLC. The transaction was financed through cash on hand and $1 billion of non-voting preferred equity from Pershing Square Holdings Ltd. (PSH). The board formed a committee of independent directors to approve the financing. The acquisition closed June 4, 2026, with no price adjustment for early closing. Watch for integration of Vantage's insurance operations and regulatory compliance.

JATT.brief: JATT II Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, entered into a Business Combination Agreement with Talawar Tx Inc. and its merger sub. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge into JATT, with JATT surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Talawar Tx, effectively taking the operating company public. The boards of both JATT and Talawar Tx approved the transaction. No exact terms such as price per share, premium, or valuation were disclosed in this excerpt. The combined entity will continue operations through Talawar Tx. This is a de-SPAC merger, which typically requires shareholder approval and regulatory review. The risk-arb angle centers on JATT stockholders' vote and potential redemptions, which could affect the available trust proceeds.

TGLS.brief: Tecnoglass Inc. filed an S-4/A registration statement on May 4, 2026, proposing to change its jurisdiction of incorporation from the Cayman Islands to Florida via a continuation under Cayman and Florida law. Shareholder approval is required at an annual general meeting; no price, premium, or consideration is involved. The company expects the continuation to become effective post-approval and SEC clearance. This is a redomestication, not a merger or tender offer. Investors should watch shareholder vote results and SEC effectiveness for timing.

IVA.brief: Inventiva S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting completion of the EIB warrant restructuring via issuance of ~15.7 million new warrants to the European Investment Bank, replacing surrendered legacy Tranche B warrants. No price/share or premium stated; this is a balance-sheet renegotiation, not a standalone M&A. The board approved via a June 30 shareholder meeting. Mechanically, legacy anti-dilution protections were eliminated. Watch share count dilution from warrant exercise and the company's financial flexibility as it advances lanifibranor development.

EDU.company: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.

EONR-WT.brief: EON Resources Inc. announced on April 16, 2026 it received a NYSE American noncompliance notice for failing to timely file its FY2025 10-K by the April 15, 2026 due date. Under Section 1007 of the NYSE American Company Guide, the company has an initial cure period until October 15, 2026 to file; an additional six-month cure period may be granted. The delay stems from ongoing work on financial reporting and close procedures, as previously flagged in a Form 12b-25. No immediate delisting effect. The company expects to file within the initial cure period but provides no assurance. Watch for filing updates and potential trading overhang.

FSHPR.brief: Flag Ship Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting that at its June 11, 2026 extraordinary general meeting, shareholders approved an amendment allowing up to twelve one-month extensions of its initial business combination deadline through June 20, 2027, with each extension requiring a sponsor deposit of the lesser of $60,000 or $0.033 per outstanding IPO share. Holders of 1,507,257 shares exercised redemption rights. On June 18, 2026, sponsor Whale Management Corp deposited the first $51,482 extension payment, extending the deadline from June 20 to July 20, 2026. Watch for future monthly extension payments and the risk of failure to consummate a de-SPAC transaction.

GWAV.brief: Greenwave Technology Solutions (GWAV) disclosed receipt of a second Nasdaq delinquency notice on May 21, 2026, for failing to timely file its Q1 2026 Form 10-Q, compounding a prior notice for its late 2025 Form 10-K. Nasdaq requires a compliance plan by June 22, 2026; if accepted, an exception may extend to October 12, 2026. The company states listing and trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market are unaffected for now. The board is not named as taking action beyond disclosure. No premium, price, or stake is involved. Watch whether Greenwave files the overdue reports by the deadline or faces potential delisting, creating risk-arb uncertainty.

TVGNW.brief: Tevogen Bio Holdings disclosed on April 16–17, 2026, that it received Nasdaq Staff deficiency letters for failing the $50 million minimum market value of listed securities (MVLS) and $15 million minimum market value of publicly held shares (MVPHS) requirements under Listing Rules 5450(b)(2)(A) and 5450(b)(2)(C). The company has 180 calendar days—until October 13, 2026 (MVLS) and October 14, 2026 (MVPHS)—to regain compliance by closing at or above the thresholds for at least 10 consecutive business days. There is no immediate delisting effect. Tevogen may explore options, including a transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market. Risk-arb angle: monitor market cap recovery; failure to comply could lead to delisting and stock volatility.

OBX.brief: Gazelle Parent, Inc. filed Amendment No. 4 to its S-4 registration statement in connection with its proposed merger with Galera Therapeutics, Inc. Under the terms disclosed, Galera shareholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of shares of Gazelle common stock, with Gazelle post-merger to be renamed Obsidian Therapeutics, Inc. The deal, announced April 14, 2026, is structured as a reverse merger to take Galera private and combine it with Obsidian. The board of Galera recommends the transaction. The S-4 is not yet effective; the deal requires shareholder approval via written consent. Regulatory clock and closing mechanics are pending SEC effectiveness and stockholder vote. Watch for SEC clearance and risk-arb spread.

KEN.brief: Kenon Holdings Ltd. filed a 6-K reporting a collar transaction on 6 million OPC Energy Ltd. shares (≈2% of OPC). Kenon bought a put and sold a call with strike prices based on a reference price of NIS 124/share. No premium paid; 3-year term; settlement in cash or shares at Kenon's election. Kenon retains upside up to the call strike and limits downside, with shares posted as collateral. No board recommendation or advisor named. The transaction enhances financial flexibility and provides potential borrowing capacity. Watch for OPC share price relative to strike prices and any early termination events.

CETY.brief: Clean Energy Technologies (CETY) disclosed via an 8-K (Item 3.01) that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on May 26, 2026, for failing to timely file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, violating Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The company has 60 days to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 calendar days (until November 16, 2026) to file. No immediate delisting effect. The company is working to file the Quarterly Report. No board recommendation or advisor named. Structural risk: if delisted, liquidity, equity-raising ability, and employee incentives could suffer. Watch for the compliance plan submission and Nasdaq's acceptance decision.

LTRYW.brief: Sports Entertainment Gaming Global Corp disclosed via 8-K that on May 21, 2026 it received a Nasdaq notice for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) due to failure to timely file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026. The delisting notice has no immediate effect; the company has 60 calendar days to submit a compliance plan. If accepted, Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days from the original due date to file. The company intends to submit a plan and work diligently to file. No advisor named. Watch for submission timing, plan acceptance, and continued listing risk.

ZSQR.brief: Z Squared Inc. entered a binding LOI on June 18, 2026, to acquire a majority membership interest in Paradox Data LLC, a digital infrastructure company. Consideration is issuance of $5,000,000 aggregate liquidation preference Series D Convertible Preferred Stock, no cash. Closing conditions include definitive documents, due diligence, technology/land/power vesting, consents, Nasdaq stockholder approval if needed, with a drop-dead date of July 31, 2026. The preferred stock is unregistered, exempt under Section 4(a)(2)/Rule 506(b). Watch for regulatory hurdles and definitive agreement terms.

JYNT.brief: The Joint Corp. files Form 8-K to report closing of an asset sale of 45 company-owned clinics in Southern California to Elite Chiro Group for ~$2.3M. On April 27, 2026, 13 clinics closed with full ownership transfer; the remaining 32 clinics are operated under a Management Service Agreement pending lease assignments. The transaction, along with prior refranchising deals, will reduce corporate-run clinics to 3 out of 960 locations, effectively making The Joint a pure-play franchisor. No board recommendation or advisors named. Watch for pace of remaining lease assignments and risk of delays affecting final close.

MTEX.brief: Mannatech disclosed on Form 8-K that Nasdaq notified it on April 20, 2026 of non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(b)(1) requiring minimum $2.5M stockholders' equity. The company reported negative equity of ($5.223M) as of December 31, 2025, a ~$7.7M shortfall, and fails alternative listing standards based on market value or net income. It has 45 days (until June 4, 2026) to submit a compliance plan to Nasdaq, which may grant up to 180 days (to October 17, 2026) to regain compliance. The intended plan includes intercompany restructuring, possible capital contributions, and cost reductions. Delisting is not immediate; non-acceptance may be appealed to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel with continued listing during appeal. Watch for the compliance plan submission timeline and any equity infusion or merger that could restore compliance, a potential risk-arb angle if a capital event emerges.

MDCXW.brief: Medicus Pharma Ltd. entered into a note purchase agreement with Streeterville Capital, LLC, issuing two secured promissory notes: a $12.9M A-1 Note (with $0.8M OID) and a $10.0M B Note. Net proceeds fund clinical development, business initiatives, and repaying a YA II PN debenture. The A-1 Note bears interest at the prime rate plus 2.5% (paid in shares at a 15% discount to market). The B Note bears 12% interest (payable in shares at a 12.5% discount). Monthly amortization is 36 months. A portion of the B Note may be exchanged into A Notes under Section 3(a)(9). Streeterville has piggyback registration rights. No board recommendation. Risk-arb angle: watch dilution from share-based interest payments; stock overhang from potential conversions.

NXGLW.brief: This 8-K filed by NexGel, Inc. reports the appointment of Brian J. Kieser and Kevin M. Harris to its board of directors alongside the issuance of convertible notes and warrants to Kieser. Kieser was issued a $1M convertible promissory note at $0.60/share (1,666,667 shares) and a warrant for 833,334 shares at $0.80/share, mirroring terms from an earlier $5.5M financing with Sequence LifeScience Inc. The appointments appear routine, not forced departures. The transactions reflect capital-raising rather than a special situation. There is no merger, tender offer, or activist campaign disclosed. The filing does not constitute an acquisition or divestiture by the company.

RYDAF.brief: Shell plc filed a Form 6-K announcing a Q1 2026 interim dividend of $0.3906 per ordinary share and the commencement of a share buyback program. The dividend is payable on June 29, 2026, with an ex-dividend date of May 22, 2026 for ADSs and May 21, 2026 for ordinary shares. Shareholders may elect to receive dividends in USD, EUR, or GBP. The buyback details are referenced but not quantified in this filing. This represents routine capital return to shareholders via dividends and buybacks, a form of capital return. What to watch: sustainability of buyback pace and cash flow generation.

UP.brief: Wheels Up Experience Inc. filed an 8-K regarding Amendment No. 4 to the Investment and Investor Rights Agreement with Delta Air Lines and other lead lenders. The amendment extends the lock-up restriction on approximately 35.6% of the company's outstanding shares held by Delta until May 22, 2027, and aligns the deadline for filing a shelf registration statement to the same date for Delta, with a conditional earlier date for CIH. This is a contractual extension with no immediate transaction impact; no board recommendation or advisors were noted. The filing primarily addresses share transfer restrictions and registration rights, not a special situation event. Watch for any future shareholder actions or registration triggers.

AMBR.brief: Amber International Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K disclosing a pro rata distribution of its Class A ordinary shares by principal shareholder Amber Global Limited (AGL) to AGL's shareholders. AGL held 309,834,748 Class A shares; no price, premium, or new shares are involved. The board authorized the distribution, expected to close on June 1, 2026. No consideration or fee is specified. The distribution is non-dilutive and shares will be restricted under the Securities Act. The registrant is merely an issuer filing a current report on a shareholder event; no special-situation M&A or restructuring is present.

GNTA.brief: Genenta Science S.p.A. filed a Form 6-K disclosing the completion of its acquisition of the remaining 80.5% equity of A.T.C. S.r.l. from its shareholders on May 29, 2026, for an aggregate price of €9,604,076.82. The consideration was paid via set-off against the issuance of 24,625,838 ordinary shares at €0.39 per share to the sellers, who are subject to a 36-month lock-up. A put option allows sellers to resell shares to the company if the volume-weighted average price falls more than 30% below the issue price, exercisable between years three and five. Genenta also holds a call option exercisable from year one to three. The deal closed immediately after board approval on May 18, 2026. Watch for potential dilution and share price volatility relative to the floor price trigger.

AVTX.brief: Avalo Therapeutics filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an underwritten public offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants. The offering includes shares and pre-funded warrants exercisable at $0.001 below the public price, with an ownership limitation of 4.99% or 9.99%. The last reported sale price on May 4, 2026, was $13.78 per share. Underwriters include Leerink Partners, TD Cowen, and BofA Securities, with a 30-day greenshoe option. This capital-raising event is not a special situation; it is a routine equity shelf takedown. The filing does not indicate a strategic review or M&A event.

GRDX.brief: GridAI Technologies Corp. filed an 8-K reporting a Debt Settlement and Subscription Agreement with lender 1396974 BC Ltd. The company will satisfy a defaulted $1,014,675 obligation by paying $800,000 in cash ($700,000 principal + $100,000 interest) and issuing 71,482 shares of common stock at a deemed price of $3.25 per share for remaining accrued interest of $232,315. The agreement resolves a prior default under a Revolving Loan Agreement whose maturity date passed on January 31, 2026. No advisor or board recommendation is mentioned. The structure is a debt-for-equity swap with partial cash settlement. Watch for shareholder dilution and any additional financing needs.

NTIP.brief: Network-1 Technologies, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K (Item 8.01) that its Board authorized and entered into a 10b5-1 trading plan for share repurchases. The plan allows a third-party broker to buy up to 500,000 shares of the company's common stock (par value $0.01) during two periods: July 10, 2026 through two trading days after Q2 fiscal 2026 earnings release, and October 1, 2026 through two trading days after Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings release, subject to price, market, volume, and timing constraints under Rules 10b5-1 and 10b-18. No stated price per share, premium, board recommendation, or advisor. The plan enables repurchases during blackout periods. Watch for execution pace versus market liquidity and potential EPS accretion.

NXPL.brief: NextPlat Corp disclosed that it received a compliance letter from Nasdaq on April 27, 2026, indicating it has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1). The company had previously fallen below the $1.00 bid price threshold and was granted a second 180-day grace period expiring April 27, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal terms are noted. The filing confirms the delisting risk is resolved; no risk-arb angle applies as this is a compliance update, not a merger or tender.

ITUB.brief: Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. filed a Form 6-K attaching summarized minutes of a Board of Directors meeting held on May 28, 2026. The board resolved to pay interest on capital to stockholders in the amount of R$0.36188 per share, net of 17.5% withholding tax (R$0.298551 per share for exempt stockholders). The record date is June 18, 2026, with ex-rights trading from June 19, 2026; payment credited on June 29, 2026. This is a routine capital return distribution, not a special-situation event. No adviser or recommendation is mentioned. This is equivalent to a US regular dividend or interest-on-capital announcement.

OWLS.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by OBOOK Holdings Inc., the foreign private issuer of OwlTing Group (NASDAQ: OWLS). The filing announces the receipt of an Ohio Money Transmitter License, expanding the company's regulated payment coverage to 42 U.S. states. The press release discusses the strategic importance of the license for OwlPay's cross-border settlement infrastructure, particularly for aerospace, defense, and industrial supply chains. No financial terms, transaction structure, or board actions are specified. The filing is a routine operational update, not a special situation.

TLIH.brief: Ten-League International Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting it regained compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid price rule after receiving a delisting determination. The company had been notified on September 9, 2025 of non-compliance and received a delisting notice on March 10, 2026. After a hearing on April 16, 2026, the Panel granted continued listing conditional on demonstrating compliance by May 15, 2026. On May 26, 2026, Nasdaq confirmed compliance, subject to a Mandatory Panel Monitor through May 26, 2027. During the monitor period, failure to maintain compliance will result in immediate delisting without grace period. Watch for any future bid price dip triggering delisting.

CXIIW.brief: Churchill Capital Corp XII filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering (IPO) of 41,400,000 units at $10.00/unit, generating $414M gross proceeds, including full exercise of the underwriter's over-allotment. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-tenth of a warrant exercisable at $11.50/share. Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 350,000 private placement units at $10.00/unit, adding $3.5M. Net proceeds of $414M were deposited into a trust account. As a blank-check SPAC, the company now has up to two years to identify and complete a business combination; watch for target announcement and redemption risks.

HWBK.brief: Hawthorn Bancshares, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement on June 26, 2026, relating to its acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc. Under the merger agreement dated April 29, 2026, a newly formed subsidiary of Hawthorn will merge with FSC, which will survive as a wholly-owned unit. FSC shareholders will receive Hawthorn common stock in the stock-for-stock deal. The proxy statement/prospectus is preliminary and subject to completion. Boards of both companies recommend the transaction; Advisors are Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP (Hawthorn) and Stinson LLP (FSC). The deal requires shareholder approvals, regulatory clearances, and SEC effectiveness. Risk-arb angle: watch for regulatory timelines and any dissenting shareholder votes.

IVF.brief: INVO Fertility, Inc. through its wholly owned subsidiary INVO Centers, LLC acquired 100% of the membership interests of HRCFG, LLC (operator of a fertility clinic joint venture in Birmingham, Alabama) per a Membership Interest Transfer Agreement dated June 23, 2026. Total consideration was $175,001: $1 cash at close, $48,000 payable in equal monthly installments over nine months starting October 2026, and $127,000 from HRCFG's free cash flow. Sellers Karen Hammond, Lisa Ray, and Nicholas Cataldo will provide transition services for four months and support for twelve months post-transition. The acquired clinic will be consolidated prospectively. Watch for integration and cash flow generation to fund deferred payments.

IACQU.brief: Irenic Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its IPO and partial over-allotment option exercise. It sold 22M units at $10.00/unit, raising $220M gross, plus 3.25M over-allotment units for $32.5M. Proceeds of ~$220M were placed in a trust account. This is a blank-check company IPO, a SPAC initial listing event, not a subsequent business combination or special situation. The filing is a routine current report for a new SPAC formation and capital raise, with no deal terms or special event beyond the IPO itself.

OPFI-WT.brief: OppFi Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a $40 million share repurchase program approved by its board on May 6, 2026, replacing the prior program. The buyback allows open-market, privately negotiated, or other method repurchases under Rule 10b-18, with potential use of 10b5-1 plans. No price per share, premium, or expiration date is specified; terms depend on market conditions and legal restrictions, including credit facility covenants. The program signals management's view of undervaluation and capital allocation priority. Watch for actual repurchase pace and impact on EPS; risk-arb angle is limited as this is an open-market authorization, not a tender.

GRO.brief: Brazil Potash Corp. filed a preliminary prospectus supplement (424B5) under Rule 424(b)(5) for an underwritten public offering of common shares and pre-funded warrants. The offering includes common shares at a price per share to be determined, with pre-funded warrants offered to buyers who would otherwise exceed a 4.99% or 9.99% beneficial ownership cap. Each pre-funded warrant has a nominal exercise price of $0.001 and is immediately exercisable with no expiration. The last reported sale price was $3.09 per share. Canaccord Genuity is sole bookrunner. This is a capital-raise, not a special situation; classify as 'Other'.

AEHL.brief: Antelope Enterprise Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of a securities purchase agreement dated April 15, 2026, under which an institutional investor purchased 12,000,000 Class A ordinary shares at $0.207 per share, for aggregate proceeds of $2,484,000. The transaction closed on April 29, 2026. The filing mentions forward-looking risks regarding Nasdaq approval and closing conditions. Given this is a private placement of equity by the issuer for capital-raising purposes (overhang), it is classified as Other, as it does not meet a special-situations category like a standard PIPE or offering would be captured under 'Rights Offerings'.

COOTW.brief: Australian Oilseeds Holdings Ltd (the acquirer) filed a Form 6-K reporting an amendment to its share purchase agreement to acquire a 51% interest in Rentbuddyuk Limited. The transaction was restructured from a purchase of existing shares to an allotment of 10,409 newly issued shares for US$5,326,840 total consideration. The acquisition closed on June 29, 2026, with US$3,672,000 paid at closing, US$918,000 previously paid, and US$736,840 due within six months. This is a completed acquisition of a controlling stake in a UK-based target, analogous to a US reporting of a closed deal. No premium or board recommendation is disclosed. Watch for future payments or integration updates.

WKEY.brief: WISeKey and SEALSQ established Quantisimo Corp., a SPAC-format special purpose vehicle, which signed a non-binding LOI with GigCapital8 Corp., a publicly traded SPAC, for a business combination. The proposed deal implies a pre-money enterprise value of ~$575 million, with a goal to reach $2 billion through build-up acquisitions of up to five additional quantum companies. Closing is expected in Q1 2027. The combined entity would be Nasdaq-listed as a 'Trusted Quantum Pure-Play' platform. The filing is a Form 6-K (press release) announcing the LOI; no board recommendation or financial advisor is named. Watch for definitive agreement negotiations, shareholder approvals, and regulatory timeline.

AREC.brief: American Resources Corp disclosed on April 24, 2026 receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Deficiency Letter for failure to timely file its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, citing non-compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The Company has 60 calendar days to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days from the original filing deadline. Trading of common stock on The Nasdaq Capital Market remains unaffected. The Company is working with its independent auditor to complete the 10-K, noting deconsolidation of certain operations and a streamlined business structure. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, price per share, or tender/merger mechanics are specified. The key risk-arb angle is the delisting risk and timeline to regain compliance.

MARA.brief: MARA Holdings, Inc. (MARA) filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Volt Texas, LLC, acquired all membership interests of MAT 1177 LLC from HIF USA LLC on July 2, 2026. The transaction closed on signing. The target holds land and a letter agreement for 2,000 MW of power capacity in Texas for a digital infrastructure campus. The aggregate purchase price is up to $600 million, structured as milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals, site acquisition, power authorization, and a lease execution. Seller retains a minority interest upon certain milestones. No formal advisor or recommendation was noted. What to watch: execution risk on achieving development milestones and partnership with Starwood Digital Ventures.

PLUN-UN.brief: Plutonian Acquisition Corp. II filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its IPO, partial underwriter over-allotment, and private placement. On April 29, 2026, it sold 10,000,000 units at $10.00 each for $100M gross, and on May 5, 2026, closed 750,000 over-allotment units at $10.00 for $7.5M, plus 7,800 private placement units to the sponsor at $10.00 for $78K. Net proceeds of $108,037,500 ($10.05/unit) were placed in trust. No premium, board recommendation, or advisor named. The SPAC must complete a business combination within 24 months or liquidate. Watch for target announcement and shareholder redemption risk.

PUMP.brief: ProPetro Holding Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of $690M aggregate principal amount of 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031, including the full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $90M. The notes are senior unsecured obligations maturing November 15, 2031, with an initial conversion rate of 43.1616 shares per $1,000 principal (conversion price ~$23.17 per share, a ~37.5% premium over the $16.85 closing price on May 4, 2026). The company may settle conversions in cash, stock, or a combination. Notes are redeemable at par on or after May 15, 2029. This convertible offering serves as a capital return mechanism; watch for dilution management and potential share repurchases with proceeds.

SNDK.brief: Sandisk Corp filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, disclosing an unsolicited mini-tender offer by Tutanota LLC for up to 100,000 shares (less than 0.07% of shares outstanding) at $1,150.00 per share. The offer price is conditioned on the closing price exceeding $1,150.00, meaning tendering stockholders may receive below-market value. Sandisk recommends rejecting the offer and notes shares can be withdrawn before the May 20, 2026 expiration. Tutanota may extend the offer for 45–180 day periods. This is a coercive mini-tender, not a full take-private bid. Watch for stockholder response and potential SEC scrutiny on mini-tender practices.

SDSTW.brief: Stardust Power Inc. (SDST) disclosed on an 8-K filed April 30, 2026, that Nasdaq notified it on April 24, 2026, of non-compliance with the $35M market value of listed securities (MVLS) requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(2). The company has a 180-day cure period, through October 21, 2026, to regain compliance by meeting any alternative standard: $2.5M stockholders' equity, $35M MVLS for 10 consecutive days, or $500K net income from continuing operations. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The notice has no immediate delisting effect; the company may appeal any future delisting to a Nasdaq hearing panel, which can grant a six-month extension. Watch for the company's progress toward compliance and potential equity or strategic actions to restore MVLS.

TIPT.brief: Tiptree Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a merger involving its subsidiary Fortegra Group, acquired by DB Insurance Co., Ltd. in a going-private transaction. Tiptree common stock was delisted from Nasdaq upon closing. The filing includes credit facility amendments consenting to the change of control. No specific financial terms or per-share price were disclosed in the excerpt. The transaction closed on May 29, 2026. Watch for final shareholder consideration details and any post-closing litigation.

VISN.brief: Vistance Networks, Inc. filed an 8-K on July 1, 2026, announcing the completion of the sale of its RUCKUS reporting segment to Belden Inc. The transaction was previously disclosed in an 8-K filed May 5, 2026. Pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, Belden acquired the business on a cash-free, debt-free basis for $1.846 billion in cash, subject to adjustments. Vistance acted as seller. The disposal is now closed; no advisory or recommendation details are in this filing. No structural or regulatory conditions remain. Watch for Vistance's deployment of sale proceeds.

BRNS.brief: Barinthus Biotherapeutics filed a definitive proxy (DEFM14A) for its acquisition via a scheme of arrangement by Beacon Topco, a newly formed entity that will also acquire Clywedog Therapeutics in a parallel merger. Barinthus shareholders will receive between 0.1 and 0.166667 Topco shares per ordinary share (ADSs on a 1:1 basis), with the exact exchange ratio set by Barinthus's board.
