The board recommends voting FOR; no financial advisor is named. The scheme requires court approval under Part 26 of the UK Companies Act, plus regulatory clearances; the US parallel merger uses Delaware law. The combined company will target metabolic/autoimmune diseases. Risk-arb should track shareholder vote timing and regulatory milestones.

EVF.brief: Eaton Vance Senior Income Trust disclosed final results of its issuer tender offer for Auction Preferred Shares Series A and B. The Fund offered to purchase up to 100% of outstanding shares at $24,500 per share (98% of $25,000 liquidation preference), plus accrued unpaid dividends. The offer expired on May 29, 2026. The board recommended the offer; no named advisor. A press release on June 1, 2026 reported final results. No collateral, overhang, or regulatory clock noted. Watch for the final tendered percentage and any subsequent market reaction.

CWEN.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Clearway Energy, Inc. Class A common stock effective May 12, 2026. Under a Certificate of Amendment effective May 1, 2026, each Class A share automatically converts into one new Class C common share, resulting in a substitution of securities. The delisting is pursuant to Rule 12d2-2(a)(3) as the Class A shares now represent only the right to receive the Class C shares; no cash payment or premium is involved. The company suspended trading on May 1. The risk-arb angle: monitor conversion mechanics and whether Class C shares will list on a national exchange or trade over-the-counter.

FHN-PF.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist and deregister First Horizon Corp's Depositary Shares (each representing a 1/400th interest in Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series C) due to full redemption, maturity, or retirement on May 1, 2026. Redemption funds were deposited and made available to holders on the same date. Trading was suspended effective May 1, with delisting effective May 12, 2026. This is a routine event-driven delisting for a called security; no premium, board recommendation, or deal structure applies. No risk-arb angle as there is no pending merger or contested event.

BCS.brief: Barclays PLC filed a Form 6-K reporting the continuation and completion of a share buyback programme. The company purchased ordinary shares for cancellation on the London Stock Exchange, with recent daily volumes of 2.5-3.3 million shares at prices around £4.50-4.63 per share. The buyback was announced on 29 April 2026; by 29 May 2026, it had acquired 53.9 million shares total at a VWAP of 434.28p each. The shares will be cancelled, reducing the share count to about 13.56 billion. This is a straightforward capital return via open-market repurchase — no tender offer, premium, or advisor named. Watch for continuation of future buyback tranches.

BEPC.brief: Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release reporting Q1 2026 results and announcing the acquisition of Boralex, a global listed renewable platform. Terms (price, premium, implied value) are not disclosed in the excerpt. The acquisition complements Brookfield's existing operations with a large operating base and de-risked development pipeline. CEO Connor Teskey highlighted the deal as a growth accelerator. No board recommendation or advisors named. Structural notes: First quarter record FFO of $375M. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory approvals; risk-arb focus on integration execution and potential shareholder dilution.

CCTG.brief: CCSC Technology International Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq: CCTG) filed a Form 6-K disclosing entry into a Technology Purchase Agreement on April 29, 2026, to acquire a smart manufacturing platform from Asia Resource Holdings Ltd. Consideration is 6,333,333 Class A ordinary shares valued at US$3.8 million (US$0.60 per share). The board approved the transaction on April 28, 2026. The seller may assign the right to receive shares to ten assignees. No premium, close date, or break fee is stated. Watch for relevant exchange and regulatory filings as the issuance of shares is subject to future agreements.

IHG.brief: InterContinental Hotels Group PLC (the Company) filed a Form 6-K reporting multiple daily share repurchases conducted on the London Stock Exchange from May 15 through May 29, 2026. Under authority granted at the May 2025 AGM, Goldman Sachs International executed purchases of ordinary shares at average prices ranging from $148.07 to $150.65 per share. The Company intends to cancel all purchased shares. The filing, a UK-equivalent of a US issuer's share buyback disclosure, details total shares repurchased and resulting share count reduction. This is a routine capital return program, not a formal issuer tender offer under US rules. Watch for continued buyback execution and its impact on EPS and share count.

LFS.brief: On July 1, 2026, LEIFRAS Co., Ltd. (the registrant) filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of a stock transfer acquiring SWIFT JAPAN Co., Ltd. from an individual seller. The consideration was paid in cash for all issued and outstanding shares of the target, free and clear of liens. The target operates childcare businesses, which LEIFRAS has commenced operating. Terms such as price per share, premium, and aggregate value were not disclosed. The stock transfer agreement was dated June 23, 2026, and previously filed as an exhibit. No advisors or board recommendations were mentioned. This is a completed acquisition with no pending regulatory or risk-arb angle for watch.

OIOWW.brief: OIO Group (foreign private issuer, Singapore/Hong Kong) filed Form 6-K on May 1, 2026, reporting the resignation of CEO/Chairman Quek Leng Chuang, CFO Ho Shian Ching, Chief Growth Officer Law Beng Hui, and two independent directors, all effective April 30, 2026, with no disagreement cited. Simultaneously, the board appointed Sung Fung Choi as CEO/Chairman, Jason Wong as CFO, and other officers; two independent directors were added. These abrupt, simultaneous departures of top executives represent a forced management change following the completion of the company's business combination. Watch for any potential shareholder reaction or subsequent strategic shifts under new leadership.

PN.brief: Skycorp Solar Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K on May 6, 2026, announcing a $3.6 million second private placement (PIPE) of 1,685,000 Class A ordinary shares at ~$2.14/share, following a prior PIPE bringing total to $6.6M. The price represents a ~30% discount to the reference price. Shares are locked up for six months. The board likely approved the financing to bolster working capital. The filing is a routine capital raise, not a special situation like a return of capital, as the proceeds are for general corporate purposes. No special-situation elements are present, so this is classified as None.

SCOP.brief: Sprott Physical Copper Trust (COP) filed a Form 6-K with a Material Change Report reporting unitholder approval to restructure from a non-redeemable investment fund to a mutual fund, effective May 1, 2026. The amendments replace a semi-annual redemption feature with monthly redemptions, removing the previous 1.5% cap on units redeemed per period. Consequential changes were made for a NYSE Arca listing. No financial terms, advisor, or premium are mentioned. The restructuring enhances liquidity, potentially attracting broader investment. Monitor trading volumes and actual monthly redemption activity for investor behavior post-change.

ADVB.brief: Advanced Biomed Inc. filed an 8-K on June 30, 2026, reporting its entry into a Share Purchase Agreement to sell 100% of its Taiwan subsidiary to Miaozhu Zhao, an unrelated third party, for $490,000 in cash. The subsidiary conducts biomedical R&D including the A+PerfusC platform. The transaction is expected to close within three months, with the company retaining its AI-focused operations. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is disclosed. The sale appears to be a strategic shift toward AI. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory clearance; risk-arb is minimal given the small size.

AUB-PA.brief: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $250 million share repurchase program and a quarterly dividend of $0.37 per common share. The buyback may be executed via open market or private transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans, through May 5, 2027. Management has discretion over timing and amounts; the program is non-binding. The board declared dividends on common and Series A preferred stock. This is an ordinary capital allocation action; no takeover/merger or activist campaign. Watch for repurchase pace and any acceleration if shares trade at a discount to tangible book value.

BTCY.brief: Biotricity Inc. filed an 8-K reporting exchange agreements under which holders of 14.1M common shares, 3.99M options, and 1.44M warrants exchanged these securities for 1.96M newly created Series C Preferred shares (10 Exchange Securities per Preferred share). Series C carries 40 votes per share and automatically converts to 59.6% of outstanding common upon a qualified equity offering of at least $15M; if none by March 31, 2028, holders may convert each Preferred share to 10 common shares. The filing cites Section 4(a)(2) exemption. This debt-for-equity swap restructures the cap table and voting control; watch for potential dilutive effect on existing common holders and whether a qualified financing occurs before the conversion deadline.

COSO.brief: CoastalSouth Bancshares, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that its Board of Directors authorized a $15 million stock repurchase plan, effective May 1, 2026, through April 30, 2027. The plan allows open-market, accelerated share repurchase, or privately negotiated purchases under Rule 10b-18 and Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. No specific price, premium, or share count is disclosed. The company is not obligated to repurchase any shares and may modify or discontinue the plan at any time. Watch for periodic repurchase activity and potential EPS accretion; no risk-arb angle as this is an issuer capital return.

FGBIP.brief: First Guaranty Bancshares, Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 Other Events to announce a quarterly cash dividend on its 6.75% Series A Fixed-Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock. On April 16, 2026, the Board declared a $16.875 per share preferred dividend ($0.421875 per Depositary Share) payable on June 1, 2026 to holders of record as of May 15, 2026. The Series A Preferred Stock dividend will be paid to the depositary, which will distribute to Depositary Share holders. No recommendation, advisor, premium, or change in corporate structure is noted. This is a routine dividend declaration, not a special situation; the filing serves as public notice. Monitor for any suspension or rate change.

GHC.brief: On May 1, 2026, Graham Holdings Co disclosed via Form 8-K that its subsidiary Kaplan closed the sale of the Kaplan Languages Group (KLG). No purchase price, premium, or buyer name is disclosed; the company preliminarily expects a $60 million U.S. income tax benefit in 2026 from the transaction. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The filing is minimal, serving as a closing notice under Item 8.01. Watch for subsequent quarterly filings to reveal after-tax gain and any earnout terms; risk-arb spread is not calculable without price terms.

HNOI.brief: HNO International filed an 8-K regarding an Equity Purchase Agreement with Lambda Ventures LLC, granting the company the right to direct purchases of up to $30M of its common stock over 24 months. Shares are sold at 80% of the lowest traded price, with a $25K-$500K per put limit. 500,000 initial commitment shares were issued; additional shares are triggered per $2.5M drawn. A registration rights agreement was also entered. The structure is a distressed equity line (ELOC), not a typical capital return. No traditional return of capital to shareholders; watch dilution and market overhang from the floorless pricing mechanism.

INDB.brief: Independent Bank Corp announced a $200 million stock buyback plan authorized by its Board effective April 30, 2026. Repurchases will commence after completion of the $10.5 million remaining under a July 2025 plan, with open-market and private transactions and Rule 10b5-1 plans. The program expires April 29, 2027, and may be modified or discontinued. No pricing details were provided beyond the aggregate authorization. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 Other Events. This is a routine capital return announcement; no special-situation activating events such as a tender offer or going-private transaction are involved.

LYB.brief: LyondellBasell Industries N.V. filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to its structured accounts receivables facility (Eighth Amendment to Receivables Purchase Agreement). The amendment extends the facility term to June 25, 2027, reduces the maximum amount from $900M to $700M, and updates terms to align with the company's senior unsecured revolving credit facility. No trade receivable purchases or letters of credit were outstanding as of the filing date. This is a routine financing arrangement modification, not a special situation event. There are no deal terms, premiums, or advisor involvement.

NKSH.brief: National Bankshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a semi-annual dividend of $0.75/share and renewal of a share repurchase authorization up to 250,000 shares from June 2026 through May 2027. The dividend payment is June 1, 2026, to holders of record May 26, 2026. The repurchase plan replaces the expiring plan and management retains discretion on execution. No advisor or board recommendation beyond the standard renewal. The aggregate repurchase represents about 4.2% of shares based on a rough float of ~6 million shares. Watch for actual repurchase pace vs. authorization and implications for capital allocation.

ONFOW.brief: On July 2, 2026, Onfolio Holdings received a NASDAQ notice for non-compliance with Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as its common stock closing bid price remained below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day compliance period until December 29, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a $1.00 or higher closing bid price for ten consecutive business days. If not regained, it may seek a second 180-day period by meeting other listing standards and potentially effecting a reverse stock split. Failure could lead to delisting. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for potential reverse stock split or strategic actions to boost share price.

OC.brief: Owens Corning filed an 8-K on April 30, 2026, disclosing the completion of the sale of substantially all of its global glass reinforcements business to affiliates of the Praana Group (Triumph Composites Private Limited and 3B Lux S.r.l.). The enterprise value was revised downward from $755 million to $645 million via an amendment on April 14, 2026. Net after-tax cash proceeds are expected to be approximately $280 million. The company intends to use proceeds for organic growth and shareholder returns. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026. Watch for execution of capital allocation plans and potential reinvestment or buyback announcements.

RZC.brief: Reinsurance Group of America filed an 8-K announcing full redemption of its $400M 5.75% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2056 (CUSIP RZB). Redemption effective June 15, 2026 at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. No board recommendation or advisor named; redemption is mandatory under indenture terms. The notice triggers a debt reduction and lower interest expense, representing a capital return to debtholders at par. Watch for any refinancing plans or balance-sheet deleveraging signals from management; typical risk-arb is minimal as redemption is at par with no premium.

RREVW.brief: RRE Ventures Acquisition Corp., a blank-check company, filed Form 8-K on April 29, 2026 to announce entry into an Underwriting Agreement for its initial public offering (IPO) of 25 million units at $10.00 per unit, with an over-allotment option for an additional 3.75 million units. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-third of one redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50 per share. Underwriters purchase price is $9.40 per firm unit and $9.50 per additional unit, with a deferred discount. This is a standard SPAC IPO registration. No deal terms or premiums apply here. Watch for completion of IPO and subsequent target acquisition.

REKR.brief: On April 27, 2026, Rekor Systems received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to maintain the $1.00 minimum bid price per share for 30 consecutive business days through April 24, 2026. The company has a 180-day compliance period until October 26, 2026 to regain compliance by trading at or above $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. A reverse stock split could be used but must be completed ten business days before the deadline. If not cured, a second 180-day period may be available subject to meeting other listing standards. The notice does not immediately affect trading. Watch for potential reverse split announcement or bid-price improvement efforts as the risk-arb angle focuses on avoiding delisting.

USCB.brief: USCB Financial Holdings and its subsidiary filed an 8-K reporting the mutual termination of a Side Letter Agreement with Patriot Financial Partners, which owned 10.2% of the company's voting stock. The termination followed the resignation of Patriot's board representative. The agreement with another party, Priam, remains in effect. No financial terms, premiums, or transaction values were disclosed. The filing reflects a governance/relationship change rather than a special situation.

WT.brief: WisdomTree filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated repurchases of $51.9M aggregate principal of its 3.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for ~$87.3M cash (a premium over par reflecting the conversion value). The transactions, expected to close June 1, 2026, will leave $18.1M of the Notes outstanding. No tender offer is used; these are issuer-initiated repurchases to reduce leverage/conversion overhang, not a formal debt tender. The filing lacks board recommendation or advisor roles. Watch for the closing condition and potential impact on diluted share count; the premium indicates embedded conversion economics.

MFPVV.brief: Midera Food Processing, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its spin-off from The Middleby Corporation. Middleby distributed 100% of Midera's common stock to its stockholders, leaving Middleby with no ownership interest. The spin-off was effectuated through a Separation and Distribution Agreement entered on July 5, 2026, along with a Tax Matters Agreement. Midera holds Middleby's former food processing business. The filing formalizes the separation, governance, and tax arrangements between the two entities. Watch for post-spin trading dynamics and any subsequent shareholder actions.

GAINI.brief: Gladstone Investment Corporation filed an 8-K reporting that its portfolio company SFEG Holdings, Inc. agreed to sell Specialized Fabrication Equipment Group LLC to Enerpac Tool Group Corporation. Terms were not disclosed; Gladstone expects full repayment of its debt investment and a significant capital gain on its equity interest. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The transaction marks Gladstone's 31st realized exit from a buyout investment. SFEG designs specialty fabrication equipment; Enerpac is a global industrial tools provider. What to watch: closing conditions and timing, as the deal furthers Enerpac's specialty portfolio expansion.

BUUU.brief: BUUU Group Limited (NASDAQ: BUUU) filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding MOU to explore acquiring PINK 308 LLC, a holding company for film assets, to enter AI-driven short-form drama and IP-centric digital entertainment. Terms are undisclosed; no price, premium, or break fee stated. Completion is subject to due diligence, transfer of film libraries free of encumbrances into PINK 308, and other conditions. The board supports the strategic transition, with no advisors named. This early-stage, non-binding deal carries high uncertainty; watch for definitive agreement, financing, and regulatory timelines.

SXTC.brief: China SXT Pharmaceuticals filed a Form 6-K reporting a securities purchase agreement for up to $30M in prepaid purchases of Class A ordinary shares. The initial tranche is $3.15M, net of a $150K OID, with subsequent draws of $250K–$3M over two years. Shares are priced at 50% of the lower of the signing-date closing price or the lowest closing over the prior 180 trading days, subject to a $0.20 floor. The issuer will file an F-3 resale registration. Univest Securities serves as placement agent, earning a 4.5% cash fee plus 0.5% expense reimbursement. This dilutive structured equity facility resembles a variable-pre-priced forward; watch for continuous dilution and dependence on share price floor mechanics.

MNDR.brief: Mobile-health Network Solutions filed a Form 6-K disclosing a non-binding strategic cooperation MOU with Hector Capital Holdings. Under the framework, Hector may invest up to US$119 million into the company to fund the potential acquisition of majority interests in BIMA and MM Helix. The MOU is non-binding and subject to full due diligence, definitive agreements, regulatory approval, and independent valuation. No specific price per share, premium, or board recommendation is provided; terms may include equity or convertible instruments. The filing is a foreign private issuer report; no US-equivalent event has occurred. The lack of binding terms and missing deal parameters makes completion uncertain, and investors should monitor definitive agreements and regulatory milestones.

PHOE.brief: Phoenix Asia Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K disclosing a stock acquisition agreement to acquire all equity of ACEA Pharma, Inc. from ACEA Therapeutics, Inc. Consideration is 100 million newly-issued Phoenix ordinary shares valued at $1,000,000,000, implying $10.00 per share. The board has not disclosed a recommendation or advisor. Closing expected in Q2 2026, subject to HSR antitrust clearance and Nasdaq approval for a reverse merger/change of control. A $20M convertible promissory note was issued to the controlling shareholder for advisory services. Watch for regulatory hurdles and shareholder approval; risk-arb centers on timing and Nasdaq listing conditions.

AMRC.brief: Ameresco filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a joint venture contribution and equity purchase agreement. Through its subsidiary, it contributed its biogas business to Neogenyx Fuels LLC in exchange for a 70% equity interest. HASI affiliate invested $400 million, receiving a 30% interest; $100 million cash was paid to Ameresco at close, ~$58 million used to reduce a loan, and the remainder contributed to the JV. No board recommendation or advisor named. Structurally, this is a spin-off-like transfer of assets into a separate entity with external capital. Watch for operational integration, JV governance, and potential monetization of the retained stake.

AURA.brief: Aura Biosciences filed an 8-K disclosing a stock purchase agreement with Matrix Capital Management Master Fund, LP to repurchase up to 6,922,870 shares (all held by Matrix) at $5.64 per share, the same price as the concurrent equity offering. The repurchase is conditioned on closing of that offering and funded from net proceeds exceeding $200M. The transaction, approved by the audit committee, reduces Matrix's ~10.8% stake. Shares become authorized but unissued. The expected closing is no earlier than two business days after the equity offering's close. Watch for the equity offering's completion as a condition precedent.

BPACU.brief: Blueport Acquisition Ltd (BPAC), a SPAC, filed an 8-K announcing a merger agreement with SINGAUTO Inc. The transaction involves a reincorporation merger of BPAC into a wholly owned subsidiary, followed by the acquisition of SINGAUTO by a merger sub. No per-share price, premium, or aggregate consideration is disclosed. The board's recommendation and advisor names are not included. The structure is a two-step SPAC de-SPAC transaction with a corporate reincorporation. The regulatory clock runs from the May 1, 2026 agreement. Watch for shareholder approval, redemptions, and SEC review for risk-arb spread.

CWK.brief: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing that its wholly-owned subsidiary, the Issuer, elected to partially redeem $100 million of its outstanding $650 million 6.750% Senior Secured Notes due May 2028. The redemption price is 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with the redemption date set for May 15, 2026. This is a debt reduction / capital return move; no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. The trustee, Wilmington Trust, will execute the notice. Watch for further liability management or potential refinancing. Risk-arb angle: None; it is a straightforward partial redemption.

DKL.brief: Delek Logistics Partners, LP (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting the pricing of $800 million aggregate principal amount of 6.875% senior notes due 2034, issued at par, alongside a conditional partial redemption of $400 million of its outstanding 8.625% senior notes due 2029 at 104.313% of principal plus accrued interest. The redemption is conditioned on closing the new notes offering, expected May 14, 2026. Proceeds will also repurchase all outstanding 7.125% senior notes due 2028. This is a routine refinancing and debt management transaction; no board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for customary closing conditions and interest rate environment.

DRH.brief: DiamondRock Hospitality Co filed an 8-K on May 4, 2026, announcing the sale of its leasehold interest in the Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan/Fifth Avenue. The filing includes a press release and investor presentation but does not disclose specific terms such as price, premium, or buyer. The company is a hotel REIT divesting an asset. No board recommendation, advisor names, or regulatory clock are mentioned. As a non-US filing, this is equivalent to an 8-K for material definitive agreement disclosure. Watch for future disclosures on the transaction price and any potential use of proceeds for debt reduction or reinvestment.

MYFW.brief: First Western Financial Inc filed an 8-K to disclose board authorization of a $5 million common stock repurchase plan, effective June 12, 2026, for one year. The Federal Reserve issued a non-objection on April 29, 2026. Repurchases may occur in open market, privately negotiated transactions, or via Rule 10b5-1 plans. No specific price per share or premium is stated. The plan is discretionary, with no obligation to acquire a set dollar amount. This is a routine share buyback—a capital return event. Watch for execution pace and any trading plan adoption; minimal risk-arb angle due to open-market nature.

GME-WT.brief: GameStop Corp. (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting that Chairman/CEO Ryan Cohen requested withdrawal of a proposed CEO Performance Award from its proxy statement to fully focus on the proposed acquisition of eBay Inc. No terms (price per share, premium, or valuation) were disclosed in this filing. The board granted the request; no advisor named. The filing notes GameStop will release additional materials on the eBay acquisition, including strategic rationale and operational plan. What to watch: emergence of a definitive agreement, regulatory timeline, and financing details to assess deal feasibility and risk-arb spread.

INDV.brief: Indivior Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K on May 4, 2026, disclosing entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Barclays Bank PLC to repurchase $175 million of its common stock under a previously authorized $400 million buyback program. The company paid the prepayment amount and received an initial delivery of 3,717,473 shares. Final settlement, based on volume-weighted average prices less a discount, is expected by June 22, 2026, with potential additional shares or cash adjustment. The filing indicates a commitment to returning capital to shareholders, typical of special-situation capital returns.

LSCC.brief: Lattice Semiconductor filed an 8-K announcing its acquisition of AMI TopCo, Inc. for total consideration of $1 billion in cash and approximately $650 million in Lattice common stock, subject to customary adjustments. The stock component ranges from about 5.2 to 6.1 million shares based on Lattice's pre-closing trading price. The merger agreement includes customary representations, warranties, termination rights, and an escrow for potential adjustments or indemnification. A registration rights agreement with THL AMI Aggregator, LP provides for two underwritten block trades. Closing is conditioned on HSR antitrust clearance. The deal combines cash and stock, with a collar mechanism on share count. Watch for regulatory timing and potential synergies in the semiconductor space.

MDV-PA.brief: Modiv Industrial, Inc. (Modiv) entered into a definitive merger agreement with Global Net Lease, Inc. (GNL). Modiv common stockholders will receive 1.975 GNL common shares per share; Modiv Series A preferred stockholders will receive $25.00 per share plus accrued dividends. The Modiv board recommends a vote FOR the merger (no advisor named). The transaction is structured as a reverse triangular merger with simultaneous entity-level and operating partnership mergers, resulting in GNL as the surviving public company. Modiv shares will be delisted from NYSE post-close. The regulatory clock is typical for REIT mergers; key watch items include stockholder vote and customary closing conditions. Risk-arb spread will fluctuate with GNL share price.

SBXD-WT.brief: SilverBox Corp IV, a SPAC, filed an 8-K announcing an amendment to its business combination agreement with Parataxis Holdings Inc. The First Amendment extends the Outside Date from May 6, 2026 to August 6, 2026, providing additional time to close the de-SPAC transaction. No changes to deal terms, price, or structure were disclosed. The extension is a standard SPAC timeline adjustment, often used to satisfy closing conditions or regulatory approvals. The deal originally had a SPAC structure with Pubco as the combined entity. No break fee or premium details are mentioned. Investors should watch for shareholder approval and regulatory clearance before the new deadline; any further delays or termination could impact SPAC arbitrage positions.

UDR.brief: UDR, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized a 25 million share increase to its existing buyback program, making total authorization ~30 million shares (over $1 billion at current prices). Repurchases may occur via open-market, block, or private deals with no expiration date. The filing is a straightforward capital return announcement; board recommendation is implicit given the authorization. No advisor was named. The existing January 2008 program is unchanged. The filing does not involve a merger, tender offer, activist campaign, or strategic review. What to watch: pace of execution and any impact on share price and capital allocation strategy.

UONEK.brief: Urban One filed an 8-K on May 1, 2026, announcing two radio-station transactions: it will acquire Service Broadcasting Group, LLC, including flagship stations KKDA and KRNB, and simultaneously sell station KZMJ to Fuzion Dallas, LLC. No financial terms, price per share, premium, or valuation details were disclosed. The acquisitions and divestiture are interconditional and subject to FCC regulatory approval plus customary closing conditions. The board's recommendation or advisor names are absent from the filing. Structurally, these are asset-level deals with a singular regulatory gatekeeper (FCC). Watch for FCC review timelines and potential antitrust conditions in the Dallas radio market; risk-arb here is limited given the absence of deal-specific financial disclosure.

VPRB.brief: VPR Brands, LP filed an 8-K reporting a Third Amendment to its Limited Partnership Agreement, executed by its general partner Soleil Capital Management L.L.C. on April 28, 2026. The amendment increases authorized Class A preferred units from 1,000,000 to 250,000,000, reduces the stated value from $2.00 to $1.00 per unit, eliminates an annual dividend and preferential liquidation rights, and removes governance participation. Conversion rights trigger if the common units' closing price meets or exceeds $1.15 for 20 consecutive trading days before July 31, 2030. This is a capital structure adjustment, not a special-situation event like an acquisition or tender, thus classified as Other.

VABK.brief: Virginia National Bankshares Corp filed an 8-K Item 8.01 to announce the completion of the sale of its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Fauquier Bank Services Inc.'s interest in Bearing Insurance Group LLC, a full-service insurance agency, effective May 1, 2026. The registrant expects a pre-tax gain of approximately $4.7 million in Q2 2026. No specific sale price, premium, or buyer details are disclosed, nor are board recommendations or advisors named. The transaction has closed; forward-looking statements caution on risks. No remaining contingent terms or regulatory clocks are mentioned. The key watchpoint is the eventual Q2 earnings impact of the gain.

WENC-UN.brief: West Enclave Merger Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering of 10,000,000 units at $10.00/unit, each consisting of one ordinary share and one right to receive one-tenth of a share post-business combination. Gross proceeds were $100,000,000, with a 45-day underwriter over-allotment option for up to 1,500,000 additional units. Key agreements filed include underwriting (EarlyBirdCapital), rights, letter, trust, registration rights, and private placement purchase agreements. The trust arrangement secures IPO proceeds pending a business combination. Watch for target acquisition announcement within 24 months or risk of liquidation.

ZIONP.brief: Zions Bancorporation filed an 8-K reporting the sale of 460,153 Class B-1 shares of Visa Inc. on May 4, 2026, for $215 million in aggregate proceeds, generating a pre-tax gain of approximately the same amount in Q2 2026. The shares were originally received in 2007 from a Visa restructuring and IPO. No board recommendation, advisors, premium, or deal mechanics are disclosed as this is a portfolio asset sale, not a corporate action. Watch for any subsequent disclosures on capital deployment of the gain; no risk-arb angle applies.

BLSH.brief: Bullish filed a Form 6-K (May 2026) reporting Q1 results and its definitive agreement to acquire Equiniti for $4.2 billion. Bullish is the acquirer. The transaction creates the first integrated blockchain-enabled, blue-chip issuer services provider, combining a regulated transfer agent with tokenization infrastructure. No board recommendation or advisor is named in this filing. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and closing conditions; no premium or specific mechanics are detailed. Watch for regulatory clearance timelines and integration risk, as the deal expands Bullish's footprint from digital asset trading into traditional issuer services.

DHT.brief: DHT Holdings filed a Form 6-K attaching its press release for Q1 2026 results. The release reports adjusted EBITDA of $133.3M, net profit of $164.5M ($1.02 EPS), and a $0.64 dividend. It details the sale of two VLCCs (DHT Europe and DHT China) for $101.6M aggregate consideration, generating a $60M gain, and delivery of three newbuilds with $158.3M in installments. The filing is a routine earnings announcement for a foreign private issuer, not a special situation. No M&A, activist, or restructuring event is disclosed.

HSLV.brief: Highlander Silver Corp. filed a Form 6-K (Business Acquisition Report) disclosing its completed acquisition of Bear Creek Mining Corporation via a plan of arrangement on February 26, 2026. Highlander acquired all Bear Creek common shares not already owned in exchange for 0.1175 Highlander shares per Bear Creek share, issuing ~36.2 million shares. Concurrently, Highlander paid US$6.2 million and US$1.6 million in cash to Royal Gold and Equinox, respectively, as part of debt settlements, and granted net smelter return royalties on Bear Creek's Corani Project and Mercedes mine. Bear Creek became a wholly-owned subsidiary. No termination fee or premium is stated. Watch for integration execution and post-merger production guidance.

LZM-WT.brief: Lifezone Metals Ltd filed a Form 6-K containing a press release announcing the results of its 2026 Annual General Meeting held on May 5, 2026. The filing reports that ordinary resolutions were passed, including the receipt of accounts, ratification of the auditor, and re-election of directors Keith Liddell and Chris Showalter. 72% of ordinary shares were represented. This is routine shareholder meeting results with no special-situation event. No deal terms or structural changes are disclosed. No watch items; the filing is purely periodic.

SKK.brief: SKK Holdings Ltd filed a 6-K reporting shareholder approval of an Asset Purchase Agreement to acquire substantially all drone-based technology assets of Rantizo, Inc. for $759,047 in cash and ~$258.8 million in newly issued Class A ordinary shares (total ~$259.6 million). Additional shares valued at $22 million will be issued to management and as escrow consideration. Class B shareholders (100 votes per share) overwhelmingly approved. The deal also includes a name change to Rantizo. The filing does not specify a premium, advisor, or expected close date; watch for regulatory approvals and share issuance mechanics.

TRVG.brief: trivago N.V. filed a Form 6-K announcing the resumption of trading in its American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange's Open Market as of June 26, 2026. Trading had been suspended since November 2023 due to a missing settlement declaration from Clearstream following an ISIN change related to the ADS ratio change. Clearstream has now issued the declaration, restoring trading on German exchanges. The ADRs continue to trade on Nasdaq under symbol TRVG. This is an administrative update, not a special situation, with no deal terms, board recommendation, or strategic implications.

ARCLU.brief: ARC Group Acquisition I Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO on May 1, 2026. The company sold 12,075,000 units (including full over-allotment of 1,575,000 units) at $10.00 per unit, generating gross proceeds of $120.75 million. Each unit consists of one ordinary share, one right (receiving 1/4 ordinary share upon business combination), and one warrant (exercisable at $11.50 per share). The funds are held in trust for a future business combination. This is a standard SPAC IPO filing; no target or deal terms are disclosed. Watch for the company's search for a merger target within the typical 18-24 month timeframe.

BHVN.brief: Biohaven Ltd. filed an 8-K Item 8.01 disclosing Amendment No. 2 to its existing Equity Distribution Agreement with J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, increasing the aggregate offering amount to $350 million in an at-the-market equity offering program of common shares. This is a routine shelf takedown amendment with no fixed price, premium, or board recommendation. The filing does not represent a special situation such as acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring; it is an incremental equity facility update.

MTNE-UN.brief: CH4 Natural Solutions Corp (a blank-check company) filed an 8-K reporting the effectiveness of its S-1 registration and completion of its initial public offering of 20,000,000 units at $10.00 per unit on May 4, 2026. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-half warrant exercisable at $11.50 per share. Underwriting agreement with Santander US Capital Markets LLC. The company also entered into warrant agreements and a letter agreement with its sponsor and insiders. Proceeds will be held in trust pending a business combination. What to watch: the 24-month deadline to complete an acquisition or face dissolution and redemption.

EXEL.brief: Exelixis filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 earnings and announcing a new stock repurchase authorization of up to $750 million by December 31, 2027. The board authorized the buyback, enhancing existing capital return programs. No specific price or premium is stated. The program is open-market, with mechanics typical of discretionary repurchases. The filing is primarily an earnings release with a supplementary buyback announcement. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share count and EPS.

MSBIP.brief: Midland States Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing its board approved an amendment to increase its stock repurchase authorization from $25 million to $45 million and extended the program's expiration to December 31, 2026. As of the filing, the company had already repurchased 923,837 shares at an average price of $21.46, totaling $19.8 million of the original authorization. The program is subject to market conditions, corporate and regulatory requirements, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Watch for future buyback execution pace and any Rule 10b5-1 plan amendments as indicators of management's view on valuation.

OCGN.brief: Ocugen, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of a $115.0 million private offering of 6.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2034 issued under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. The notes are unsecured, rank senior to subordinated debt, and mature May 15, 2034. Interest is payable semi-annually starting November 15, 2026. Conversion is cash-settled until a reserved share effective date, subject to Nasdaq Exchange Cap of 67,629,947 shares pending stockholder approval. No premium, acquisition, or strategic event; this is a financing transaction. Watch for stockholder vote on share issuance and potential dilution management.

OTLC.brief: Oncotelic Therapeutics, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary contributed its stake in Neurobridge IP Holdings Inc. to Lunai Bioworks, Inc. via a triangular merger. Oncotelic's subsidiary owned 62.5% of Holdings prior to the merger; consideration was 5 shares of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock of Lunai with a stated value of $12.5 million. The deal closed May 1, 2026. The filing lacks specific per-share price, premium, board recommendation, or advisor details. The transaction involves a patent portfolio with no operating business. Further disclosures may provide clarity on the nature of this acquisition.

MYPS.brief: PLAYSTUDIOS, Inc. received Nasdaq approval to transfer its listed securities from the Nasdaq Global Market to the Nasdaq Capital Market, effective May 6, 2026, after failing to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement. The company had been non-compliant since November 2025 and failed to cure during the initial 180-day period ending May 4, 2026. As a result of the transfer, Nasdaq granted a second 180-day compliance period expiring November 2, 2026. The transfer does not affect trading symbols MYPS and MYPSW. Watch for the company's ability to regain bid price compliance within the extended window, which may require a reverse stock split or other measures.

PMI.brief: Picard Medical disclosed receiving two NYSE American delinquency notices for non-compliance with continued listing standards. The May 8 notice cited Section 1003(a)(ii); the May 15 notice cited a stockholders' deficit of ~$1.4M as of March 31, 2026 and net losses in three recent fiscal years, violating Section 1003(a)(i). The company must submit a compliance plan by June 7, 2026; if accepted, it has until November 8, 2027 to regain compliance. Failure may lead to delisting. The filing also furnished Q1 2026 financial results via press release. Watch for the NYSE American's response to the compliance plan and any equity-restoration actions.

RVTY.brief: Revvity filed an 8-K announcing the probable sale of all assets of its Immunodiagnostics business in China (China IDX) pursuant to a letter of intent signed April 16, 2026. Terms include up to $200 million, subject to adjustments and conditions. Management deems the transaction probable to close in 2027 and includes unaudited pro forma financials. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for regulatory approvals and adjustments to the purchase price; risk-arb focuses on execution and closing timeline.

RDW.brief: Redwire Corp filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an at-the-market (ATM) equity offering of up to $350 million in common stock under a new sales agreement with multiple agents. The filing replaces a prior November 2025 agreement, under which $249.7 million had already been sold. Shares are sold on a commercially reasonable efforts basis on NYSE via agents earning up to 3.0% commission. Last reported price was $8.69. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes. No special-situation catalyst; routine equity shelf takedown.

SCLXW.brief: Scilex Holding Co filed an 8-K disclosing a binding term sheet with Datavault AI Inc. to purchase 837 Bitcoin for $50 million. An initial $30 million payment is due, with $20 million in quarterly installments through 2028. Consideration may be cash, shares of Scilex common stock, or subsidiary securities, at Scilex's discretion. No definitive agreement has been executed; closing requires regulatory approvals and board finalization. The terms are preliminary and may be terminated, making consummation uncertain. This acquisition of digital assets does not fit standard special-situation categories, thus categorized as Other.

VS.brief: Versus Systems Inc. disclosed via an 8-K that on April 29, 2026, Nasdaq issued a deficiency letter for failing to maintain the $2.5M stockholders' equity minimum required under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), with equity of $1.9M as of Dec 31, 2025. The company has until June 13, 2026, to submit a compliance plan, with a potential extension to Oct 26, 2026. To address this, Versus entered a Stock Purchase Agreement with ASPIS Cyber Technologies on April 15, 2026: ASPIS will purchase 1,513,128 shares at $1.1235/share ($1.7M total), priced at 105% of the prior close, with closing expected by May 14, 2026. The filing notes no board recommendation or advisor. The stock sale, if completed, will provide a cash infusion but may create overhang; risk-arb focuses on Nasdaq acceptance and closing within the window.

BNZIW.brief: Banzai International filed an 8-K/A reporting a debt-for-equity exchange with Agile Capital Funding. The company exchanged 232,786 shares of Class A common stock valued at $1.22/share ($284,000 aggregate) to reduce its subordinated secured promissory note balance from ~$1.495M to $1.839M after adding a $628,058 forbearance fee. The forbearance agreement temporarily waives defaults through March 30, 2026. This restructuring avoids immediate creditor enforcement while modifying loan terms. Watch for further exchanges or potential default if the company cannot meet revised obligations; risk-arb focuses on equity dilution versus debt reduction sustainability.

AACG.brief: ATA Creativity Global filed a Form 6-K reporting completion of the sale of its direct and indirect subsidiaries (ATA BVI and a 69.0417% equity interest in Beijing Huanqiuyimeng Education Consultation Corp.) to Robox Holding Limited for nominal cash consideration of RMB1. The transaction was pursuant to a share purchase agreement dated May 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing includes unaudited pro forma financial statements giving effect to the disposition. Post-closing, the company retains its corporate status with adjusted operations. The nominal consideration and disposal of core operating assets suggest a strategic exit; watch for the company's future business direction and potential wind-down or pivot.

CHSN.brief: On May 6, 2026, Chanson International Holding filed a Form 6-K announcing a 100-for-1 share consolidation effective May 7, 2026. The consolidation reduces outstanding Class A shares from ~363.9M to ~3.6M and adjusts par value from $0.0001 to $0.01. No fractional shares will be issued; shareholders receive one whole share in lieu. The ticker CHSN remains unchanged. This is a capital structure event typical for Nasdaq compliance, not a special situation like a tender offer or going-private transaction.

FTS.brief: Fortis Inc. filed a Form 6-K attaching its Q1 2026 investor presentation materials used in its earnings conference call. This is a routine periodic report of a foreign private issuer, not a special situation. No acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, tender offer, going-private transaction, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC event, or abrupt management change is described. The filing is merely an earnings-related disclosure.

IPHA.brief: Innate Pharma SA (Nasdaq: IPHA) filed a Form 6-K with a press release announcing a conference call and webcast for its Q1 2026 business update. Management roster for the call includes CEO Jonathan Dickinson, CMO Sonia Quaratino, COO Yannis Morel, and CFO Frederic Lombard. The event is scheduled for May 13, 2026, to discuss quarterly progress. No financial terms, M&A, or special-situation catalyst are disclosed. This is a routine business update announcement under Rule 13a-16 by a foreign private issuer. The filing does not trigger any special-situations classification; it is strictly a periodic operational update with no transactional or structural changes. What to watch: Standard quarterly performance review, no risk-arb angle.

TMCR.brief: The registrant, The Metals Royalty Company Inc., filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of its acquisition of a 1.0% index-priced gross overriding production royalty on the Mesabi Metallics iron ore project for total consideration of $132.5 million (including $7.5 million in shares). The company also exercised an option to acquire an additional 1.0% royalty on the same terms, which if completed by July 31, 2026 would double the royalty to 2.0%. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The transaction establishes near-term royalty cash flow from a tier-1 DR-grade iron ore project in the U.S., with commissioning expected in H2 2026. Watch for the funding of the additional royalty and commissioning milestones.

NSFDF.brief: NXT Energy Solutions Inc. filed a Form 6-K on July 2, 2026, announcing the appointment of Marvin Singer to its board as the representative for Ataraxia Capital per an Investor Rights Agreement. No financial terms are disclosed. The addition follows a prior agreement, not a sudden forced departure. As a routine board appointment without abrupt change, this filing does not constitute a special situation under the Management Changes category unless the change is itself a forced event. The filing is a standard disclosure of a director appointment.

PAAS.brief: Pan American Silver Corp. (exact-name: Pan American Silver Corp.) filed a Form 6-K reporting first quarter 2026 financial results, highlighting record cash of $1,495M and an enhanced shareholder return framework. The report includes interim financial statements and MD&A. While no specific share repurchase or dividend increase is quantified in this excerpt, the disclosure of a record cash balance and enhanced return framework suggests a capital return initiative. The filing is a routine financial update but the explicit mention of an enhanced return framework justifies a special situation classification. The company is the issuer. Watch for subsequent announcements of share buyback programs or special dividends.

MMM.brief: 3M Company filed an 8-K reporting its subsidiary, Fire Safety Platform Holdco, Inc., entered into a credit agreement for a $1.43 billion term loan facility and a $200 million revolving credit facility. The proceeds will finance the acquisition of Madison Safety Flow Holdings LLC from Madison Industries. The facilities mature 364 days after closing, extendable by up to 12 months. 3M guarantees the borrower's liabilities. Terms of the acquisition itself (price, premium, etc.) are not disclosed. The filing establishes the debt financing for a pending acquisition. Watch for further details on the target and regulatory clearance.

MASS.brief: 908 Devices Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of NIRLAB SA for $15M headline price (subject to adjustments), consisting of $13M cash and 293,368 shares of 908 Devices common stock. The stock consideration was priced at the higher of the 30-day VWAP closing price or a $5.88 floor. An additional $8M in earn-out consideration is payable. The board deemed the terms fair and authorized the deal. Sellers provided customary representations; a general holdback secures post-closing obligations and releases after 12 months. The transaction closed on May 4, 2026. To watch: earn-out milestones and integration of NIRLAB's spectroscopy tech.

BVFL.brief: BV Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 5, 2026, disclosing the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond non-objection to a stock repurchase program of up to 10% of outstanding common stock (~861,000 shares). Repurchases will commence after the current program finishes (~45,000 shares remaining). Purchases may be made via open market, private transactions, block trades, or a Rule 10b5-1 plan. No specific price, premium, or timeline was given. The board has not retained an outside advisor. The filing is a routine capital return announcement, not a special situation. Watch: execution pace and any future accretive actions.

BNGO.brief: Bionano Genomics filed an 8-K announcing the hiring of Alex Hastie, Ph.D. as Chief Scientific Officer, effective July 20, 2026. This is an executive appointment, not a forced departure, but the filing itself constitutes the event. No deal terms, prices, or premiums are involved. The company issued a press release (Exhibit 99.1) highlighting Dr. Hastie's foundational role in optical genome mapping and his return to lead scientific strategy. The filing is routine in nature but qualifies as a management change. What to watch: integration of Dr. Hastie into the leadership team and potential impact on R&D direction; no risk-arb angle.

RENEF.brief: Cartesian Growth Corp II (a blank-check company) issued an unsecured promissory note for $250,000 to its sponsor, CGC II Sponsor LLC. The note bears no interest and is payable upon the earlier of an initial business combination or winding up. The sponsor may convert principal into working capital warrants on identical terms to its IPO private placement warrants. The filing is a routine working capital facility for a SPAC, not a special situation event.

CHYM.brief: Chime Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 6, 2026, reporting Q1 2026 financial results and disclosing a new share repurchase authorization. On May 4, 2026, the board approved a $200 million repurchase of Class A common stock, to be executed through open market or private transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans, with no fixed obligation or timeline. The company also raised full-year guidance. As a capital return event, the buyback signals management's confidence in undervaluation. Monitor execution pace and any insider selling for risk-arb perspective; no premium or close date applies.

XRN-PB.brief: Chiron Real Estate Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the sale of seven inpatient rehabilitation hospital properties for $217.0 million aggregate purchase price under a Purchase Agreement dated June 26, 2026. The buyers were subsidiaries of COMREF Chiron IRF, LLC. The sale closed on June 29, 2026. Post-closing, the properties are owned by a joint venture between Chiron and a U.S. public pension fund, with the pension fund holding 85% and Chiron holding 15% as managing member. No premium, board recommendation, or advisors are mentioned. The transaction was completed quickly. Watch for any post-closing adjustments or operational impact from the retained 15% interest.

ERII.brief: Energy Recovery, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that CEO David Moon will retire after a successor is appointed, and CFO Mike Mancini resigned effective May 6, 2026, with no financial or accounting disagreements. Interim CFO Aidan Ryan was appointed. The filing reports Q1 2026 earnings but the material event is the simultaneous departure of two top executives. No financial terms, premium, or board recommendation are given. The transition is voluntary but abrupt; watch for a permanent CEO hire and any strategic shift under new leadership. No risk-arb angle.

NXDR.brief: Nextdoor Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing Q1 2026 results and a newly authorized share repurchase program of up to $100.0 million in Class A common stock, to expire June 30, 2028. Repurchases may occur on the open market or in private transactions under Rule 10b-18, at management's discretion with no obligation to buy any specific amount. No premium, price per share, or advisor was named. The program is purely discretionary and can be modified or suspended anytime. Watch for actual execution pace and market reaction to the buyback authorization as a signal of management's capital allocation priorities.

WHLRL.company: Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc.
WHLRL.brief: Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust filed an 8-K on June 19, 2026, announcing the engagement of CBRE's National Retail Partners to market 35 of its 59 properties (primarily retail shopping centers across 14 states) as a portfolio sale transaction. No price, premium, or timetable has been disclosed; the board has not yet approved any transaction. The filing is a preliminary, non-binding engagement with no definitive agreement. Watch for the launch of a formal sale process and any unsolicited bids; risk-arb depends on buyer interest and market conditions.

MBGL.brief: Mobility Global Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its spin-off from S&P Global Inc., effective July 1, 2026. S&P Global distributed 100% of Mobility Global common stock to its shareholders on a one-for-one basis as of the June 15 record date. The separation, involving restructuring transactions and several ancillary agreements (Separation and Distribution, Tax Matters, Transition Services, Employee Matters), left Mobility Global an independent public company listing on NYSE under "MBGL" with no retained ownership by S&P Global. No premium, price, or advisor is specified. The distribution was tax-free to S&P Global shareholders. Watch for Mobility Global's first earnings as a standalone entity and any post-spin trading dynamics.

IVPR.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to remove Inspire Veterinary Partners, Inc.'s Class A common stock from listing, effective at the open on June 15, 2026. The delisting follows Nasdaq Staff's November 13, 2025 determination that the Company no longer met Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) (minimum bid price). The Company appealed to a hearings panel, which suspended the stock on January 21, 2026; the delisting became final on March 6, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms are involved. Risk-arb watch: no transaction, so focus is on potential OTC trading or restructuring.

AUGO.brief: Aura Minerals filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing a new share repurchase program. The Board authorized buybacks of up to US$200 million of common shares and Brazilian Depositary Receipts, effective June 18, 2026 until June 18, 2027, open market or privately negotiated. Funded from existing cash. CEO Rodrigo Barbosa emphasized capital returns alongside dividends; LTM yield ~4.5% after Q1 2026 dividend of US$0.78/share. The plan is opportunistic, with periodic board review. Watch for actual buyback execution rate and balance with growth capex; no regulatory clock or imbalanced risk.

HIMX.brief: Himax Technologies, Inc. filed a Form 6-K disclosing that one of its equity-method investees entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by an independent third-party semiconductor technology company for US$80 million in cash. Himax holds approximately 31% of the investee's fully diluted equity. It estimates a pre-tax gain on disposal of US$23-24 million upon closing, subject to working capital and net cash adjustments. The transaction is subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals, expected to close in Q4 2026. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory clearance.

IBN.brief: ICICI Bank Limited filed a Form 6-K disclosing RBI approval to purchase up to an additional 2% stake in its subsidiary ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company to maintain shareholding above 50%. The filing references a prior announcement on February 28, 2026, but does not state price per share, premium, or deal value. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The acquisition is subject to RBI conditions and regulatory compliance. What to watch: regulatory timeline and impact on minority shareholders.

KEP.brief: KEPCO filed a Form 6-K to convene an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on May 21, 2026. The sole agenda is the election of Kim, Tae-Ok as Standing Director, Comptroller Auditor General, and Audit Committee Member. The meeting will be held at KEPCO headquarters in Naju-si, Korea. Shareholders registered as of April 13, 2026 may vote. This is a routine governance item, not a special situation. No transaction, activist campaign, or strategic review is involved. The filing updates foreign private issuer shareholders on a non-routine board election, comparable to a US proxy statement for director election.

LU.brief: Lufax Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K on May 7, 2026, announcing it regained compliance with NYSE continued listing standards after filing delinquent periodic reports. The company had delayed its 2024 20-F due to an auditor change but filed it on February 17, 2026, within an NYSE extension through April 30, 2026. On April 30, 2026, it also filed semi-annual financials for the period ended June 30, 2025, becoming current with SEC filings. The NYSE confirmed compliance and will remove the late-filer indicator. No specific deal terms, financial consideration, or board recommendations are provided. This is a routine regulatory compliance update, not a special situation.

MDA.brief: MDA Space Ltd. filed a 6-K attaching a pricing term sheet for a treasury offering of 20 million common shares at US$35.60 per share, raising US$712 million (US$818.8 million if over-allotment exercised). The proceeds fund the acquisition of ~70% of CLS via a put option agreement. The offering is a secondary capital raise, not a direct capital return to shareholders; thus it is classified as Capital Returns because the issuer is raising equity for a specific acquisition, which is a special-situation financing. The filing includes a 30-day over-allotment option for underwriters. Watch for regulatory approvals and the closing of the CLS acquisition.

NOMD.brief: Nomad Foods Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the implementation of a Co-Investment and Share Option Matching Sub Plan under its 2025 Equity Incentive Plan, effective May 5, 2026. The plan grants options to certain directors and senior leaders, including the CEO, CFO, and Co-Chairmen, contingent on their purchase and holding of a specified number of ordinary shares. Options cliff-vest based on share price hurdles ranging from $16.00 to $25.00 or more, with a five-year term and exercisable between the third and fifth anniversaries. This is an equity incentive arrangement, not a special situation like an acquisition or activist campaign.

PONY.brief: Pony AI Inc. filed a Form 6-K attaching a monthly return submitted to HKEX for April 2026. The return reports an increase in authorized share capital of 20,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares (par value USD 0.0005, added USD 10,000 to authorized capital) via re-designation of undesignated shares, approved at an EGM on April 2, 2026. No shares were issued during the month; total issued shares remained 352,452,783. The filing includes a public float sufficiency confirmation. This is a routine capital maintenance disclosure, not a special situation.

RYET.brief: Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. (Nasdaq: RYET) filed a Form 6-K on May 22, 2026, attaching a press release announcing that its strategic associate, Link Door Smart Company, entered a procurement and service agreement with Alfyaseh Trading Est. for the HanLink Chinese Learning Platform in Saudi Arabia. The agreement includes a one-year non-exclusive platform license, deployment, training, support, and updates, with service coordination through Ruanyun's Saudi Regional Headquarters. This is a commercial agreement with no disclosed financial terms, premiums, or board recommendations. While it follows prior Saudi market initiatives, the filing does not constitute a special situation event like an acquisition or restructuring; it is an ordinary business development announcement. Watch for further updates on international expansion and the planned transition toward the Formind Group identity.

WBX.brief: Wallbox N.V. files Form 6-K announcing court approval of its financial restructuring plan by the Commercial Court of Barcelona. The plan refinances approximately €169.6 million of outstanding financial debt and includes a capital increase. Following customary formalities, the plan becomes binding on all affected creditors and will implement a new capital structure. The restructuring aims to strengthen liquidity and support operational continuity while pursuing sustainable profitability. No transaction price per share, premium, or advisor is disclosed. Watch for effectiveness date and execution of the business plan; risk-arb focus is limited as this is a creditor-led reorganization.

WYHG.company: Wing Yip Food Holdings Group Ltd
WYHG.brief: Wing Yip Food Holdings Group filed a Form 6-K disclosing an EGM to approve a private placement of 14,000,000 new ordinary shares at KRW 1,600 per share, raising KRW 22.4 billion (~HKD 113.6 million). Proceeds are allocated to working capital, marketing, and R&D. The board recommends approval, with subscribers including Wang Tingfeng, Wong Sio Chan, and Rui Xing International. Shares are subject to a one-year lock-up and delivered through KSD. The ESG is a rights-style issuance to specific investors.

AORT.brief: Artivion, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of Endospan Ltd., an Israeli aortic-stability-device company. The base purchase price was $175.0 million, paid entirely in cash, with a net payment of approximately $131.3 million after offsetting intercompany loans. Contingent consideration of up to $200.0 million is payable based on future milestones. The transaction was executed via a Securities Purchase Option Agreement dated September 11, 2019, as amended. Escrow accounts of $16.5 million (indemnity) and $1.0 million (adjustment) were established. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Artivion financed the deal from internal sources. The acquisition closed immediately upon filing. Watch for integration of the Nexus product line and potential milestone achievements triggering contingent payments.

AEI.brief: Alset Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing it terminated a February 5, 2026 agreement to sell 505,341,376 shares (99.55%) of Hapi Metaverse Inc. to HWH International Inc. for $19,910,603 via a convertible promissory note at $1.85/share, with 1% simple interest and a 5-year maturity. Management mutually determined termination was in both parties' best interests; no penalties or fees were paid. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium details are mentioned. The filing reports only the termination of the prior accord. The key watchpoint is whether any alternative transaction for Hapi Metaverse emerges.

BBT.brief: Beacon Financial Corp filed an 8-K announcing receipt of Federal Reserve non-objection for a $50 million stock repurchase program adopted April 29, 2026. The program runs from May 5, 2026 to May 4, 2027, authorizing open-market or negotiated repurchases at prevailing market prices. Terms: $50 million total authorization, no per-share price or premium stated. The board approved the program subject to regulatory clearance, which is now received. This is an issuer capital-return event via open-market buybacks. Watch for execution pace, potential price support, and impact on share count going forward.

BBIO.brief: BridgeBio Pharma filed an 8-K announcing a $500 million stock repurchase program approved by its Board on May 6, 2026. Repurchases may be executed in open market or private transactions at management's discretion under Rule 10b-18, with no obligation to repurchase any specific amount. The program can be suspended or discontinued anytime. No price, premium, or expected completion date was disclosed. This capital return signal reflects management's view of undervaluation. Watch for actual repurchase pace and potential impact on share overhang; risk-arb angle is limited as it is not a fixed-price tender.

FCCO.brief: First Community Corp announced a share repurchase plan authorized by its Board, allocating up to $7.5 million (approx. 3.4% of total shareholders' equity as of Mar 31, 2026) to buy back common stock through May 5, 2027. Repurchases may occur via open market or privately negotiated transactions at management's discretion, subject to market conditions, share issuance, and regulatory requirements. The plan is not a binding obligation and can be suspended or cancelled at any time. No specific price, premium, or tender offer mechanics are outlined. Focus on execution pace, actual buyback volumes, and potential EPS accretion.

FTHAW.brief: Forefront Tech Holdings Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering of 10,000,000 units at $10.00/unit, raising $100M gross proceeds. Simultaneously, it completed a private placement of 370,000 units at $10.00/unit to sponsor Next Lion Sponsor Holdings LLC and BTIG, LLC, raising an additional $3.7M. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-half redeemable warrant ($11.50 exercise price). The SPAC now has $103.7M in trust. Filed as a blank-check company IPO. Next watch: target acquisition announcement within 24 months or liquidation.

GUT-PC.brief: The Gabelli Utility Trust filed an 8-K reporting that Mario J. Gabelli, a key figure, was hospitalized after a medical incident. His condition is improving but return timeline is unknown. GAMCO implemented its succession plan, naming Christopher J. Marangi as President. Day-to-day operations continue under co-CEOs and the Gabelli Value team co-CIOs lead portfolio management. No deal terms, financial transactions, or strategic corporate actions are disclosed. The filing is an informational update on a leadership disruption, not a special situation event.

GTN-A.brief: Gray Media announced a quarterly cash dividend of $0.08 per share on common and Class A common stock, payable June 30, 2026 to holders of record June 15, 2026. The Board authorized this recurring capital return via an 8-K filing with press release. No special event or strategic change is attached; the filing solely details the dividend declaration. This represents a routine capital return to shareholders. Investors should watch for future dividend declarations and any shifts in payout policy, though no arbitrage angle is present.

GENVR.brief: Gen Digital Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing financial results and a Board-approved restructuring program on May 5, 2026. The restructuring aims to streamline operations and adopt AI technologies, with expected charges of ~$50M implemented over twelve months. This is an internal cost-reduction initiative; no acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation event is identified. The restructuring is described as part of ongoing transformation efforts, with estimates subject to change. The disclosure is strategic, but lacks specific details like job cuts or advisors, and the program is not a standalone event typically triggering a major category. Watch for future updates on costs and timing.

KDKRW.brief: Kodiak AI filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, announcing a private placement of 15,384,609 shares at $6.50 per share and accompanying warrants exercisable at $6.00 per share, for gross proceeds of ~$100M. Investors include new institutional holders, existing stockholders, and an Ares affiliate. The warrants are immediately exercisable, expire in five years, and include cashless exercise provisions. The company intends to use net proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes. There is no acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation; this is a standard equity financing.

LTH.brief: Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a share repurchase from affiliates of Leonard Green, TPG, and Partners Group. The company bought 2,192,500 shares at ~$28.60 each for ~$62.7 million in a private transaction. The repurchase was authorized under a board-approved stock buyback program from February 2026. Mechanics: the deal was a private sale exempt from registration, reducing overhang from large sponsors. What to watch: the company may continue repurchases under its existing program; no premium or discount relative to market was disclosed, so the risk-arb angle is minimal.

LPCN.brief: Lipocine Inc. filed an 8-K (Items 8.01 and 9.01) on May 7, 2026, solely to disclose that it had updated its corporate investor presentation, filed as Exhibit 99.1. No merger, tender offer, activist campaign, strategic review, restructuring, or other special situation event is described. The filing is a routine update of marketing materials, constituting an ordinary current report. No deal terms, prices, premiums, advisors, or board recommendations are mentioned. The disclosure is purely informational and does not trigger any special-situations classification.

RITE.brief: MineralRite Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a private transaction between two existing securityholders: Abstract Concepts 1618 LLC agreed to acquire 6.9 million shares of Series NMC Convertible Preferred Stock and associated warrants from NMC, Inc. The company is not a party. No new securities are issued. Specific economic terms were not disclosed. Post-transaction, Abstract will beneficially own ~37% of common stock on a converted basis. The company entered a Shareholder Control Limitation and Standstill Agreement capping Abstract's voting power at 45% and prohibiting control attempts. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for any future proxy contests or triggering events that could alter the standstill.

ON.brief: On June 25, 2026, ON Semiconductor (onsemi) filed an 8-K announcing a definitive agreement to acquire Synaptics via a merger. Under the terms, each Synaptics share will be exchanged for 1.350 shares of onsemi common stock, implying Synaptics equityholders will own ~12% of the combined company. The onsemi Board unanimously approved the deal; no appraisal rights are available. Synaptics stock will be delisted from Nasdaq post-close. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger. The filing did not state a premium or fixed price. The close depends on regulatory and shareholder approvals; the risk-arb spread hinges on relative stock movements and deal completion timing.

OGEN.brief: Oragenics Inc. filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, disclosing a signed Letter of Intent with Sigyn Therapeutics to license CardioDialysis, an extracorporeal blood purification technology, for treating TBI-induced systemic inflammation. The license would grant exclusive rights to develop and commercialize CardioDialysis for TBI and other neurodegenerative diseases. No deal price, premium, or specific financial terms were announced. The license is complementary to Oragenics' existing ONP-002 program. The transaction is contingent on a definitive agreement. Watch for execution risk and potential shareholder updates on licensing milestones.

PCTY.brief: Paylocity Holding Corp filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, announcing its board approved a $1 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, supplementing the $350 million remaining as of March 31, 2026. The program allows repurchases via open market, 10b5-1 plans, or private transactions, with timing and amount dependent on market conditions and other factors. No specific price or expiration was set; the program does not obligate repurchase of any shares and may be modified or suspended. This capital return signals management's view of undervaluation; watch for actual buyback pace to gauge commitment.

POST.brief: Post Holdings filed an 8-K disclosing the planned transition of President/CEO Robert V. Vitale to Executive Chairman, effective October 1, 2026, and the appointment of COO Nicolas Catoggio as President/CEO. The board approved the changes on May 5, 2026. No deal terms are provided as this is a management succession event. The filing also includes routine quarterly earnings results. The transition is orderly with sufficient notice, making this a forced/planned departure rather than abrupt. Watch for any strategic shifts under new leadership or potential related activism.

SPT.brief: Sprout Social, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing that its board authorized a $50 million share repurchase program. The program allows the company to buy back its Class A common stock (NASDAQ: SPT) in open-market or privately negotiated transactions. No specific price, premium, or duration was disclosed; execution details will be determined by management. The repurchase is discretionary and may be suspended or terminated at any time. The filing is a routine capital-return event, not a tender offer. Watch for subsequent 10b5-1 plans or actual repurchase disclosures for sizing and execution pace.

AGNT.brief: eXp World Holdings filed an 8-K announcing it acquired NextHome, Inc., a national real estate franchise, effective May 7, 2026. The acquisition integrates NextHome's franchise model with eXp's cloud-based brokerage, forming a multi-model platform for real estate professionals. No financial terms (price, premium, consideration) were disclosed. eXp also announced a ticker change from EXPI to AGNT, effective May 8, 2026. NextHome's management will continue leading the franchise. The filing lacks structural details or advisor names. Watch for future disclosures on purchase price, accretion, and integration progress; the deal signals a strategic pivot to a hybrid franchise/cloud model.

ECCV.brief: Eagle Point Credit Co Inc. filed an 8-K regarding its conversion from a Delaware corporation to a Delaware Statutory Trust, effective May 22, 2026, along with a name change to Eagle Point Credit Company. Stockholder and board approvals were obtained. Each common and preferred share converts into corresponding beneficial interest shares. All tickers and exchange listings remain uninterrupted. No consideration, premium, or special distribution is involved. This is a structural reorganization, not a typical special situation. Watch for potential tax implications or operational changes post-conversion.

CNI.brief: Canadian National Railway Co (CN) filed a Form 6-K announcing a public debt offering of US$750 million, consisting of US$300 million 4.350% Notes due 2029 and US$450 million 4.950% Notes due 2036 under an effective shelf registration statement. Joint bookrunners are J.P. Morgan, RBC Capital Markets, and SMBC Nikko. Proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including commercial paper repayment. The offering closes May 12, 2026, subject to customary conditions.
