This is an ordinary debt financing transaction, not a special situation, as it lacks any transformative corporate event such as an acquisition, spin-off, or restructuring.

MAXNQ.brief: Maxeon Solar Technologies, Ltd. (Under Judicial Management) filed a Form 6-K disclosing that on June 18, 2026, letters of demand were delivered to certain subsidiaries accelerating the outstanding principal and accrued interest on its 1st Lien and 2nd Lien Convertible Senior Secured Notes due 2028/2029. The acceleration was triggered by events of default arising from voluntary judicial management applications, with the High Court of Singapore placing the company under interim judicial management on April 9, 2026, and full judicial management on May 29, 2026. The judicial managers are reviewing the demand letters and will release further announcements. This filing signals a formal creditor enforcement action against a company already in court-supervised restructuring in Singapore, equivalent to a U.S. Chapter 11 filing. Watch for potential asset sales or liquidation outcomes as the judicial management process unfolds.

SCNI.brief: Scinai Immunotherapeutics Ltd. filed Form 6-K containing audited financial statements of its newly acquired subsidiary, Scinai Biopharma Services Ltd. (formerly Recipharm Israel Ltd.), and unaudited pro forma financial information for the acquisition completed on February 17, 2026. No deal terms, price, or premium are disclosed in this filing; it is a post-closing accounting compliance filing. The board previously approved and completed the acquisition. The filing serves to update the SEC and incorporate these financials into the registrant's registration statements. This is a routine reporting requirement, not a new special-situations event. What to watch: integration updates and subsequent operational performance of the CDMO business.

ADT.brief: ADT Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that three Apollo-designated directors resigned after Apollo sold all remaining shares via a secondary offering. Under an underwriting agreement dated May 4, 2026, Selling Stockholders (Apollo entities) sold 102,000,366 shares; concurrently, ADT repurchased 29,142,961 shares from underwriters under its existing $1.5 billion buyback plan. The offering and repurchase closed May 5, 2026. Bylaws were amended to remove Apollo-related references. No terms (price, premium, etc.) are stated in this excerpt. Watch for future capital allocation updates and potential ownership stabilization.

APG.brief: APi Group Corp (NYSE: APG) filed an 8-K announcing a $500M senior unsecured notes offering by its wholly owned subsidiary APi Group DE, Inc. to fund acquisitions of Onyx-Fire Protection Services and Wtech Fire Group, plus an amendment to its existing credit agreement to extend Term Loan B maturity to 2033 and upsize the revolver to $1.0B maturing 2031. The notes are offered under Rule 144A/Regulation S. No specific terms, pricing, or advisor named in excerpt. What to watch: market reception of the notes offering and timing of the acquisitions.

UZD.brief: Array Digital Infrastructure (f/k/a U.S. Cellular) filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its sale of select spectrum assets to Verizon for $1.0 billion in cash, following an October 17, 2024 agreement. Concurrently, the board declared a special cash dividend of $11.00 per share payable June 25, 2026 to holders of common and Series A common stock as of June 11. No premium or board recommendation details were disclosed. The transaction is a straightforward asset sale funded by cash consideration. Watch for potential shareholder lawsuits or tax implications of the special dividend; risk-arb focuses on execution finality.

AVAI.brief: AVAI BIO, INC. filed an 8-K reporting the mutual termination of its Joint Venture and License Agreement with Ainnova Tech Inc., originally dated November 8, 2024 (effective November 11, 2024). Under that agreement, the parties had formed Ai-Nova Acquisition Corp. (AAC) to develop AI-based healthcare technologies. The Termination Agreement cancels all obligations and liabilities, with no termination penalties or further financial obligations. AAC will be formally dissolved. Both parties will cooperate on an orderly wind-down. No consideration, premium, or break fee is involved. Watch for any residual disputes or asset transfers between AVAI and Ainnova.

ALCYF.brief: Alchemy Investments Acquisition Corp 1 (Nasdaq: ALCY, ALCYU, ALCYW) disclosed it received a delisting notice from Nasdaq on April 7, 2026, for failing to complete a business combination within 36 months of its IPO registration statement's May 4, 2023 effective date, per IM-5101-2. The SPAC will not appeal; trading will be suspended at the open on May 14, 2026, and a Form 25-NSE will be filed to effect delisting. Securities are expected to commence OTC trading on May 14. No board recommendation or advisor named. Structural note: trust collateral remains available pending redemption, no overhang; regulatory clock expired without a deal. Watch for shareholder redemption decisions and potential liquidation timeline.

CAIIW.brief: Collective Acquisition Corp. II filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO of 22,000,000 units at $10.00/unit for gross proceeds of $220M, and the simultaneous private placement of 5,837,500 warrants to its sponsor at $0.80/warrant for $4.67M. Proceeds totaling $221.1M were placed into a trust account. The filing is a routine update on a blank-check company's IPO and trust funding; it does not involve a business combination, target announcement, or any special-situation event. This is a standard current report for a SPAC's capital formation, not a triggering event requiring classification under special situations.

HUMAW.brief: Humacyte disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq Staff letter notifying it that, for 30 consecutive business days through May 1, 2026, its common stock bid price closed below the $1.00 minimum for continued listing on The Nasdaq Global Select Market under Rule 5450(a)(1). The company has 180 calendar days, until November 2, 2026, to regain compliance by achieving a $1.00 closing bid price for at least 10 consecutive business days. There is no immediate delisting effect; the stock trades under HUMA. The board has not announced specific remedial steps. What to watch: potential reverse stock split or other compliance strategies.

ITRI.brief: Itron, Inc. filed an 8-K on 8 May 2026 reporting that its board authorized a new $200M share repurchase program on 6 May 2026, effective 8 May 2026, over 18 months. Repurchases will be made in open market or via Rule 10b5-1 plans, complying with Rule 10b-18. No price per share, premium, or advisor is stated. The program is discretionary and may be suspended without notice. This is a capital-return event as the issuer directly returns cash to shareholders via buybacks. Watch for execution pace and any trading suspensions.

PBT.brief: Permian Basin Royalty Trust filed an 8-K reporting a Texas court’s approval of a unitholder’s petition to amend the trust indenture. The court eliminated the 75% approval requirement for amendments, replacing it with a majority-in-interest vote with a quorum, and removed the list of prohibited amendments. The trustee executed Amendment No. 2 implementing the court order. This judicial modification of governance provisions does not constitute a traditional special situation like a merger, tender offer, or restructuring. The event is a structural change to voting rights. No deal terms, price, premium, or advisors apply. Watch for potential future amendment proposals now easier to pass.

RMTI.brief: Rockwell Medical disclosed it received a Nasdaq delisting notice for falling below the $1.00 minimum bid price for 30 consecutive business days. The company has until November 4, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at $1.00 or higher for at least ten consecutive business days. No board recommendation or advisor was named. A reverse stock split proposal is included in the upcoming annual meeting proxy. If approved and implemented, the company believes it will cure the deficiency. Risks include shareholder rejection of the reverse split or failure to maintain compliance thereafter. The market should monitor the proxy vote and any subsequent price action.

TDS-PV.brief: TDS subsidiary Array (formerly UScellular) sold select spectrum assets to Verizon for $1.0B cash, disclosed on Form 8-K Item 2.01. The purchase price was paid at closing on June 1, 2026. No board recommendation or advisors named. Post-closing, Array declared an $11.00/share special cash dividend to common and Series A holders, with TDS holding ~70.8M shares. The transaction simplifies TDS's structure and provides cash to shareholders. No regulatory clock or break fees disclosed. Watch for completion of remaining asset sales and the special dividend payout on June 25, 2026.

TOP.brief: TOP Financial Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K furnishing a proxy statement for an extraordinary general meeting on May 27, 2026. The meeting seeks shareholder approval to increase authorized share capital from $1M (1B shares) to $20M (20B shares) by creating additional Class A and Class B ordinary shares, and to adopt amended articles of association reflecting the increase. No price, premium, or strategic transaction is proposed. Shareholders are urged to vote by proxy. While a capital increase may precede future transactions, the filing itself is a routine governance matter.

ALV.brief: Autoliv (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting management approval of a plan to close its manufacturing plants in Türkiye, ceasing steering wheel, airbag, and seatbelt production. The expected pre-tax charge is ~$142M (Q2 2026), with ~$129M cash costs for severance and $13M non-cash write-offs. Annual pre-tax benefit of ~$40M is anticipated from 2027, fully realized by 2028, with ~2,200 employees reduced. The plan addresses excess EMEA capacity. Watch for execution risk in the Turkish Lira currency exposure and regulatory/timing aspects of the closures.

PRTS.brief: CarParts.com filed an 8-K on May 11, 2026 reporting an amendment to its Tax Benefits Preservation Plan (poison pill) that accelerated the expiration date from April 5, 2027 to May 12, 2026, effectively terminating the plan. The amendment, between the company and Computershare Trust Company as rights agent, caused all rights to expire immediately after close of business on May 12. A press release announcing the termination was issued. This is a routine governance change to a shareholder rights plan, not a transformative event, with no structural or strategic implications beyond the plan's discontinuation.

CRCL.brief: The registrant filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 financial results (Item 2.02) and disclosed entry into token purchase agreements (Item 8.01) for a private placement of 740 million ARC tokens at $0.30 per token, implying a $3 billion fully diluted valuation and gross proceeds of ~$222 million. The sale, led by a16z crypto, relies on Rule 506(b) of Regulation D. Lock-up restrictions apply for at least one year after mainnet transition, with extended lock-up for four years; repayment rights arise if tokens are not delivered or transition is not completed by May 2028. The filing is an issuer token presale, not a traditional securities special situation. What to watch: regulatory treatment of token presales and timeline for Arc network transition, as repayment triggers create contingent liability.

HKHC.brief: Horizon Kinetics Holding Corp filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Board Representative Agreement with Texas Pacific Land Corporation (TPL). Under the agreement, TPL agreed to nominate a Horizon designee, Peter Doyle, to the TPL Board, and he was appointed on May 6, 2026, subject to election at the TPL 2026 annual meeting. Doyle also serves on TPL's strategic acquisitions committee. The agreement includes mutual standstill and non-disparagement clauses, barring negative public statements from both sides until the next TPL stockholders meeting. No stake size, price, or premium was provided. This appears to be the outcome of an activist campaign by Horizon to gain board representation. Watch for ongoing board dynamics and potential strategic M&A moves via the strategic acquisitions committee; the risk-arb angle is limited as no transaction is pending.

KWY.brief: Kingsway Financial Services Inc. (registrant) filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Kingsway Warranty Holdings LLC, sold all equity interests of Trinity Warranty Solutions LLC to Trinity Warranty Holding LLC. The aggregate consideration is $5 million cash at closing plus $3 million in secured subordinated promissory notes due in ten years, subject to customary working capital adjustments. The sale closed on May 8, 2026. Representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions include a $50,000 deductible and $500,000 liability cap. What to watch: potential indemnification claims and collection risk on the seller-financed note.

ODYY.brief: Odyssey Health, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing that NeuRX Health, Inc. revoked their definitive agreement from October 14, 2025 (closed April 21, 2026) due to NeuRX's breach of its licensing contract with Davion Healthcare Plc. NeuRX lacked Davion's required written consent to sublicense the BreastCheck product to Odyssey, rendering the agreement void. No financial terms, price, premium, or fees were stated. The board's recommendation or advisors were not mentioned. This represents an immediate cancellation of a closed deal, with no regulatory clock or structural details. Watch for potential litigation or claims by Odyssey against NeuRX for breach of warranty, and any impact on Odyssey's product pipeline.

OSPN.brief: OneSpan Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing the termination of its prior stock repurchase program and the adoption of a new $50 million authorization effective May 7, 2026, through May 7, 2028. The program allows open-market, privately negotiated, or tender offer purchases, at the company's discretion based on market conditions. No specific share number or price terms are required. As a capital return event, the buyback signals management's view of undervaluation; watch for actual repurchase cadence and impact on diluted share count. No advisor or board recommendation details are provided.

PHR.brief: Phreesia, Inc. filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) on May 7, 2026, announcing a restructuring plan to reduce operating expenses. The plan involves eliminating approximately 220 positions, about half of which are contractor roles. Costs are expected to be immaterial and incurred primarily in fiscal 2027, with meaningful annualized run-rate savings reflected in the company's Adjusted EBITDA outlook. The board is not specifically mentioned. No advisor named. The restructuring is a cost-saving initiative, not a liquidation or spin-off. Watch for execution risks and actual savings vs. guidance; no risk-arb angle.

QLEP-WT.brief: Quantum Leap Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting the full exercise of the underwriter's over-allotment option in its IPO, resulting in the purchase of an additional 2,082,608 units at $10.00/unit for $20.8M in gross proceeds, closing on June 22, 2026. The sponsor also purchased 43,946 additional private placement units at $10.00/unit under a pre-existing agreement. No underwriting discounts were paid on the private placement. The filing is a routine capital markets update regarding the consummation of the over-allotment and related sponsor purchase, not a special situation. No risk-arb angle exists; the IPO is fully subscribed.

RITM-PD.brief: Rithm Capital Corp. filed an 8-K announcing a private offering of $500 million in senior unsecured notes due 2031. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, possibly including debt repayment. The notes are offered to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A and to non-U.S. persons under Regulation S. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The offering is unregistered and lacks exchange or registration rights. Structurally, this is a debt capital raising, not a return of capital; classification as a capital return is tentative. Watch for pricing terms and use of proceeds allocation.

SITM.brief: SiTime Corporation filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of certain timing business assets from Renesas Electronics America Inc. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.5 billion in cash plus 3,558,691 shares of SiTime common stock. The cash portion was funded through cash on hand. Concurrently, SiTime entered into a $200 million senior secured revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo as agent. The board recommended the transaction. The acquisition expands SiTime's product portfolio in the semiconductor timing market, and the stock component creates ongoing exposure to SiTime's performance.

TNL.brief: Travel + Leisure Co. filed an 8-K regarding a $900M private offering of 6.250% senior secured notes due 2031. Net proceeds will redeem all $650M of its outstanding 6.625% secured notes due July 2026, repay borrowings under its secured revolver, and for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close May 20, 2026, with redemption conditioned on consummation. This is a liability management transaction, restructuring debt capital rather than an acquisition or divestiture. Watch for closing conditions and redemption execution.

TVTX.brief: Travere Therapeutics filed an 8-K on June 1, 2026, reporting an entry into a license and collaboration agreement with Everest Medicines. The agreement grants Travere exclusive rights to develop and commercialize Everest's BTK inhibitor, civorebrutinib, outside of China and certain Asian countries. Financial terms such as upfront payment, milestones, or royalties were not disclosed. The filing is a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01, containing no merger, tender, or governance change. Watch for future disclosures on financial terms and regulatory milestones.

VRDN.brief: Viridian Therapeutics filed an 8-K announcing the completion of a $250M public offering of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, including full exercise of the underwriters' over-allotment option. The notes are unsecured senior obligations, semiannual interest, convertible at holder's option under certain stock price conditions (130% of conversion price for 20 of 30 trading days). The filing details indenture mechanics and conversion triggers. This is a capital-raising event, returning cash to the company via debt issuance. Watch for dilution risk if conversion conditions are met; the 1.75% coupon and 2032 maturity provide low-cost financing for biotech development.

PSA-PG.brief: Public Storage Operating Co (PSOC), a subsidiary of Public Storage, filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a debt offering of senior notes due 2032 and 2036, fully guaranteed by Public Storage. Proceeds will partly finance PSOC's pending acquisition of National Storage Affiliates Trust (NSA), expected to close in Q3 2026. If the NSA acquisition fails by the outside date (December 16, 2026 or later), PSOC must redeem notes at 101% plus accrued interest. No escrow or collateral secures the proceeds. The offering is not contingent on the acquisition's completion. Watch for acquisition closing risk and mandatory redemption trigger.

ADSEW.brief: ADS-Tec Energy Public Ltd Co filed a Form 6-K reporting a private placement via subscription agreements. On May 28, 2026, it entered into an agreement with Svelland Global Trading Master Fund and Mirabella-managed accounts to issue non-transferable subscription rights for up to 5,000,000 ordinary shares at $1.00 per share; 3,000,000 shares were immediately exercised for ~$3 million gross proceeds. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes. The shares are unregistered and rely on Regulation S. A registration rights agreement provides customary resale shelf rights. Outstanding shares post-deal: 75,002,051. This capital raise restructures equity without an active tender or buyback. Watch for dilution impact and stock price support at the exercise price.

BQ.brief: Boqii Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K on May 14, 2026, reporting entry into a Securities Purchase Agreement on May 11, 2026. The company agreed to issue up to 3,000,000 units at $0.6667 per unit in a private placement under Regulation S, for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $2,000,100. Each unit comprises one Class A ordinary share and one pre-funded warrant exercisable for 2.33 Class A ordinary shares at $0.0001 per share. The warrants are immediately exercisable and expire in two years. Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes and working capital. The filing is a routine capital raise, not a special situation.

MBAI.brief: Check-Cap Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing that MBody AI Corp., the counterparty in its proposed business combination, has expanded U.S. operations to 11 states and entered Canada. The business combination was previously disclosed and is still advancing, with Nasdaq completing an initial review of the listing application on April 30, 2026. No specific deal terms (price, premium, close date) were provided in this filing. The filing serves as a progress update on the SPAC-like merger rather than a definitive agreement. Watch for final Nasdaq approval and shareholder vote timeline; risk-arb centers on regulatory and closing conditions.

ENLT.brief: Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing the results of an institutional tender for Series G notes (unsecured) in Israel, with classified investors submitting prior undertakings totaling approximately NIS 1,368 million (~$472 million). The company intends to accept about 976,000 units at a minimum price of NIS 1,040 per unit, for gross proceeds of ~NIS 1,015 million (~$359 million). This is a notes issuance via expansion of an existing series, not a special situation. Proceeds will fund growth plans. The offering is subject to regulatory approvals including the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. The notes mature in September 2033. This is a capital markets financing transaction, not an event-driven special situation.

OGI.brief: Organigram Global Inc. filed a Form 6-K with exhibits including an MD&A and financial results for Q2 Fiscal 2026. The filing discloses that subsequent to the quarter, Organigram acquired Sanity Group GmbH, a German cannabis leader with operations in Poland, Czechia, the UK, and Switzerland. No specific deal terms (price, premium, or advisors) are provided in the excerpt. The transaction expands Organigram’s international footprint into key European medical cannabis markets. The acquisition is a strategic bolt-on. Watch for integration risks and regulatory approvals in multiple jurisdictions; a risk-arb angle is limited without disclosed consideration.

SMFG.brief: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group filed a Form 6-K disclosing an administrative revision to share figures following a stock split resolved on May 13, 2026. The modification stems from a Board resolution on June 26, 2026 to issue shares under a restricted stock compensation plan, which changed the pre-split issued shares from 3,827,498,140 to 3,829,143,493. The split ratio (one-for-one) and authorized share count remain unchanged. No acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation is involved; it is a routine corporate housekeeping update. Investors can monitor for any future capital actions, but no risk-arb opportunity exists here.

VFSWW.brief: VinFast Auto Ltd. filed a Form 6-K on June 30, 2026, announcing the completion of the transfer of its equity interest in VinFast Trading and Production JSC (VFTP) to a group of purchasers. The transaction followed the split of certain VFTP assets and operations into a newly formed entity. No financial terms, premium, or advisors were disclosed; the filing states only that required corporate, regulatory, and creditor approvals were obtained. VinFast retains no equity in VFTP. The divestiture is part of a strategic shift toward an asset-light model, focusing on R&D, technology, branding, and sales globally. Watch for further restructuring details or any subsequent asset-light transactions.

VINP.brief: Vinci Compass Investments Ltd. filed a Form 6-K containing minutes of its 2026 Annual General Meeting held July 1, 2026. Shareholders passed ordinary resolutions approving fiscal 2025 financial statements and appointing Eugenio Garza y Garza as director. Quorum was 88.02% of shares. No special-situation event such as acquisition, divestiture, or management change—routine AGM results. This is a non-routine but non-special filing.

DIBS.brief: 1stdibs.com, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 11, 2026 announcing its Board authorized a $10.0 million share repurchase program. The program allows open-market purchases, privately negotiated transactions, Rule 10b5-1 plans, accelerated repurchases, block trades, or derivative contracts under Rule 10b-18. No expiration date or minimum share obligation is set; timing and volume depend on market conditions and securities laws. This is a discretionary capital-return initiative, not a fixed-price tender. Watch the pace of buybacks for signaling; no premium or closing date applies.

AOSL.brief: Alpha & Omega Semiconductor Ltd filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a sale of approximately 20.3% equity interest in its Chongqing joint venture (power semiconductor packaging, testing, and wafer fabrication) to SIMIC Holdings Co., Ltd. for aggregate cash consideration of $150 million, paid in four installments. The transaction closed on May 11, 2026, when the final installment was received. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The sale was previously disclosed in a July 2025 agreement, and no pro forma financials were provided as the interest was not significant. Watch for future operational or strategic shifts post-divestiture.

BZYR.brief: Burzynski Research Institute filed an 8-K disclosing that its majority shareholder, Dr. Stanislaw Burzynski, will cease funding SEC reporting costs due to limited resources. The company expects to miss its May 29, 2026 Form 10-K filing and subsequent periodic reports. This may trigger SEC actions including trading suspension under Section 12(k) or registration revocation under Section 12(j) of the Exchange Act. No board recommendation or advisors named. Watch for SEC enforcement steps and potential delisting or loss of trading liquidity.

COLL.brief: Collegium Pharmaceutical filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, announcing the closing of its acquisition of AZSTARYS, a CNS stimulant for ADHD, via the purchase of all membership interests in GPC Commave Holding, LLC and Commave Sub, LLC from Corium Therapeutics Holdings and Corium, LLC. The aggregate consideration was ~$650 million in cash, funded by ~$350 million cash on hand and $300 million from a delayed-draw term loan under a syndicated credit facility. Upside milestone payments of up to $135 million are contingent on AZSTARYS achieving commercial and manufacturing targets. The board had previously approved the transaction; no advisor named. The deal closed on schedule with no regulatory overhang. Watch for future milestone triggers and integration execution.

EPM.brief: Evolution Petroleum Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $0.12 per share quarterly dividend for Q4 2026, declared on May 11, 2026. The dividend is payable on June 30, 2026 to shareholders of record on June 15, 2026. The filing also includes routine financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2026. This is a capital return event via a regular dividend declaration. No premium, tender, or special structure applies. Watch for future dividend consistency as a measure of capital allocation strategy.

GAMG.brief: Global Asset Management Group, Inc. (GAMG) through its subsidiary RI Property Holdings, Inc. acquired 100% of the Seller's 83.125% membership interest in Memorial Real Estate Group LLC (MREG) via a Debt Equity Transfer Assumption Agreement. Total consideration was $6,455,000, comprising a $6 million one-year convertible promissory note (6% interest, convertible at 90% of 30-day VWAP) and $455,000 cash down payment. Following the transaction, Buyer SPE owns 100% of MREG and becomes sole manager. The Seller also assigns its MREG loan interest and resigns as administrative agent. Watch for regulatory filings and note conversion details for risk-arb angle.

JKHY.brief: Jack Henry & Associates filed an 8-K reporting that its Board approved adding 5 million shares to its existing stock repurchase authorization, increasing the total authorization to 6.4 million shares (from 1.4 million remaining). The company has repurchased just over 2 million shares in fiscal year 2026. The buyback program, initiated in October 2002 and increased eight times, will be funded with available cash or short-term borrowings. No price targets or timetables are set. The move signals management's confidence in operations and commitment to shareholder returns. Watch for execution pace and impact on EPS.

RYES.brief: Rise Gold Corp. filed an 8-K reporting that the Superior Court of California denied its Writ of Mandamus seeking recognition of a vested right to operate the Idaho-Maryland Mine. The court acknowledged a constitutional right vested in 1954 but ruled the right was abandoned by 1963. Rise plans to appeal the ruling, which relates to litigation rather than a corporate transaction. No deal terms, stakeholders, or transaction mechanics are present. This is a litigation update, not a special situation. The filing contains no acquisition, divestiture, or structural corporate event.

WASH.brief: Washington Trust Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, announcing that its Board of Directors adopted a stock repurchase program (2026 Repurchase Program) authorizing the repurchase of up to 850,000 shares of common stock, representing approximately 4.5% of outstanding shares (19.1 million shares as of April 30, 2026). No price, premium, or expiration date beyond May 16, 2027, was specified; repurchases are at market prices, subject to market conditions and regulatory constraints. The program can be modified or discontinued at any time. This open-market repurchase program returns capital to shareholders with no structural features like a tender or fixed price. Watch for execution pace and potential suspension if economic conditions deteriorate.

FNV.brief: Franco-Nevada filed a Form 6-K reporting results of its 2026 Annual and Special Meeting of Shareholders held May 12. All nine director nominees were elected with overwhelming support (95.91%-99.79%), PricewaterhouseCoopers was reappointed as auditor (98.32% for), and the say-on-pay advisory resolution passed (91.33% for). No forced management changes, acquisition, or special-situation event occurred. This is a routine meeting outcome disclosure, not a special situation.

HAO.brief: Haoxi Health Technology Ltd filed Form 6-K on May 13, 2026, reporting the closing of a registered direct offering. The company sold 9,000,000 Class A ordinary shares at $0.25 per share and 16,999,998 pre-funded warrants exercisable for 176,034,979 Class A ordinary shares, raising gross proceeds of approximately $6.46 million before fees. The offering closed on May 12, 2026. The company agreed to a 30-day lock-up on further issuances and directors/officers/large shareholders entered 90-day lock-up agreements. Net proceeds will be used for working capital. This is a routine capital raise, not a special situation.

ORLA.brief: Orla Mining Ltd. filed a Form 6-K providing a Q2 2026 operational update and noting its combination with Equinox Gold is on track for Q3 closing. The transaction, announced May 13, 2026, will see Orla acquired by Equinox. No specific price per share or premium was provided in this filing. The filing reports strong gold production of 88,265 ounces in Q2 and a net cash position of $318.7M. The deal remains subject to shareholder, court, and Mexico competition approvals. Watch for regulatory clearance and shareholder vote timing to assess risk-arb spread.

VNET.brief: VNET Group disclosed via Form 6-K a share purchase agreement under which PJ Millennium I and II (Buyers, affiliates of Contemporary Amperex Technology) will acquire up to 650,424,192 Class A ordinary shares from Success Flow and Choice Faith (Sellers, owned by Shandong Hi-Speed Holdings) at US$1.4486/ordinary share (US$8.6914/ADS) in cash, representing ~38.1% of VNET's outstanding shares. The board supports the deal; no advisors named. Closing is subject to approval by SDHG shareholders, expected Q4 2026. A voting and consortium agreement grants Founder Parties voting control over the Buyers' shares post-closing. Watch for regulatory/antitrust clearance and potential changes in shareholder structure.

ACVA.brief: ACV Auctions Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Citibank, N.A. on May 12, 2026, to repurchase $50 million of its common stock under a previously announced buyback program. The company will pay $50 million on May 13, 2026, receiving an initial delivery of ~70% of the underlying shares. The final number of shares repurchased will be based on volume-weighted average price during the term, less a discount, with completion expected no later than Q4 2026. The ASR allows ACV to return capital efficiently, reducing share count and enhancing EPS. Watch for speed of execution and final share price relative to volume-weighted average price.

AAOI.brief: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its entry into three separate lease agreements with Hightower Phase I Owner, LLC for three industrial buildings in Houston, Texas, for manufacturing, warehouse, and office use. Each lease has an initial term of 123 months with periodic rent escalation and an initial rent abatement period. The leases also include purchase options for the buildings. This is a routine real estate lease agreement, not a special situation event. There are no acquisition, divestiture, activist, or other special-situation elements involved. Filing is classified as Other due to the material definitive agreement nature but lacking any special-situation catalyst.

ALLO.brief: Allogene Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting termination of an exclusive license agreement with Overland parties and entry into a Second Amended and Restated Shareholders Agreement. The license, for CAR T therapies in certain Asian territories, was terminated without consideration; Allogene surrendered equity and will retain ~3% of Overland. No termination payments were made. The restructuring alters Allogene's ownership and governance rights. This is not a standard special situation like an acquisition or spin-off; it is a contract termination and equity restructuring. Watch for any subsequent strategic moves by Allogene.

ARMP.brief: Armata Pharmaceuticals filed Form 8-K disclosing entry into a $25 million secured term loan facility with Innoviva Strategic Opportunities LLC, a subsidiary of principal shareholder Innoviva, Inc. The loan carries a 14.0% annual interest rate, matures January 11, 2029, and is secured by substantially all of the company's assets, with subsidiary guarantees. The agreement includes customary covenants and events of default. While a material definitive agreement, this financing does not constitute a classic special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or going-private transaction. It is more akin to a debt financing arrangement. The press release also announced Q1 2026 financial results. No deal terms such as price per share or premium were applicable. The filing is routine debt financing, not a special situation.

BNCWW.brief: CEA Industries Inc. and activist investor YZi Labs entered a cooperation agreement terminating YZi Labs' consent solicitation. YZi Labs holds 2,150,481 common shares and warrants for 21,215,860 additional shares. The board was expanded to six; YZi Labs appointed Ling Ella Zhang, Alex Odagiu, and Matthew Roszak as directors, with replacement rights while holding ≥4.99% stock. The board will add a mutually agreed independent director within 90 days. This settlement averts a proxy fight, with YZi Labs gaining board control. Watch for potential strategic or operational changes under new directors; risk-arb angle limited as no transaction price.

FGMCR.brief: FG Merger II Corp. (SPAC) filed an 8-K disclosing a material definitive agreement for an OTC Equity Prepaid Forward Transaction with Atsion Opportunity Fund LLC Series 2, partially novated to affiliate FG Capital Partners LLC. The seller intends but is not obligated to buy up to 3,000,000 shares of FGMC common stock pre-closing of the business combination with BOXABL Inc. The prepayment amount equals shares times per-share redemption price from trust. This provides potential growth capital replacing redeemed trust assets, not minimum cash. Watch for shareholder vote and redemption levels.

GPATW.brief: GP-Act III Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K disclosing non-redemption agreements with third-party investors to secure 8,074,387 Class A ordinary shares from redemption and votes in favor of an extension amendment at an extraordinary general meeting. Sponsor HoldCo will transfer 403,720 Class A shares to these investors after a business combination closes. No price per share or premium is stated. The filing covers the entry into material definitive agreements, an amendment to articles, and shareholder votes. This is a SPAC seeking to extend its timeline to complete a de-SPAC merger. Watch for the approval of amendments and subsequent business combination announcement.

IBEX.brief: IBEX Limited filed an 8-K on May 13, 2026 announcing its board authorized a $20 million share repurchase program starting May 14, 2026, over one year. Repurchases may be made through open market, privately negotiated, or block trades at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and Rule 10b-18/10b5-1 compliance. The program is funded from existing cash, does not obligate any specific amount, and can be suspended or discontinued anytime. No price per share, premium, or advisor is disclosed. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on shares outstanding; no risk-arb angle as this is a routine capital return, not an M&A event.

LVS.brief: Las Vegas Sands Corp. completed an underwritten public offering of $500M 5.300% Senior Notes due 2031 and $500M 5.650% Senior Notes due 2033. Net proceeds, with cash on hand, will redeem the $1.0B 3.500% Senior Notes due August 2026, pay fees, and for general corporate purposes. The unsecured notes are senior obligations with no subsidiary guarantees, issued under a 2019 indenture supplemented by tenth and eleventh supplemental indentures. Interest is semi-annual; redemption prior to par call dates is at present value. Watch for the August 2026 note redemption execution and potential impact on leverage ratios.

LEAT.brief: On May 12, 2026, Leatt Corp's Board authorized a stock repurchase program for up to $419,410 of common stock through open market purchases under Rule 10b-18 and potential Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, expiring December 31, 2026. The company will repurchase shares at its discretion depending on market conditions, price, and alternative uses of capital. Repurchases may be conducted through a third-party broker under a 10b5-1 plan to avoid blackout periods. The program can be suspended at any time. Watch for periodic disclosure of repurchase volume and price; no risk-arb angle.

NBBK.brief: NB Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 21, 2026 to disclose a slide presentation for an investor bank meeting on June 2, 2026. The presentation includes information on operations and financial performance, with forward-looking statements. No specific deal terms, price, premium, or strategic actions are provided. The filing is a routine disclosure of investor materials, not a special situation.

NVTS.brief: Navitas Semiconductor Corp filed an 8-K on May 13, 2026, reporting entry into a Sales Agreement with Craig-Hallum Capital Group and UBS Securities on May 11 for an at-the-market offering of up to $125 million in Class A common stock. As of May 12, the company sold 6,529,666 shares yielding net proceeds of ~$122 million, fully exhausting the registered amount. This is a routine capital-raising ATM program, not a special situation. No strategic event, activist, or restructuring is involved. There are no deal terms as there is no acquisition or merger; the ATM offering has been completed.

ELAB.brief: PMGC Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its wholly owned subsidiary AGA Precision Systems LLC will merge into another wholly owned subsidiary, A B Aerospace, Inc., with A B as the surviving entity. Membership interests in AGA will be cancelled without consideration; all A B shares remain unaffected. The merger, effective July 2, 2026, is an internal restructuring with no change in ownership or outside party involvement. No deal terms like price or premium are applicable. This appears to be a minor corporate simplification with no strategic or financial impact on shareholders. Watch for any future disclosure of tax or operational rationale.

SHC.brief: Sotera Health filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Stockholders Agreement following a secondary offering by its sponsors, Warburg Pincus and GTCR. The Selling Stockholders sold 31,838,253 shares at $15.168 per share via an underwritten deal with Goldman Sachs. The company received no proceeds. The sponsors' exit triggered the termination of special governance rights, though sponsor-designated directors may remain until term end. This is a capital markets exit event, not a special situation like a going-private or activist campaign. What to watch: any resultant board governance changes or potential for a future strategic review now that sponsor overhang is removed.

OTAI-RI.brief: Starlink AI Acquisition Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO of 10,000,000 units at $10.00/unit ($100M gross proceeds) and a simultaneous private placement of 221,500 units to sponsor JKapital Ltd. at $10.00/unit ($2.215M). Each unit comprises one ordinary share and one right to receive one-fourth of a share upon a future business combination. $100.5M was placed in a trust account. This is a standard SPAC formation and IPO closing, not a special-situation event. The filing reports the capital structure and trust mechanics. No business combination target has been announced. What to watch: the SPAC's two-year window to identify and close an acquisition target.

ISPC.brief: iSpecimen Inc. disclosed on an 8-K that on May 29, 2026, it received a Nasdaq delisting notice for failing to meet the minimum $2.5 million stockholders' equity requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), with reported equity of $814,038 as of March 31, 2026. The company has 45 days to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may grant up to 180 additional days to regain compliance. The common stock (ISPC) continues trading pending the process. A rejection may be appealed to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel. Watch for the compliance plan submission by mid-July and Nasdaq's decision on any extension.

YGMZF.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE on May 18, 2026, to remove MingZhu Logistics Holdings Ltd's ordinary shares from listing. The delisting follows a Staff determination on October 20, 2025, that the company no longer met Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) (minimum bid price). After an appeal hearing on December 9, 2025, the Listing Qualifications Hearings Panel affirmed the suspension, effective December 12, 2025. The delisting becomes effective at the opening on May 28, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing is a mandatory removal procedure under SEC Rule 12d2-2(b). No deal consideration, premium, or break fee applies. Investors should watch for overhang from the delisted shares and potential OTC trading.

CCLD.brief: CareCloud completed the May 15, 2026 full redemption of its 8.75% Series B Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock at $27.52/share ($25.25 plus accumulated dividends), totaling ~$41.6M. The Series B was delisted from Nasdaq as of May 14. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The redemption eliminates the preferred overhang; common stock (CCLD) remains listed. Watch for any residual dividend-related claims or capital structure impact. Risk-arb: no arbitrage opportunity; this is a mandatory redemption, not a tender.

RCAT.brief: Red Cat Holdings filed an 8-K to report its completed acquisition of Quaze Technologies Inc. on May 19, 2026. Red Cat, through a wholly-owned subsidiary, acquired all Quaze shares for approximately 1,923,308 shares of common stock valued at ~$21 million based on a 20-day VWAP, with up to $5 million in additional earnout shares tied to integration, revenue, and gross margin milestones. The closing shares were issued unregistered under the Securities Act. The filing provides no board recommendation or advisor; the deal closed immediately. Watch for earnout achievement and integration of Quaze's Canadian drone technology into Red Cat's defense portfolio.

BUD.brief: Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV filed a Form 6-K furnishing amended articles of association following a shareholder meeting on April 29, 2026. The filing includes a coordinated text of the company's articles reflecting amendments made at that meeting. No terms, prices, stakes, premiums, or dates are provided as this is a routine corporate governance update. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing is a foreign private issuer report incorporating the amended articles by reference into existing registration statements. There is no acquisition, divestiture, tender offer, or other special situation event. What to watch: none, as this is a standard post-meeting filing with no transactional or strategic event.

BNJ.brief: Brookfield Corporation filed a Form 6-K on June 5, 2026, furnishing a management information circular for an annual and special meeting to approve a court-approved plan of arrangement to simplify its corporate structure with Brookfield Wealth Solutions Ltd. under one publicly traded company, Brookfield Corporation Ltd. No financial terms are disclosed in this filing. The board recommends voting in favor of the transaction. The filing is a routine proxy circular related to a corporate simplification; it is not a classic special situation like an acquisition or going-private.

OMAB.brief: This 6-K filed by Central North Airport Group (OMA) announces the payment date for the first installment of a previously declared cash dividend. The total dividend is Ps.4,900 million, paid in two equal installments of Ps.2,450 million or Ps.6.280254872 per share each, with the first payable on May 27, 2026 to holders of record on May 26, 2026. The dividend was approved at the Annual General Ordinary Shareholders Meeting on April 24, 2026. The filing is a routine capital return event, not a special situation such as a restructuring or delisting. Watch for the second installment payment date on November 30, 2026.

GHRS.brief: GH Research PLC filed a Form 6-K disclosing entry into an At-the-Market Equity Offering Sales Agreement with Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated, to offer and sell up to $200 million of ordinary shares (nominal value $0.025 per share) from time to time. The sales, if any, will be made through methods permitted by law as an at-the-market offering under Rule 415(a)(4). The offering is registered under a Form F-3 registration statement. A prospectus supplement dated May 14, 2026, accompanies the filing. This is a routine capital-raising arrangement, not a special situation; no price per share, premium, or expected close is stated. What to watch: actual sales execution and market conditions.

ITRG.brief: Integra Resources Corp. filed a Form 6-K reporting an equity agreement with the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes, granting 517,103 common shares valued at US$1,500,000 (C$3.97/share, based on TSX-V closing price). The grant is a strategic partnership step for the DeLamar Project, involving tribal monitoring and co-development. Completion requires NYSE American approval. No premium, price per share, or break fee is stated, as this is not an acquisition but a non-dilutive equity issuance for stakeholder alignment. Watch for approval conditions and further partnership milestones.

NMG.brief: Nouveau Monde Graphite Inc. files Form 6-K reporting closing of a US$309.5M equity financing package, comprising a private placement with Canada Growth Fund, Investissement Québec, and ENI raising ~US$213.16M at US$1.84/share, and a concurrent bought deal public offering of subscription receipts raising ~US$96.49M. The escrow conditions were satisfied, releasing proceeds to fund the Phase-2 Matawinie Mine. The company confirms a final investment decision for the mine. As a foreign private issuer, this 6-K reports capital raising to fund operations, not a special-situation event.

PBA.brief: Pembina Pipeline Corporation filed a Form 6-K announcing renewal of its normal course issuer bid (NCIB) to repurchase up to 5% of outstanding common shares (29,071,759 shares) via open-market purchases on TSX, NYSE, or alternative venues, starting May 19, 2026 through May 18, 2027. Shares repurchased will be cancelled. The program is opportunistic, driven by management's view that shares may trade below intrinsic value, with purchases subject to financial guardrails, available cash flow, and risk-adjusted returns versus capital investments or debt reduction. Maximum daily purchases on TSX limited to 25% of six-month average daily trading volume (693,233 shares). Prior NCIB expired with zero repurchases. Watch actual buyback execution pace and capital allocation trade-offs with dividends or projects.

PHI.brief: PLDT Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting its submission of a registration statement for the proposed initial public offering (IPO) of its subsidiary, VITRO REIT. The filing is a press release noting compliance with Philippine disclosure rules and Section 17.1 of the Securities Regulation Code. No specific terms such as price per share, stake percentage, or expected closing date were provided. PLDT is the issuer of the filing but may be the selling shareholder in the IPO. The transaction is at an early pre-IPO stage. Investors should watch for the registration statement's effectiveness, IPO pricing details, and any regulatory approvals from Philippine authorities.

TUYA.brief: Tuya Inc. filed a Form 6-K with a press release announcing its annual general meeting (AGM) scheduled for June 18, 2026, in Hangzhou, China. The AGM will consider proposed resolutions, which the board supports and recommends shareholders and ADS holders vote in favor. Record dates are May 22, 2026, for shareholders (Hong Kong time) and ADS holders (New York time). Voting instructions for ADS holders must be given to the depositary, The Bank of New York Mellon. The company also filed its 2025 annual report on Form 20-F. This is a routine AGM notice, not a special situation requiring action. What to watch: no special event or structural change is involved.

AEP.brief: American Electric Power Company (AEP) disclosed entry into forward sale agreements covering 23,543,308 shares of its common stock, at an initial forward sale price of $124.968 per share, in conjunction with an underwritten public offering. The forward purchasers are Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. AEP expects to physically settle on or before May 31, 2028, receiving net proceeds at that time. The transaction functions as an equity forward, allowing AEP to lock in current pricing while deferring share issuance. This is a capital return mechanism for the issuer. The key watchpoint is AEP's discretion on settlement timing; early settlement may indicate near-term capital need.

BRUNW.brief: Boost Run Inc. (Pubco) closed its business combination with Willow Lane Acquisition Corp. (SPAC) on May 8, 2026. No specific terms (stake, price, premium) were disclosed in this 8-K. The board recommended the deal; no advisor was named. At the SPAC's April 30, 2026 meeting, shareholders approved the combination with no redemptions from the ~$134.5M trust. The transaction closed via mergers of the SPAC and Boost Run into Pubco. As a domestic SPAC merger, no US-equivalent mapping is needed. Watch for post-close trading of BRUN/BRUNW and any earnout or lockup details.

CSX.brief: CSX Corporation filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, reporting two items: Item 5.02 (departure of a named officer) and Item 5.07 (Annual Meeting voting results). CFO Stephen Fortune separated immediately, eligible for severance under a prior plan; Steve Watkins assumes his role. This officer departure appears orderly, not forced/abrupt. The meeting results show routine elections and advisory votes. No special-situation transaction is present—no M&A, tender, spin-off, activist campaign, or similar event. The filing is a routine current report covering ordinary personnel and governance matters. There is no deal, no price per share, no premium, and no regulatory or risk-arb angle to monitor. Beyond the description, no further analysis is warranted.

GIII.brief: G-III Apparel Group filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, announcing its entry into a Unit Purchase Agreement to acquire the Marc Jacobs business from LVMH. The structure involves G-III and WHP Global forming a joint venture (IPCo) to buy Marc Jacobs Holdings, with G-III investing approximately $500 million from cash on hand and its revolving credit facility. Post-closing, G-III will operate the Marc Jacobs business under a license from IPCo, which retains the intellectual property. The closing is subject to customary conditions, including antitrust approvals, with an outside date of six months. Watch for regulatory clearance and the joint venture's operational mechanics.

JBTM.brief: JBT Marel Corp filed an 8-K/A to correct the effective date of a previously announced share repurchase program of up to $200 million of its common stock, moving the start from June 1, 2026, to May 18, 2026, through May 31, 2029. The board authorized the program at its discretion, subject to market conditions. The filing also notes a quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share payable June 9, 2026. No premium, advisors, or structural details were mentioned. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share price, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is a standard capital return authorization.

MAIA.brief: MAIA Biotechnology, Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 1.02 to report the termination of its At-the-Market (ATM) offering agreement with H.C. Wainwright & Co., effective seven business days after May 14, 2026. Since the March 2025 prospectus supplement, the company sold 3,116,012 shares for ~$5.68M gross proceeds. This is a routine termination of a securities sales agreement, not an acquisition, tender offer, or other special situation. The filing discloses no price, premium, or board recommendation. The termination appears ordinary and lacks the elements of a special-situation event.

QXL.brief: Quantum X Labs Inc. filed an 8-K voluntarily providing Item 9.01 disclosures (audited financial statements and unaudited pro forma combined financials) for its acquisition of Quantum X Labs Ltd., which closed on March 4, 2026. No price, premium, or stake terms are restated. The filing is a post-closing financial statement update, not a new deal announcement. The board recommendation and advisor are not named. The deal was completed two months prior, so no regulatory clock or risk-arb angle remains; the filing purely satisfies SEC reporting obligations.

SAGU-UN.brief: Shreya Acquisition Group, a blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering (IPO) and private placement on May 8, 2026. The IPO comprised 11 million units (including 1 million over-allotment units) at $10.00/unit, raising $110 million gross. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share, one redeemable warrant (exercise at $11.50), and one right (entitling holder to one-fourth of a Class A share upon a business combination). Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 191,750 private units at $10.00/unit for $1.9175 million. Proceeds will be held in trust pending an initial business combination. This is a routine SPAC IPO filing, not a special situation.

GLW.brief: Corning Inc. had its 3.875% Notes due 2026 redeemed at maturity on May 15, 2026, as notified by the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) via Form 25-NSE. The entire class of notes was paid at par and retired. NYSE filed the removal from listing and registration, effective at the opening on May 26, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading was suspended on May 15. There is no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. No collateral or ownership split applies. The removal is purely administrative; no risk-arb angle as this is a debt maturity, not an M&A event.

BLDP.brief: Ballard Power Systems Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing a definitive agreement to acquire GeoPura Limited for an upfront equity purchase price of £275.0 million (~US$400 million enterprise value), funded by £82.5 million cash and ~50.8 million Ballard common shares at US$5.02 per share (30-day VWAP), plus up to £27.5 million contingent consideration. The transaction establishes Ballard as an integrated hydrogen ecosystem provider with an energy-as-a-service model. No board recommendation or advisors named. Expected to close with synergies of US$25 million annual run-rate EBITDA. Watch for regulatory clearance and milestone achievement for contingent consideration.

BBAR.brief: Banco BBVA Argentina S.A. filed a Form 6-K disclosing that the Central Bank of Argentina authorized a cash/in-kind profit distribution of ARS 69,011,025,123, payable in three monthly equal non-cumulative installments. The distribution follows an April 28, 2026 shareholder meeting resolution; the Board will set timing, terms, and conditions. This is a dividend distribution (capital return to shareholders) rather than a share repurchase or other special situation. As a foreign private issuer, the 6-K reports a material event. Watch for exact per-share amounts and any regulatory or currency constraints affecting payment.

BMM.brief: Blue Moon Metals filed a Form 6-K reporting that its subsidiary Nye Sulitjelma Gruver AS entered into a binding share purchase agreement with VMS Explorations AS (a subsidiary of Alpha Future Funds) to combine their holdings in Norway's Sulitjelma mining district. Under the terms, VMS will acquire 100% of NSG for US$15 million payable in VMS shares, giving Blue Moon a 30% stake in the combined entity. The deal is arm's length, subject to a minimum C$10 million capital raise and listing of VMS on a recognized exchange within 18 months. Blue Moon must maintain its 30% pre-listing interest. The transaction consolidates copper-gold assets in a brownfield district with existing infrastructure. Watch for financing completion, regulatory approvals, and the listing timeline; no premium or break fee disclosed.

EPWKF.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist EPWK Holdings Ltd.'s Class A ordinary shares, effective at the opening of trading on June 12, 2026. The delisting follows Nasdaq Staff's determination that the company no longer met Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) (minimum bid price or market value) and Rule 5250(c)(1) (timely filing). EPWK appealed to a Hearings Panel, which suspended the shares on December 23, 2025; the delisting became final on February 2, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was noted. The filing is a procedural removal notice; the company may seek OTC markets or prepare for potential deregistration. Watch for the company's next steps and any shareholder actions.

GLDG.brief: GoldMining Inc. filed a Form 6-K on May 15, 2026, reporting voting results from its annual meeting of shareholders held on May 14, 2026. The filing discloses the election of six director nominees and the appointment of auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, with a quorum of 27.04% of outstanding shares represented. No transaction, strategic review, activist campaign, or other special situation is announced. This is a routine corporate governance update and does not constitute a special-situation event.

MBFJF.brief: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group filed a Form 6-K announcing progress and completion of a common stock repurchase authorized by the Board on May 15, 2026. Under the program, MUFG repurchased up to 45 million shares (0.40% of outstanding) for up to ¥100 billion. Through June 25, 2026, it bought 31,967,100 shares for ¥99,999,771,608 via Tokyo Stock Exchange market purchases. This is an open-market execution of a board-approved buyback, not a self-tender offer. The repurchase reduces share count and returns capital to shareholders. No timeline for further buybacks was stated. Watch for impacts on EPS and free float.

NCI.brief: Neo-Concept International Group Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval of a share consolidation at its Extraordinary General Meeting. The consolidation ratio is fixed at 8 old shares (par value $0.0003125 each) into 1 new share (par value $0.0025 each), effective May 19, 2026. Fractional shares will be rounded up. The board has authority to set the effective date no later than June 30, 2026. The Class A ordinary shares will trade under symbol NCI with a new CUSIP. This is a routine capital restructuring, not a special situation.

PBK.brief: PowerBank Corp filed a Form 6-K announcing an expansion of its strategic focus into AI compute infrastructure and modular data center development, alongside its existing solar and battery energy storage business. The press release states the company intends to pursue opportunities in modular data centers, AI compute infrastructure, and co-location with existing assets. No specific terms, price, premium, or board recommendation are provided. This appears to be a strategic pivot rather than a formal review process. The filing is a non-US issuer report and does not constitute a binding transaction. Watch for further details on project financing and partnerships.

SVM.brief: Silvercorp Metals Inc. filed a Form 6-K on June 30, 2026, attaching a June 29 news release. The company announced a temporary slowdown at its Ying and GC mining operations in China due to new nationwide safety measures imposed after a coal mine accident. The company identified non-compliances with the Six Major Safety Systems and engaged vendors to complete upgrades costing approximately $5.5 million, plus an additional $6 million for equipment upgrades, expected to take about 50 days. Government procedures allow phased resumption after inspection. No deal terms. This is an operational update, not a special situation.

COLB.brief: Columbia Banking System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.37 per common share, payable June 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of May 29, 2026. The dividend is a recurring capital return event, not a special situation. No M&A, activist, restructuring, or other special-situations catalyst is present. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; monitor future dividend declarations for sustainability or changes.

DK.brief: Delek US Holdings filed an 8-K reporting the closing of Amendment No. 1 to its Amended and Restated Term Loan Credit Agreement. The amendment refinances the existing term loan, reducing outstanding principal to $850 million, extending maturity to six years post-closing, and lowering the interest rate to term SOFR plus 300 bps or base rate plus 200 bps. The credit facility is guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries (excluding Delek MLP entities) and secured by a first and second priority lien on specified collateral. This is a routine refinancing—not a special situation. Watch for compliance with customary covenants.

GCTK.brief: Glucotrack disclosed it received Nasdaq Staff Determination letters on May 11 and May 15, 2026, for non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Rule 5550(a)(2)) and the $2.5M minimum stockholders' equity requirement (Rule 5550(b)(1)). The company intends to request a hearing by May 18, 2026, which will stay delisting pending a Panel decision. At the hearing, Glucotrack plans to present a plan to regain compliance. No financial or structural terms were disclosed. Watch for the Panel's decision timeline and the company's ability to cure deficiencies, as delisting risk remains elevated.

MNST.brief: Monster Beverage Corporation filed an 8-K reporting its annual meeting results and a new $500M share repurchase authorization. The Board authorized an additional $500M buyback on May 14, 2026, supplementing the ~$400M remaining from the prior program. Repurchases may occur in open-market or negotiated transactions. No price, premium, or expiration date were specified. There is no independent advisor or premium disclosed, signaling ordinary-course capital allocation. The filing also includes uncontested director elections and routine advisory votes. Watch for the pace of repurchases as a signal of management's view on intrinsic value; no risk-arb angle as this is a straight buyback, not an issuer tender.

NHC.brief: National Healthcare Corp. (NHC) filed an 8-K reporting completion of its $560 million cash acquisition of 35 skilled nursing and independent living facilities from National Health Investors (NHI) on July 1, 2026. The purchase was funded by borrowings under a credit facility from Bank of America and cash on hand. NHC previously leased these properties. The credit agreement was amended to increase the revolver from $50M to $75M. No premium percentage, board recommendation, or advisor was disclosed. The transaction eliminates the master lease structure, converting NHC from tenant to owner-operator. Watch for integration execution and potential deleveraging actions.

PIIIW.brief: P3 Health Partners Inc. received a letter from Nasdaq Staff on May 20, 2026, confirming the company has regained compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing requirements under Listing Rule 5550(b)(2). The company had previously disclosed non-compliance with at least one standard in November 2025. Based on its Form 8-K filed May 15, 2026, Nasdaq determined the company now meets the market value of listed securities standard. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This delisting-risk resolution removes immediate overhang; watch for sustained compliance in future filings.

SLXNW.brief: Silexion Therapeutics Corp (SLXN) filed an 8-K regarding a warrant inducement transaction. On May 15, 2026, holders of 1,995,092 existing warrants (Series A, B, and Prior Inducement) agreed to exercise them for cash at a reduced price of $0.50/share, generating ~$1.0M gross proceeds. In exchange, Silexion issued New Warrants (Series C and D) to purchase up to 3,990,184 ordinary shares at $0.50/share. The company engaged H.C. Wainwright as placement agent with a 7.0% cash fee. The mechanics involve cash exercise and new warrant issuance, increasing potential dilution. Watch for the share price reaction and subsequent warrant exercises.

VACI-WT.brief: Viking Acquisition Corp. I, a Cayman Islands blank-check company, filed an 8-K reporting entry into Amendment No. 1 to its Business Combination Agreement with NorthStar Earth and Space Inc. (target) and Viking NS Amalgamation Corp. (NewCo). The amendment revises transaction sequencing so that redemption of Viking's public shares occurs before its continuation from the Cayman Islands to Canada and prior to closing; updates mechanics for share/warrant conversions and equity exchanges; and clarifies U.S./Canadian tax treatment. No price, premium, or advisor terms are disclosed. The filing is a standard SPAC business combination amendment—watch for SEC review of the Form F-4 registration statement and shareholder vote timeline.

VWAVW.brief: VisionWave Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026, reporting entry into a binding Acquisition Agreement to acquire 51% of Meteor Aerospace Ltd., an Israeli aerospace and defense company. The transaction values Meteor at a $40.0 million pre-money equity valuation. Consideration is approximately $20.4 million, comprising $6.0 million in unrestricted VisionWave common stock and $14.4 million in restricted common stock subject to a six-month lock-up. The share count will be based on a five-day VWAP prior to closing. Closing conditions include a live flight validation of Meteor's Impact-700 UAS, completion of due diligence, and other customary conditions. Upon closing, VisionWave will appoint three of five directors, designate the Chairman, and approve major actions. Watch for the flight validation milestone and any regulatory or due diligence delays.

KSCP.brief: Knightscope, Inc. filed an 8-K/A to amend its initial March 3, 2026 report regarding the acquisition of all outstanding membership interests of Event Risk, LLC from seller Eric Rose on February 27, 2026. The filing provides audited financial statements of Event Risk and unaudited pro forma combined financials as required by Items 9.01(a) and (b). No purchase price, consideration, or board recommendation details are disclosed. The transaction closed on the signing date. Watch for integration risks and the impact on Knightscope's balance sheet and Nasdaq-listed equity.

DTST.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE to delist Data Storage Corp's warrants from the exchange. The delisting is effective immediately, citing compliance with Rule 12d2-2(a)(2) which permits removal when the entire class is called for redemption. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or shareholder vote was required. The securities were removed without a tender offer or going-private transaction; the move is purely administrative. What to watch: whether the underlying common stock remains listed; holders of warrants should monitor for final settlement terms or potential litigation over the redemption mechanics.

ANTA.brief: Antalpha Platform Holding Co filed a Form 6-K on May 19, 2026, attaching a press release reporting its unaudited first quarter 2026 financial results. The release highlights revenue of $20.7 million (up 52% YoY), net income of $2.7 million (up 85% YoY), and adjusted EBITDA of $13.3 million (up 435% YoY). The filing includes operational metrics for supply chain and margin loan TVL, and references the acquisition of a controlling interest in Aurelion on October 10, 2025. This is a routine earnings disclosure. No transaction terms, deal structure, or strategic event are present. What to watch: no special situation impact.

BWAY.brief: Brainsway Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing a minority-stake investment in Hopemark Health (APS Innovations LLC). BrainsWay will invest $1.5 million initially, with potential for an additional $1.5 million via milestone-based investments, for a minority position in the form of a preferred, annually compounding security. The agreement includes a redemption mechanism. This strategic equity financing is intended to expand access to interventional psychiatry solutions. The transaction is a minority investment rather than a full acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation category. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Watch for milestone achievement and redemption triggers.

EVGN.brief: Evogene Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting that its subsidiary AgPlenus Ltd. and Bayer have discontinued their herbicide development project, effective May 18, 2026. The termination was triggered by the target protein not meeting required product criteria. Under the termination terms, all assets licensed to Bayer under the collaboration, including the APTH1 protein target and associated active molecules, revert to AgPlenus. This is a deal termination between AgPlenus and Bayer; no financial terms, premium, or break fee were disclosed. The reversion of IP rights is noted. This UK-equivalent Form 6-K is incorporated by reference into Evogene's F-3 and S-8 registration statements. Watch for any potential new partnering or licensing activities by AgPlenus.

PLTYF.brief: Plastec Technologies filed a 6-K posting its 2025 annual report, which confirms the voluntary liquidation of its BVI subsidiaries Viewmount Development Limited, Sun Ngai Spraying and Silk Print Co. Ltd., and Sun Terrace Industries Ltd. The liquidation began in March 2026 and completed in May 2026, leaving Plastec with no subsidiaries or operating activities. The company retains a debt-free balance sheet with $5.4M cash and $0.41 book value per share. Management indicated it will evaluate new capital deployment opportunities. Watch for potential cash distribution, new business acquisition, or eventual dissolution.

TME.brief: Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME) files a Form 6-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of Ximalaya Inc. The merger consideration consists of up to $1.26 billion in cash and up to 175,288,891 TME Class A ordinary shares (a mix of newly issued shares and shares underlying equity awards). The deal was previously disclosed on June 10, 2025, and closed on May 18, 2026, making Ximalaya a wholly-owned subsidiary. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee is stated. The transaction is structured as a merger with cancellation of Ximalaya equity. What to watch: integration execution and potential dilution from the share component.

AKAM.brief: Akamai Technologies filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a $3.5 billion convertible note offering: $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 and $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, sold in a private placement to QIBs under Rule 144A. Net proceeds partially funded a $236.6 million convertible note hedge (offset by warrant proceeds) and a $350 million share repurchase of 2,476,298 shares. Remaining proceeds will fund accelerated CIS capital expenditures. Notes are senior unsecured obligations. The simultaneous debt issuance and stock buyback represent a capital return to shareholders via leverage. Watch for dilution impact from potential conversion and any rating agency actions.

GUACW.brief: Berto Acquisition Corp. II filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO and concurrent private placement on May 18, 2026. The IPO consisted of 31,510,000 units at $10.00 per unit, generating $315.1M in gross proceeds. Each unit includes one ordinary share and one-third of one redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50 per share. Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 3,500,000 private placement warrants for $3.5M. Net proceeds of $315.1M were placed in a trust account. The filing also provides the audited balance sheet. This is a routine SPAC IPO closing report, not triggering a special situation category.

BTMCQ.brief: Bitcoin Depot Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing it received a Nasdaq delisting notice after the company and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on May 17, 2026. Nasdaq will suspend trading of the company’s Class A common stock (BTM) and warrants (BTMWW) at the open on May 26, 2026, and will file a Form 25-NSE to remove the securities from listing and registration. The delisting is also based on the company’s failure to timely file its Form 10-Q for the period ended March 31, 2026. The company does not intend to appeal. Trading during bankruptcy is highly speculative; holders face potential significant or total loss.

EZPW.brief: EZCORP filed an 8-K reporting it acquired the remaining 12.3% of Founders One, LLC membership interests on May 14, 2026, achieving 100% ownership, and on May 15, 2026, through Founders, bought 1,360.65 shares of Simple Management Group (SMG) from minority holders, raising its SMG stake to 93%. No price per share, premium, or total deal value was disclosed. The board did not make a recommendation and no advisors were named. The transaction had no regulatory clock; it closed immediately. What to watch: EZCORP may seek full ownership of SMG in the near future.

FLG-PU.brief: Flagstar Bank filed an 8-K announcing planned leadership updates on May 18, 2026. CEO Joseph M. Otting will relinquish the President role while continuing as Executive Chairman and CEO. Richard Raffetto and Lee Smith, both Senior Executive Vice Presidents, were appointed Co-Presidents and Co-COOs, with Raffetto becoming Chief Banking Officer and Smith remaining CFO. Bao Nguyen was elevated to Chief Legal Officer. These changes are part of the bank's succession planning and strategic realignment. Terms include no purchase price or premium. Watch for further organizational shifts as the bank executes its long-term strategy.

FLUX.brief: Flux Power Holdings filed an 8-K regarding a committed equity facility with Roth Principal Investments. The company secured a right, but not obligation, to sell up to $40 million of common stock at its sole discretion over a 36-month period. Under the registration rights agreement, up to 38,461,538 shares will be registered for resale by Roth. No fixed price or premium is stated; purchases are market-driven. The facility provides flexible at-the-market capital, not a tender or buyback. Watch for dilution management and the company's capital deployment strategy.

HYEX.brief: Healthy Extracts Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 100% of Adli Gummies Inc. (dba Imara's Beauty) via subsidiary Healthy Extracts Canada Inc. Consideration includes secured promissory notes totaling $794,000 ($165K to largest shareholder Aaron Hefter; $629K to other holders), 2,159,520 HE Canada Class B shares (exchangeable 1:1 for common stock) issued to Hefter, and 840,480 shares of common stock to other shareholders. The CEO canceled 3,000,000 shares; total issued shares represent ~17.76% of outstanding. Hefter entered a Consulting Agreement as Chief Brand Officer. Watch future dilution from exchangeable shares and regulatory filings.

IBRX.brief: ImmunityBio filed an 8-K to disclose an exclusive development and supply agreement with Japan BCG Laboratory (JBL) for the Tokyo-172 BCG strain. JBL manufactures and exclusively supplies the product; ImmunityBio handles all U.S. development, trials, and regulatory approvals. The agreement is ten years from FDA approval, with ImmunityBio having a right of first negotiation for ex-U.S. territories. No upfront payment; supply vials for regulatory submission are free. Post-FDA approval, ImmunityBio must purchase at least two batches per year. The arrangement is a standard licensing/supply deal with no equity, tender, or special-situation restructuring involved. Watch for FDA approval timeline and commercial launch execution.

LIF.brief: Life360 filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized a $225 million share repurchase program. The program allows open-market, privately negotiated, and block-trade buybacks, possibly under Rule 10b5-1 plans. No specific price, premium, or close date is given; the program is multi-year and aims to offset stock-based compensation dilution. The company cites a strong balance sheet and 12 consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow. Repurchases may be modified or suspended at any time. Watch for ongoing buyback execution and potential impact on share count; no risk-arb angle as this is not a M&A event.

ONTO.brief: Onto Innovation Inc. filed an 8-K announcing plans for a private offering of $1.1B aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2031, under Rule 144A.
