The proceeds will be used for share repurchases and capped call transactions. No specific price per share, premium, or board recommendation was disclosed. The offering is subject to market conditions. The mechanics include a convertible issuance alongside hedging via capped calls to reduce dilution. Watch: pricing terms, conversion premium, and overall capital return impact to equity value.

SSEAR.brief: Starry Sea Acquisition Corp, a blank-check company, filed an 8-K disclosing that its letter of intent (LOI) with Forever Young International Limited for a proposed business combination expired on January 12, 2026, after the exclusivity period ended without definitive agreements. The company stated it does not intend to proceed with the transaction. While this is a SPAC-related update, the filing only reports a terminated LOI without a formal deal, making it distinct from a typical SPAC merger extension or trust announcement. The event is essentially a failed exploratory process, not a conclusive special situation.

SCCG.brief: Sachem Capital Corp. filed an 8-K to report entry into a Contribution Agreement to acquire IRG Master Holdings, LLC from Industrial Realty Group Global, LLC. IRG Global will contribute 100% of the membership interests in exchange for OP Units and shares of Class B common stock. The consideration is equity-based, with no specified price per share or premium. The Sachem Board unanimously approved the transaction. Pre-closing steps include forming an operating partnership, redomesticating to Delaware, and a 20-to-1 reverse stock split. Closing is expected by end of 2026. Investors should monitor regulatory approvals and the successful completion of pre-closing reorganization steps.

SLN.brief: Silence Therapeutics plc filed an 8-K to report entry into an Open Market Sale Agreement with Jefferies LLC, replacing a prior 2021 agreement. The company may offer and sell ADSs (each representing three ordinary shares) in at-the-market offerings up to a maximum program amount, with Jefferies receiving up to 3.0% commission. The filing is a routine at-the-market issuance facility, not a transformative special situation. No specific deal terms, premiums, or change of control are involved. No board recommendation or advisor role is noted beyond Jefferies as sales agent. Watch for market-price-dependent issuance updates, but no arbitrage angle exists.

SNYR.brief: Synergy CHC Corp. disclosed in an 8-K that on May 15, 2026, it received a Nasdaq notice for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Rule 5550(a)(2)) over 30 consecutive business days. The delisting notice has no immediate effect; the company has 180 calendar days, until November 11, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days. If it fails, it may qualify for an additional 180-day period subject to meeting other listing standards and potentially executing a reverse stock split. The board has not announced a recommendation or advisor. Watch for management's plan to cure the bid price deficiency, potential reverse stock split, and risk of eventual delisting.

RPID.brief: Rapid Micro Biosystems filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a direct offering of 71,607 shares of Class A common stock at $1.955 per share, along with Series A warrants (exercisable at $1.955 for one year) and Series B warrants (exercisable at $2.34 for five years), sold directly to directors and officers without an underwriter. The offering is contingent on a concurrent underwritten offering of 3,581,000 shares plus warrants via TD Securities and Lake Street Capital Markets, expected to close May 20, 2026. Proceeds are ~$140,000 before expenses. The filing is a routine capital raise, not a special situation.

NNNN.brief: Anbio Biotechnology filed a Form 6-K reporting results of a Class A meeting and an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) held on May 15, 2026. Shareholders approved an authorized share capital increase from $0.50 to $3,000, creating new Class C ordinary and preference shares; a voting rights increase for Class B shares from 50 to 500 votes per share; and changes to Class B conversion rights. The moves appear aimed at restructuring share classes and voting control. No price, premium, or special-situation deal terms were disclosed. Watch for potential effects on corporate governance or future capital actions.

MT.brief: ArcelorMittal (issuer) filed a Form 6-K announcing the completion of the first tranche and commencement of the second tranche of its 2025–2030 share buyback programme. The first tranche repurchased 10 million shares at an average price of €49.32 per share; the second tranche targets up to 10 million shares. Repurchased shares are held in treasury pending cancellation. The programme aims to reduce capital and meet employee share obligations, with execution dependent on post-dividend free cash flow (minimum 50% returned) and market conditions. The filing is a routine capital return update with no premium or advisor disclosure; monitor continued buyback pace and shareholder authorization.

GCLWW.brief: GCL Global Holdings Ltd (GCL) filed a Form 6-K on May 19, 2026, announcing that its publishing subsidiary, 4Divinity Pte. Ltd., received an additional $10.0 million strategic investment from ADATA Technology Co., Ltd., following prior investments of $3.0M (Dec 2025) and $10.0M (Jan 2026). The investment is intended to support 4Divinity’s game title acquisitions and digital distribution, with potential operational synergies between ADATA's hardware and GCL's game IP. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is disclosed. The transaction appears collaborative rather than transformative; watch for integration details and future funding rounds.

SAM.brief: The Boston Beer Company filed an 8-K announcing a 10b5-1 plan to repurchase up to $25 million of its Class A Common Stock during a period from June 29, 2026 to September 25, 2026. The repurchase is an issuer share buyback undertaken under a pre-arranged trading plan to allow repurchases during blackout periods. The filing includes no details on board recommendation or advisors. The mechanics are a standard 10b5-1 plan, reducing shares outstanding and returning capital to shareholders. Watch for the actual pace of repurchases and any impact on EPS.

BFC.brief: Bank First Corp (BFC) filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a definitive merger agreement to acquire PSB Holdings, Inc. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger, with PSB shareholders receiving 0.3470 BFC shares per PSB share. The aggregate consideration is subject to downward adjustment if PSB's tangible book value falls below $122.8M at closing. Boards of both companies unanimously approved. PSB preferred stock will be purchased by BFC or converted into new BFC preferred shares. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to customary conditions. Watch for regulatory approvals and tangible book value calculations that could affect final consideration.

DAIO.brief: Data I/O Corp filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a private placement, raising $9 million via 869,840 common shares, a $6.8254M convertible debenture (4% coupon, 5-year maturity, convertible into Series B Preferred at $1,000/share), and warrants for 1.08M common shares. The investors are Lytton-Kambara Foundation and Alice W. Lytton Family LLC. Proceeds serve as growth capital; automatic conversion triggers upon shareholder approval at the 2026 annual meeting. This is a structured capital raise, not a standard buyback or dividend. Watch dilution impact and conversion mechanics; no risk-arb angle unless conversion terms change.

ETSS-UN.brief: Energy Transition Special Opportunities filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering (IPO) and a simultaneous private placement on May 18, 2026. The SPAC issued 15,000,000 units at $10.00 per unit, each consisting of one Class A ordinary share and one-half warrant, for gross proceeds of $150 million. Concurrently, the sponsor and underwriter representative purchased 5,375,000 private placement warrants at $1.00 each, generating $5.375 million. Net proceeds of $150.75 million, including $6 million deferred underwriting commissions, were placed in trust. This is a standard SPAC IPO; watch for future business combination announcement and shareholder vote.

AGM-PI.brief: Farmer Mac filed an 8-K reporting the completion of an exempt public offering of 4,000,000 shares of 6.875% Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, Series I. The sale was made under an underwriting agreement dated May 12, 2026, with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC as representative of the underwriters. Terms include a 6.875% dividend rate, non-cumulative, with no stated price per share or premium disclosed. No board recommendation or advisor referenced beyond the underwriter. This is a routine capital-raising transaction, not a special-situation event. Watch for subsequent dividend payments and potential future issuance; no risk-arb angle applies.

HWCPZ.brief: Hancock Whitney Corp. filed an 8-K on May 19, 2026, disclosing a definitive merger agreement to acquire OFB Bancshares, Inc. for $29.273 per share in cash. The transaction involves a two-step merger structure: OFB Bancshares first merges with a Hancock subsidiary, then into Hancock Whitney, followed by a bank-level merger of One Florida Bank into Hancock Whitney Bank. The boards of both companies approved the deal. The agreement includes customary representations, warranties, and covenants. The parties will seek regulatory and third-party consents. The risk-arb angle focuses on regulatory approval timeline and any potential appraisal rights exercised by OFB shareholders.

KMT.brief: Kennametal filed an 8-K under Items 5.02, 8.01, and 9.01 announcing the appointment of Amanda Cole as Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer effective July 21, 2026, succeeding Judith Bacchus who will retire as Chief Administrative Officer on October 1, 2026. Ms. Cole joins from Wesco International and will enter into standard indemnification and officer employment agreements. No material terms such as price, premium, or deal value were disclosed. The filing is a routine officer appointment with no structural mechanics or regulatory clock, and does not constitute a special situation event.

KRP.brief: Kimbell Royalty Partners, LP filed an 8-K announcing the completed acquisition of mineral and royalty interests in the Permian Basin from Mesa Visa Royalties and related sellers. Total consideration was ~$44M cash plus 6.929M OpCo common units and an equal number of Class B units exchangeable for Kimbell common units. No board recommendation or advisor named. The registration rights agreement covering common units issuable upon exchange suggests overhang management. Watch for share dilution drag and any purchase price adjustments; risk-arb focus is on post-close unit exchange mechanics.

NXL.brief: Nexalin Technology, Inc. acquired 100% of PONM, Inc. from GreenLight Ventures LLC for $1.3 million in stock. The consideration shares are issued in four tranches: 45% at closing (959,016 shares), then 20%, 20%, and 15% at 90, 180, and 270 days post-closing. The number of shares is based on a 30-day VWAP before closing, with price floors and ceilings ($0.61-$1.15). The acquisition secures an exclusive license to GLV's software for Nexalin's HALO Clarity program and NeuroCare virtual clinic. The filing does not mention a board recommendation or advisors. Watch for regulatory compliance and future tranche issuances.

PNSB.brief: PSB Financial, Inc., the proposed holding company for Pioneer State Bank, filed an 8-K announcing the upcoming close of its mutual-to-stock conversion and related initial public offering. The subscription offering was oversubscribed by eligible account holders, with 1,719,250 shares sold at $10.00 per share (including 137,540 shares to an ESOP). The conversion closes May 21, 2026, with OTCQB listing expected May 22, 2026. The filing details a rights offering structure where existing depositors had first priority. No advisor, board recommendation, or premium is stated. Watch for regulatory approval timing and post-conversion trading liquidity.

PLMKW.brief: Plum Acquisition Corp. IV, a blank-check SPAC, filed an 8-K announcing an estimated redemption price of ~$10.6973 per public share in connection with its extraordinary general meeting to approve an extension of its business-combination deadline from July 16, 2026 to up to July 16, 2027 via monthly extensions. Shareholders may elect redemption at the trust-account per-share price before the meeting. The closing price on Nasdaq was $10.77. This is a routine SPAC extension/redemption disclosure, not a distinct special-situation event. What to watch: shareholder vote outcome, redemption levels, and ability to find a target before extended deadline.

RPT-PC.brief: Rithm Property Trust Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing that a wholly-owned subsidiary consummated the purchase of a portfolio of multifamily residential transition loans from Genesis Capital LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Rithm Capital Corp. The purchase was executed under a Flow Mortgage Loan Purchase and Sale Agreement with Rithm Loan Aggregation Trust, an affiliate of the Company's external manager. The agreement allows for periodic purchases of loans that meet eligibility criteria, with the Company engaging Genesis as servicer. No specific purchase price, premium, or shareholder vote is mentioned. The filing indicates a related-party transaction but lacks material deal terms. The purchase is effective May 13, 2026.

VAL-WT.brief: Valaris Ltd files an 8-K reporting that CFIUS clearance has been obtained for Transocean Ltd's acquisition of Valaris. Under the Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026, Valaris shareholders will receive 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share. The deal is still subject to HSR Act clearance; a Second Request from the DOJ has been received, and the parties have agreed not to close until at least 60 days after certifying substantial compliance, expected no earlier than late September 2026. Closing remains targeted for H2 2026. The key risk-arb factor is the regulatory timeline from the DOJ Second Request.

PNC.brief: PNC Financial Services Group filed a prospectus supplement (424B5) for an offering of senior fixed/floating-rate and floating-rate notes due 2029. It is a debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. The filing details terms, underwriting, and risk factors but involves no M&A, activist, restructuring, or other event-driven category. No deal terms are applicable. This is a routine debt issuance.

NXE.brief: NexGen Energy Ltd. filed a Form 6-K on May 20, 2026, announcing the appointment of Ryan Podrasky as Chief Financial Officer, effective May 25, 2026, succeeding Benjamin Salter, who is stepping down as CFO but remaining as an advisor for transition. No financial terms, board recommendation, or advisor are mentioned. This is a management change event triggered by a CFO departure and replacement. The filing is a foreign private issuer report under Rule 13a-16. Watch for operational continuity and any future strategic impacts.

PSO.brief: The Form 6-K filed by Pearson plc on May 20, 2026 reports a PDMR transaction: President of Higher Education & Virtual Learning Tom ap Simon purchased 2,621.78 ADRs at $15.1965 each ($39,841.88 total) under the company's Dividend Reinvestment Plan on May 18, 2026. This is a routine insider equity acquisition arising from a standing DRIP, not a special-situation event. No deal terms, board recommendation, or regulatory mechanics apply.

HDL.brief: Super Hi International Holding Ltd. filed a 6-K announcing the resignation of executive director Ms. Liu Li due to work adjustment and duty re-allocation, effective May 20, 2026, with no disagreement with the board, and the appointment of Ms. Jiang Bingyu as executive director effective the same date. Ms. Jiang, age 39, has over 15 years of restaurant operations experience, currently serves as Canadian regional manager, and led the establishment of eight Haidilao hotpot restaurants in Canada. No price, premium, or financial terms are involved. This is a routine board-level change with no special situation beyond management departure.

CTRE.brief: CareTrust REIT, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 18, 2026, announcing a common stock offering of 12,500,000 firm shares (plus up to 1,875,000 optional shares) at $40.225 per share to underwriters. The offering closed on May 20, 2026. Concurrently, the Company entered forward sale agreements with Wells Fargo and JPMorgan for the firm shares, under which forward sellers borrowed and sold shares, with physical settlement expected by May 20, 2027. The Company may elect cash or net share settlement. This structured equity capital raise, via forward sales, defers dilution and provides proceeds; watch for eventual settlement method and share price impact.

NNVC.brief: NanoViricides filed an 8-K reporting a registered direct offering via a securities purchase agreement. It sold 1,133,334 common shares at $1.50/share, plus pre-funded warrants at $1.49999 each (exercisable at $0.00001) for 200,000 shares, and common warrants for 1,333,334 shares at $1.75, exercisable after six months expiring in three years. The offering was under an effective S-3 shelf. The company agreed to a 30-day issuance standstill and a 10-day ATM suspension. This is a capital-raising event; though a warrant overhang exists, the primary purpose is equity issuance without a change of control. Watch for dilution and potential shareholder pushback.

PRSU.brief: Pursuit Attractions & Hospitality, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an amendment to its Equity Purchase Agreement with Flyover Attractions B.V. and Brogent Technologies, Inc. to extend the outside closing date from May 21, 2026, to July 31, 2026, for the sale of its Flyover flying theater attractions business. No price, premium, or advisor was mentioned. The amendment only modifies the deadline; other terms remain unchanged. Closing is subject to customary conditions. The extension pushes back a potential termination date, signaling ongoing regulatory or logistical hurdles. Watch for whether the deal closes by the new deadline or is terminated.

RSRV.brief: The Reserve Petroleum Company filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 Annual Meeting results and a board-approved $10.00 per share cash dividend. All eight director nominees were elected, and HoganTaylor LLP was ratified as auditor. The dividend, declared on May 19, 2026, goes to holders of record on June 3, 2026, payable June 16, 2026. This represents a substantial cash return to shareholders outside a regular quarterly pattern. There are no stated premium, deal structure, or regulatory clocks beyond standard exchange requirements. Watch for whether this signals a broader capital return policy shift or potential corporate simplification.

SCKT.brief: Socket Mobile, Inc. disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency letter on May 19, 2026, for non-compliance with the minimum $1.00 bid price rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)). The company has 180 calendar days, until November 16, 2026, to regain compliance by maintaining a closing bid price of at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days. If compliance is not achieved, Nasdaq may grant an additional 180-day period if other requirements are met. The notice does not immediately affect the listing of the company's common stock (SCKT) on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The company intends to monitor its stock price and evaluate options to cure the deficiency. Investors should watch for any reverse stock split or other remedial actions taken before the deadline.

SGLY.brief: Singularity Future Technology Ltd. disclosed on Form 8-K that Nasdaq granted it an additional 180-day compliance period, until November 16, 2026, to regain the $1.00 minimum bid price for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market under Rule 5550(a)(2). The company previously received a deficiency notice on November 19, 2025. To cure, the closing bid price must be at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days before the Compliance Date. The company may effect a reverse stock split if needed. Failure to comply will trigger a delisting notice, with a right to appeal to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel. Watch for the company's actions to boost share price or execute a reverse split to maintain its listing.

TOMZ.brief: TOMI Environmental Solutions (TOMZ) filed an 8-K reporting entry into a merger agreement to acquire Carbonium Core, Inc. via a merger sub. Consideration comprises TOMZ common stock (19.99% of outstanding pre-close) and Series C preferred stock that, upon conversion, gives Carbonium holders at least 90% of TOMZ capital stock on a fully converted basis, effectively a reverse merger. No cash price per share is disclosed. The board has not yet recommended; shareholder approval is required post-closing for conversion and name change. The deal is a stock-for-stock acquisition with significant dilution risk for TOMZ existing shareholders. Watch for Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635 shareholder vote and regulatory timing.

XXI.brief: Twenty One Capital, Inc. filed an 8-K/A amending its May 20, 2026 filing, disclosing a NYSE non-compliance notice received May 29, 2026, due to its audit committee lacking two independent members under Section 303A.07(a). The NYSE requires cure by June 5, 2026; otherwise, a below-compliance indicator will appear on June 9, 2026. The company expects to appoint an independent member promptly. No price, premium, or deal mechanics are involved. Watch for timely cure or potential delisting risk.

WSBCO.brief: WesBanco, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 20, 2026, announcing a new stock repurchase program approved by its Board of Directors authorizing the repurchase of up to an additional 4.0 million shares of common stock, combining with 0.9 million remaining from a prior authorization for a total of 4.9 million shares, representing approximately 5.1% of shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026. The program has no expiration date and may be effected through open market purchases, privately-negotiated transactions, block trades, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, funded from existing cash and liquidity sources. The filing is a standard capital return event. Watch for execution pace against market conditions.

SLMT.brief: Brera Holdings PLC (d/b/a Solmate Infrastructure) reported results of its June 26, 2026 AGM on Form 6-K. All five director nominees were re-elected with 62%-70% support on 71.49% turnout, defeating a vote-no campaign by RBCH Ltd., an affiliate of RockawayX. RBCH, led by Viktor Fischer, had sought board control after the Board rejected Fischer's proposal to sell RockawayX to the Company, which the Board deemed not in shareholders' interest due to inflated valuation. RBCH also filed a derivative lawsuit pre-AGM. The Company views the campaign as a self-interested control attempt. Watch for further litigation or activist escalation.

HUBCZ.brief: Hub Cyber Security Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting its purchase of Evofem Biosciences' senior subordinated convertible notes and purchase rights from multiple sellers. Hub issued 31,623,000 of its ordinary shares (valued at $1.560/share, based on June 24, 2026 closing price) as consideration, totaling ~$49.3 million. No board recommendation or advisors named. The acquired notes and rights are convertible/exercisable at $0.0154/share into ~1 billion Evofem shares, giving Hub ~88% ownership on a basic basis but only 14% fully diluted due to other instruments. The deal closed on June 26, 2026. The non-US filing is treated as a current report. Watch for regulatory review of ownership limits and potential subsequent steps by Hub to consolidate Evofem.

NBTX.brief: Nanobiotix S.A. filed a Form 6-K providing a first-quarter operational and financial update. The update notes a follow-on offering in May 2026 for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately €86.1 million, including pre-funded warrants, but does not specify price per share, terms, or use of proceeds. The offering is mentioned as part of a broader business update, not as a standalone event. The filing does not detail a board recommendation or advisor. No specific structural or regulatory timeline is provided. What to watch: any subsequent filings detailing terms or why the offering was structured with pre-funded warrants.

SVA.brief: Sinovac Biotech Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing an extension of the deadline for shareholders to submit payment instructions for a previously declared special cash dividend of US$55.00 per common share, payable to holders of record as of May 23, 2025. The submission deadline has been extended from December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026. The dividend represents a significant return of capital to shareholders. The company acts as issuer, distributing cash. Shareholders who have not yet submitted instructions are urged to do so by the new deadline. The extension suggests administrative delays in processing payments. Risk-arbitrage angle: monitor shareholder uptake and any potential litigation or trading disruption related to the dividend mechanics.

YSG.brief: Yatsen Holding Ltd announced the completion of the first tranche of a previously disclosed private placement of RMB-denominated convertible senior notes and warrants, raising an aggregate principal amount equivalent to ~US$120 million. The first tranche closed on May 21, 2026, with Hillhouse joining Trustar Capital and CEO Jinfeng Huang as co-investors in the purchasing vehicle. Proceeds are intended for R&D, supply chain integration, overseas expansion, and M&A. The offering is exempt from SEC registration. Second tranche is expected later this year pending closing conditions. Investors should monitor final terms, conversion mechanics, and potential dilution from the warrants.

AMAN.brief: Amanat Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering on May 18, 2026. The SPAC issued 7,500,000 Class A ordinary shares at $10.00 per share, generating $75 million in gross proceeds; the underwriter has a 45-day option for up to 1,125,000 additional shares. Key agreements include an underwriting agreement with Leerink Partners, a letter agreement with sponsor Amanat Sponsor Holdings LLC, and trust, registration rights, private placement, and administrative services agreements. The proceeds will be held in trust pending a business combination. Watch for the target acquisition announcement and deal structure.

BXSL.brief: Blackstone Secured Lending Fund (BXSL) entered into an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture for $650 million aggregate principal amount of 5.900% notes due 2031, issued pursuant to an effective shelf registration statement on Form N-2ASR. The notes mature on May 21, 2031, bear semi-annual interest, and are unsecured general obligations ranking senior to subordinated debt, pari passu with unsecured unsubordinated debt, and effectively junior to secured debt. The fund may redeem notes at its option at any time. A change-of-control repurchase event triggers an offer to repurchase at 100% principal plus accrued interest. No terms such as price per share or premium are applicable. This debt issuance, while capital markets activity, does not fit any core special-situation category (e.g., capital return, restructuring); it is a routine shelf takedown. What to watch: the fund's asset coverage ratio compliance and note trading levels relative to straight corporate debt.

GTLS.brief: Chart Industries filed an 8-K reporting that Baker Hughes filed a Form CO with the European Commission on May 21, 2026, initiating Phase I review for their pending acquisition. Under the July 2025 Merger Agreement, Chart will be acquired by Baker Hughes via a merger of Merger Sub into Chart, with Chart surviving as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary. The filing does not disclose financial terms or advisor names. The Phase I review timeline suggests closing expected in July 2026, subject to EC and other regulatory approvals. Watch for Phase I clearance or a Phase II referral; risk-arb focuses on regulatory timeline and any conditions imposed.

NOEMR.brief: CO2 Energy Transition Corp. (SPAC) filed an 8-K reporting that on May 18, 2026, its sponsor deposited $229,700 into the trust account to extend the deadline to complete a business combination by one month, from May 22, 2026 to June 22, 2026. The sponsor also issued a convertible promissory note for the same amount. The board authorized the extension; no advisor named. Up to five further one-month extensions are possible. Watch for the June 22, 2026 deadline and risk of liquidation if no deal is announced.

CHUC.brief: Charlie's Holdings filed an 8-K reporting an unregistered sale of equity securities. On May 20, 2026, the company entered subscription agreements for 6,350,000 common shares at $0.20/share. Total consideration was $1.27M: $270k cash plus $1.0M debt forgiveness. Proceeds for working capital / amending PMTAs. No board recommendation or advisor named. Exempt under Section 4(a)(2). This is a private placement / capital raise, not a special situation.

CODX.brief: Co-Diagnostics filed an 8-K disclosing a $3.0M private placement with institutional and accredited investors. The company will issue 54,915 shares of common stock at $1.821 per unit (share plus common warrant), pre-funded warrants to purchase 1,592,532 shares at $0.0001 each, and common warrants for 3,294,894 shares exercisable at $1.571 per share for five years. Proceeds fund general corporate purposes. Maxim Group LLC acted as exclusive placement agent. The deal includes a 60-day lock-up on further equity issuance. This is a capital-raising event, not a strategic restructuring or acquisition. What to watch: potential dilution from warrant exercise and aftermarket stock price pressure.

QBTS.brief: D-Wave Quantum Inc. filed an 8-K announcing it signed a non-binding Letter of Intent for $100M in proposed funding under the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act, administered by the Department of Commerce. The funding would be provided in exchange for $100M in D-Wave common stock issued to the Department, contingent on executing definitive award documents. The funds are intended to accelerate development of annealing and gate-model quantum systems at R&D facilities in Florida, Connecticut, and Canada. This is a government grant/strategic partnership, not a traditional M&A or capital markets event. Watch for definitive agreement execution and further CHIPS Act award details.

EQR.brief: Equity Residential filed Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 on July 9, 2026, in connection with its merger with AvalonBay Communities, Inc. announced May 20, 2026. The all-stock deal values AvalonBay at $0.442 per share and Equity Residential at 0.442 per share (subject to exchange ratio). Boards of both companies unanimously recommend the merger; Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Goodwin Procter serve as legal advisors. The transaction is structured as a merger of equals, with Equity Residential issuing shares to AvalonBay stockholders. Collateral includes stock exchange mechanics; no break fee disclosed. Closing expected in early 2027 pending regulatory approvals and shareholder votes. Watch for FTC clearance and shareholder meeting dates.

LXU.brief: LSB Industries filed an 8-K reporting it will assume full ownership of a carbon capture and sequestration project at its El Dorado, Arkansas facility from Lapis Carbon Solutions. Total consideration and remaining completion capital are estimated at approximately $95 million, with portions contingent on timely achievement of defined milestones and completion activities. The effective date is May 18, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, deal structure, or regulatory timeline is disclosed. This is not a standard special-situation transaction; watch for project completion milestones and cost overruns as key risk factors.

LILAP.brief: Liberty Latin America Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing the declaration of a special dividend of Series A Preference Shares. For every ten common shares, holders receive one share of newly issued 9.0% Fixed Rate Cumulative Perpetual Redeemable Series A Preference Shares, par value $0.01. The dividend is payable quarterly starting September 15, 2026, at 9.0% per annum of the liquidation price. Unpaid dividends accumulate and increase the liquidation price after a 30-day cure period. The board authorized the dividend via an authorized committee. This capital return distributes preferred equity, not cash, enhancing shareholder yield. Watch for potential redemption terms and liquidity impact on common shares; risk-arb angle is limited as it's a dividend, not an M&A event.

NNUP.brief: Nocopi Technologies filed an 8-K reporting its wholly owned subsidiary's acquisition of substantially all assets of Polymeric U.S., Inc.'s specialty ink and coating business. Consideration totaled $2,650,000, comprising $1,900,000 cash ($1,750,000 paid at closing, $150,000 holdback), assumption of specified liabilities, and issuance of 500,000 Nocopi common shares. Closing occurred simultaneously on May 18, 2026. The board authorized the agreement; no advisor named. The holdback secures working capital adjustments and indemnification, released in tranches over 18 months. Watch for post-closing working capital resolution and any earnout or indemnity claims affecting final economics.

PSBD.brief: Palmer Square Capital BDC Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a $0.03/share supplemental dividend for Q2 2026, payable July 13, 2026 to holders of record June 26, 2026. This is in addition to the base $0.36/share dividend. The supplemental dividend is paid from excess undistributed net investment income. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium is mentioned as this is a routine dividend declaration. The filing is a standard disclosure of a capital return event. Investors should monitor future quarters for recurring supplemental dividends.

RACC.brief: Research Alliance Corp III files Form 8-K reporting the completion of its initial public offering (IPO) on May 21, 2026. The SPAC issued 7,500,000 Class A ordinary shares at $10.00/share, generating $75M in gross proceeds. Simultaneously, the sponsor purchased 275,000 private placement shares at $10.00/share for $2.75M. Net proceeds of $75M were deposited into a trust account with Continental Stock Transfer Trust Company. The filing includes an audited balance sheet. As a blank-check company, the focus now shifts to identifying a target for a business combination within the required timeframe. Watch for subsequent acquisitions or liquidation risk if no deal is announced.

STX.brief: Seagate Technology Holdings plc filed an 8-K announcing the closing of privately negotiated exchange agreements with holders of its subsidiary's 3.50% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2028. Under the exchanges, $185.908 million principal amount of notes was exchanged for $185.908 million in cash plus 2,023,124 ordinary shares of Seagate. The share count was determined over one trading day beginning May 21, 2026. The exchanges closed on May 26-27, 2026. This debt-for-equity swap reduces leverage and dilutes shareholders. No board recommendation or external advisors were disclosed. Watch for potential further liability management or impact on credit ratings.

TRINZ.brief: Trinity Capital Inc. filed an 8-K to report the issuance and sale of $300 million aggregate principal amount of its 7.000% Notes due 2031, entered into via an underwriting agreement with Keefe, Bruyette & Woods and MUFG Securities Americas Inc. The notes are senior unsecured obligations, maturing May 21, 2031, with semi-annual interest. The filing also includes an eighth supplemental indenture with the trustee. This is an ordinary debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation.

UNMA.brief: Unum Group filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Unum Life Insurance Company of America, entered a Master Transaction Agreement with Fortitude Reinsurance Company Ltd. to reinsure a portion of its closed block individual long-term care business. The agreement includes a partial recapture from a captive and a retrocession to a third-party reinsurer. Terms such as price or premium are not disclosed; statutory reserves for the reinsured business were $3.8B as of March 31, 2026. Closing is expected in 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and execution of related agreements. Watch for regulatory clearance and the final structure of the retrocession.

NFBK.brief: Northfield Bancorp stockholders are being asked to vote on the proposed acquisition by Columbia Financial, Inc., a newly formed Maryland corporation, in conjunction with Columbia Financial's conversion from mutual to fully public stock holding company structure. Under the merger agreement dated January 31, 2026, each Northfield Bancorp share will be exchanged for a variable number of Columbia Financial, Inc. common shares (exchange ratio between 1.8729 and 2.5340), with the merger closing immediately after the conversion. Columbia Financial, Inc. is concurrently offering up to ~192.6 million shares at $10.00/share, requiring a minimum sale of ~142.4 million shares. Unsubscribed subscription shares may be issued as merger consideration to Northfield Bancorp stockholders, subject to a cap below 50% of post-merger outstanding shares. The merger is conditioned on shareholder approvals and regulatory clearances. Watch for subscription offering results and regulatory timeline.

ABIT.brief: Athena Bitcoin Global filed Form 15 with the SEC on May 22, 2026, certifying termination of its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act and suspending its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The filing cited Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and related provisions. As of the certification date, the company had approximately 215 holders of record of its common stock, par value $0.0001 per share. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The deregistration eliminates ongoing SEC reporting obligations, reducing transparency. What to watch: the stock may become illiquid; risk-arb angle is inapplicable as this is a deregistration, not a going-private transaction.

BPTH.brief: Bio-Path Holdings filed an 8-K announcing a shareholder update and repositioning, including cancellation of a reverse split, engagement of advisors for strategic and financial investor introductions, and board approval of a digital asset treasury 2.0 program using AI to trade and accumulate cryptocurrencies. The company also approved the assignment of up to $10M of a $57.9M judgment (plus interest) awarded to CEO Vikram Grover, to be paid in notes, preferred stock, or common shares upon monetization. No specific terms, prices, or timing are provided. This filing is not a standard M&A, tender, or restructuring event but a strategic pivot into crypto operations, warranting a special-situation classification.

AMT.brief: American Tower Corp (AMT) filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Strategic Collocation Agreement with DISH Wireless L.L.C., effective June 2, 2026. The termination notice was delivered by AMT, and DISH revenue has been fully reflected in churn since January 1, 2026, with no expected impact on 2026 financial results. AMT continues litigation against DISH regarding obligations under the agreement. This is not a special situation but a contractual termination and legal dispute.

NRXP.brief: NRx Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K announcing its intention to conduct an underwritten public offering of common stock, with BTIG as lead bookrunner and Lucid Capital Markets as joint bookrunner. The offering includes a 30-day underwriter option for an additional 15% of shares. Proceeds will be used for working capital and general corporate purposes. The offering is subject to market conditions and will be made under an existing effective shelf registration statement (Form S-3). As a routine capital-raising announcement without a definitive price, size, or timeline, this is not a special situation but an ordinary public offering filing. Investors should watch for the prospectus supplement for final terms.

EZGO.brief: The filing is a Form 6-K disclosing an update to an existing at-the-market (ATM) equity offering facility. EZGO Technologies Ltd. reported that as of May 14, 2026, it had issued 325 million ordinary shares under the Sales Agreement with AC Sunshine Securities LLC, raising ~$24.9M gross proceeds (~$21.8M net after 3% commissions). The company has ~$75.1M remaining capacity under the $100M facility. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, including R&D and US subsidiary expansion. This is a routine capital-raising update, not a special situation event.

ELOG.brief: Eastern International Ltd. filed a Form 6-K containing a notice, proxy statement, and proxy card for an Extraordinary General Meeting of shareholders scheduled for June 22, 2026. The meeting will consider ordinary resolution 1 to re-designate 1,000,000 issued preferred shares as Series A preferred shares and adjust authorized share capital, and special resolution 2 to adopt an amended memorandum and articles of association. This is a routine corporate governance matter involving share class redesignation and charter amendments, not a transformative special situation event. No price, premium, advisor, or transaction mechanics are disclosed. Watch for shareholder vote outcome.

EMPG.brief: Empro Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K on May 22, 2026, disclosing receipt of a delinquency notification from Nasdaq on May 19, 2026, for failure to file its annual report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, violating Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The company has 60 days to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, it may receive up to 180 days from the original due date, until November 11, 2026, to regain compliance. Trading has been suspended since October 9, 2025. The company is working with professionals to prepare the 20-F and compliance plan. Watch for the filing of the compliance plan and potential hearing if rejected.

FUTU.brief: Futu Holdings Ltd filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of an investigation notice and administrative penalty pre-notification from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) regarding unlicensed securities, fund sales, and futures business in mainland China. The proposed penalty is approximately RMB1.85 billion (USD271 million) plus a personal fine of RMB1.25 million on CEO Li Hua. The company may submit defenses and request a hearing; it has implemented rectification measures. Funded accounts from mainland China represent ~13% of total. This regulatory enforcement action is not a special situation category but an Other material event. Monitor CSRC final determination and business impact.

NMM.brief: Navios Maritime Partners L.P. filed a Form 6-K containing its quarterly operating and financial review and prospects for the three months ended March 31, 2026, with no specified deal terms, board recommendations, or advisors. The report discusses forward-looking statements, risks, and financial condition, but does not announce any transaction or special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring. This is a routine earnings update filed by a foreign private issuer, equivalent to a domestic issuer's earnings release. No special-situation event is present; the filing is purely informational and operational in nature.

SA.brief: Seabridge Gold Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing the closing of its spin-out of Valor Gold Corp. via a statutory plan of arrangement under the Canada Business Corporation Act, effective June 3, 2026. Seabridge transferred its 100% interest in the Courageous Lake gold project to Valor. Each Seabridge share was exchanged for one new Seabridge share and approximately one Valor share per 1.957 Seabridge shares held, resulting in 55,000,000 Valor shares outstanding. The Supreme Court of British Columbia approved the arrangement on May 27, 2026. Old Seabridge shares were suspended from trading on June 4, 2026, with new Seabridge shares and Valor shares listing on June 5, 2026. Watch for Valor's OTCQB listing and post-spin valuation.

SELXF.brief: Semilux International Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Determination Letter dated May 15, 2026, indicating delisting from The Nasdaq Capital Market due to failure to regain compliance with the $1.00 bid price rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)) by May 11, 2026, and ineligibility for a second compliance period due to not meeting the $5 million stockholders' equity initial listing requirement. Additionally, the company has not filed its Form 20-F for FY2025. Delisting is scheduled for May 26, 2026, unless a hearing is requested. The company intends to request a hearing and an extended stay, but there is no assurance of success. Watch for the hearing outcome and the company's compliance plan.

WAI.brief: Top KingWin Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of a disposition. Its wholly-owned indirect subsidiary Sky KingWin (HK) sold its subsidiary Guangdong Tiancheng Jinhui Enterprise Development Group Co., Ltd. to Junze Management Co., Limited for $218,100 cash. The transaction closed on June 18, 2026, after all conditions were satisfied. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The buyer is unaffiliated. Following closing, the buyer assumed all assets and liabilities. This is a small divestiture; watch for any subsequent restructuring or strategic pivot by the registrant.

YDKG.brief: Yueda Digital Holding filed a 6-K to provide notice and proxy for an extraordinary general meeting on June 12/13, 2026 to consider a share capital reduction and reorganization under Cayman Islands law. The proposal reduces par value of issued Class A and B ordinary shares from US$4.00 to US$0.0001 by cancelling US$3.9999 paid-up capital per share, creating a distributable reserve. Authorized but unissued shares are subdivided 1-for-40,000, then a cancellation reduces authorized share capital to US$1,000 split into 9,000,000 Class A and 1,000,000 Class B shares at US$0.0001 par. No price, premium, advisor, or stake is stated. This is a capital structure simplification/recapitalization, not an acquisition or special situation event. Watch shareholder approval and Cayman legal compliance; no arbitrage angle.

ZENA.brief: ZenaTech, Inc. filed a Form 6-K press release announcing that it signed a binding agreement to acquire a Brisbane-headquartered Australian land surveying and spatial services firm (35-year-established). Terms include no stated price, premium, or advisors; it is the 22nd DaaS acquisition, subject to regulatory approvals. The target has three offices in Queensland and serves government/infrastructure clients. The deal expands ZenaTech's AI drone platform into Asia-Pacific. Watch for regulatory clearance timeline and integration into the DaaS network; no risk-arb spread available due to undisclosed terms.

AHRT-PA.brief: AH Realty Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the first closing of its Multifamily Disposition, selling 9 of 11 multifamily properties for ~$485M in aggregate proceeds under a $562M purchase agreement with an unrelated third party. The remaining two properties are expected to close by end-2026 and mid-2027. No board recommendation or advisor is named in this filing. The transaction reduces the company's multifamily exposure and generates significant cash. Watch for completion of the remaining sales and use of proceeds.

AVXL.brief: Anavex Life Sciences Corp. disclosed in an 8-K filed May 22, 2026, that it received a Nasdaq delinquency notice on May 20, 2026, for failing to timely file its Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q due to the period ended March 31, 2026, violating Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The notice has no immediate delisting effect; shares trade under AVXL on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The company has until July 20, 2026, to submit a compliance plan, with a potential 180-day extension to November 16, 2026, if accepted. Non-acceptance triggers a hearings panel appeal. Anavex stated it is working to file the 10-Q and regain compliance. What to watch: Timeliness of the 10-Q filing and Nasdaq's plan acceptance; risk-arb angle is limited as this is a compliance issue, not a M&A event.

CVCO.brief: Cavco Industries filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) announcing a $150 million stock repurchase program approved by its board on May 18, 2026. Purchases may be made in open market or privately negotiated transactions; no specific price, share count, or expiry date is set. The program is discretionary and can be suspended at any time; it will be funded by existing cash. The filing also contained fiscal Q4 and FY2026 earnings results. The buyback announcement is a non-binding capital return authorization. Watch for actual execution pace as a signal of management's view on undervaluation. There is no risk-arb angle as this is not an M&A event.

GTBP.brief: GT Biopharma disclosed on Form 8-K that on May 20, 2026, it received a Nasdaq Staff letter granting an additional 180-day compliance period, through November 16, 2026, to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)). The company had previously been notified of non-compliance on November 20, 2025, and failed to cure during the initial period ending May 19, 2026. Nasdaq found the company eligible for the extension because it meets all other initial listing standards for the Capital Market. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The company plans to monitor its stock price and evaluate options to regain compliance. There is no assurance of cure; delisting risk remains if the bid price does not hold at $1.00 for ten consecutive business days by the deadline. The risk-arb angle: no M&A event here—this is a routine deficiency notice; only actionable if the company pursues a reverse stock split or other remedial action, which may create trading volatility.

LVWR-WT.brief: LiveWire Group (through its wholly owned subsidiary LiveWire EV, LLC) acquired substantially all assets of Dust Motorcycles, Inc., covering electric motorcycle and dirt bike design, development, manufacturing, distribution, and powertrain technology. Consideration totals up to ~$14.0 million, comprising $375k cash, $500k in common stock at closing, three annual installments of $875k each in stock, and contingent earn-out payments of up to $11.25 million in stock. Shares valued using 30-day VWAP. The filing includes entry into a material definitive agreement and indemnification provisions. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for integration milestones, earn-out achievement, and stock-based dilution risk.

RNAZ.brief: Transcode Therapeutics filed an 8-K/A disclosing a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the $2.5M minimum stockholders' equity requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), with reported equity of $1.25M as of March 31, 2026. The company has 45 days (until July 3, 2026) to submit a compliance plan. It expects to regain compliance via stockholder approval of Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock conversion at an upcoming meeting; a preliminary proxy was filed May 8, 2026. If no approval by December 31, 2026, holders may elect redemption at estimated fair value, with the preferred classified as temporary equity. Watch the stockholder vote and potential redemption overhang on equity.

CCAP.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the 5.00% Notes due 2026 of Crescent Capital BDC, Inc. The entire class of notes matured and was redeemed on May 25, 2026, as permitted by 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(2). Trading was suspended on May 26, 2026, with delisting effective June 8, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is cited. The action is a routine removal following debt maturity; no collateral, overhang, or ownership implications exist. For risk-arb watchers, this is a non-event as the notes have been fully redeemed—focus should be on reinvestment alternatives.

GMM.brief: Global Mofy AI Ltd filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an offering of 8,247,420 Class A ordinary shares accompanied by Series A and Series B warrants, at a price of $0.97 per unit. The Series A warrants have a five-year term and a reset feature based on 80% of the lowest VWAP during a ten-day period, with a floor of $0.194; Series B warrants have a two-year term and allow cashless exercise. The company is raising capital through this equity-linked structure. There is no board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for dilution from warrant exercises and the potential impact of the reset price mechanism on share price.

HKIT.brief: HiTek Global Inc. filed a Form 6-K furnishing its Notice of 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and proxy statement. The meeting will be held on July 29, 2026. Proposals include re-appointment of directors and auditors, a 1:3,750 subdivision of Class A ordinary shares to reduce par value from $0.375 to $0.0001, authorization for the board to implement one or more share consolidations (aggregate ratio not exceeding 1-for-6,000) within two years, and a name change to Biddance AI Systems, Inc. These are routine governance and capital structure proposals. No special-situation event is disclosed.

ICLR.brief: ICON plc filed a Form 6-K disclosing a Nasdaq deficiency notice due to delayed Form 20-F filing. The company missed the periodic filing deadline, triggering a 60-day cure period. No transaction, activist, or restructuring event is underway. The filing is a routine non-compliance update, not a special situation. The only event is a potential future delisting risk if the plan fails. Watch for the plan submission and eventual 20-F filing.

KNRX.brief: KNOREX Ltd., a Singapore-based foreign private issuer, filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a NYSE American notice of non-compliance for failing to file its annual Form 20-F for FY2025 by the extended deadline of May 15, 2026. The NYSE American has provided up to a six-month Initial Cure Period through November 15, 2026, with a possible Additional Cure Period through May 15, 2027, at the Exchange's discretion. If the filing is not cured, suspension and delisting procedures will commence. The Company is working with advisors to file the 2025 Form 20-F but cannot assure regaining compliance. The stock continues trading during the cure period. This filing maps to a US equivalent of a late filing notice triggering potential delisting. Watch for the next filing date and any further NYSE American actions.

KYIVW.brief: This is a Form 6-K furnished by Kyivstar Group Ltd. disclosing its acquisition of six solar power plants in the Lviv region. The total consideration is UAH 3.6 billion (~USD 80.8 million) for 105 MW capacity. No per-share price, premium, or board recommendation/advisor is mentioned. The assets generated UAH 682 million revenue and UAH 596 million EBITDA in 2025. The acquisition is part of Kyivstar's energy diversification strategy. Regulatory rules for Ukraine's unified energy system apply. Watch for integration progress and impact on energy cost hedging.

TGB.brief: Taseko Mines Ltd. filed a Form 6-K (foreign private issuer report) attaching a press release about its upcoming annual general meeting (AGM), which includes a proposal to change the corporate name from Taseko Mines Ltd. to Trekor Metals Ltd., subject to shareholder vote. No financial terms, price, premium, or transaction consideration are disclosed. The board unanimously recommends voting FOR all resolutions. This is a routine AGM circular/notice requesting approval of name change, director elections, auditor appointment, and say-on-pay. No special-situation transaction or extraordinary event is announced. What to watch: shareholder vote outcome on June 24, 2026.

EDIT.brief: Editas Medicine filed an 8-K to announce an underwritten public offering of 55,555,556 shares of common stock and accompanying warrants to purchase an equal number of shares. The combined public offering price is $2.25 per unit, with net proceeds estimated at ~$117 million. Cantor Fitzgerald and Wells Fargo Securities are lead underwriters. The company expects closing on May 27, 2026. The warrants have an exercise price of $3.50, are immediately exercisable, and expire 30 days after announcement of Phase 1 data. This dilutive financing strengthens the balance sheet and funds operations, so the key watchpoint is potential near-term dilution and the stock's reaction to the offering.

XZO.brief: Exzeo Group filed an 8-K announcing a $12 million share repurchase program authorized by its Board, effective immediately. A Rule 10b5-1 trading plan was adopted, allowing repurchases in open market or private transactions via a third-party broker subject to SEC constraints. No price or premium was specified, and the program is discretionary. The filing is a routine capital return announcement with no time-bound commitment or specific terms. The action is a standard buyback, not tied to activism or restructuring. Key risks include lack of obligation to repurchase and potential suspension.

HLLY-WT.brief: Holley Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a $25 million share repurchase program approved by its Board. The program has no time limit, no minimum purchase obligation, and may be modified or discontinued at any time. Repurchases may occur on the open market (Rule 10b-18), in private transactions, or via other lawful means. The company reaffirmed its commitment to year-end net leverage below 3.5x. No price per share, premium, or specific timeline is stated. The program signals board confidence but lacks specific terms; watch for pace of buybacks and any leverage or debt reduction updates as indicators of execution. Risk-arb angle: minimal as this is an open-market authorization with flexibility.

KNSA.brief: Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K regarding a deed of waiver with Baker Bros. Advisors LP, on behalf of certain shareholders. The deed waives the shareholders' conversion rights for Class A1/B1 shares into Class A/B shares if such conversion would result in beneficial ownership exceeding 49.9% of the company's outstanding voting rights. The waiver requires a 75% shareholder vote to amend, terminate, or waive. This is a governance/ownership restriction, not a capital markets event or restructuring. What to watch: any future attempts to modify the ownership cap or change in control dynamics.

LCCCR.brief: Lakeshore Acquisition III Corp., a blank-check company, filed an 8-K on May 22, 2026, disclosing entry into a merger agreement with CPRO Electronics Holding Limited and its subsidiary. The SPAC will first undergo a reincorporation merger into a Cayman subsidiary, then Merger Sub will merge with CPRO Korea. No specific price per share, premium, or valuation was disclosed. The board issued no recommendation in the excerpt. Structural notes include automatic unit separation and share conversion. A risk-arb angle awaits definitive valuation, shareholder vote, and regulatory approvals with a timeline to close.

NL.brief: NL Industries, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its reincorporation merger from New Jersey to Delaware, effective May 26, 2026. The merger was executed via an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated May 19, 2026, under which Predecessor Corporation merged into NLI Holdings, Inc., the surviving entity. Each share of Predecessor common stock automatically converted into one share of successor common stock with identical par value. The reincorporation was approved by shareholders on May 14, 2026. This filing also establishes NLI Holdings as the successor issuer under Rule 12g-3. No terms are applicable as this is a domicile change, not an acquisition or restructuring. Watch for normal NYSE listing continuation under the new name.

NOG.brief: Northern Oil and Gas, Inc. (NOG) filed an 8-K reporting its completed acquisition of oil and gas assets from Parallax Energy Operating Inc. for CA$237.0M in cash (including a CA$37.5M escrow deposit) plus 3,689,413 NOG common shares. The cash portion is subject to post-closing settlement and was funded via cash on hand, free cash flow, and the revolving credit facility. NOG also entered into a registration rights agreement for the stock consideration. The deal was previously announced on May 22, 2026, and closed on June 1, 2026. Watch for final purchase price adjustments and potential dilution from share resales.

PGNY.brief: Progyny, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K that its Board approved a share repurchase program of up to $200 million of common stock. The program will be funded from available cash; repurchases may occur in the open market (including Rule 10b5-1 plans) at management's discretion based on stock price and market conditions, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. No specific price, premium, or timeline was provided. The program does not commit the company to any particular number of shares. Watch for periodic disclosures of repurchase activity under this authorization.

XHLD.brief: TEN Holdings issued 500,000 shares of common stock to a single investor at $1.00 per share, raising gross proceeds of $500,000 in a private placement exempt from registration under the Securities Act. Concurrently, the company entered into a registration rights agreement requiring a resale registration statement to be filed within 30 days. The financing follows a Nasdaq deficiency notice received May 26, 2026, citing non-compliance with the $2.5 million stockholders' equity requirement for continued listing. The company has 45 days to submit a plan to regain compliance. The risk-arb angle centers on whether the equity injection will satisfy Nasdaq's listing standards and avoid delisting.

GECCI.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed a Form 25-NSE to delist the 5.875% Notes due 2026 of Great Elm Capital Corp., effective May 27, 2026. The delisting is pursuant to 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(1), indicating the notes have reached maturity or are otherwise no longer traded. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or shareholder vote is applicable. The action removes the notes from Nasdaq listing, with no structural complexities like collateral or overhang. Watch for the final redemption or call of the notes and any subsequent dissolution of the security.

TBBB.brief: BBB Foods Inc. (Tiendas 3B) filed a Form 6-K announcing a proposed follow-on public offering of 13,304,174 Class A common shares, with 700,000 shares from the company and 12,604,174 from selling shareholders, plus a 30-day underwriter option for up to 1,995,626 additional shares from the issuer. The offering, subject to market conditions, will use proceeds for general corporate purposes and strategic investments. J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are global coordinators; BTG Pactual, Santander, and Scotiabank are joint bookrunners. No price, premium, or close date is specified. This is a registered secondary offering, not a special situation.

IMOS.brief: ChipMOS filed a Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval of a cash dividend distribution of NT$1.23 per common share (approx. US$0.78 per ADS) from capital surplus, declared February 24, 2026, with ex-dividend date June 29, 2026, record date June 29, 2026, and distribution date July 24, 2026. The withholding tax rate decreased from 21% to 0% due to payout from capital surplus. This is a routine dividend announcement, not a special-situation event. The filing serves only as a notice to ADS holders via Nasdaq.

DETX.brief: Liberty Defense Holdings, Ltd. filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing a HEXWAVE system deployment at LaGuardia Terminal B and a shares-for-debt settlement. In the shares-for-debt transaction, the company will settle CAD$117,000 in outstanding debt by issuing 23,306 common shares at CAD$5.02 per share, plus a CAD$350,000 cash payment. The board determined the issuance is in the company's best interest to preserve cash. The closing requires TSX Venture Exchange approval. The shares are subject to a four-month hold period and are not registered under U.S. securities laws. This non-dilutive debt settlement is a routine financing arrangement, not a transformative special situation. Watch for exchange approval and potential shareholder dilution.

PASW.brief: Ping An Biomedical Co., Ltd. filed a Form 6-K disclosing it received a Nasdaq deficiency letter for failing to maintain a minimum $1 bid price per share. The company was granted an additional 180-day compliance period until November 23, 2026, and intends to cure the deficiency via a reverse stock split if necessary. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing serves as a notification of potential delisting risk. What to watch: whether the company can sustain a closing bid price of at least $1 for ten consecutive days before the deadline, or if it will implement the reverse split to regain compliance.

PLRZ.brief: Polyrizon Ltd. filed a 6-K (equivalent of a US 8-K) to disclose a letter agreement extending the exclusivity and negotiation period under a non-binding MOU to acquire a 51% stake in Arrow Aviation Ltd. No price per share, premium, or deal value was stated. The board has not yet made a definitive recommendation; no advisors named. The extension suggests ongoing due diligence or negotiation. Mechanically, the deal is structured as a partial acquisition via MOU, now extended to June 30, 2026. The exclusivity extension reduces near-term deal-uncertainty but does not guarantee a definitive agreement. Watch for a definitive agreement or termination notice by month end.

SMXWW.brief: SMX (Security Matters) Public Ltd Co filed a Form 6-K announcing a reverse stock split, effective June 1, 2026, with a split ratio of 2.285:1, reducing outstanding shares from ~1.5 million to ~650,000. No shareholder approval was needed as authority was granted in 2025. The par value adjusts accordingly; fractional shares will be sold and proceeds distributed. The move aims to meet Nasdaq listing requirements. No advisor or board recommendation is mentioned. The filing is a routine corporate action and does not constitute a special situation. What to watch: potential impact on trading liquidity and compliance.

ASPCR.brief: ASPAC III Acquisition Corp. (a SPAC) disclosed on May 20, 2026 that it received a Nasdaq deficiency letter for failing the minimum $2.5M stockholders' equity requirement under Listing Rule 5550(b)(1) as of its March 31, 2026 10-Q. The company has 45 days to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 additional days for cure. No board recommendation or advisor named. Risk-arb angle: SPACs with low equity risk liquidation or forced de-SPAC; watch compliance plan acceptance and potential capital infusion or merger timeline.

ABXL.brief: Abacus Global Management filed an 8-K announcing the closing of its $52.9 million acquisition of a minority indirect position in Manning Napier. The deal was previously announced March 12, 2026. Abacus joins other institutional investors. A Strategic Alliance Agreement was also entered for collaboration on lead generation, product development, and joint client solutions, leveraging Abacus's longevity data. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. No specific price per share, premium, board recommendation, or advisor names were disclosed. Watch for operational integration and potential further strategic moves as the partnership unfolds.

APLE.brief: Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting annual meeting voting results and extending its share repurchase program to July 2027 with a $242.5 million authorization. Repurchases may be made in open market, through 10b5-1 plans, or in private transactions, depending on market conditions. No advisor or board recommendation details are provided beyond the board's approval. The filing is not a routine current report, as the program extension is a capital return event. Focus on actual repurchase execution against the authorization, noting that conditions, including market conditions and other factors, may affect timing and volume.

CCZ.brief: Comcast Corp filed an 8-K announcing plans to separate its media and technology businesses into two independent public companies: NBCUniversal (premier global media and entertainment with theme parks, film, TV, streaming) and Comcast (broadband/connectivity technology). The transaction is structured as a tax-free spin-off to shareholders. No specific price, premium, or timeline is stated; no advisor or board recommendation is detailed. Watch for shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and IRS ruling on tax-free treatment; risk-arb will focus on relative valuation splits and potential activist interest post-separation.

MIRA.brief: MIRA Pharmaceuticals, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to its exclusive license agreement with MIRALOGX LLC for Ketamir-2, expanding the licensed territory from the US, Canada, and Mexico to worldwide where patent rights exist, and broadening the patent portfolio. No material modification to core economic terms, including royalties, was disclosed. The amendment supports global development toward Phase 2a. This is a strategic commercial expansion, not a special situation like an acquisition or restructuring, and does not involve new capital raising, shareholder payout, or board changes.

MYRG.brief: MYR Group Inc. filed an 8-K on May 27, 2026, announcing its acquisition of all shares of Valley Holdings I, Inc. (Valley), a Washington-based electrical contractor, for approximately $328 million, subject to post-closing adjustments. The consideration is cash funded from cash on hand and revolving credit facilities. There are additional contingent payments for key executives based on performance targets. Board recommendation, advisor, and premium were not disclosed. The deal requires regulatory approval and other customary conditions. Watch for regulatory timeline and any counterbids; risk-arb focuses on financing and closing certainty.

NHICW.brief: NewHold Investment Corp. III (SPAC) filed an 8-K on May 27, 2026, regarding a Business Combination Agreement with NewCleo Ltd. and its subsidiaries. The agreement involves two mergers: Merger Sub 1 merging into SPAC, then surviving company merging into Merger Sub 2, with SPAC becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Newcleo. Terms (price, premium, implied value) and board recommendation are not detailed in the excerpt. The structure uses a dual-merger chain to re-domesticate. No advisor or regulatory clock mentioned. Watch for shareholder vote on de-SPAC and redemption risk.

PFLA.brief: PennantPark Floating Rate Capital Ltd. filed an 8-K reporting entry into an underwriting agreement for a public offering of $100 million aggregate principal amount of 7.375% Notes due 2031, with an option for underwriters to purchase an additional $15 million within 30 days. The offering is made under an existing shelf registration statement and will close on June 1, 2026. Proceeds will repay revolving credit facility debt and for general corporate purposes. The notes will list on NYSE under symbol PFLA. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation.

PWR.brief: Quanta Services, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 Annual Meeting results and announcing a new stock repurchase program authorized by the Board as of May 21, 2026. The filing discloses director elections and advisory votes but does not specify the size, terms, or duration of the buyback authorization. This capital return mechanism signals a commitment to return value to shareholders, though lacking detail. Watch for a subsequent 8-K with program parameters to assess scale and execution pace.

SINT.brief: Sintx Technologies filed an 8-K disclosing a letter agreement with MedTech Ceramics LP to restructure existing equity-linked instruments. The company will issue 255,267 released shares and a pre-funded warrant for 251,987 shares, both for no additional consideration, and will cancel an existing warrant for 760,881 shares in exchange for a new warrant to purchase 1,268,135 shares at $2.14 per share. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The pre-funded warrant has no expiration, is subject to a 9.99% blocker, and the new warrant expires in five years with full-ratchet anti-dilution. This is a capital structure management transaction, not a classic special situation. Watch for stockholder dilution and Nasdaq compliance.

SOUNW.brief: SoundHound AI, Inc. filed an amended S-4 registration statement on July 8, 2026, relating to its pending acquisition of LivePerson, Inc. The merger agreement, as amended and restated on July 2, 2026, provides that Merger Sub I will merge with and into LivePerson. Terms of consideration and per-share price are not detailed in this filing. LivePerson's board recommends the deal. SoundHound's advisor is Latham & Watkins; LivePerson's advisor is Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson. The transaction is subject to SEC effectiveness and stockholder approval. Watch for regulatory clearance timing and any competing bids; arbitrageurs will focus on deal spread and closing conditions.

AAPG.brief: Ascentage Pharma Group International filed a Form 6-K furnishing a voluntary announcement regarding the trustee's on-market purchase of 100,000 existing shares at an average price of HK$39.77 per share (total consideration HK$3,977,000) for the company's 2022 RSU scheme. This is a routine share purchase to satisfy RSU vesting obligations, not a tender offer, capital return, or other special situation. The trustee holds 2,265,000 shares and will not exercise voting rights. No new awards were granted. This filing is an ordinary disclosure by a foreign private issuer; no special-situation event is present.

ATS.brief: ATS Corp (ATS) filed a Form 6-K press release reporting Q4 FY2026 results. The CEO stated the company took decisive steps to restructure and reposition transportation-related businesses, consolidating operations, right-sizing facility footprint, and repositioning engineering/automation capabilities. No specific terms such as stake, price, premium, or advisors were provided. The restructuring is operational, aimed at improving cost structure, margin expansion, and free cash flow. As a Canadian filer using 6-K, this maps to a US voluntary restructuring disclosure. Watch for progress on reorganization initiatives and financial flexibility in upcoming quarters.

CCGWW.brief: Cheche Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing that founder and CEO Lei Zhang intends to purchase company shares using personal funds in open-market or private transactions, with no fixed price, number, or timing. There is no board recommendation; purchases will comply with Rule 10b5-1 and insider trading policies. The statement is non-binding and discretionary, driven by the CEO's confidence after reaching 2025 profitability. This is a unilateral insider intention, not a formal capital return program. Watch for eventual Form 4 filings and schedule 13D amendments to gauge actual stake accumulation.

MIMI.brief: Mint Incorporation Ltd filed a 6-K furnishing a press release announcing a non-binding MOU with Ascendze Pte. Ltd. to acquire a controlling or majority equity stake. No price, premium, or valuation terms are disclosed. The target, Ascendze, is a Singapore semiconductor/robotics firm serving Fabrinet. The board (CEO Damian Chan) supports the deal. Definitive agreements are targeted within 90 days, subject to due diligence and regulatory clearances. The MOU itself is non-binding. The 6-K maps to a US current report. Watch for binding terms, valuation, and competition/regulatory hurdles in Singapore's tech sector.

SQNS.brief: Sequans Communications filed a Form 6-K announcing completion of full redemption of all remaining convertible debt issued July 2025, funded by sale of a portion of its Bitcoin holdings. The company now holds ~658 Bitcoin, all unrestricted. No price per share, premium, or implied value stated. Board/CEO recommended as pure-play focus on IoT semiconductors. Mechanical: debt fully redeemed via Bitcoin monetization, balance sheet simplified, no external financing. Structural notes: debt-free, treasury strategy ended, remaining Bitcoin monetization planned. What to watch: execution on 5G roadmap and cash burn trajectory; risk-arb angle minimal as this is a capital structure cleanup, not a transaction with spread.

APOG.brief: Apogee Enterprises, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of all outstanding equity interests of Keller Companies, Inc. and its subsidiaries, including Kalwall Corporation and Structures Unlimited, Inc., for $105 million in cash at closing plus up to $10 million in contingent consideration based on future performance. The acquisition was funded with available cash and borrowings under its revolving credit facility. The board recommended the transaction; no advisor is named. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, with customary post-closing adjustments. Watch for potential earn-out achievement and integration risk as Apogee expands its architectural products portfolio.

AXTA.brief: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. filed a definitive proxy statement for a special meeting on August 5, 2026, to approve its all-share merger of equals with Akzo Nobel N.V. Each Axalta share will be exchanged for 0.6539 AkzoNobel ordinary shares, plus a special pre-closing cash dividend of up to €2.5 billion. Based on recent prices, implied value is ~$34.36 per share. Axalta shareholders will hold ~45% of the combined entity. The board recommends voting for the deal. Post-merger, shares will trade on the NYSE and Euronext Amsterdam, with Amsterdam delisting planned ~12 months later. Key watch items: shareholder approval, regulatory clearance, and FX fluctuations affecting deal value.

BESS-WT.brief: Bimergen Energy Corp via subsidiary Emergen Energy LLC contributed 100% equity in three BESS project companies to JV Company FPU-BEC Development Topco (Cerberus-affiliate) on May 21, 2026. Consideration: 75 Class B Units (7.5% of JV equity) plus $1,176,159 reimbursement payment. Two projects closed at signing; third closes within 15 days or Emergen makes capital contribution. The filing reports a completed asset contribution forming a joint venture, not a standalone acquisition or divestiture. Watch for project development milestones and potential additional capital calls under the JDA.

DUOT.brief: Duos Technologies disclosed via Form 8-K that substantially all assets of New APR Energy, LLC, in which it holds a 5% non-voting ownership interest, were sold to a third party. Duos received net proceeds of approximately $50.4 million from the sale, with an additional ~$9.9 million held in escrow for indemnity obligations, distributable after 12 months. The filing does not name the buyer, offer specific per-share or premium details, or mention a board recommendation or advisor. Structurally, this is a minority stake sale driven by an underlying asset divestiture. The escrow release timeline and potential indemnity claims warrant monitoring.

LOCO.brief: El Pollo Loco Holdings filed an 8-K announcing a $40M share repurchase program approved by its Board of Directors. Shares may be bought on open market, block trades, or privately, with management discretion on timing and amount. No specific price, premium, or date set; no advisors named. Mechanics allow Rule 10b5-1 plans, but program is non-binding and may be suspended. This is a discretionary buyback, not a tender offer. Watch for actual repurchase execution and impact on free cash flow.
