HNNA.brief: The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Hennessy Advisors Inc.'s 4.875% Notes due 2026 from Nasdaq under SEC Rule 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(1). The delisting is effective June 29, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing involves the removal of the specified notes from exchange listing; no tender offer, merger, or shareholder vote is involved. The delisting follows the maturity or redemption of the notes, eliminating exchange-trading. What to watch: any residual claims or conversion rights, though the filing suggests the notes are fully settled.

H.brief: Hyatt Hotels Corp filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.0 billion share repurchase program for its Class A and Class B common stock. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, Rule 10b5-1 plans, or accelerated share repurchase transactions at the company's discretion, subject to market conditions and applicable law. The authorization does not obligate Hyatt to repurchase any specific amount and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Investors should watch the pace of buyback execution and potential impact on earnings per share.

LVLU.brief: Lulu's Fashion Lounge Holdings disclosed on May 21, 2026, that it received a Nasdaq Staff deficiency letter for failing to meet the $2.5 million stockholders' equity minimum required by Listing Rule 5550(b)(1). As of March 29, 2026, the company reported stockholders' equity of approximately $(525) thousand. The company does not meet alternative compliance standards. It has until July 6, 2026, to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days to cure. The delisting notice has no immediate effect on trading under symbol LVLU. The company is evaluating options to regain compliance.

NTAP.brief: NetApp filed an 8-K reporting fiscal Q4 2026 results and announcing a $1.0B share repurchase authorization. The new buyback has no expiration date; repurchases may be executed via open-market (Rule 10b-18), 10b5-1 plans, privately-negotiated transactions, or accelerated share repurchases. No specific price per share, premium, or close date is stated. The board authorized the repurchase; no financial advisor is named. The program offers flexibility but no commitment. Watch for the pace of execution under the renewed buyback authorization; the lack of set terms leaves the rate of capital return uncertain.

PD.brief: PagerDuty, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a new $100 million share repurchase program authorized by its Board, replacing earlier programs. The program allows repurchases via open market, private transactions, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, with no obligation to buy a specified number; it will be funded from existing cash and run through May 26, 2028, unless extended or terminated. PagerDuty is the issuer. Watch for execution pace and any market reaction; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a discretionary buyback, not a fixed-price tender.

PEB-PG.brief: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust filed an 8-K reporting the sale of the 115-room Chamberlain West Hollywood Hotel in Los Angeles, CA, for $43.5 million to a third party, closing on May 27, 2026. The price reflects gross proceeds from a single property sale; no per-share price, premium, or advisor is stated. Proceeds will be used for debt reduction, preferred equity paydown, opportunistic share repurchases, and other capital allocation priorities. The sale is a straightforward asset divestiture with no special terms or regulatory clock noted. Watch for further hotel dispositions or capital return updates as part of Pebblebrook's portfolio optimization.

RR.brief: Richtech Robotics Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its purchase of a 79,325 sq ft building in Las Vegas for $21.18M in cash via its subsidiary Richtech Rainbow Holdings. The property will serve as a US facility for warehousing, assembly, light manufacturing, and R&D. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This is a routine real estate acquisition for operational purposes, not a transformative special situation. Watch for integration updates, but there is no risk-arb angle.

TFSL.brief: TFS Financial Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $0.2825/share cash dividend payable June 24, 2026 to holders of record June 10, 2026. The MHC, owning 81% of shares, has waived its dividend right for this and prior quarters through July 8, 2026, per member and Fed approval. The board also reduced its size from 12 to 11 after director Meredith Weil retired. This is a pure capital return event; structural overhang from MHC control remains. Watch for continued dividend waivers as a quasi-buyback signal.

TSCO.brief: Tractor Supply Company (TSCO) acquired VIP Petcare (operating as VIP Petcare and PetVet) from PetIQ, a Bansk Group company, as announced in an 8-K filed May 28, 2026. VIP Petcare is the largest U.S. mobile veterinary care provider, operating in ~2,700 retail locations, including 1,700 Tractor Supply stores, serving over 1 million pets annually. Terms—price, premium, and consideration—were not disclosed. The acquisition strengthens Tractor Supply's pet health platform by integrating veterinary services, pharmacy, and retail. No board recommendation or advisors named. The deal is expected to close pending regulatory approvals; watch for integration updates and any antitrust review.

TMGI.brief: Transglobal Management Group, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of all outstanding shares of Continuum Software Technologies, Inc. (CSTI) under a Share Exchange Agreement dated March 20, 2026. As consideration, Transglobal issued 50,645,000 shares of its common stock to CSTI shareholders; no cash price per share or implied value is stated. The board recommended the transaction; no financial advisor is named. The stock was issued in reliance on Section 4(2) of the Securities Act as an unregistered sale to accredited investors. The acquisition closed immediately upon signing, with no regulatory clock or break fee disclosed. Watch for post-close integration and potential dilution from the large share issuance.

EAF.brief: GrafTech entered into an equity distribution agreement (May 29, 2026) to sell up to $50M of common stock via an at-the-market (ATM) offering through Evercore as agent. Stock price was $10.00/share on May 28. The company pays a 3.0% commission; settlement next trading day via DTC. This is a shelf takedown under Rule 415 — proceeds typically used for general corporate purposes or capital returns. No board recommendation or advisor mentioned. The ATM structure allows gradual issuance, reducing market overhang. Watch dilution pace and use of proceeds for buybacks or debt reduction.

BWMX.company: BETTERWARE DE MEXICO, S.A.P.I. DE C.V
BWMX.brief: Betterware de Mexico (BeFra) filed a 6-K to announce the completion of its acquisition of 100% of Tupperware's operating assets in Latin America. The total consideration is US$250 million on a debt-free, excess-cash-free basis, comprising US$215 million in cash (debt-funded) and US$35 million in newly issued BeFra shares, with the shares subject to a nine-month lock-up. The transaction closed after receiving Mexican antitrust clearance and shareholder approval. Each brand will operate independently under BeFra's platform. Watch for integration execution and synergies across brands.

OPTH.brief: Optimi Health Corp. filed a Form 6-K acknowledging updated TGA recommendations in Australia that expand psychedelic-assisted therapy access for psilocybin and MDMA. The changes broaden therapist eligibility, allow treatment in medically supervised non-hospital settings, and reinforce Australia's commercial leadership. No transaction, stake, price, premium, or board action is stated. Optimi is a GMP-compliant manufacturer positioned to support patient volume increases. This is a regulatory update, not a special situation; the filing is an ordinary foreign private issuer report on rule changes. Watch for patient volume growth and potential revenue impact, but no deal mechanics or arb angle.

SHIP.brief: Seanergy Maritime Holdings Corp. filed a Form 6-K reporting the pricing of a EUR 100 million unsecured corporate bond offering to investors in Greece. The bonds carry a 4.90% coupon, mature in July 2031, and were issued at par. Settlement is set for July 10, 2026, with trading on Euronext Athens commencing July 13, 2026. Proceeds will fund newbuilding or second-hand vessel acquisitions, general corporate and working capital purposes. Estimated offering expenses are EUR 4.4 million. This is a routine capital markets transaction, not a special situation. There are no deal terms applicable as this is a bond offering, not an M&A event. Watch for the use of proceeds and impact on fleet growth.

AXINR.brief: SPAC Axiom Intelligence Acquisition Corp 1 filed an 8-K on May 25, 2026, announcing entry into a Business Combination Agreement with Swiss quantum computing company Terra Quantum AG. The de-SPAC transaction involves formation of a Swiss PubCo and a Cayman merger sub, with Terra Quantum shareholders contributing shares to a Swiss HoldCo pre-closing. Transaction terms (price per share, implied value, premium) are not disclosed in the excerpt. The special committee and boards of both SPAC and Terra Quantum approved the deal. No break fee or timeline is provided. Watch for shareholder vote, redemptions, and regulatory clearances in a risk-arb context.

EDBLW.brief: Edible Garden AG Inc disclosed on May 27, 2026, that it received a Nasdaq Staff letter for failing the minimum bid price rule ($1/share) for 30 consecutive business days. Due to prior reverse stock splits (cumulative ratio >250:1 over two years), the company is ineligible for any compliance period. Trading will be suspended from Nasdaq at open on June 5, 2026, unless the company timely appeals by June 3, 2026. The company intends to request a hearing before a Nasdaq Hearings Panel, which would automatically stay suspension pending further action. No board recommendation or advisor named. Key risk: no assurance the Panel will grant additional time or that the company can meet continued listing criteria. Watch for hearing outcome and potential OTC trading.

IDT.brief: IDT Corporation filed a Form 8-K to announce a quarterly cash dividend of $0.07 per share declared by its Board of Directors. The dividend is payable on June 18, 2026, to stockholders of record as of June 9, 2026. The filing is a routine dividend announcement with no special-situation event such as a merger, tender offer, restructuring, or management change. The registrant is acting solely as the issuer of the dividend, and there are no deal terms, advisors, or structural mechanics applicable. This is a standard capital allocation action and does not qualify as a special situation.

NNE.brief: Nano Nuclear Energy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 100% of Secured Transportation Services LLC via a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement dated May 22, 2026. Total consideration is up to $13.0M, comprising approximately $6.0M cash (subject to a $0.5M adjustment) plus $1.0M in restricted common stock at closing and $6.0M in stock paid over five annual installments (capped at 10,364,476 shares). The board recommended the deal; no advisors named. The acquisition closed immediately on signing. What to watch: post-closing working capital adjustment mechanics and potential dilution from earn-out shares.

NEOVW.brief: NeoVolta Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an underwritten public offering of 12,195,122 shares of common stock at $2.05 per share, raising net proceeds of approximately $23.5 million, with a 30-day overallotment option for up to 1,829,268 additional shares. The offering was conducted under an effective shelf registration statement (Form S-3) and is a capital-raise event, not a transformative special situation. Proceeds are intended for joint venture obligations, working capital, and general corporate purposes. The underwriter is Lake Street Capital Markets, LLC, receiving a 6.0% discount. A 60-day lock-up restricts further equity sales. Watch for potential dilution impact and use of proceeds on operations.

ORRF.brief: Orrstown Financial Services Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing two events: (a) a full redemption of its $31M 4.5% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2030 on June 30, 2026, at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. The notes were assumed from its July 2024 merger with Codorus Valley Bancorp. (b) A vendor cybersecurity incident exposing customer information, but the company's systems were not breached and no material impact is expected. The redemption is a routine debt management action; the cybersecurity disclosure is an operational update. Neither constitutes a classic special-situation event, and no strategic shift is announced.

OHACU.brief: Oceanhawk Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO and over-allotment option on May 22, 2026, selling 18.4M units at $10.00/unit for $184M gross. Simultaneously, it sold 530K private placement units to sponsor and underwriter for $5.3M. Net proceeds of $184.92M were placed in a trust account. The non-US Cayman Islands SPAC follows blank-check company rules. The filing documents the IPO closing, with standard SPAC mechanics and trust funding. What to watch is the timeline for a business combination target announcement ahead of the 2-year deadline.

BTU.brief: Peabody Energy Corp filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of $225 million aggregate principal amount of 0.50% convertible senior notes due 2031, offered privately to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A. The notes are senior unsecured obligations, settle June 2, 2026, with an underwriter option for an additional $25 million. Interest is payable semi-annually; conversion rights begin December 1, 2030, with settlement in cash, stock, or a combination. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. No special-situation elements are present.

RWAX.brief: TAP Real Estate Technologies filed an 8-K regarding an Option to Purchase Agreement with Wasatch Springs Management Holdings for the Zermatt Resort in Midway, Utah. The initial 60-day option was extended by 90 days to May 22, 2026. No price per share, premium, or implied value is disclosed; the filing is silent on consideration and board recommendation. The option is non-binding pending financing and operational due diligence. Watch for definitive purchase agreement terms, financing commitment, and regulatory approvals.

JFU.brief: 9F Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of an entrustment transaction with SCLOUDPAY (HONGKONG) INTERNATIONAL LIMITED. 9F purchased loan receivables for HKD 101 million on behalf of the Principal and then transferred them. The Principal will pay in installments by November 30, 2026, with 8% annual funding expenses, secured by pledge and custody arrangements. The transaction is not a special situation under typical categories, as it is a routine asset purchase and entrustment arrangement. Observe installment payments and safeguard provisions for risk assessment.

CCJ.brief: Cameco filed a Form 6-K announcing the closed acquisition of TEPCO Resources Inc.'s 5% participating interest in the Cigar Lake Joint Venture. Cameco and Orano Canada Inc. together purchased the stake; Cameco's ownership increased by 2.871 percentage points to 57.418%, with Orano's rising by 2.129pp to 42.582%. The transaction closed on July 2, 2026, with terms detailed in Cameco's June 1, 2026 release. No purchase price, premium, or advisor was disclosed in this filing. The deal increases Cameco's control of the high-grade uranium mine. Watch for integration details and potential output updates.

DXST.brief: Decent Holding Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting a share subscription agreement with Chairman Dingxin Sun, who purchased 400,000 Class B ordinary shares at $2.00 per share for total consideration of $800,000. The transaction closed on June 1, 2026. Following the close, Sun beneficially owns approximately 90.5% of total voting power, indicating a significant insider equity injection. The filing does not disclose a board recommendation, advisor, or premium. Structurally, this is a direct share issuance increasing insider control, not a public tender. Watch for potential governance or liquidity impacts given the concentrated ownership and small float, as insider-led capital raises may precede other corporate actions.

BBDC.brief: Barings BDC, Inc. filed an 8-K to report entry into a new Credit Support Agreement (New CSA) with its adviser Barings LLC upon termination of the prior CSA from 2022. The New CSA provides credit support for two legacy portfolio investments valued at $10.99 million, with the adviser obligated to cover losses exceeding proceeds through April 1, 2032. Settlement occurs via waiver of incentive fees and base management fees over four quarters after the settlement date. This is a contractual arrangement between fund and adviser, not a corporate event. No special-situation category applies.

BSBK.brief: Bogota Financial Corp. filed an 8-K disclosing its entry into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with GSL Savings Bank, whereby GSL will merge into Bogota Savings Bank. Consideration involves Bogota issuing additional common shares to its mutual holding company parent equal to GSL's fair value as determined by an independent appraiser; no per-share price or premium is stated. The boards of both parties unanimously approved the deal. The merger is expected to close in the second half of 2026, subject to regulatory and other customary conditions. Termination provisions include a $750k fee payable by GSL in certain circumstances. Watch for regulatory approval timeline and appraisal outcome.

CTNT.company: CHEETAH NET SUPPLY CHAIN SERVICE INC.
CTNT.brief: Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of 100% of Super International Trading Limited, a Hong Kong company trading large-scale industrial equipment, for undisclosed terms. The acquisition closed on May 27, 2026, pursuant to a Share Transfer Agreement with Leyan Yang dated April 16, 2026. Super became a wholly owned subsidiary. No board recommendation, advisor, or financial details were disclosed. What to watch: future integration disclosures and any earn-out or contingent consideration; risk-arb is moot as deal is closed.

CBU.brief: Community Financial System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of ClearPoint Federal Bank Trust, a federally chartered savings association and leader in trust administration for the death care industry. The deal, originally announced January 14, 2026, was effected via merger with Community Bank, N.A., a wholly-owned subsidiary. ClearPoint has over $1.5 billion in assets under management and a historical three-year revenue CAGR of 9.7%. No financial terms, price per share, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The acquired business will operate as ClearPoint Trust, a division of Community Bank. Watch for integration updates and revenue contribution from Nottingham Financial Group.

CWBHF.brief: Charlotte's Web Holdings filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a subscription agreement with BAT DE Investments Inc., a British American Tobacco subsidiary, under which BAT purchased 14,662,765 common shares at C$0.94 per share for total proceeds of ~C$13.9M (US$10M). The transaction is structured as a direct equity investment, not a tender or a going-private transaction. BAT holds a convertible debenture originally issued in 2022, with a conversion price of C$2.00 per share subject to a 19.9% ownership cap. The deal strengthens BAT's existing stake. What to watch: potential further conversion of the debenture or additional equity investments that could shift control.

EMYB.brief: Embassy Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing an expansion of its stock repurchase program by an additional $5 million, effective June 1, 2026. The original program, announced October 27, 2025, authorized up to $5 million; through Q1 2026, the company repurchased 258,301 shares for $4.856 million, leaving $144,000 unused. The expanded program allows open market or privately negotiated repurchases. Management expressed confidence in the company’s balance sheet and capital allocation. No premium, price per share, closing date, or advisor was disclosed. Watch for future repurchase pace disclosures in quarterly filings.

EHC.brief: Encompass Health issued $500M of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 via a private Rule 144A/Reg S offering, netting ~$491.2M after discounts and expenses. Proceeds will redeem $400M of its 4.500% notes due 2028 at par and repay $100M under its revolver, representing a liability management / capital-return event through refinancing to lower near-term debt. The indenture with Computershare includes standard make-whole redemption provisions. No change in equity structure; watch ability to refinance remaining $400M of 2028 notes if callable. This is a debt capital return, not an equity distribution.

FCPT.brief: Four Corners Property Trust (FCPT) filed an 8-K disclosing its entry into a Purchase and Sale Agreement to acquire up to 102 veterinary properties from Shore Capital Real Estate Partners for up to $268 million. The properties are net-leased to Mission Pet Health with a ~10-year weighted average remaining term. An initial $4 million deposit was made. The transaction is subject to due diligence and customary closing conditions. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The deal is structured as a portfolio acquisition under master leases. Watch for completion of due diligence and satisfaction of closing conditions; risk-arb uncertainty revolves around the contingent nature of the acquisition.

HCACR.brief: Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp (HCAC) filed an 8-K on June 3, 2026, reporting its entry into a Business Combination Agreement dated May 31, 2026, with REEcycle Holdings, Inc., a rare-earth elements recycler. HCAC, a blank-check SPAC, will domesticate as a Delaware corporation and merge via its wholly owned subsidiary, with REEcycle surviving. The boards of both companies approved the transaction. No specific price per share, premium, or implied value are disclosed in this excerpt. The filing includes the Business Combination Agreement (Exhibit 2.1) and related agreements. Watch for shareholder redemptions and completion timeline; risk-arb spread will depend on trust valuation and deal vote.

KRMN.brief: Karman Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an underwritten secondary offering of 14,000,000 common shares (plus a 30-day underwriter option for up to 2,100,000 additional shares) by selling stockholders at $61.00 per share, which closed on June 1, 2026. The company is the issuer but receives no proceeds; it agreed to a 90-day lock-up on share issuance. The filing involves customary underwriting provisions and an indemnification clause. This is a routine secondary offering, not a special situation, as it does not involve a merger, acquisition, activist campaign, restructuring, or other transformative event. It is a standard capital markets transaction.

KPEA.brief: Kun Peng International Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing a 1-for-10 reverse stock split effective June 2, 2026, approved by the board and 85.4% of shareholders via written consent in January 2026. Outstanding shares decrease from 400M to ~40M, authorized shares cut from 1B to 100M, and par value increases from $0.0001 to $0.001. The stock will trade under symbol KPEAD for 20 days then revert to KPEA. This is a capital-structure adjustment, not a special situation event, so classification is Other.

NUTR.brief: Nasdaq notified NusaTrip Inc on May 27, 2026 of its non-compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) due to failure to timely file its Form 10-K for FY2025 and Form 10-Q for Q1 2026. The company has 60 days (until July 27, 2026) to submit a compliance plan. If accepted, Nasdaq may grant an extension to October 12, 2026. Non-compliance could lead to delisting of NUTR. Management expects to file within the 60-day period and has issued a press release. Watch for the company's timely filing and Nasdaq's plan acceptance; delisting risk if deadlines are missed.

ORLY.brief: On June 1, 2026, O'Reilly Automotive's board approved a $2.0 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization, raising the aggregate to $31.75 billion, effective for three years. Repurchases will be made in open market transactions at prevailing prices based on market conditions and corporate factors, with no fixed timetable or obligation to buy any shares. The program may be modified, suspended, or terminated at any time. No advisor, premium, or price terms are disclosed. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 (Other Events) announcing expanded buyback capacity. Watch for actual repurchase cadence; the authorization signals management's view on capital allocation and undervaluation but carries no commitment.

SRG-PA.brief: Seritage Growth Properties subsidiary entered an option purchase and sale agreement with Arena Development Intermediate for a Dallas property. Purchase price is $50,760,000 with adjustments; closing is the earlier of 90 days after entitlements period expiration or January 31, 2028. Option payments start at $169,200 on effective date, then monthly amounts from July 2026 to January 2028, all non-refundable and incremental to price. The PSA is cross-conditioned with a related PSA for adjacent land by unaffiliated owners. There are no assurances the option will be exercised, making this a contingent asset sale with no definitive terms.

STEP.brief: StepStone Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the third exchange completed May 29, 2026, acquiring ~5% equity interests in each of three Asset Class Entities (SRE, SRA, SPD) from third-party sellers. The aggregate consideration was approximately $10M cash (pre-adjustment ~$11M), 972,685 shares of Class A common stock, and 2,438,273 Class D units. Post-exchange, StepStone holdings rose to 65% in each entity. Consideration based on exchange ratios tied to estimated adjusted net income and an adjusted trading multiple. Shares and units issued unregistered under Section 4(a)(2). Watch for continued step acquisitions and potential full consolidation or future registration events.

TMQ.brief: Trilogy Metals Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to a binding letter of intent with South32 Limited, Ambler Metals LLC, and the U.S. Department of War (DOW). The amendment extends the closing deadline for a previously announced US$35.6 million strategic equity investment by the DOW from May 31, 2026, to July 31, 2026, to finalize definitive documentation. Other terms remain unchanged. The extension is procedural, not a fundamental change in deal structure, so this is not a new special situation. Watch for completion by the new deadline or further delays.

UFPI.brief: UFP Industries Inc. filed an 8-K on June 1, 2026, announcing that its Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $300 million of its outstanding common stock, expiring April 30, 2027. The repurchases may be executed via open market, private negotiations, or Rule 10b5-1 plans. Timing and amount depend on market conditions and share price. The company is not obligated to repurchase shares. The prior authorization was replaced. Watch for future buyback execution pace; no premium or advisor was noted.

VVX.brief: V2X, Inc. disclosed through subsidiaries a refinancing of existing term loans via Amendment No. 6 to the First Lien Credit Agreement. The amendment creates New Term Loans of $868.5 million maturing December 6, 2030, replacing all outstanding prior term loans. Interest is SOFR + 2.00% or base rate + 1.00%, with a potential 0.25% step-down based on ratings. Voluntary prepayments are allowed without penalty except for certain repricing events. This is a debt restructuring/refinancing, not a special-situation transaction like a sale or acquisition. Terms are routine for credit agreements; no premium, equity stake, or board recommendation is involved.

VIASP.brief: Via Renewables, Inc. filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective July 1, 2026, suspending its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The filing covers the company’s 8.75% Series A Fixed-to-Floating Rate Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock, par value $0.01 per share. The certification states there are zero holders of record of this class as of the filing date. No board recommendation, advisor, or premium was disclosed. The deregistration is permitted under Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and related rules. What to watch: The company will no longer file periodic reports with the SEC, reducing public transparency and potentially limiting liquidity for remaining security holders. No risk-arb angle applies.

GOOGM.brief: Alphabet Inc. filed a prospectus supplement on Form 424B5 for an offering of 167.5M Series A Depositary Shares, each representing a 1/20th interest in a share of 6.25% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock at $50 per depositary share, raising ~$8.38B proceeds before expenses. The preferred stock carries a $1,000 liquidation preference per share and pays cumulative dividends at 6.25% annually, payable quarterly in cash or Class A common stock. Mandatory conversion occurs by May 2029 into a variable number of Class A common shares based on VWAP. The company intends to list the depositary shares on Nasdaq under GOOGM. Underwriters include an over-allotment option. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, capital returns, and potential buybacks. Watch for conversion mechanics and dilution, but no special-situation M&A or activist angle applies.

TTI.brief: The filing is a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement by TETRA Technologies, Inc. for a proposed public offering of $100,000,000 of its common stock, with an underwriter over-allotment option of up to $15,000,000. The price per share is to be determined based on the market, with the last-reported price of $10.36 on June 1, 2026. The offering is underwritten by J.P. Morgan as lead book-runner and Jefferies. Proceeds will go to the company. This is a routine capital-raising equity follow-on offering, not a special situation.

WAVE.brief: Eco Wave Power filed a Form 6-K (report of foreign private issuer) announcing the closing of a $4.0M registered direct offering with a single strategic institutional investor. The deal consisted of 400,000 ADSs at $10.00/ADS, a 10.7% premium to the prior close, plus warrants to purchase 300,000 ADSs at $12.00/ADS (32.9% premium) expiring June 2029. Maxim Group acted as sole placement agent. The shelf takedown was made under an effective F-3. Net proceeds will fund global project deployment and AI capabilities. This is a routine financing by a non-US issuer, not triggering a special-situations classification.

FSV.brief: FirstService Corp filed a Form 6-K announcing an amendment to its normal course issuer bid (NCIB) to increase the maximum number of common shares repurchasable from 1,600,000 (3.9% of public float) to 4,118,199 (10% of public float), effective June 4, 2026. The NCIB runs from August 26, 2025 to August 25, 2026, with daily purchase limits on TSX and NASDAQ. Shares repurchased will be cancelled. The amendment reflects management’s view that repurchases are an appropriate use of funds and mitigate dilution from stock options. No advisor or premium is specified. Watch for the pace of buybacks and impact on float/reducing share count.

GEBRF.brief: Greenbriar Sustainable Living Inc. filed Form 6-K reporting amendments to its CAD $1.0 million convertible debenture and warrants. The maturity and conversion period were extended to June 30, 2028, and the conversion price reduced to CAD $1.00 per share. Warrants expiry was similarly extended; exercise price remains CAD $1.30. No new money was raised, and no advisor or recommendation was disclosed. This is a routine debt restructuring under Canadian TSXV rules, not a transformative special situation. The filing is a foreign private issuer report corresponding to a US Form 8-K for material modification of security holder rights, but the event is incremental and administrative in nature.

NIPG.brief: NIP Group Inc., the registrant, filed a Form 6-K disclosing additional closing of the second tranche of its Bitcoin mining capacity acquisition. The initial closing on January 9, 2026 was settled with 167,917,734 Class A ordinary shares. On May 29, 2026, a second closing issued another 62,579,674 Class A ordinary shares to sellers/assignees, replacing previously contemplated convertible notes as consideration. The remaining closing is also expected to be settled in shares. No price per share, premium, or advisor is stated. This is an equity-funded asset purchase; risk-arb focuses on dilution mechanics and completion timing.

AVA.brief: Avista Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a non-binding MOU with a developer for a large load electric service interconnection. The customer seeks 125 MW starting in 2029, expanding to 500 MW by 2032. Next steps include an Engineering and Procurement Contract, regulatory approval from the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, and definitive agreements. No financial terms, board recommendation, or advisors are named. This is a preliminary infrastructure development agreement, not a special situation, with no M&A or corporate action. Watch for regulatory filings and definitive agreements.

BRKHU.brief: BurTech Acquisition Corp II filed Form 8-K reporting the consummation of its initial public offering (IPO) of 8,000,000 units at $10.00/unit, raising $80M gross proceeds, and a simultaneous private placement of 252,000 units to Sponsor and an institutional investor at $10.00/unit for $2.52M. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50/share. Net proceeds of $80.4M were deposited into trust. This is a standard blank-check company IPO filing. No board recommendation or deal terms are applicable. What to watch: the sponsor's ability to identify and complete an initial business combination within the required timeframe.

SCOR.brief: Comscore Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the sale of its Movies Business (box office measurement and Hollywood Software) to an affiliate of Advaya Capital, Flix Buyer Inc., for $70M cash via an Equity Purchase Agreement signed and closed on May 27, 2026. The transaction includes customary reps, warranties, and a five-year non-compete. Proceeds were partly used to repay all obligations under Blue Torch Finance's Credit Agreement. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for any post-closing working capital true-ups or transition service issues.

WLYB.brief: John Wiley & Sons, Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, John Wiley & Sons Ltd., entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement on June 1, 2026, to acquire all outstanding equity of CIG Emerald Midco LLC (doing business as Emerald Publishing) from CIG Emerald Midco LLC and Emerald Holding. The purchase price is GBP 337.5 million (~$452 million) in cash, funded from cash on hand. The acquisition of over 480 peer-reviewed journals and 8,000 books expands Wiley's research publishing portfolio. The filing includes customary representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions. No advisor or board recommendation is stated. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

PRA.brief: ProAssurance Corp filed Form 15 on July 6, 2026, voluntarily terminating its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, effective immediately. The company certifies it has only one holder of record of its common stock. This action suspends its duty to file reports under Sections 13(a) and 15(d). The termination is based on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and related rules. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal terms are specified. The move likely stems from a prior going-private transaction or ownership consolidation. What to watch: deregistration reduces ongoing disclosure obligations; holders of unregistered stock may face liquidity constraints.

URGN.brief: UroGen Pharma filed an 8-K announcing it entered into a settlement and license agreement with Teva resolving patent litigation over Jelmyto (mitomycin). Teva will receive a non-exclusive license to sell a generic version starting September 15, 2030, conditional on FDA approval. All ongoing litigation in the District of Delaware will be terminated. The agreement is subject to FTC/DOJ review. This is a routine patent settlement/licensing event, not a special situation. No deal terms or financial details are disclosed.

SPCE.brief: Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a notice of redemption for up to $30.5M of its 9.80% First Lien Notes due 2028. The redemption, set for June 10, 2026, will be settled by issuing common stock at par plus accrued interest. The exact shares depend on a five-day VWAP; a floor price limits redemption if VWAP falls below it. This follows a prior $10M redemption, retiring all mandatory principal payments through 2027. The move is part of broader liquidity management ahead of commercial operations in Q4 2026. Watch share count dilution and stock price floor mechanics.

ATNI.brief: ATN International, Inc. subsidiaries completed the initial closing of a sale of tower portfolios to Everest Infrastructure Partners for up to $297 million in cash. At closing, $153.4 million was paid for Assigned Sites and $114.3 million for Managed Sites, with deferred sites to close later. The transaction was governed by a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated February 11, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed in the filing. The deal is structured as a staged asset sale with management agreements for sites not yet conveyed. Watch for subsequent closings of deferred sites and potential regulatory approvals affecting the timeline.

HIG-PG.brief: The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a definitive agreement to sell its Hartford Funds business to Wellington Investment Advisors Holdings, LLP, parent of Wellington Management Company LLP. Consideration includes $300 million cash at close plus ongoing quarterly payments representing 95% of after-tax available cash from the combined business over an expected 7-year period, with net present value estimated at $1.9 billion (11% discount rate). The board supports the deal. Closing is expected Q1 2027, subject to regulatory and fund approvals. Hartford Funds will be reported as discontinued operations from Q2 2026. What to watch: regulatory clearance timeline and the performance-based earnout structure affecting ultimate proceeds.

REED.brief: Reed's, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing receipt of a NYSE American delisting notice on May 29, 2026, for failure to meet continued listing standards under Sections 1003(a)(ii) and (iii) due to insufficient stockholders' equity ($4M/$6M thresholds) with recurring losses. The company must submit a compliance plan by June 28, 2026; if accepted, it has until November 29, 2027, to regain compliance. Shares remain listed under "REED" with a ".BC" designation. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch: plan submission outcome, quarterly monitoring, and risk of delisting if compliance is not achieved.

RGNX.brief: REGENXBIO Inc. filed an Amendment No. 2 to its Schedule TO reporting final results of an exchange offer for non-executive employee stock options. The offer expired July 1, 2026; 184 holders tendered options covering ~1.94 million shares (67% of eligible options). Tendered options were cancelled July 2, 2026, and replaced with options to purchase 775,401 shares at an exercise price of $13.28 (the July 2 closing price). The replacement options were granted under the 2025 Equity Incentive Plan. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for employee retention effects and potential dilution impact from the new options.

SREA.brief: Sempra filed a preliminary prospectus supplement on Form 424B5 to offer floating rate notes due 2028. The notes are unsecured, unsubordinated obligations ranking equally with existing debt. Interest is based on Compounded SOFR plus a spread. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes. The offering is underwritten by BMO Capital Markets and Academy Securities. No redemption is permitted before maturity. The notes will not be listed on any exchange. This is a routine debt offering, not a special situation.

ZJYL.brief: Jin Medical International Ltd. filed a Form 6-K on June 29, 2026, reporting its entry into a VIE Control Acquisition and Share Issuance Agreement with its WFOE, Beijing Tongsheng Technology Co., Ltd. (Target), and Chang Gil Lee (Seller). The Company will issue Class A Ordinary Shares valued at US$105,329,974 as consideration, with the per-share price determined by the lowest 90-day VWAP prior to execution. The acquisition grants contractual control over the Target via VIE agreements, which include economic benefit rights, equity pledge, voting proxy, and exclusive option rights. No legal title to Target's equity is obtained. The transaction requires shareholder approval at an EGM and Class A/B meetings. No advisor or board recommendation explicitly stated. Watch for shareholder vote outcome; risk-arb focus on approval and VIE structure enforceability.

LGCL.brief: Lucas GC Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting entry into an At the Market Offering Agreement with Maxim Group LLC to sell up to $20 million of Class A ordinary shares at-the-market. The filing describes a sales agreement with a 3% placement fee and expense reimbursements, with no specific price, premium, or dates beyond the agreement date. The program is discretionary; there are no required terms like price per share or premium. The filing is routine and does not constitute a special-situation event but rather a capital market engagement.

MRNOW.brief: Murano Global Investments Plc filed a Form 6-K announcing a milestone in the restructuring of its $300M 11.000% Senior Secured Notes due 2031. The company terminated its hotel management agreement with Hyatt and entered a new arrangement with Ennismore to rebrand its Grand Island I hotel as Mondrian, converting 328 rooms into residential condominiums for sale. The restructuring aims to improve financial performance. No price/share, premium, or advisor named. Watch for completion of the full restructuring plan and its impact on noteholder recoveries.

NU.brief: Nu Holdings Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing a US$1.0 billion share repurchase program authorized by its board. The program allows repurchases of Class A ordinary shares in open market or privately negotiated transactions over 12 months ending June 3, 2027. Repurchases may use Rule 10b-18 and 10b5-1 plans, funded from cash balances. Shares will be retained in treasury or canceled. No specific price, premium, or commitment to acquire any number of shares is stated. Watch for execution pace and potential program size adjustments.

SOPH.brief: SOPHiA GENETICS SA filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to explore forming a joint venture for a precision oncology hub. No definitive terms, price, or timeline were disclosed; the MOU outlines a strategic collaboration to combine MSK's clinical data with SOPHiA's AI platform. The filing is a preliminary announcement with no binding deal, so it falls outside standard special-situation categories. Watch for subsequent definitive agreements or material developments.

ZYBT.brief: Zhengye Biotechnology Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency notice on May 29, 2026, because its Class A ordinary shares closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day compliance period through November 25, 2026, to regain compliance by having the bid price close at $1.00 or more for at least ten consecutive business days. If not cured, it may seek a second 180-day grace period and may effect a reverse stock split. No transaction, acquisition, or restructuring is involved; this is a routine listing standards notification.

BRT.brief: BRT Apartments Corp. filed an 8-K reporting an agreement to acquire The Waterford on Piedmont, a 153-unit multifamily property in Atlanta, GA, for ~$35 million (subject to customary adjustments). The registrant (BRT) is the acquirer. Terms: anticipated ~$22 million mortgage and ~$14 million funded from property refinancings. Board recommendation not stated; no advisor named. Mechanics: customary due diligence and closing conditions. Expected close: quarter ending September 30, 2026. The filing is an Item 8.01 disclosure of a material acquisition. What to watch / risk-arb angle: review due diligence outcomes and mortgage terms.

CEIN.brief: Camber Energy, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of an amalgamation on June 1, 2026 between its subsidiary Simson-Maxwell Ltd. and T T Power Group Inc. under Canadian law (CBCA). The amalgamated entity operates Simson's former business. As a result, Viking Energy (Camber's subsidiary) received 5,750,000 Class A Preference Shares with no voting rights, while T T's sole shareholder obtained 100,000 Class A Common Shares (100% voting interest). This restructuring follows a prior deconsolidation of Simson in April 2025. No price per share or premium is stated. A unanimous shareholders agreement appointed the T T shareholder as sole director. The filing is a structural reorganization rather than a classic acquisition or spin-off, with no public market terms.

DGAC-UN.brief: Disciplined Growth Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting the closing of its IPO of 15,000,000 units at $10.00/unit for gross proceeds of $150 million, and a simultaneous private placement of 345,000 private placement units at $10.00/unit to the sponsor, underwriter Maxim Group LLC, and at-risk capital investors for $3.45 million. The units consist of one Class A ordinary share and one right to receive one-fourth of a share upon an initial business combination. This is a standard SPAC formation filing; the company is a blank-check issuer. Watch for the exercise of the underwriters' 45-day over-allotment option and future business combination announcements.

IVHI.brief: Invech Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a settlement agreement with Arnold F. Sock to cancel a $6,400 unpaid legal balance in exchange for the acceleration of 900,000 previously committed shares of IVHI common stock (1.2M shares at $0.0053/share implied value, quarterly vesting 300K—300K earned as of Q1 2026, 900K accelerated per agreement). No board recommendation or advisor named; the stock-for-services settlement avoids cash outlay and resolves an undisputed obligation. The shares were already disclosed in the Q1 10-Q. Watch for dilution impact and any future share issuances under this arrangement.

JBIO.brief: Jade Biosciences, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 3, 2026 to disclose entry into an underwriting agreement for an underwritten public offering of 10,000,000 shares of common stock at $15.00 per share, with a $14.10 per share purchase price for underwriters. The filing is a routine capital raise via an existing shelf registration statement (Form S-3), not a special situation. The offering is expected to close June 5, 2026 and proceeds of ~$140.3 million will fund general corporate purposes. No activist campaign, acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or other control event is involved.

KAPA.brief: Kairos Pharma filed an 8-K to issue a press release summarizing first-half 2026 achievements and second-half milestones. The release announces a signed term sheet to acquire worldwide rights to CL-741, a Phase 1-ready c-MET inhibitor for NSCLC and gastric cancers, from Celyn Therapeutics (backed by OrbiMed and Torrey Pines). No specific price, stake, premium, or close date is provided. The board has not yet made a formal recommendation, and no financial advisor is named. The acquisition is still at the term sheet stage, so terms are non-binding. Watch for a definitive agreement and any shareholder vote or regulatory clearance.

SMID.brief: Smith-Midland Corp disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice on May 29, 2026 for failure to timely file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, violating Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The notice has no immediate effect on listing; the company is working to file the 10-Q promptly. If unable to file by July 28, 2026, it plans to submit a compliance plan to Nasdaq. The board recommended no action beyond the disclosure; no advisor named. The process involves a standard 180-day cure period with potential for additional time under a submitted plan. Risk-arb angle: no deal; watch for filing delays or potential delisting if compliance not regained, which could pressure equity.

VERU.brief: Veru Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a clinical supply agreement with Novo Nordisk for the Phase 2b PLATEAU study, evaluating enobosarm combined with Novo Nordisk's Wegovy in older adults with obesity. Veru sponsors the study; Novo Nordisk supplies Wegovy at no charge. No financial terms, stake, or premium disclosed. Novo Nordisk receives a right of first negotiation should Veru later develop enobosarm with a Novo GLP-1 product. This is a collaborative R&D arrangement, not a merger, acquisition, or capital event. Watch for trial data and potential future partnership or licensing deals.

HNVR.brief: Hanover Bancorp filed a Form S-4 registration statement to register the exchange of up to $35M aggregate principal amount of 7.25% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2036. The New Notes (registered) will be exchanged for any and all outstanding Old Notes (unregistered) issued in a private placement on March 12, 2026. The exchange offer expires at 11:59 p.m. NY time on a date to be set, unless extended. No board recommendation or advisor is named in the excerpt. No premium is implied as the exchange is for identical terms. The transaction is a standard exchange offer to satisfy registration rights. Rule 462(b) securities registration instructions are noted. The offer is for cashless exchange, so no collateral or overhang; no ownership split changes. The exchange offer remains subject to SEC effectiveness. What to watch: the expiration date when set and final SEC effectiveness.

XOSWW.brief: Xos, Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a firm-commitment offering of 1,090,910 common shares at $5.50 per share, representing a ~26% discount to the June 3 close of $7.46. The offering aims to raise ~$6.0M gross ($5.61M net after 6.5% placement agent fee). Roth Capital Partners is the sole placement agent on a reasonable best-efforts basis. The offering is conducted under a shelf registration (S-3), with an overhang limit per General Instruction I.B.6. Proceeds will be used for working capital and general corporate purposes. No special-situation event like a tender, going-private, or restructuring is present. Risk-arb focus: watch for Nasdaq compliance and shareholder dilution impact.

MYND.brief: Mynd.ai, Inc. filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a NYSE American notice for non-compliance with continued listing standards (stockholders' deficit of $(17.5M) and losses in 3 of 4 fiscal years). The company must submit a compliance plan by July 2, 2026, with a cure deadline of December 2, 2027. No price, premium, or deal terms are applicable; this is a listing-standard deficiency notice. There is no board recommendation or advisor named, and the stock remains listed during the cure period. Key watchpoint is whether the plan is accepted and compliance regained; otherwise, delisting proceedings commence.

TAK.brief: Takeda completed an issuance of new shares and disposal of treasury shares under its Long-Term Incentive Plan for group employees outside Japan. The transaction involved 16,877,109 ordinary shares at 5,050 yen per share, with a total value of approximately ¥85.2 billion. The number of shares decreased slightly from the original plan due to partial forfeiture of rights by some allottees. The filing is a routine employee compensation transaction with no change of control or strategic implications. This is not a special situation. The impact on financials is immaterial.

TRIB.brief: Trinity Biotech plc filed a Form 6-K announcing it delivered notice of termination of its Standby Equity Purchase Agreement (SEPA) with YA II PN, LTD., an affiliate of Yorkville Advisors Global. No specific financial terms (price/share, premium, break fee) were disclosed. The company stated it does not intend to make further use of this equity line of credit facility, reflecting a shift in financing strategy. The termination is effective immediately per the notice. The board did not issue a recommendation or name advisors for this action. This is a unilateral termination of a standby equity facility, not a merger or tender. Watch for any subsequent financing arrangements or capital structure changes.

CCU.brief: Compañía Cervecerías Unidas (CCU) filed a Form 6-K disclosing its acquisition of Nestlé's 49.9% stake in Aguas CCU-Nestlé for ~CLP 164,597 million, implying a 100% enterprise value of ~CLP 322,377 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The SPA was executed June 5, 2026, following unanimous board approval on May 6, 2026. No advisors or recommendation were mentioned. The transaction makes CCU the 100% owner of the water subsidiary; price is subject to customary adjustments. The deal closed same-day; watch for future financial impact disclosures and continuing commercial distribution agreement with Nestlé.

AASP.brief: Agassi Sports Entertainment Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the entry into Subscription Agreements with accredited investors for a private placement of 235,000 restricted common shares at $5.00 per share, raising $1,175,000. Concurrently, the Company entered into a Registration Rights Agreement obligating it to file a resale registration statement within 45 days and maintain effectiveness for up to three years. Failure to file triggers escalating liquidated damages of 5% of held shares per 30-day period, capped at an aggregate limit. This capital-raising event, while material, is not an acquisition, divestiture, tender offer, or other typical special situation; it represents an ordinary equity financing with registration rights. Watch for the registration statement filing deadline in early July 2026 and potential dilution from penalty shares.

FCN.brief: FTI Consulting filed an 8-K disclosing its annual shareholder meeting results (routine) and a board authorization to repurchase an additional $370 million of common stock under its existing Stock Repurchase Program. The program has cumulative authorizations of $2.6 billion, with 19,104,867 shares repurchased through June 2, 2026. No specific price, premium, or timeline is given; the authorization expands available capacity. The filing is a routine capital-return disclosure, not a full self-tender or other special situation. Watch for future repurchase pace and program exhaustion.

HYPD.brief: Hyperion DeFi, Inc. filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) reporting the termination of two agreements: a Temporary Use Agreement with Native Markets (effective June 18, 2026) and a HAUS Agreement with Felix Foundation (wind-down agreed June 5, 2026). Under the Native Markets agreement, the company received all fees owed and had 300,000 HYPE tokens unstaked and returned. The Felix agreement expects 500,000 HYPE tokens to be unstaked by June 22, 2026, with full availability by June 29, 2026. The company plans to reposition the ~800,000 HYPE tokens to more profitable strategies. No financial terms beyond asset values (~$10.4M and ~$18.3M) were disclosed. This is a business wind-down, not a special-situation event.

LTGRU.brief: Long Table Growth Corp., a blank-check company, filed an 8-K to report the consummation of its IPO of 17,250,000 units at $10.00/unit (including the full over-allotment) for gross proceeds of $172.5 million. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-half of one redeemable warrant. The filing attaches the underwriting agreement (with Santander US Capital Markets as representative), warrant agreement, letter agreement among insiders and sponsor, and investment management trust agreement. As a SPAC, the funds will be held in trust pending a future business combination. The company expects to identify a target within the allotted timeframe.

NMEX.brief: Northern Minerals & Exploration Ltd. filed an 8-K regarding its entry into a Memorandum of Understanding to acquire a 5.4165 net mineral acre leasehold interest in Garvin County, Oklahoma, from R.A. Miller Energy, Inc. The consideration is $21,666 total, comprising $10,833 cash (due by July 31, 2026) and 216,660 shares valued at $10,833. The leasehold carries a 77% net revenue interest. The company must also participate in a force pooling order for the Bosworth well. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The transaction is small, with no premium or regulatory clock indicated. The cash-and-stock consideration suggests a straightforward asset acquisition, not a tender or going-private. Watch for completion of the pooling order and drilling commitments.

CYRX.brief: Cryoport, Inc. filed a Form 15 to terminate the registration of its warrants to purchase common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act. The warrants expired on February 24, 2015, and the company reported zero holders of record as of the certification date. The filing relies on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and Rule 12h-3(b)(1)(i). No board recommendation, advisor, price, premium, or merger mechanics were stated. The deregistration eliminates Cryoport's reporting obligations for the warrants only; common stock remains registered. No risk-arb angle; this is an administrative deregistration following the warrants' expiration.

FUFUW.brief: BitFuFu Inc. (NASDAQ: FUFU) filed a Form 6-K announcing a US$5 million share repurchase program authorized by the Board on June 22, 2026. The program covers Class A ordinary shares over 24 months starting June 24, 2026, via open-market or private transactions under Rule 10b-18. Funded from existing cash, the repurchases are discretionary based on market conditions and stock price. The move signals management's confidence in long-term prospects and commitment to shareholder value. Risk-arb watchers should monitor execution pace; no premium or advisor named.

ECXWW.brief: ECARX Holdings Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting a share exchange agreement with Qualcomm Ventures LLC dated July 7, 2026. Under the agreement, Qualcomm will acquire 10,329,562 Class A ordinary shares of ECARX at the 20-day VWAP prior to signing. Consideration is Qualcomm's transfer of its equity interest in DreamSmart, tied to ECARX's prior plan to acquire a minority interest and IP from DreamSmart. No specific price per share, premium, or board recommendation is stated. The transaction is expected to close in August 2026, subject to customary conditions, and the acquired shares will be subject to a six-month lock-up. This is a structured share-for-asset swap, not a typical open-market acquisition; watch for regulatory approvals and final VWAP calculation.

MANU.brief: Manchester United plc filed a Form 6-K announcing it secured a 25-acre site approximately 350m north-west of Old Trafford from Indurent, a Blackstone portfolio company, to build a new 100,000-seat stadium. The club states the land acquisition is a milestone in its long-term plan to transform the Old Trafford area. The filing does not disclose specific financial terms such as purchase price. The project is coordinated with Trafford Council and the Old Trafford Regeneration Mayoral Development Corporation for wider regeneration. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This is a corporate real estate development update, not a special situation transaction. Watch for further details on the stadium development timeline and any financial disclosures.

RDHL.brief: RedHill Biopharma Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting a private placement of 8,571,429 ADSs (each representing 10,000 ordinary shares) with Series A-1 and A-2 warrants at a combined price of $0.70 per ADS and accompanying warrants. The placement was made to an accredited investor under Section 4(a)(2)/Regulation D. H.C. Wainwright served as exclusive placement agent, receiving a 7.5% cash fee and warrants. The filing includes registration rights and customary terms but does not constitute a special situation; it is a capital-raising transaction with no change of control, restructuring, or acquisition.

APGE.brief: Apogee Therapeutics filed a preliminary proxy statement (PREM14A) in connection with its proposed acquisition by AbbVie Inc. Under the merger agreement dated June 18, 2026, each share of Apogee common stock will be converted into the right to receive $135.11 per share in cash. Apogee's board unanimously recommends stockholders adopt the merger agreement, with Goldman Sachs likely serving as financial advisor (not named in excerpt). The merger will be effected via a reverse triangular merger with AbbVie's wholly owned subsidiary, leaving Apogee as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of AbbVie. The special meeting is expected to occur in 2026. Risk-arb watchers should focus on regulatory timelines and any potential competing bids.

KFY.brief: Korn Ferry filed an 8-K disclosing entry into a Sale and Purchase Agreement to acquire all shares of Auxey Holdco Limited (AMS) for ~£850 million (~$1.1 billion) through ~£659M cash and ~£191M in stock. The stock component is subject to a collar (85%-115% of $71.3815 VWAP). The deal uses a locked-box mechanism with a December 31, 2025 locked-box date and standard leakage protections. The filing does not name a board recommendation or advisor. Closing awaits regulatory and customary conditions; watch for regulatory clearance timing and collar mechanics that could shift the stock portion's value.

NXTS.brief: Nexentis Technologies Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a securities purchase agreement for a registered direct offering and concurrent private placement of common stock and warrants. The company sold 410,998 shares at $7.056 per share, with an equal number of warrants exercisable at same price for five years, raising ~$2.9M gross. No premium expressed or board recommendation noted; the offering priced at a premium to Nasdaq minimum. The offering closes June 24, 2026; resale registration required within 30 days. This is a routine equity financing, not a special-situation event; risk-arb not applicable.

UNFI.brief: United Natural Foods, Inc. filed an 8-K regarding a Term Loan Amendment entered on June 18, 2026. The amendment reprices approximately $371 million outstanding term loan, reducing the applicable margin over SOFR from 4.75% to 4.00%. The Co-Borrowers include SUPERVALU INC., UNFI Wholesale, Inc., and UNFI Distribution Company, LLC. JPMorgan Chase Bank serves as administrative and collateral agent. No board recommendation or advisor is named. All other material terms remain unchanged. This is a routine debt repricing, not a special situation. Watch for potential future refinancing or leverage changes.

VRSSF.brief: Verses AI Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing the resignation of President and COO James Hendrickson due to disagreements over compensation practices, including non-payment of wages. Concurrently, the company announced a strategic pivot: discontinuation of all AI R&D activities to pursue alternative business opportunities. No financial terms were disclosed. The board determined the shift is in shareholders' best interests given limited capital and market conditions. No advisors were named. Filing is equivalent to a US strategic review announcement. Watch for potential sale, merger, or liquidation as the company exits its core business.

CASIF.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist CASI Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ordinary shares, effective at the opening on July 6, 2026. The delisting follows Nasdaq Staff's determination on November 5, 2025, that the Company failed to comply with Listing Rule 5550(b)(2). CASI appealed to a Hearings Panel, which initially allowed continued listing but later suspended the shares on February 26, 2026 after the Company failed to regain compliance. The Staff determination became final on April 9, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, price, or deal terms are specified. The filing is a standard exchange-required notification under Rule 12d2-2(b). Watch for any potential over-the-counter trading or further corporate actions post-delisting.

AZI.brief: Autozi Internet Technology (Global) Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempt company, reported in a Form 6-K that it converted a $7,000,000 interest-free loan from CEO/Chairman Houqi Zhang into 10,000,000 newly issued Class B ordinary shares (par value $0.0005, 200 votes each). The conversion settlement is immediate upon share deposit into a DRS account; shares are subject to a three-year lock-up restricting transfer without company consent. No premium, third-party advisor, or board recommendation is mentioned. This equity-for-debt swap reduces liabilities and dilutes existing holders via voting stock. Watch for shareholder pushback or governance concerns given the CEO's dual role in setting terms.

GDTC.brief: The Chairman, Choo Chee Kong, offered to acquire up to 200,000 shares via private purchases from arm's-length shareholders for cash (minimum 100,000 shares); this is a non-issuer transaction with no proceeds to the company. Separately, his wholly owned EP Capital invested S$300k ($250k) in subsidiary LongevityBank, raising its stake from 6.4% to 12.0% at a post-money valuation of S$5M. The filing reports a private takeover attempt by an insider. No board recommendation, advisors, premium %, or close date are given. Watch for further share acquisition disclosures.

EPOW.brief: E-Power Inc. filed a 6-K reporting a private placement subscription agreement dated June 16, 2026, with a purchaser to issue 15,841,585 Class A ordinary shares at $1.01 per share for $16 million total, relying on Regulation S for non-U.S. persons. The deal was approved by the board, with closing expected around June 26, 2026. The transaction is a share issuance, not a capital return per se, but the category is selected as the closest fit; no buyback or return is involved. The filing is a foreign private issuer's 6-K, equivalent to a U.S. current report on Form 8-K for entry into a material definitive agreement. Watch for dilution impact on existing shareholders and stock price movement around the placement date.

QMMM.brief: QMMM Holdings Ltd. filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Delisting Determination on June 17, 2026. NASDAQ determined to delist the company's securities under Listing Rule IM-5101-4 (discretionary authority) and independently for delayed filing of Form 20-F for FY ended September 30, 2025 under Rule 5250(c)(1). The company plans to appeal via an oral hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel, requesting a stay of suspension and an exception to listing standards. There is no assurance the panel will grant relief. The stock remains halted during the process. Watch for the panel's decision on the compliance plan and potential further stay.

SBSW.brief: Sibanye Stillwater Ltd filed a Form 6-K with the SEC on June 23, 2026, as a foreign private issuer. The filing includes a market release (Exhibit 99.1), but the provided text does not disclose any specific transaction, event, or special situation. The excerpt consists largely of metadata, signatures, and non-ASCII graphics data, with no substantive details on acquisitions, divestitures, or other corporate actions. Without explicit mention of a special-situation event, this appears to be a routine foreign issuer report. The filing likely relates to ordinary business updates, but the opaque content prevents definitive categorization.

SDM.brief: Smart Digital Group Ltd (Nasdaq: SDM) filed a Form 6-K disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq delisting notice on June 17, 2026. Nasdaq determined to delist the company under Listing Rule IM-5101-4 due to an SEC-issued trading suspension on September 29, 2025, citing potential third-party manipulation. Unless the company appeals by June 24, 2026, trading will be suspended June 26, and Nasdaq will file a Form 25-NSE to complete delisting. An appeal would stay suspension pending a Panel decision. The company is evaluating options. Watch for appeal outcome and potential OTC trading if delisted.

BOLD.brief: Boundless Bio (filer) entered into a merger agreement to acquire Serapha Bio via a reverse-merger structure. In the merger, each share of Serapha common/preferred stock will convert into a number of Boundless Bio common stock shares per the Exchange Ratio; Serapha will survive as a wholly owned subsidiary. Options/exercisable warrants will convert into Boundless Bio options/warrants. The transaction qualifies as a tax-free reorganization under Section 368(a). No explicit price per share, premium, or deal value was stated. Board recommendation and advisor were not named. The filing also notes bound to close conditions typical for such reorganizations. Watch for regulatory clearance and potential dissenting votes.

ETR.brief: Entergy Corp filed an 8-K reporting the physical settlement of ATM and underwritten forward sale agreements. On June 22, 2026, it delivered 2,057,826 shares under ATM forward agreements for ~$126M cash, settling all outstanding ATM forwards, and 6,650,417 shares under underwritten forward agreements for ~$546M. Post-settlement, 11,145,984 shares remain under underwritten forwards (proceeds ~$915M), plus 19,247,788 additional shares from May 5, 2026 agreements. The forward sales, disclosed in annual/quarterly reports, effectively raise capital through equity forwards. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or close date cited. Watch potential dilution impact and additional settlements.

FISV.brief: Fiserv Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a public offering of €500 million aggregate principal amount of 3.750% Senior Notes due 2030 and €500 million of 4.250% Senior Notes due 2034. The notes were issued under an existing indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee, supplemented by a Thirty-Ninth and Fortieth Supplemental Indenture. Proceeds use is not specified; the offering expands the company's debt capital structure. This is a routine debt issuance, not a special situation. No special-situation trigger exists; watch for use of proceeds in capital allocation.

FCFS.brief: FirstCash Holdings (through subsidiary Chess Bidco) announced a recommended cash acquisition of Ramsdens Holdings PLC via a court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under UK law. Ramsdens shareholders will receive 609 pence per share (600 pence from Bidco plus a 9 pence permitted dividend). The deal requires approval from a majority in number and 75% of voting Ramsdens shareholders, High Court sanction, and FCA regulatory clearance. The board of Ramsdens has recommended the offer. Closing is expected after conditions are met; watch for shareholder vote and regulatory timeline to assess risk-arb spread.

HSCSW.brief: HeartSciences Inc. (Parent) entered a merger agreement to acquire Fortitude Mining HoldCo (a Zcash mining platform) from its sole owner Digital Currency Group via its merger subsidiary Cordis Acquisition. Consideration is 100% stock: Parent will issue Class V common stock (one vote per share, no economic rights) while existing stock becomes Class A (economic with votes). The deal lacks explicit per-share price, premium, or value terms in the excerpt. The Parent board seeks stockholder approval for charter amendments. Operational focus shifts to digital-asset mining. Watch regulatory clearance and shareholder vote timing; risk-arb centers on valuation uncertainty and approval risk.

RMR.brief: The RMR Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its majority-owned subsidiary, RMR LLC, entered into amended management agreements with Office Properties Income Trust (OPI) upon OPI's emergence from Chapter 11 bankruptcy on June 17, 2026. The new agreements have a five-year initial term, with an annual business management fee of $14 million for the first two years, a 3% property management fee, and a 5% construction supervision fee. RMR LLC also received 2% of OPI's common equity on the effective date and is eligible for up to 8% of OPI's common equity upon achieving performance metrics. This marks OPI's reorganization exit; watch for execution and equity milestones.

TONX.brief: TON Strategy Co received a Nasdaq Letter of Reprimand on June 18, 2026, for inadvertently issuing excess equity awards under its 2019 Stock and Incentive Compensation Plan, violating shareholder approval requirements under Listing Rule 5635(c). The company self-reported the violation on March 27, 2026, after discovering the over-issuance. Nasdaq determined the failure was not deliberate and opted for a reprimand rather than delisting. The shares will remain listed on the Nasdaq. No price, premium, or consideration terms were involved. The event closes without structural or regulatory clock implications. Risk-arb angle: none; this is a compliance resolution with no deal or activist campaign.

CRBD.brief: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFM14A) for their merger. Under the agreement, each Corebridge share converts into 1.000 share of New Equitable common stock, and each Equitable share converts into 1.55516 shares of New Equitable. The boards of both companies unanimously approved the deal. No premium is explicitly stated; Corebridge stock is exchanged at par. The combined entity will have $1.5 trillion in assets under management, serving over 12 million customers. Special meetings are set for July 30, 2026. The transaction is structured as an all-stock merger with fractional shares paid in cash. Risk-arb watchers should monitor regulatory clearance and stockholder votes at both companies.

EQH-PC.brief: Equitable Holdings, Inc. and Corebridge Financial, Inc. filed a definitive proxy statement for a merger to create New Equitable. Under the agreement, each Corebridge share converts into 1.000 share of New Equitable common stock, and each Equitable share converts into 1.55516 shares. The transaction, unanimously approved by both boards, is structured as a stock-for-stock merger with no premium. Special meetings are set for July 30, 2026. The combined entity will have $1.5 trillion in assets. The key risk-arb angle is the exchange ratio, which is fixed; any divergence in stock prices between the two companies will affect the arbitrage spread.

EJH.brief: E-Home Household Service Holdings filed a Form 6-K providing notice and proxy statement for an extraordinary general meeting on July 15, 2026. The meeting will consider a special resolution for a capital reorganization, comprising a reduction of issued share capital by canceling $1.24999 per $1.25 par ordinary share, reducing par value to $0.00001, followed by subdividing each authorized but unissued $1.25 par share into 125,000 new shares of $0.00001 par. The credit from the reduction will offset accumulated losses. This is a routine capital restructuring, not a special situation.

FRTT.brief: Fort Technology Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding LOI for a strategic investment and partnership with Logia USA Inc. The proposed deal involves acquiring 50.1% of Logia USA (subject to equity rebalancing), extending a credit facility of up to USD 2 million (with potential for an additional USD 5 million line), and performance-based equity compensation. The partnership aims to provide critical power infrastructure and fuel maintenance solutions for data centers. No definitive agreement has been signed; the transaction remains subject to due diligence, TSX Venture Exchange approval, and negotiation of definitive agreements. This is an early-stage, non-binding preliminary arrangement, not a consummated special situation.

ASR.brief: Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR), a Mexican airport group reporting on Form 6-K, proposes internalizing technical assistance services via a merger, paying two extraordinary cash dividends of Ps.10.00 each in November and December 2026, and amending bylaws. The internalization would issue ~7.251M new shares and was overseen by its Audit Committee with J.P. Morgan as advisor. This is equivalent to a US special dividend and internal reorganization proposal. Watch shareholder vote on the internalization and dividend approval; no risk-arb as this is not a take-private.

AMIX.brief: Autonomix Medical filed an 8-K reporting a 1-for-21 reverse stock split effective June 24, 2026, approved by stockholders at the October 30, 2025 annual meeting and authorized by the board. The split reduces outstanding shares from 11,409,344 to ~542,000 with no par value change and authorized shares remain at 500 million. Proportional adjustments apply to options/warrants. The action aims to maintain Nasdaq listing compliance and does not involve a tender or capital return event. Watch for continued listing requirements and potential future shareholder dilution.

BRBR.brief: BellRing Brands filed an 8-K on June 24, 2026, disclosing workforce realignment actions approved to streamline operations and improve efficiency. The company expects annualized run-rate operating expense savings of $10–$12 million pre-tax ($3M non-cash stock compensation), to begin in Q4 fiscal 2026 with majority in fiscal 2027. One-time charges of ~$6 million (cash severance) will be incurred primarily in Q3 fiscal 2026, with actions substantially complete by end of Q3. Separately, Chief Growth Officer Douglas J. Cornille stepped down effective June 24, 2026, with departure on September 1, 2026, receiving severance per existing plans. This restructuring is a cost-cutting reorganization, not a special situation category like a strategic review or activist campaign.

CBAN.brief: Colony Bankcorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 24, 2026, announcing its entry into a merger agreement to acquire First Reliance Bancshares, Inc. (FSRL). Each FSRL share will be converted into the right to receive either $19.75 in cash or 0.94 shares of Colony common stock, subject to proration such that 20% of shares receive cash and 80% receive stock. The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction. Expected to close in Q4 2026, the deal is subject to customary conditions. Watch for regulatory approvals and shareholder elections to gauge the risk-arb spread.

DAKT.brief: Daktronics filed an 8-K reporting its board authorized an additional $40M for share repurchases under an existing program. No specific price or premium is given; repurchases may occur in open market or private transactions at management's discretion. The program has no fixed expiration and can be suspended anytime. No advisor or recommendation is named. The filing is a routine capital allocation update, not a formal tender offer. Watch for actual repurchase pace and potential impact on share float.

DH.brief: Definitive Healthcare Corp. disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 18, 2026, for failing the minimum $1.00 bid price requirement over 30 consecutive business days through June 17. The company has a 180-day cure period, until December 15, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at $1.00 or more for at least ten consecutive business days.
