If unmet, an additional 180-day period may be available if other listing standards are satisfied, potentially via a reverse stock split. The notice has no immediate delisting effect; stock continues trading under symbol DH. Watch for compliance progress or potential reverse-split resolution.

DFTX.brief: Definium Therapeutics (filer) filed an 8-K reporting entry into an underwriting agreement for a public offering of 20,588,236 common shares at $34.00 per share, plus a 30-day over-allotment option for 3,088,235 shares exercised in full, expected to close June 25, 2026. Gross proceeds ~$805M, net ~$758M, used for R&D, potential commercialization of DT120 ODT, and working capital. Underwriters include J.P. Morgan, Jefferies, Leerink, BofA. This is a standard equity financing, not a special situation.

FCEL.brief: FuelCell Energy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Capital Equipment Purchase Agreement with Fit Energy USA LP to manufacture and deliver up to 380 MW of carbonate fuel cell blocks in phases for data center baseload power. The initial 30 MW phase is effective; further phases are at Fit's option with milestone payments. Concurrently, the company issued warrants to purchase up to 12 million shares at $26.44, vesting upon receipt of non-refundable deposits. This is a commercial supply agreement with an equity kicker, not a change-of-control or capital-return event. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for deposit milestones to gauge commitment.

GHXIU.brief: Gores Holdings XI, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO and a simultaneous private placement. The IPO of 35,880,000 units at $10.00/unit generated gross proceeds of $358.8 million; each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-fourth of a warrant exercisable at $11.50. The sponsor purchased 225,000 private placement shares at $10.00/share. A total of $358.8 million was placed in trust. This is a standard SPAC formation event; no business combination is announced. Watch for the de-SPAC timeline and potential target announcement within the typical 24-month window.

INVE.brief: Identiv, Inc. entered into a Stock and Asset Purchase Agreement to sell its specialty IoT business to Trackonomy Systems, Inc. for $50 million in Series C Preferred Stock ($20.07/share) plus assumption of certain liabilities. The sale includes substantially all operating assets and shares of Identiv (Thailand) Co., Ltd., with $25 million cash transferred subject to working capital adjustments. Closing requires stockholder approval from both parties, no enjoining orders, and a charter amendment for Series C Preferred shares. Watch for stockholder vote timing and potential regulatory risks.

OPRT.brief: Oportun Financial Corp filed an 8-K on June 22, 2026, regarding a settlement agreement with activist investor Bradley L. Radoff and The Radoff Family Foundation. Under the agreement, two current Class I directors will retire by the 2026 annual meeting; the Radoff Parties are subject to a standstill limiting beneficial ownership to under 4.9% of voting securities, with proxy solicitation and extraordinary transaction restrictions. During the Restricted Period (through ~15 days before 2028 nomination deadline), they must vote in line with Board recommendations, except when ISS and Glass Lewis recommendations conflict, or on extraordinary transactions. The company reimburses the Radoff Parties' reasonable expenses. This resolves the activist campaign; watch for board composition changes and any future activist moves.

PTY.brief: The registrant, PIMCO Corporate & Income Opportunity Fund, filed an 8-K disclosing a board-approved change to its 80% investment policy, effective August 28, 2026. The policy now requires at least 80% of net assets be invested in corporate debt obligations of varying maturities and/or income-producing investments, including non-corporate issuers. This is a routine portfolio guideline adjustment, not a special situation event. No shareholder vote, advisor engagement, or financial terms were disclosed. The filing includes a supplement to the prospectus and statement of additional information. Investors should monitor for quarterly portfolio composition updates.

PLD.brief: Prologis filed an 8-K announcing an indicative all-share proposal to acquire SEGRO plc, a UK industrial REIT, on June 16, 2026. Terms of the all-stock transaction are not specified in terms of price per share or premium. SEGRO's board unequivocally rejected the proposal on June 23, 2026. Prologis urged SEGRO shareholders to encourage engagement. Under UK Takeover Code Rule 2.6(a), Prologis must announce a firm intention to make an offer or walk away by July 22, 2026. The filing is a non-US takeover mapped to an acquisition. Watch for Prologis's next move: a possible hostile bid or walkaway.

ROC.brief: Rank One Computing Corp (ROC) filed an 8-K on June 23, 2026, reporting its agreement to acquire 100% of ZTC Holdco, Inc. for aggregate consideration of $500,000 cash at closing (subject to adjustments for debt, expenses, and net working capital), $2.5 million in restricted stock (vesting over three years), and up to $7 million in revenue share payments over seven years. ROC will also grant up to $500,000 in retention RSUs. Closing requires regulatory approvals, third-party consents, employment agreements, and completion of ZTC's 2024-2025 audit. Watch for audit completion and regulatory timing; risk-arb centers on financing and clearance.

BASA.brief: Basanite, Inc. filed Form 15 on June 25, 2026, to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act, effective immediately. The company certifies it has fewer than 300 record holders (274 as of filing date) and relies on Rule 12g-4(a)(1). No board recommendation or advisor is named. The deregistration suspends the duty to file periodic reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). The action does not involve a transaction, consideration, or premium. Risk-arb angle: No arb opportunity; focus is on reduced disclosure obligations and potential illiquidity for remaining holders.

EHGO.brief: EShallgo Inc filed a Form 6-K reporting a securities purchase agreement dated June 30, 2026, for a registered direct offering. The company issued 200,000 Class A ordinary shares at $1.00 per share and pre-funded warrants for 550,000 shares at $0.99 per warrant, raising ~$750,000 gross proceeds. The warrants were exercised immediately at $0.01 per share. Univest Securities acted as placement agent, receiving 7% cash fee plus up to $50,000 expense reimbursement. Proceeds are for working capital. This is a routine capital raise, not a special situation; the filing is a standard disclosure of a shelf takedown under an effective F-3 registration statement.

GIBOW.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by Gibo Holdings Ltd reporting a share consolidation (reverse stock split) approved at an EGM. The board implemented a 25-for-1 consolidation effective May 25, 2026, with trading on Nasdaq expected to begin on a split-adjusted basis on June 29, 2026. No fractional shares will be issued; fractional entitlements are rounded down. The consolidation affects all shareholders uniformly without altering percentage interests, except for fractional shares. The filing also covers warrant adjustments and a change in authorized share capital structure. This is a routine corporate action to meet listing requirements, not a special situation. The transfer agent, Transhare, is the exchange agent. What to watch is the potential impact on liquidity and any subsequent listing compliance.

NEXA.brief: Nexa Resources filed a Form 6-K confirming awareness of ongoing negotiations between its controlling shareholder Votorantim S.A. and Boliden AB regarding a potential transaction that would impact Nexa. No specific terms (stake size, price per share, premium) were disclosed. The company has no certainty an agreement will be reached and will not comment further until appropriate. This is a preliminary-stage M&A rumor/confirmation without a definitive agreement or formal proposal. The risk-arb angle is to monitor for a binding offer or further disclosures.

PLSM.brief: Pulsenmore Ltd. (a foreign private issuer) filed a Form 6-K reporting a registered direct offering of pre-funded and ordinary warrants to an institutional investor. The combined purchase price is $4.7999 per unit, with aggregate gross proceeds of ~$7.5 million. Pre-funded warrants are exercisable at $0.0001 per share and do not expire; ordinary warrants are exercisable at $4.80 per share for five years. A.G.P./Alliance Global Partners acted as sole placement agent. The company intends to use proceeds for marketing, commercialization, and working capital. This is a capital-raising event, not a special situation such as a tender, acquisition, or restructuring; it is ordinary financing. What to watch: the registration statement filing and any subsequent resale of shares.

TII.brief: Titan Mining Corporation filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing that its subsidiary, Empire State Mines, received Conditional Selection Notices from the U.S. Army for Enhanced Use Lease opportunities at two defense installations to build a graphite purification plant. The filing does not involve a transaction meeting special-situation categories; it describes a government contract award with no disclosed financial terms, board recommendation, or structural mechanics typical of M&A or capital events. This is a routine disclosure of a business development.

ASPI.brief: ASP Isotopes Inc. filed an 8-K regarding its entry into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with ENDRA Life Sciences Inc., Noble Africa LLC, Renergen Limited, and Kruger Merger Sub LLC. The transaction involves Merger Sub merging into Noble, with Noble surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of ENDRA. ASPI will contribute its equity in Renergen to Noble for 55.5 million Class B units, and Noble will sell units for ~$50 million. The terms imply a reverse Morris trust-like spin-off/merger, where ASPI shareholders will hold 10-vote-per-share ENDRA stock. The board recommendation is not detailed; no advisors named. Regulatory timelines are unspecified. Key watch: shareholder approvals and Nasdaq listing of combined entity.

AZZ.brief: AZZ Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a fiscal 2027 Q1 cash dividend of $0.24/share, a 20% increase from the prior $0.20/share. The dividend is payable on July 30, 2026, to shareholders of record July 9, 2026. The Board authorized the dividend; no advisors were named. This is a routine capital return event (regular dividend), not a special situation. The filing includes a press release and inline XBRL. No risk-arb angle exists; watch for continued dividend policy as a signal of shareholder value commitment.

AESPW.brief: This 8-K reports the closing of Aeon Acquisition I Corp.'s initial public offering and full exercise of the underwriters' over-allotment option. The company sold 14,375,000 units at $10.00 per unit, each consisting of one Class A ordinary share, one redeemable warrant (exercise price $11.50), and one right to receive one-fourth of a share upon a business combination. Gross proceeds total $143.75 million, deposited into a trust account. As a blank-check company, this filing marks a milestone in its lifecycle. The next key event is the identification and announcement of a target business combination, which will trigger redemption rights and determine sponsor economics.

GXAI.brief: Gaxos.ai Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of an asset sale to Game Foundry AI on June 18, 2026. The company sold substantially all of its gaming assets, including mobile games and Gaxos Gaming Lab, in exchange for 2,200,000 shares of the buyer's common stock valued at approximately $1,760,000. The shares were issued under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act. No board recommendation or advisors were named in the filing. The mechanics involve a private issuance of shares, with no premium or cash consideration stated. The transaction closed simultaneously with execution. What to watch: valuation of the buyer's stock and any subsequent trading of Gaxos.ai shares post-sale.

GIWWR.brief: GigCapital8 Corp., a blank-check company, filed an 8-K announcing a non-binding letter of intent for a business combination with Quantisimo Corp., a special purpose vehicle established by WISeKey and SEALSQ for quantum technologies. The pre-money enterprise value of Quantisimo is approximately $575 million. Under the terms, former equityholders of both entities will hold equity in the combined public company, with Quantisimo's existing equityholders owning a majority. The transaction requires definitive documentation, due diligence, shareholder approval, regulatory review, and financing. Watch for execution risk and potential dilution from rollover equity.

HIVE.brief: HIVE Digital Technologies' wholly-owned subsidiary issued $130M (including underwriters' $15M option) of 0% exchangeable senior notes due 2031, guaranteed by the issuer. The notes are exchangeable into common shares at $4.83/share, a 27.5% premium over the June 25, 2026 closing price. No regular interest accrues; settlement may be cash, stock, or a combination at the issuer's option. Issuer can redeem on or after July 5, 2029 if shares trade at 130% of the exchange price for 20 days. Watch dilution if notes convert; risk-arb focuses on stock price trajectory relative to the exchange premium.

NGTF.brief: NightFood Holdings filed an 8-K reporting a non-binding LOI to acquire 51% of Jiun Jiang Enterprise via share exchange, with consideration solely in NightFood common stock (final terms to be set). The transaction would make JJ Enterprise a majority-owned subsidiary. No price, premium, or break fee stated; no board recommendation or advisor named. The deal is subject to definitive agreements and closing conditions, with no guarantee of consummation. Watch for definitive agreement and due diligence updates; risk-arb is speculative given non-binding nature.

OSBC.brief: Old Second Bancorp Inc filed an 8-K disclosing a new $61.2 million share repurchase program authorized by its Board, effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago has issued a nonobjection. Repurchases may be conducted via open market, trading plans, or private transactions at management's discretion based on market conditions and regulatory requirements. The program is discretionary, with no obligation to repurchase any shares; it replaces an existing plan expiring June 30, 2026. Watch for execution pace and any regulatory constraints.

PBI-PB.brief: Pitney Bowes Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to its credit agreement adding $150M incremental term loans, bringing total tranche A term borrowings to $302M. Proceeds were used, with other cash, to redeem $347M of 6.875% Senior Notes due 2027. The incremental loans share the same maturity and terms as existing term loans. The redemption eliminates a near-term maturity, extending overall debt profile. This is a liability management restructuring, not a standard refinancing. Watch for potential credit rating impact and whether further liability management steps follow.

PETV.brief: PetVivo Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 24, 2026, announcing entry into an Agreement and Plan of Merger to acquire PiezoBioMembrane, Inc. (PBM) via its wholly-owned subsidiary Merger Sub. Consideration consists of 3,000,000 shares of PetVivo restricted common stock, with milestone-based vesting tied to development and regulatory milestones. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The merger is structured as a reverse triangular merger, with PBM surviving as an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary. The filing lacks transaction value, premium, or expected close date. Watch for milestone achievement timelines and regulatory progress.

SUIG.brief: SUI Group Holdings Ltd. filed an 8-K reporting the approval of a form of Indemnification Agreement for directors and officers, a standard corporate governance matter, and the appointment of Kristina Campbell as an independent director and audit committee chair. No special-situation event such as a merger, tender offer, activist campaign, or restructuring is disclosed. The filing is routine and not classified as a special situation. No deal terms are present; the summary reflects ordinary board actions and compensatory arrangements.

SYNA.brief: Synaptics Inc. filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement to be acquired by ON Semiconductor Corporation (onsemi). Under the agreement, each share of Synaptics common stock will be converted into 1.350 shares of onsemi common stock (stock consideration). The merger consideration is all-stock; no per-share dollar price or premium percentage is stated. The deal is structured as a reverse triangular merger with Synaptics surviving as an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary. Board recommendation and advisors are not named in this excerpt. Regulatory approvals are subject to conditions, with no expected close date provided. Watch for shareholder vote and antitrust clearance for risk-arb spread.

SHAZ.brief: SharonAI Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing the closing of a $900 million private placement of equity and pre-funded warrants on June 23, 2026. The company issued ~6.72M shares at $68.73/share and ~6.37M pre-funded warrants at $68.7299 each, exercisable at $0.0001 per share. The warrants include ownership limitations (9.99% initially, increasing to 19.99% after HSR clearance and to 100% after NASDAQ stockholder approval). This is a capital-raise event, not a special-situation transaction like an acquisition or restructuring. Watch for the resale registration statement and stockholder vote to remove the ownership cap.

SLNG.brief: Stabilis Solutions filed an 8-K (Items 1.02, 9.01) disclosing the termination of a time charter agreement between its subsidiary Stabilis GDS and Seaspan Energy Ltd. for the LNG bunkering vessel Seaspan Garibaldi. The Owners exercised a termination option on June 24, 2026, effective that day, under a Termination Option Agreement dated June 11, 2026. Stabilis GDS must pay a $750,000 early termination fee due January 1, 2027, plus ~$1.1 million in accrued amounts payable in Q3 2026. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for potential liquidity impact or alternative vessel arrangements; no risk-arb angle as this is a contract termination, not a merger.

AAWH.brief: Ascend Wellness Holdings filed a preliminary proxy statement for a special meeting on August 28, 2026, to approve a reverse stock split of its Class A Common Shares at a ratio of 1-for-10 to 1-for-50, as determined by the Board, to be effected before a national exchange listing or within one year. The Board recommends approval, with no advisor named. Adjournment proposal included. The split aims to meet exchange listing requirements. No premium, price, or cash consideration. Watch stockholder vote outcome and subsequent exchange listing timeline.

IDXG.brief: Interpace Biosciences filed a preliminary proxy statement (PREM14A) with the SEC soliciting shareholder approval for a pending acquisition or business combination. The filing does not disclose specific terms such as price per share, premium, or transaction value. The board has not publicly recommended the deal; no financial advisor is named. As a preliminary filing, mechanics like collateral, overhang, or ownership implications remain unstated. The regulatory clock has not yet started; definitive materials will follow. What to watch: final proxy terms and board recommendation once the definitive 14A is filed; risk-arb spreads will depend on disclosed consideration structure and close timeline.

CLNV.brief: Clean Vision Corp filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, effective June 26, 2026. The company had 190 holders of record as of the certification date. The action was taken pursuant to Rule 12g-4(a)(1), suspending its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and 15(d). No price, premium, or board recommendation was provided. The filing allows the company to cease SEC reporting, reducing public disclosure obligations. Risk-arb watchers should note the absence of any going-private transaction or tender offer; this is a unilateral deregistration by the issuer, typically requiring careful review of shareholder base and state law implications.

DFSCW.brief: DEFSEC Technologies Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a public offering of 673,006 common shares at CAD$3.74 per share to accredited investors, paired with a concurrent private placement of warrants exercisable at CAD$4.39 for five years. The offering is limited by the one-third public float restriction under General Instruction I.B.5 of Form F-3, with aggregate proceeds capped at ~US$1.77 million. H.C. Wainwright Co., LLC serves as placement agent but does not purchase or sell securities. While this is a capital markets transaction, it does not meet the special-situations criteria as it lacks a corporate control event such as a merger, tender offer, or restructuring. The filing is an ordinary at-the-market-like offering. Watch for dilution impact on existing shareholders and the exercise of warrants, but no risk-arb angle applies.

CAAP.brief: Corporacion America Airports S.A. (CAAP) filed a Form 6-K disclosing that its subsidiary Inframerica entered a Transition Amendment Agreement with ANAC to renegotiate the Brasilia airport concession. Key changes include replacing a fixed concession fee with a variable one, Infraero's exit from Inframerica's capital (CAAP holds 51%, Infraero 49%), adding 10 regional airports, and requiring additional investments. A fast-track public tender for 100% of Inframerica shares is required by December 2026; CAAP intends to participate. If no bids, the amended concession automatically grants to Inframerica. Material change in economic equilibrium drives this court-ordered restructuring. Watch for tender outcome and regulatory clearance.

SVREW.brief: SaverOne 2014 Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding term sheet to acquire 33.3% of Gryphen Aircraft Industries for $5 million, with an option to increase to 53% within 24 months based on a €30 million valuation. The board’s recommendation is not stated; no advisors named. The transaction is subject to due diligence and definitive agreements. The investment targets the military UAV market, leveraging Gryphen’s existing aircraft platforms. Watch for execution of definitive agreements and milestone achievements; risk-arb centers on due diligence outcomes and regulatory clearance for this cross-border minority stake.

EDTK.brief: Skillful Craftsman Education Technology Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the resignation of its independent auditor, HTL International, LLC, effective June 22, 2026, and the engagement of Guangdong Prouden CPAs GP on June 25, 2026. The prior audit report for FY ended March 31, 2025 was unqualified, with no disagreements or reportable events except previously disclosed material weaknesses. The company provided HTL International with disclosures and attached their agreeing letter as Exhibit 16.1. This auditor change is a routine corporate governance event, not a special situation requiring transactional analysis. What to watch: any future restatements or regulatory delays linked to the new auditor.

UPC.brief: Universe Pharmaceuticals INC filed a Form 6-K reporting entry into a Share Purchase Agreement on June 17, 2026, to acquire 100% of Best Praise International Limited for $10,751,000, payable entirely via 4,376,552 Class A ordinary shares. The target holds five PRC patents in age-related, neurodegenerative, cognitive, and cardiovascular pharmaceutical technologies. The board ratified the deal on June 24, 2026; consideration was based on an independent valuation by King Kee Appraisal. Closing conditions include board/regulatory approvals, Nasdaq compliance, and no change of control. The deal must close within 120 days or either party may terminate; watch for patent validity and share issuance compliance risks.

TVIVU.brief: Texas Ventures Acquisition IV Corp filed Form 8-K reporting the completion of its IPO and concurrent private placement on June 22, 2026. The company sold 17.25M units at $10.00/unit, each consisting of one Class A share and one-half warrant, raising $172.5M in gross proceeds. Simultaneously, it sold 6.1M private placement warrants at $1.00/warrant to sponsor TXV Partners IV and underwriter Cohen, generating $6.1M. Net proceeds of $173.36M were placed in trust. The filing confirms the SPAC's formation and funding, with the trust serving as collateral for future de-SPAC. No target is announced; watch for a business combination announcement within the typical 24-month window, with risk-arb spread hinging on deal terms and shareholder redemption.

ULH.brief: Universal Logistics Holdings (ULH) indirectly sold a Kearny, NJ facility for $38M cash and simultaneously acquired all membership interests of Passaic Ventures LLC (owner of Newark, NJ facility) from Lakeshore Ventures LLC in a related-party transaction approved by disinterested directors. The Kearny REPA and Passaic MIPA were executed June 24, 2026. No premium, share price, or break fee stated. The buyer/swap partner is affiliated with ULH's Chairman and a director, requiring independent committee oversight. What to watch: potential minority shareholder scrutiny of the valuations and any related-party fairness opinion.

CREX.brief: Creative Realities, Inc. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for an underwritten public offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants. The offering size and price are not yet fixed; the last sale price was $4.10 per share. Pre-funded warrants are exercisable at $0.01 per share with an ownership limitation and no expiration. The company notes a one-third market value limitation under Form S-3 I.B.6. Underwriter compensation, a 30-day greenshoe option, and director/officer interest up to $850,000 are disclosed. This is a routine capital raise, not a special situation. Watch pricing and any subsequent at-the-market sales.

CURB.brief: Curbline Properties Corp. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a forward-sale offering of 10,000,000 common shares (up to 11,500,000 with overallotment). Shares are borrowed and sold by forward purchasers (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo); Curbline receives proceeds only upon physical settlement within ~18 months, with option for cash or net-share settlement. The last sale price was $31.27/share. The structure defers proceeds and dilutes over time; proceeds are for general corporate purposes, not a return of capital directly. Watch forward settlement elections and any cash-settlement risk, which could reduce or eliminate proceeds. Risk-arb angle: minimal typical arbitrage, but monitor execution timing and settlement method.

BTOG.brief: Bit Origin Ltd (BTOG) filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release on its acquisition of 16 NVIDIA Blackwell B300 AI servers with related contractual rights for $1M cash and $10M in equity, closed June 28, 2026. The board recommends the deal as a balance-sheet strengthening move. No advisor is named. The transaction is expected to support AI computing operations after delivery in Q3 2026 and helps Bit Origin meet Nasdaq equity minimum of $2.5M. Watch for delivery timing and any Nasdaq compliance updates as the accounting treatment is finalized.

IMRN.brief: Immuron Ltd filed a 6-K with the SEC regarding a notification to the ASX under Appendix 3H. The company is cancelling 3,805,528 ordinary shares at AUD 0.032 per share as part of a buy-back of unmarketable parcels, announced on ASX on June 23, 2026. This is a de minimis capital return program targeting small shareholdings, not a broader issuer tender or special dividend. After cancellation, quoted shares will be 322,848,081. The filing is a routine report of a share cancellation, not a transformative capital event. No advisor or board recommendation is noted. Watch for any shareholder response if the buy-back expands.

NRRWF.brief: NuRAN Wireless Inc. filed a Form 6-K announcing two capital markets milestones: (i) filing a Form 40-F registration statement with the SEC for a proposed Nasdaq listing, and (ii) a confidential preliminary short-form base shelf prospectus filed with the BCSC for an offering of up to C$100,000,000. The filings are preparatory steps to access U.S. capital markets and provide flexible financing capacity, but do not themselves constitute a specific transaction. No terms such as price, premium, or close date are disclosed. Watch for SEC effectiveness of the 40-F and Nasdaq approval, which would determine listing timing. The shelf prospectus, if receipted, allows future offerings over 25 months. No risk-arb angle exists as no deal is announced.

ORIO.brief: The filing is a Form 6-K by Orion Digital Corp. disclosing a Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency notification. The company has 180 days until December 22, 2026 to regain compliance by having the bid price close at $1.00 or above for ten consecutive business days. No specific action, terms, or deal structure are provided. This is a routine listing compliance notice, not a special situation event. As a foreign private issuer report, it mirrors a US filing that would be a generic 8-K item 3.01 notice. There are no advisory, premium, or structural details to analyze. Watch for subsequent reverse stock split or other compliance measures.

CMRF.company: CIM REAL ESTATE FINANCE TRUST, INC.
CMRF.brief: CIM Real Estate Finance Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a multi-step acquisition of Legacy CIM's real assets management business and investment portfolio. The registrant formed a new operating partnership (New OP), contributed all its equity interests in its existing operating partnership and other material assets/liabilities, while CIM Group Holdings contributed all equity of CIM Group Management, LLC and CIM Group Investments, LLC plus $1,000 cash to New OP in exchange for newly issued Class A LP units with equal economic rights. Terms were not disclosed for price per share or premium. No board recommendation or break fee was specified. The transaction closed June 24, 2026; watch for regulatory filings and integration risks.

DLR-PL.brief: Digital Realty Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K describing the creation of non-voting common stock in connection with the closing of the Blackstone Acquisition, making Digital Realty the target. The filing references Articles Supplementary designating 12,310,249 shares as non-voting common stock, which convert to voting common stock upon transfer by the initial holder or affiliate. No specific price, premium, advisor, or board recommendation is stated. The mechanical detail is the automatic conversion feature tied to transfer. Key watchpoint: regulatory approvals and integration timeline for the Blackstone deal, with risk-arb focus on deal completion conditions and any potential shareholder dissent.

GLP-PB.brief: Global Partners LP filed an 8-K announcing the full redemption of all outstanding Series B Fixed Rate Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Units (NYSE: GLP pr B) on July 30, 2026. The redemption price is $25.00 per unit plus accrued and unpaid distributions to the redemption date, payable in cash. The board approved the redemption; Equiniti Trust Company, LLC acts as redemption agent. All units will be redeemed, ceasing trading on NYSE. This capital return event returns cash to preferred holders. Watch for redemption mechanics and potential tax implications.

ROLR.brief: High Roller Technologies filed an 8-K (Items 8.01, 9.01) announcing its wholly owned subsidiary ROLR US LLC received a guaranteed introducing broker license from the National Futures Association (NFA) to enter prediction markets, with operations guaranteed by Crypto.com FCM via a guarantee agreement with OG Markets US, Inc. No deal terms, prices, or stakes are involved. The filing is a routine regulatory milestone update for a planned platform launch, not a special situation. What to watch: Monitor regulatory approvals and progress toward commercial launch of the ROLR prediction markets platform.

USDW.brief: Made in USA Inc. filed Form 8-K announcing completion of an asset acquisition from affiliated seller Made in USA One LLC on June 26, 2026. Consideration was 5,000,000 restricted shares of common stock, with no cash paid. The acquired assets include domain names, AI tools, blockchain infrastructure, and operational platforms for a Made-in-USA verification business. The registrant acted as acquirer in this related-party deal. No premium, board recommendation, or advisor details were disclosed. Watch for shareholder dilution and resale restrictions under Rule 144.

MTX.brief: Minerals Technologies Inc. (MTI) filed a Plan of Reorganization in Chapter 11 cases of its subsidiaries BMI OldCo Inc. and affiliated debtors, as announced via press release on June 29, 2026. The filing complies with a court deadline. No specific financial terms (stake, price, premium) are disclosed. The board is not explicitly recommending, and no advisors are named. Mechanically, the plan involves non-debtor affiliates; the bankruptcy proceedings are in the Southern District of Texas. Watch for court approval and potential creditor negotiations; risk-arb centers on plan confirmation and exit financing terms.

TE.brief: T1 Energy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its publicly traded and private warrants (exercisable for common stock at $11.50 per share) will expire on July 9, 2026. As of March 31, 2026, there were approximately 14.8 million public and 9.8 million private warrants outstanding. To settle pre-expiration exercises, public warrants will cease trading on the NYSE at market open on July 9, 2026. The NYSE will file a Form 25 to delist and deregister the public warrants. The common stock (symbol TE) remains listed. The event is a scheduled contractual expiration, not a special situation; watch for any exercise activity near expiry.

TSNDF.brief: TerrAscend Corp. filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026, announcing a preliminary proxy statement for a special meeting to vote on a share consolidation (reverse stock split) of its common, exchangeable, and preferred shares. No definitive terms (ratio, price per share, premium) are disclosed; the filing is a procedural update. The board has not yet made a formal recommendation, and no advisor is named. The company is Canadian, trading OTCQX, and the proxy solicitation follows SEC and SEDAR+ requirements. Watch for the definitive proxy with consolidation ratio and meeting date; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is structural, not transactional.

ALRTF.brief: ALR Technologies SG Ltd. (registrant) filed a Form 6-K furnishing a press release announcing it has entered into a Letter of Intent to acquire CGM Medical Technology Singapore Pte. Ltd. and CGM Medical Technology Shenzhen Ltd. The filing does not disclose exact terms such as price per share, premium percentage, or implied value, nor does it name a board recommendation or advisors. The filing is a non-US issuer report on a proposed acquisition. What to watch: progress toward a definitive agreement, regulatory approvals, and potential risk that the LOI does not result in a binding deal.

ANGHW.brief: Anghami Inc. filed a 6-K confirming receipt of a preliminary, non-binding going-private proposal from controlling shareholder OSN Streaming Limited to acquire all outstanding ordinary shares not already owned by OSN at $3.39 per share in cash. OSN currently owns ~67% of the Company's outstanding shares. The Board appointed three new independent directors and formed a special committee to review and negotiate the proposal. The acquisition is expected to be funded with equity or other financing from OSN's shareholders and is not subject to a financing condition. No formal recommendation has been made yet. What to watch: the special committee's evaluation, potential competing bids, and the timeline for a definitive agreement; risk-arb spread relative to $3.39 offer price.

BDRX.brief: Biodexa Pharmaceuticals filed a Form 6-K disclosing a registered direct offering and concurrent private placements. On June 29, 2026, the company entered a securities purchase agreement with an institutional investor to issue 82,809 ADSs at $2.85/ADS and 200,143 pre-funded warrants at $2.8499/ADS (exercise price $0.0001). A first private placement includes Series M warrants for 282,952 ADSs exercisable at $2.85/ADS, subject to shareholder approval and beneficial ownership limits of 4.99% or 9.99%. The offering uses an existing Form F-3 shelf registration. This is a capital raise, not a special situation like restructuring or going-private. Watch for shareholder vote and warrant exercise dynamics.

GGAL.brief: Grupo Financiero Galicia S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting a material event: a cash dividend payment schedule. The Board resolved to pay a total cash dividend of ARS 39,999,772,000 in three equal installments of ARS 13,333,257,333.33 each, payable between July 1-15, August 1-15, and September 1-15, 2026. This follows approval at the Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting on April 28, 2026. No advisor or recommendation is mentioned. The filing is a routine dividend schedule with no special-situation elements beyond a significant capital return. Investors should monitor currency and regulatory timing in Argentina.

HMC.brief: Honda Motor Co., Ltd. filed a Form 6-K announcing a partial amendment to the acquisition of an additional 21% equity interest in Astemo, Ltd. from Hitachi, Ltd., converting Astemo from an equity-method affiliate into a consolidated subsidiary. The transaction was originally scheduled to close in Q1 FY2027 but is now extended to by the end of Q3 FY2027 due to pending regulatory approvals in some countries. Terms such as price per share, total value, and premium were not disclosed. The deal involves Honda increasing its stake and structural changes with Hitachi and JIC Capital Ltd. Watch for completion of regulatory approvals and the impact on Honda's consolidated financials. Risk-arb: extension of timeline adds uncertainty.

RAY.brief: Raytech Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the closing of a registered direct offering on June 29, 2026, under a shelf registration statement. The company sold 3,149,832 ordinary shares at $1.97 per share for aggregate gross proceeds of ~$6.2 million. CBC Securities Inc. acted as exclusive placement agent on a reasonable best-efforts basis, receiving a $50,000 fee. Participation by affiliated investors (Fortune Genesis Holdings and WK Frater Holdings) was approved by the board and audit committee under related-party procedures, with a lock-up through September 20, 2026. Net proceeds will fund general corporate purposes, expansion into personal health care electronics, and integration costs for the acquisition of Worry free Group. This is a capital-raising event rather than a special situation, as it is an ordinary shelf takedown. Watch for post-offering share price dilution and the company's execution on its strategic expansion.

ANGX.brief: Angel Studios, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into amended and restated merger agreements to acquire Tuttle Twins Show, LLC and Toothy Cow Productions, LLC. The amendments extend the outside date to October 31, 2026 and remove a showrunner condition. Consideration involves Angel Studios Class A common stock; company related parties own 41.6% of TTS units and will receive shares. The board recommends the transactions; no advisor named. The deals remain subject to closing conditions. Watch for regulatory approval and shareholder vote timing; risk-arb focuses on insider stake alignment and extended outside date.

EOSER.brief: Eos Energy Enterprises filed an 8-K reporting two director changes that appear contractual under preferred-stock designation rights, not a forced departure. Greg Nixon resigned as preferred stock director; Nathaniel Fick succeeded him. Fick then resigned as Class III director to become preferred stock director; Haiyan Song succeeded him as Class III director. The holder of Series B Preferred Stock elected Fick. No price, premium, or strategic transaction is involved. This is a routine board rebalancing, not a special situation. Watch for no further regulatory or risk-arb implications.

ULCC.brief: Frontier Group Holdings (via subsidiary Frontier Airlines) filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to its existing Credit Card Affinity Agreement with Barclays. The Seventh Amendment extends the term from 2029 to 2037, enhances net compensation, includes pre-paid consideration, and increases a pre-purchased miles facility from $200M to $375M with payback starting June 2036. It also modifies financial covenants. No acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, or other classic special situation is present; this is a routine commercial contract amendment. Watch for any material changes in loyalty-program economics or leverage.

LCII.brief: LCI Industries entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Patrick Industries and two merger subs. Under the terms, each LCI share will be converted into 1.2440 shares of Patrick common stock (stock consideration). Post-closing, pre-merger Patrick shareholders will own about 52% of the combined entity; LCI shareholders the remainder. Both boards unanimously approved the transaction. The deal involves a two-step merger structure, with First Merger Sub merging into LCI, then the surviving entity merging into Second Merger Sub. Watch for shareholder votes, regulatory clearances, and the exchange ratio adjustment mechanics.

LPBBU.brief: Launch Two Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, filed a Form 8-K disclosing entry into a Business Combination Agreement with NuCube Energy, Inc. on June 25, 2026. The transaction involves Launch Two first re-domiciling from Cayman Islands to Delaware, then merging a wholly-owned subsidiary with NuCube, with NuCube surviving. Terms were not specified in the excerpt. The board's recommendation and advisors are unnamed. The structure includes a domestication step followed by a reverse merger. What to watch: risk-arb angle focuses on SPAC timeline, shareholder approval, and redemptions; typical de-SPAC volatility applies.

MBOT.brief: Microbot Medical Inc. filed an 8-K under Items 7.01 and 8.01 disclosing a Letter of Agreement with Sanmina Corporation to manufacture its LIBERTY Endovascular Robotic System. No financial terms, stake percentage, price, premium, or board recommendation were provided. The agreement is aimed at expanding manufacturing capacity and supporting cost reduction. This is a routine manufacturing supply arrangement, not an acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation. The filing includes no deal mechanics, advisors, or regulatory clock. What to watch: future revenue impact and production ramp.

KITTW.brief: Nauticus Robotics filed an 8-K reporting entry into an Exchange Agreement with an institutional investor to exchange ~$4.0M of secured convertible term loans into 4,800 shares of Series C Convertible Preferred Stock with ~$4.8M aggregate stated value. The exchange closed June 26, 2026, under Section 3(a)(9) exemption with no commissions. The holder retains rights to require additional exchanges of remaining debt. This debt-for-equity swap reduces leverage and interest burden. Watch for potential dilution and further conversions, which may signal ongoing financial restructuring rather than a standalone capital return event.

NUMD.brief: Nu-Med Plus, Inc. (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting a Share Exchange Agreement to acquire 100% of Avid Gold Ltd. Consideration is 4,500,000 shares of Series A Preferred Stock to Avid Gold shareholders pro-rata plus assumption of a $100,000 promissory note. No per-share price, premium, or implied value is stated. Closing is subject to customary conditions with a required date of July 8, 2026, extendable by mutual consent. The board has not disclosed a recommendation or advisor. The transaction is structured as a reverse triangular merger. Watch for regulatory or shareholder approvals; if delayed, risk-arb focuses on termination provisions including a 30-day cure period and ability to close within 12 months.

PATK.brief: Patrick Industries (PATK) filed an 8-K on June 30, 2026, announcing its acquisition of LCI Industries via a two-step merger structure. Under the Agreement and Plan of Merger, each LCI share will be converted into 1.2440 shares of PATK common stock (stock consideration). Post-closing, PATK shareholders will own ~52% and former LCI shareholders ~48% of the combined company. The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction. The filing does not specify a premium, closing date, or break fee. Watch for regulatory clearance and shareholder votes; risk-arb spread will reflect execution timeline and stock consideration volatility.

RVP.brief: Retractable Technologies filed an 8-K announcing a dividend declaration on its Series II and Series III Class B Convertible Preferred Stock. The aggregate dividends amount to $57,611.25 ($39,050.00 + $18,561.25), accruing at $1.00 per share per annum for the period April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026. The payment date is July 20, 2026 to holders of record on July 10, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The filing is a routine dividend declaration, not a transformative capital return event. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; monitoring recurring preferred dividend coverage is key.

SWMR.brief: Swarmer, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting two master supplier agreements for its software used in unmanned aerial vehicles. Its subsidiary amended a prior agreement with Meta Bureau, reducing fees to ~$2.5M, and entered a new agreement with Progress TRW S.R.O. for ~$1.4M, totaling ~$3.9M in upfront fees. These are ordinary commercial contracts, not a change-of-control transaction or special situation. The filing is a routine material definitive agreement that does not involve an acquisition, divestiture, or other transformative event. There is no special-situation angle to monitor.

TALO.brief: Talos Energy Inc. filed an 8-K announcing that its subsidiary, Talos Production Inc., priced an $800M offering of 8.000% second-priority senior secured notes due 2034. The net proceeds will fund a portion of the cash consideration for a previously announced Gulf of America acquisition. Additionally, a conditional notice of redemption was issued for all outstanding 9.000% second-priority senior secured notes due 2029, redeemable at 104.500% of principal plus accrued interest, contingent on the closing of the offering. This is a debt financing transaction and redemption, not a change-of-control event. The filing does not disclose the acquisition terms or target. Watch for closing of the offering and the related acquisition.

VANI.brief: Vivani Medical, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the results of its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 24, 2026, and related director elections and shareholder votes. The filing discloses that the omnibus incentive plan amendment was approved, increasing authorized shares by 11 million, but no special situation event—such as a merger, acquisition, activist campaign, or restructuring—is involved. The report includes routine items like election of directors and advisory vote on executive compensation. As this is a standard corporate governance update, it does not qualify as a special situation filing.

DMB.company: BNY Mellon Municipal Bond Infrastructure Fund, Inc.
DMB.brief: Saba Capital Management, L.P. filed a preliminary proxy statement (PREC14A) seeking shareholder support at BNY Mellon Municipal Bond Infrastructure Fund's 2026 annual meeting. Saba is nominating one independent director to address the Fund's persistent trading discount, which stood at -6.16% as of June 29, 2026 (three-year average -10.26%). The proposal follows shareholder approval in 2025 to declassify the board; the Board has put forth a charter amendment to implement annual director elections. The virtual meeting is scheduled for [ ], 2026, with Campaign Management serving as proxy solicitor. Saba frames the election as a mechanism to hold directors accountable and close the discount. Risk-arb angle: monitor shareholder response and the Board's stance on the declassification proposal.

EVGOW.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE to delist EVgo Inc.'s warrants (exercisable for one share of Class A common stock at $11.50 per share) under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The delisting became effective July 1, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a standard exchange notification; no premium, stake, or deal terms apply. Overhang is limited to outstanding warrants. Watch for trading migration to OTC markets and potential cash exercises if the stock price remains above the strike.

INUV.brief: Inuvo, Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a public offering of 1,631,121 common shares at $1.00/share and pre-funded warrants for 1,337,693 shares at $0.999/warrant, alongside a private placement of Class A and B warrants exercisable at $1.28/share. The last sale price was $1.36 on June 29, 2026. Ladenburg Thalmann acts as placement agent with a 6% fee. The securities are immediately separable; warrants become exercisable in six months. Proceeds before expenses total roughly $2.79M. Watch for market reaction to the dilutive offering and potential exercise of warrants.

SOC.brief: Sable Offshore Corp. filed a 424B5 pricing term sheet for a combined offering of 32,467,533 common shares at $3.08 per share and $300 million of 6.5% convertible senior notes due 2031. The offerings are cross-conditioned with new senior secured credit facilities and a term loan refinancing. Net proceeds from common stock are estimated at $92.8 million; combined proceeds will repay existing senior secured term loan and pay fees. J.P. Morgan is the book-running manager. The filing is a routine capital raise, not a special situation. What to watch: execution risk from cross-conditioning.

DDC.brief: DDC Enterprise Limited filed a Form 6-K announcing a share repurchase program approved by its board on June 9, 2026. The program authorizes up to $10 million in purchases of Class A ordinary shares, limited to 20% of outstanding shares, over 18 months. Repurchases may occur via 10b5-1 plans or open market purchases, with timing at management's discretion. Funding comes from free cash flow, and Bitcoin may be used as collateral for related arrangements. The program is not binding and may be suspended at any time. Watch for execution pace and Bitcoin collateral impact.

EVAX.brief: Evaxion A/S filed a Form 6-K on July 1, 2026, furnishing a press release announcing the presentation of new preclinical data for its cytomegalovirus vaccine candidate EVX-V1 at the International Herpesvirus Workshop. The filing is a routine disclosure by a foreign private issuer of a scientific conference presentation. No corporate event such as an acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or capital return is involved. The filing provides no deal terms, board recommendations, or structural changes. This is a standard operational update without special-situation implications.

GP.brief: GreenPower Motor Company Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting the completion of the third tranche of a preferred share financing. On June 30, 2026, it issued 1,500 Series A Convertible Preferred Shares for gross proceeds of $1,425,000 under a November 14, 2025 agreement with an institutional investor. The agreement was also amended to increase the aggregate stated value by $2 million. Each preferred share is convertible into common shares at a conversion price based on 105% of stated value divided by 125% of the prior day's closing price. A 5% cash placement fee is payable to Digital Offering LLC. This is a capital-raising transaction, not a special situation.

IQMXW.brief: IQM Quantum Computers Oyj filed a Form 6-K reporting completion of its business combination with Real Asset Acquisition Corp. (RAAQ), a Nasdaq-listed SPAC. Under the definitive agreement, RAAQ merged with IQM US LLC, with IQM issuing 14,381,747 existing shares to RAAQ shareholders via ADSs (symbol: IQMX). RAAQ warrants were assumed as IQM Warrants (symbol: IQMX WS) with an $11.50 exercise price. Concurrently, a PIPE investment of 14,548,000 shares was placed with institutional investors. The transactions closed July 1, 2026, with Nasdaq trading starting July 2, 2026, and Nasdaq Helsinki trading expected July 3, 2026. Board appointments included Juho Sarvikas and Jeff Tuder. Watch for trading liquidity and warrant overhang.

NGG.brief: National Grid plc filed a Form 6-K announcing that its subsidiary, National Grid Ventures, will invest $1.75 billion to acquire a 35% stake in Joulent LLC, a platform developing integrated power solutions for US large-load customers. The investment supports Joulent's foundational project, Project Kilby, a 2.67 GW co-located power facility in West Texas partnering with Chevron, supplying electricity to a Microsoft data center under a 20-year PPA. No board recommendation or advisor is named; the deal is a minority equity investment with no premium or price per share disclosed. The transaction targets first power in 2028; watch for regulatory approvals and execution milestones.

RZLVW.brief: Rezolve AI plc (NASDAQ: RZLV) filed a Form 6-K on June 30, 2026, announcing shareholder approval at its AGM of a capital reduction and authority to launch a share repurchase program of up to $300 million. The buyback, subject to UK Court approval, aims to address a perceived disconnect between public market valuation and hyper-growth trajectory; no price per share or premium was specified. Q1 2026 unaudited revenue was ~$60M, with FY26 guidance of ~$360M. The board has flexibility to execute repurchases opportunistically. Monitor UK Court timeline and actual buyback initiation for signal of value return.

TECK.brief: Teck Resources filed a Form 6-K on June 30, 2026, mailing a Letter of Transmittal for its merger-of-equals with Anglo American plc under a court-approved plan of arrangement. Each Teck share exchanges for 1.3301 Anglo ordinary shares (or exchangeable shares for eligible Canadian holders), with no cash consideration. The board recommended the transaction in a prior proxy circular dated November 3, 2025. The mechanism involves depositing shares through Computershare, with settlement via CDS, DTC, or DRS. The transaction eliminates Teck's public listing, effectively taking it private within Anglo. What to watch: shareholder elections and regulatory closing conditions.

ABR-PF.brief: Arbor Realty Trust Inc. filed an 8-K to report the issuance and sale of $375M aggregate principal amount of 6.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029, including full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $50M. The notes are senior unsecured, bear 6.25% interest payable semiannually, and mature July 1, 2029; they are convertible prior to April 1, 2029 upon satisfaction of conditions and anytime thereafter. Upon conversion, the company will settle in cash and/or common stock at its election. The initial conversion rate is 164.0016 shares per $1,000 principal, equivalent to ~$6.10 per share. No redemption or sinking fund is provided. This is a capital-return transaction via convertible note offering; watch for dilution upon conversion and interest payment obligations.

BDC.brief: Belden Inc. filed an 8-K to report the completion of its acquisition of Vistance Networks’ RUCKUS reporting segment (the "RUCKUS Acquisition") on July 1, 2026, pursuant to a Purchase Agreement dated April 29, 2026. To fund the transaction, Belden entered into a $1,850 million senior secured term loan credit facility maturing July 1, 2033, bearing interest at term SOFR + 2.25% or base rate + 1.25% p.a., with customary covenants. No per-share price, premium, or valuation details were disclosed. The Transaction is closed. What to watch: post-acquisition integration and debt-service metrics.

BFNH.brief: Bioforce Nanosciences Holdings filed an 8-K reporting the receipt of an assignment of federal oil and gas leases covering ~19,957 acres in Nye County, Nevada from Natural Minerals Trust, LLC (controlled by majority shareholder Nexus Capital). The assignment is pending BLM approval; no deal price, stake, or premium is stated. If approved, Bioforce intends to develop the leases, with primary terms of 10 years and a 12.5% royalty. This is a non-routine operational update but does not fit standard special-situation categories like acquisitions or divestitures; it is more akin to an asset assignment subject to regulatory approval. Watch for BLM action and any subsequent partnership announcements.

ES.brief: Eversource Energy filed an 8-K announcing the completed sale of its subsidiary Aquarion Water Company to Aquarion Water Authority, a Connecticut quasi-public entity, for $2.4 billion in cash. The sale was executed after satisfying all regulatory terms and requirements. Adjusted net equity proceeds of approximately $1.7 billion will be used to displace Eversource debt. The company expects a non-cash after-tax charge of ~$115 million ($0.31/share) in Q2 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, break fee, or premium was disclosed. The filing is a closing announcement, not a pending transaction. What to watch: the deployment of proceeds and any impact on credit ratings.

XOM.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist Exxon Mobil Corp common stock (OLD XOM) effective July 13, 2026, following a redomiciliation merger completed July 1, 2026. The reorganization, under an April 8, 2026 merger agreement among ExxonMobil, ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (TX), and Ensign LLC, converted each old share into the right to receive an immediate cash payment representing a new share of the successor entity (NEW XOM, CUSIP 30233Q108). This is solely a listing change; registration of the new stock under Section 12(b) continues. No premium or valuation terms disclosed. Watch for seamless trading migration to the new CUSIP.

IHT.brief: InnSuites Hospitality Trust disclosed receipt of a NYSE American non-compliance notice for failing continued listing standards under Section 1003(a)(i) due to a stockholders' deficit of ~$(921,921) as of April 30, 2026, and recent net losses. No immediate delisting; the Trust must submit a compliance plan by July 24, 2026, with a cure deadline of December 24, 2027. Potential remedies include converting RRF LLLP units into IHT shares, converting related-party debt to equity, capital raises, or restructurings, each subject to approvals. Listing will show a .BC indicator. Watch for plan acceptance and quarterly progress updates; risk-arb remains thin given no M&A event.

KR.brief: Kroger Co. filed an 8-K announcing it has entered into a merger agreement to acquire Giant Eagle, Inc. for approximately $1.65 billion, consisting of $1.25 billion in cash and $400 million in assumed liabilities. The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to HSR antitrust clearance and customary conditions. Kroger anticipates limited store divestitures to satisfy regulatory requirements. No board recommendation or advisor is named in the filing. Risk-arb watchers should monitor the antitrust review timeline and potential store sale process.

KE.brief: Kimball Electronics (KE) filed an 8-K to report its acquisition of Helvoet Polymer Technologies B.V. and Helvoet Rubber Plastics Technologies (India) Pvt. Ltd. from Hydratec Industries N.V. The all-cash purchase price was approximately €90 million (~$103 million), subject to post-closing working capital adjustments. Approximately €1.8 million of the cash consideration is held in escrow as security. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, funded by cash and existing credit lines. The agreement includes customary representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions. No board recommendation, advisor names, or premium percentage were disclosed. Watch for post-closing adjustments and integration updates.

NNBR.brief: NN, Inc. filed an 8-K Item 1.01 reporting a Securities Purchase Agreement with institutional investors for a private placement of 24,509,804 shares at $3.06/share, total gross proceeds $75.0M. The transaction is a direct equity issuance, not a tender offer or buyback. Craig-Hallum Capital Group serves as placement agent with a 6% fee. The company also entered a Registration Rights Agreement for resale registration. No premium, board recommendation, or break fee was disclosed. The filing represents a capital raise, not a return to shareholders, but falls under Capital Returns as a corporate action changing equity structure. Watch customary closing conditions and NASDAQ listing compliance.

PPHC.brief: Public Policy Holding Company (PPHC) filed an 8-K reporting completion of its acquisition of Tancredi Intelligent Communication Ltd. The press release lacks exact price, premium, or share terms but notes the deal is earnings-accretive, adding 22 staff and $4.3M net revenues (2025). Tancredi operates under PPHC's TrailRunner International. PPHC's board recommended the deal. No regulatory clock or break fee mentioned. Watch for post-close integration details to assess accretion timing.

INIS.brief: Radnostix Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing its acquisition of certain assets related to the Lara System technology platform and Ellexa Explorer Software from Lucerno Dynamics, LLC. The initial purchase price was $900,000, comprising $150,000 cash and $750,000 in common stock valued via 20-day VWAP. Potential milestone payments include up to $500,000 in stock for regulatory approval and $250,000 in stock for sales milestones, plus cash earn-outs. The board recommends the transaction. No advisor named. The deal closed on the effective date. Watch for milestone achievements and integration risk; the small size limits arbitrage interest.

SKFG.brief: Stark Focus Group, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a change in control via a stock purchase agreement dated June 9, 2026, with closing on June 25. Purchaser MJG Polo LLC acquired 8,300,000 shares (83.43% of outstanding common stock) from selling stockholder Compass North Holdings Limited for $355,000 total ($0.0428 per share). No premium, board recommendation, or advisor named. The Purchase Agreement includes customary representations, warranties, and indemnities. What to watch: regulatory scrutiny of a controlling stake transfer and potential subsequent going-private or squeeze-out transaction; risk-arb focuses on minority shareholder treatment and liquidity.

XLAB.brief: D. Boral ARC Merger Corp filed an S-4 registration statement for its proposed business combination with Exascale Labs Inc., a software company. The transaction involves the merger of D. Boral Acquisition I Corp., a blank-check company, with Exascale. Exact terms (stake %, price/share, implied value, premium %, dates) are not specified in this filing. The board recommends the deal; no advisor is named. Mechanics: the merger structure is typical of a SPAC de-SPAC transaction, with shareholders of Exascale receiving shares in the combined entity. Regulatory clock: the S-4 review by the SEC will precede a shareholder vote. What to watch: risk-arb angle focuses on potential redemptions and regulatory approval timeline; spread will tighten on clearance.

ABVX.brief: Abivax S.A. filed a prospectus supplement on Form 424B5 for a public offering of 6,400,000 American Depositary Shares (ADSs) at $125.00 per ADS, with total proceeds to the company of $762 million before expenses. The offering is an ordinary shelf takedown, not a special situation. The ADSs are listed on Nasdaq, and ordinary shares are traded on Euronext Paris. Underwriters include Leerink Partners, Morgan Stanley, Piper Sandler, and Guggenheim Securities. Delivery is expected July 6, 2026. This is a routine capital raise, not a special-situation event. No special structural mechanics, premium, or break fee apply.

MTVA.brief: MetaVia Inc. filed a prospectus supplement (424B5) to increase its at-the-market (ATM) offering capacity from $2.3M to $4.0M of common stock under an existing Sales Agreement with Ladenburg Thalmann. $2.126M had already been sold. The shares are listed on Nasdaq under MTVA; last sales price was $1.45 on July 1, 2026. The filing supplements prior prospectuses and is qualified by them. This is an equity offering to raise capital, not a return of capital or special distribution. While it involves share issuance, it is an ATM program increase and does not fit the typical special-situations categories like tender offers or going-private. The offering is subject to Rule 424(b)(5) and General Instruction I.B.6 of Form S-3 limiting sales to one-third of public float. Watch for potential dilution impact on share price.

BNRG.brief: Brenmiller Energy Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting its purchase of a 1.2 MWp photovoltaic facility adjacent to a planned industrial energy project in Hungary. The acquisition price is approximately $1.1 million. The facility is expected to generate ~$173,000 in average annual revenue. The purchase supports Brenmiller's BNRG360 strategy of owning and operating integrated clean-energy assets. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a foreign private issuer report under Rule 13a-16; the transaction is a straight asset purchase with no structural complexities. Watch for integration into a larger BNRG360 hub and eventual revenue contributions from expanded solar, battery, and TES systems.

LHSW.brief: Lianhe Sowell International Group Ltd filed Form 6-K disclosing a share subscription agreement on June 30, 2026, with its CEO and Chairman, Yue Zhu, via Lianyue Holding Limited to issue 2,400,000 Class B ordinary shares at $0.165 per share (average closing price of Class A shares over five trading days). Gross proceeds were $396,000. The audit committee approved the transaction, which closed immediately. Post-closing, Yue Zhu beneficially owns 939,688 Class A plus 2,550,000 Class B shares, representing 97.69% aggregate voting power. This effectively consolidates control and reduces minority influence, resembling a going-private step. No premium, advisor, or termination fee disclosed. What to watch: potential follow-on going-private transaction or minority squeeze-out. The non-US filing is mapped to Form 6-K, equivalent to a US current report.

AA.brief: Alcoa Corp filed an 8-K disclosing its entry into an Umbrella Implementation Deed to acquire South32 Limited's bauxite, alumina, and aluminum smelting operations. The aggregate upfront consideration is $3.1 billion in cash plus approximately 17 million shares of Alcoa common stock valued at about $1 billion (based on a $58.79/share 10-day VWAP), representing ~6% post-issuance ownership. Alcoa also agrees to pay up to $750 million in cash as a contingent value right based on alumina/aluminum prices over four annual periods. The transaction is subject to South32 shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and other customary conditions, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. A termination fee of $41M or $82M is payable by South32 in certain circumstances. Watch for shareholder vote and regulatory timelines.

ALPXU.brief: Alpex Acquisition Corp filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its IPO of 11.5M units at $10/unit (including over-allotment) for $115M gross proceeds, and a concurrent private placement of 187.5K units to its sponsor for $1.875M. The proceeds were placed in a trust account with Equiniti Trust Company for the benefit of public shareholders. As a blank-check SPAC, this filing merely documents the IPO closing and trust funding; no business combination, tender, or other special situation is announced. The only notable watch item is the eventual target announcement within the SPAC's 24-month deadline.

AAC-UN.brief: Ares Acquisition Corp III filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its IPO of 39,500,000 units at $10.00 each, including 5,000,000 units from the underwriters' partial over-allotment exercise. Each unit consists of one Class A ordinary share and one-tenth of a redeemable warrant exercisable at $11.50 per share. Gross proceeds were $395M. Concurrently, the sponsor purchased 7,466,667 private placement warrants at $1.50 each, generating $11.2M. Net proceeds of $395M were placed in trust for public shareholders. The SPAC will seek a business combination within the required timeframe. Watch for the target announcement and shareholder vote.

BSVN.brief: Bank7 Corp. entered a Stock Purchase Agreement on July 1, 2026 to acquire ~71% of Century Financial Services Corp. from a court-appointed receiver for $68.0M cash. The board unanimously approved the agreement. This is a stalking horse bid subject to court approval and higher offers, with a $7.25M deposit, a $2.04M break fee, and regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve required. Closing must occur by Nov 30, 2026, or either party may terminate. Watch for competing bids or court auction outcomes; risk-arb centers on auction dynamics and regulatory timeline.

CELZ.brief: Creative Medical Technology Holdings filed an 8-K disclosing warrant exercise inducement offers entered into on June 30, 2026. Holders of 2,790,340 existing warrants (exercise price $2.86/share) agreed to exercise at a reduced price of $1.60/share, generating ~$4.5M gross proceeds, in exchange for new inducement warrants to purchase 5,580,680 shares at $1.60/share. The new warrants are unregistered, require stockholder approval per Nasdaq rules, and have a five-year term. Proceeds will fund working capital. A resale registration statement is to be filed within 30 days. This is a warrant repricing/refinancing, not a standard special situation; no M&A, activist, or restructuring event.

CRVW.brief: CareView Communications filed an 8-K reporting entry into the Fifteenth Amendment to its Credit Agreement, which extends the maturity date. The filing details a series of prior amendments with lender PDL Investment Holdings. No specific terms such as price, stake, or premium are disclosed. The board recommendation is not mentioned. This is a routine debt modification, not a special situation. What to watch: any further amendments or restructuring signals.

CLPR.brief: Clipper Realty Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that its subsidiary 250 Livingston Owner LLC entered into a Consent and Cooperation Agreement with the lender on a $125M loan secured by a Brooklyn property. The agreement provides for a 45-day marketing period to sell the loan to a third party, after which the lender may foreclose or accept a deed in lieu. The borrower retains the right to submit a competing offer. The loan matures in 2029 at 3.63% interest-only. This represents a distressed debt restructuring with potential property transfer, not a standard M&A or activist event. Watch for the outcome of the marketing period and any borrower bid.

BEATW.brief: HeartBeam received a Nasdaq deficiency letter (June 30, 2026) for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)). The company has 180 calendar days, until December 28, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, a second 180-day period may be available if other listing standards are met. The board has not yet announced a specific remedy. The stock remains listed and trading during the cure period, but delisting risk persists if compliance is not achieved. Watch for any reverse stock split or other price-boosting measures the company may pursue.

KRG.brief: Kite Realty Group, L.P. issued $345 million (with a $45 million greenshoe fully exercised for $390 million total) of 3.25% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2032 in a private placement under Rule 144A. The notes are senior unsecured obligations of the operating partnership, issued under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust as trustee. The proceeds likely support capital-return activities such as share buybacks or debt reduction. Exchangeability and conversion mechanics are not detailed. Watch for potential dilution or balance sheet restructuring impacts on equity value.

MVO.brief: MV Oil Trust filed an 8-K announcing the termination of its net profits interest on June 30, 2026, after reaching the cumulative production threshold of 14.4 MMBoe (11.5 MMBoe net to the trust), triggering dissolution per the trust agreement. The trustee notified the NYSE of intent to voluntarily delist units, with trading expected to cease before market open on July 27, 2026, following a final quarterly cash distribution on July 24 to holders of record July 15. The trust will file Form 15 to terminate SEC registration and suspend reporting. Risk-arb: no takeover premium; unitholders receive only final distribution, no buyout. Watch for trust liquidation timeline and cancellation mechanics.

PRSO.brief: Peraso Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a Common Stock Purchase Agreement with Roth Principal Investments LLC, allowing Peraso to sell up to $25 million of newly issued common stock at its discretion over 36 months. No specific price per share or premium is stated; the stock will be sold at market prices with a threshold floor. The board has not made a recommendation, and no advisor is named. This is an at-the-market equity facility, not a tender or return of capital. What to watch: frequency of draws and dilution impact on existing shareholders; the arrangement gives Peraso flexibility but may pressure the stock price.

SXI.brief: Standex International, via its Singaporean subsidiary Mold-Tech Singapore, filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Securities Purchase Agreement on June 26, 2026 to acquire the remaining 9.90% of Narayan Powertech Private Limited from minority shareholders. This follows a prior 90.10% acquisition on October 28, 2024, where the second closing via share swap was contingent on RBI approval which was not obtained by October 28, 2025, triggering put/call options. Instead, parties negotiated a direct sale. No price, premium, or advisor disclosed. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory clearance in India.

USDEW.brief: StableCoinX Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a business combination with TLGY Acquisition Corp. and StableCoinX Assets Inc. on June 25, 2026. Pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement, SPAC Merger Sub merged into TLGY and Company Merger Sub merged into SC Assets, making TLGY and SC Assets wholly-owned subsidiaries of StableCoinX. No specific price, stake, or premium details are stated in this excerpt. The board recommendation and advisors are not named. The transaction closed on schedule, merging the entities into a publicly traded company. The filing is a de-SPAC transaction; watch for post-combination trading performance and any earnout or lockup provisions.

NIMU.brief: Non-Invasive Monitoring Systems (NIMS) filed an S-4 registration statement with the SEC on July 2, 2026, for a business combination with Gravitics Inc. The merger will involve NIMS issuing shares to Gravitics stockholders, with Gravitics becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary. The filing implies a reverse merger structure, as NIMS is a public shell company. No specific terms (price per share, premium, or implied value) were disclosed. The board of NIMS has recommended the deal; no financial advisor was named. The transaction is subject to shareholder approval, SEC effectiveness of the S-4, and customary closing conditions. The target is Gravitics, a private company in the aerospace sector. Risk-arb: watch for shareholder vote timing and regulatory clearance for the combined entity.

USGO.brief: U.S. GoldMining Inc. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement to increase its at-the-market (ATM) offering by up to $4.25 million of common stock via H.C. Wainwright and co-agents. The filing updates prior supplements under an existing S-3 registration; total prior sales were $10.7 million. Shares trade on Nasdaq (symbol USGO); last price $8.84. The offering is a routine capital raise through an ATM facility, not a distressed or transformative special situation. There is no premium, recommendation, or structural complexity; watch for dilution risk from continued ATM sales.

BTCT.brief: BTC Digital Ltd. filed a Form 6-K disclosing a $7M registered-direct/private placement of 6,140,350 Common Units at $1.14 per unit, each consisting of one ordinary share (or pre-funded warrant) plus two PIPE warrants exercisable at $1.71 for 60 months. The offering closed on June 29, 2026, conducted under Section 4(a)(2) with Aegis Capital as sole placement agent on a best-efforts basis, earning 7% commission. The warrants include a 4.99% (or up to 9.99%) beneficial ownership limitation. This is a standard capital raise, not a special situation, as it involves no change of control, tender, or restructuring.

DSGX.brief: Descartes Systems Group filed a Form 6-K announcing its acquisition of Drivin, a Latin American last-mile delivery management platform. The up-front cash consideration is approximately US $30 million, plus a potential performance-based earn-out capped at US $5 million payable in fiscal 2029 if revenue targets are met. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or timeline details were provided. The deal expands Descartes' fleet performance offering and Global Logistics Network in Latin America, funded from cash on hand. Watch for integration execution and earn-out achievement as key risk-arb factors.

GELS.brief: Gelteq Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting shareholder approval and closing of the second tranche of a debt financing with an institutional investor. The aggregate principal amount is up to $3.5 million across two tranches; the first tranche of $1.0 million (net of $150,000 OID) closed on May 7, 2026, and the second tranche of $2.5 million (net of $375,000 OID) closed on June 26, 2026. Each tranche issued a convertible promissory note convertible into ordinary shares at 93% of the lowest daily VWAP during the five trading days preceding measurement. The financing is a structured capital return through convertible debt, not a standard reorganization or buyback. The board recommended approval, required under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d). Watch for dilution risk from the conversion feature and potential shareholder overhang.

PDC.brief: Perpetuals.com Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting results of its extraordinary general meeting held April 30, 2026. Shareholders approved a resolution to reduce stated capital. 8,402,172 votes (36.81% of exercisable votes) were present; 8,319,502 voted for, 81,540 against, 1,130 abstained. This capital reduction is a routine corporate action, not a merger, tender, or restructuring. No deal terms, advisors, or premium were mentioned. The filing is a procedural report on shareholder approval.

RCI.brief: On July 6, 2026, Rogers Communications Inc. announced via Form 6-K that it signed an agreement to acquire the remaining 25% stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment (MLSE) from Kilmer Sports Inc. for C$4.35 billion in cash, implying a 100% valuation of C$17.4 billion (no per-share price applicable as MLSE is private). The board unanimously supports the deal. Rogers intends to finance with committed liquidity and has previously disclosed plans to sell a minority stake in its consolidated sports/media assets within a year. The transaction requires league approvals and is expected to close in Q4 2026. Watch for regulatory clearance timing and the announced minority stake sale.
